abdominal aortic aneurysm.basic_details: An abdominal aortic aneurysm is a weak, bulging spot in the main blood vessel that carries blood from your heart down through your belly. If it gets too big, it can burst and become very dangerous.
emergency_signs: Sudden severe stomach or back pain
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Cut down on salty foods to help keep your blood pressure low.
Avoid greasy and fatty foods to keep your heart healthy.
treatment_options: surgery to fix the blood vessel
small tube placed inside the vessel
recovery_time: If you have surgery, you will usually need to stay in the hospital for a few days.
Most people need about four to six weeks of gentle rest at home to heal fully.
You might feel tired and sore around your belly for the first couple of weeks.
Your doctor will check on you regularly to make sure you are healing the right way.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks every day to build up your strength slowly.
Do not lift anything heavy, like furniture or heavy groceries, for several weeks.
Avoid high-impact sports, running, or heavy weightlifting.
Stop exercising right away if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or sharp pain.
recommended_tests: Get an ultrasound, which uses safe sound waves to take pictures of your belly.
Have a CT scan if your doctor needs a very detailed look at your blood vessel.
Check your blood pressure regularly at home and during doctor visits.
Get routine blood tests to check your overall health and cholesterol levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have sudden belly pain
if you have back pain that does not go away

abdominal hernia.basic_details: An abdominal hernia happens when a part of your inside body pushes through a weak spot in your belly muscles. This can cause a small lump that might hurt when you bend over or lift things.
emergency_signs: Unable to push the bulge back
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your stomach soft.
Choose whole grains like brown bread and oatmeal every day.
Drink lots of water to help your digestion stay smooth.
Stay away from spicy or greasy foods that can upset your tummy.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling a bit better after one to two weeks.
It usually takes about six weeks for your belly to fully heal.
You might need to rest more than usual during the first month.
Listen to your body and do not rush back to your normal routine.
physical_activities: Take short, gentle walks around your house to help your body heal.
Do not lift anything heavy, even bags of groceries or pets.
Avoid hard exercises like running or sit-ups until your doctor says it is safe.
Bend at your knees with a straight back if you need to pick something up.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where the doctor gently presses on your belly.
An ultrasound scan to look at the inside of your stomach muscles.
A CT scan if the doctor needs a clearer picture of the lump.
Blood tests to make sure your body is ready if you need surgery.
when_to_visit_doctor: you see a painful lump on your belly
the bulge changes color to red or purple
you feel very sick to your stomach and vomit
the pain gets worse very fast

abscess of nose.basic_details: An abscess of the nose is a painful, swollen lump filled with pus that forms on or inside the nose. It happens when germs get trapped in a hair pore or a small cut and cause an infection.
precautions: Visit a doctor if swelling increases
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Drink lots of water every day to stay hydrated and flush out sickness.
Choose soft foods if your nose hurts when you move your mouth to chew.
Avoid very salty or spicy foods that might make you uncomfortable.
treatment_options: doctor cuts and drains the pus
recovery_time: Most nose abscesses start to feel better within a few days after seeing a doctor.
Complete healing usually takes about one to two weeks with proper care.
Larger infections or ones that needed a small procedure might take a little longer.
Always finish all your medicine even if you start feeling better quickly.
physical_activities: Rest as much as possible for the first few days to let your body recover.
Avoid heavy exercise or sports that could cause someone to bump your nose.
Take gentle, short walks around your home if you feel up to moving.
Avoid swimming pools or hot tubs until the infection is completely gone.
recommended_tests: A simple physical check where the doctor looks closely at your nose.
A gentle swab test if the doctor needs to find out what kind of germ caused it.
A blood test sometimes, just to see how well your body is fighting the infection.
No complicated scans are usually needed for a simple nose abscess.

abscess of the pharynx.basic_details: An abscess of the pharynx is a painful pocket of pus that forms in the back of your throat due to an infection. It can make it very hard to swallow food or even your own spit.
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and applesauce that do not hurt your throat.
Drink plenty of cold water and clear broths to keep your body from drying out.
Stay away from spicy foods, chips, and crusty bread that can scratch your throat.
Avoid very hot drinks and acidic juices like orange juice because they will sting.
treatment_options: draining the pus with a small cut
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within three to five days after getting treatment.
You might need a small medical procedure to drain the pus, which speeds up healing.
It usually takes about one to two weeks to be fully healed and back to normal.
Always finish all your prescribed medicine even if you start feeling better early.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest to help your body fight off the severe infection.
Avoid heavy lifting, running, or hard workouts until you are completely healed.
Take it slow and easy around the house during your first few days of recovery.
Only go back to work or school once your fever is gone and you feel strong again.
recommended_tests: A doctor will use a small light to look closely inside your mouth and throat.
You might need a gentle neck scan, like a CT scan, to see how big the pocket of pus is.
Doctors may take a small swab of your throat to find the exact germ causing the trouble.
Blood tests might be done to check how well your body is fighting the infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: you have a very sore throat
it is hard to swallow your spit

acanthosis nigricans.basic_details: Acanthosis nigricans is a skin condition that causes dark, thick, and velvety patches to appear, usually in the body folds like the neck and armpits. It is most often linked to having too much insulin in your body, usually because of weight or diabetes.
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh vegetables and whole grains instead of white bread.
Cut down heavily on sugary snacks, candies, and sweet drinks.
Choose healthy fats like olive oil and nuts.
Eat smaller portions to help manage your weight.
recovery_time: The dark skin fades very slowly, often taking several months.
Improvement depends mostly on fixing the root cause like high insulin.
Making lasting lifestyle changes brings the fastest results.
Every person heals at a different speed based on their health.
physical_activities: Try to walk briskly for 30 minutes every single day.
Do fun activities like swimming, cycling, or dancing.
Add light weight training to help your body use sugar better.
Find a workout buddy to help keep you moving and motivated.
recommended_tests: A blood sugar test to check for diabetes or pre-diabetes.
A blood test to check your body's insulin levels.
Hormone blood tests to see if your glands are working right.
A simple visual check by a skin doctor.
when_to_visit_doctor: if the skin starts to hurt

acariasis.basic_details: Acariasis is a very small skin problem caused by tiny bugs like mites living on your body. It can make your skin feel super itchy and uncomfortable.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your skin healthy and hydrated.
Eat healthy foods like chicken or beans to give your body strength.
Try to stay away from junk food and sugary snacks while you are healing.
treatment_options: Wash all clothes in hot water
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better after about one or two weeks.
The annoying itching might stay for a few days even after the bugs are gone.
You must wash all your clothes and bed sheets in hot water so the bugs do not come back.
Go back to see your doctor if your skin does not get better soon.
physical_activities: You can still go for light walks outside while you are healing.
Try not to sweat too much because sweat can make your itchy skin feel worse.
Do gentle stretching exercises at home to stay active.
Rest as much as you can so your body has energy to fight the skin problem.
recommended_tests: The doctor will look closely at your itchy skin with a magnifying glass.
Sometimes the doctor takes a tiny, painless scrape of your skin to look under a microscope.
A skin test helps the doctor make sure you have tiny bugs and not something else.
You might answer a few simple questions about where you have been traveling or sleeping.
when_to_visit_doctor: Skin gets very red or infected
Treatment does not work after two weeks

achalasia.basic_details: Achalasia is a rare swallowing problem where the muscular tube that carries food from your mouth to your stomach fails to open properly, making it hard to eat and drink.
reason: Nerve damage in the food pipe
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes, yogurt, and soup that slide down easily.
Drink plenty of water with your meals to help push food down into your stomach.
Take small bites and chew your food very thoroughly before swallowing.
Avoid dry breads, tough meats, and very cold drinks which can make swallowing harder.
recovery_time: Recovery after a simple stretching procedure usually takes just one to two days.
Healing after a small surgery to cut the tight muscle generally takes about one to two weeks.
You might need to eat only liquids for the first few days while your throat heals.
Most people return to their normal daily routines within a couple of weeks.
physical_activities: Take gentle walks every day to keep your body moving and help your digestion.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts for the first week or two after any treatment.
Do not lie flat right after moving or exercising to prevent food from coming back up.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel tired or low on energy.
recommended_tests: A special test where you swallow a liquid while an X-ray watches how it moves down.
A tube test that measures the pressure and squeezing strength inside your swallowing tube.
A camera test where a doctor looks inside your food pipe to check for irritation.
Basic blood tests to check your overall health and nutrition levels.

acne.basic_details: Acne is a common skin problem that happens when tiny holes in your skin get blocked with oil and dirt. This causes pimples, blackheads, and red bumps to show up on your face, back, or chest.
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water every day to keep your skin clean from the inside.
Eat more fresh fruits and green vegetables to help your skin heal.
Try to eat less sugary foods like candy, soda, and sweet treats.
Cut back on fast food and very greasy snacks that can make skin oily.
recovery_time: Small pimples usually start to go away in just a few days to a week.
Big, painful bumps under the skin can take several weeks to fully heal.
Clear skin takes time, so you might need to wait two to three months to see big changes.
Old red marks or dark spots can take a few months to fade away completely.
physical_activities: Go ahead and play sports or work out to stay healthy and happy.
Wash your face right after you sweat a lot so oil does not get trapped.
Wear loose, breathable clothes when you exercise so your skin does not get rubbed.
Take a quick shower right after working out to keep your body clean.
recommended_tests: Most people just need a doctor to look at their skin with their eyes.
A skin doctor might check your hormone levels with a simple blood test.
Sometimes a skin scrape test is done to check for tiny germs or mites.
Women might get hormone checks if their acne keeps coming back around their period.
when_to_visit_doctor: If over-the-counter medicine does not work
If acne leaves dark spots or scars
If you feel very sad about your skin

actinic keratosis.basic_details: Actinic keratosis is a rough, dry patch on the skin caused by too much time in the sun. It is important to treat it early because it can sometimes turn into skin cancer.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your skin stay healthy.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body hydrated.
Include foods with healthy fats, like fish and nuts, to protect your skin.
Try to cut down on sugary snacks and processed foods.
recovery_time: Most skin spots heal in about one to three weeks after treatment.
Redness and swelling usually go away after a few days.
Complete healing depends on how many spots you had and the treatment used.
Your skin might look pink and fresh as the new skin grows in.
physical_activities: You can do your normal light workouts and daily walks without worry.
Avoid heavy outdoor sports during peak sun hours in the middle of the day.
Wear loose clothing so it does not rub against the healing skin spots.
Stay indoors if your skin is raw or still healing from treatment.
recommended_tests: Let a doctor do a full body check to look at all your skin spots.
The doctor might use a special magnifying tool to look closely at the patch.
Sometimes, they take a tiny skin sample to test it in a lab.
Go for yearly skin check-ups to catch any new spots early.
when_to_visit_doctor: Spots start to bleed or hurt
Spots do not go away after treatment
New rough spots appear on the skin

acute bronchiolitis.basic_details: Acute bronchiolitis is a common chest infection that makes the smallest breathing tubes in the lungs swell up and fill with mucus. It mostly happens to babies and young children, making it hard for them to breathe.
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water and fluids to stay hydrated.
Eat small, easy meals if eating makes you too tired.
Feed babies smaller amounts of milk more often.
Eat warm soups to help soothe your throat.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within one to two weeks.
A mild cough might stick around for up to three weeks.
Rest as much as possible to help your body heal faster.
Keep track of your symptoms to make sure they do not get worse.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and rest while you are feeling sick.
Avoid heavy exercise or running until you are fully better.
Do only light walking around the house when you have energy.
Take deep breaths slowly when you are resting.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually just listen to your chest with a stethoscope.
A simple nose swab might be done to check for the virus.
A small sensor on your finger may check the oxygen in your blood.
An X-ray of the chest is rarely needed unless symptoms are severe.
when_to_visit_doctor: very sleepy or hard to wake up

acute bronchitis.basic_details: Acute bronchitis is a short-term illness where the breathing tubes in your chest get swollen and make a lot of mucus, leading to a long-lasting cough.
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of warm water and clear soup to keep your throat wet.
Eat honey in warm tea to help calm your coughing.
Choose soft fruits and vegetables that are easy to swallow.
Stay away from spicy or fried foods that can make you cough more.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within one to two weeks.
The annoying cough can sometimes linger for up to three weeks.
Your body needs plenty of rest to heal completely.
Go back to the doctor if you are not getting better after two weeks.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and rest as much as possible for the first few days.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard exercises until your cough goes away.
Take slow, gentle walks around your home only when you feel up to it.
Wait until your breathing returns to normal before starting normal workouts.
recommended_tests: A doctor will usually just listen to your chest with a stethoscope.
You might get a quick nose swab to check for the flu.
Sometimes a chest x-ray is done to make sure it is not pneumonia.
An oxygen check on your finger may be done to see how well you breathe.
when_to_visit_doctor: fever lasts more than three days

acute bronchospasm.basic_details: Acute bronchospasm is a sudden tightening of the muscles in your airways, making it very hard to breathe and causing wheezing and coughing.
precautions: Stay indoors in bad air quality
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of warm water throughout the day to keep your throat and airways clear.
Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables to help keep your immune system strong.
Stay away from foods that give you gas or make you feel bloated, as they can press on your chest.
Limit very salty and heavily processed foods which can sometimes trigger breathing trouble.
treatment_options: sit up straight and stay calm
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within a few minutes after using their quick-relief inhaler.
Full recovery from a bad episode can take a few hours of quiet rest and steady breathing.
If your breathing does not get better quickly, you must get emergency medical help right away.
Your recovery speed depends on how fast you take your medicine when the tight feeling starts.
physical_activities: Rest completely and sit upright until your breathing goes back to normal.
Avoid heavy exercise or running until your doctor says your lungs are fully healed.
Try gentle and slow stretching once you feel better and can breathe easily again.
Warm up very slowly if you do light exercises later, and stop immediately if you start to wheeze.
recommended_tests: A breathing test that measures how much air you can blow out of your lungs.
Checking the oxygen levels in your blood using a small clip placed on your finger.
Listening to your chest with a stethoscope to hear any whistling sounds in your lungs.
An allergy check to see if certain things in the air are causing your airways to tighten.

acute glaucoma.basic_details: Acute glaucoma is a sudden and painful buildup of pressure inside your eye. It happens when fluid cannot drain properly, and it needs fast medical help to protect your sight.
things_to_avoid: Waiting for it to get better
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water throughout the day instead of all at once.
Eat lots of colorful fruits and green vegetables to keep your eyes healthy.
Cut back on salty foods, as salt can increase fluid pressure in your body.
Limit how much caffeine you drink from coffee, tea, and soda.
treatment_options: Surgery to make a new fluid drain
recovery_time: Your eye pressure usually starts to drop within a few hours of treatment.
Most people start feeling much better after a few days of using their drops.
Full healing after any quick laser fix or surgery takes about one to two weeks.
You will need regular check-ups for the rest of your life to keep your eyes safe.
physical_activities: Rest quietly with your eyes closed during the first few days.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts that strain your face and eyes.
Do not bend over with your head lower than your waist.
Keep your head propped up with extra pillows when you sleep.
recommended_tests: An eye pressure test to check how hard or soft your eyeball is.
A special look inside your eye using a lighted magnifying tool.
A vision test to see if you can read letters clearly from far away.
A scan to look at the front part of your eye where fluid drains.
when_to_visit_doctor: Blurry vision with halos around lights
Red eye with nausea and vomiting

acute kidney injury.basic_details: Acute kidney injury is when your kidneys suddenly stop working well and cannot clean your blood like they should. This usually happens very fast over a few hours or days.
diet_recommendation: Eat less salt to help keep your blood pressure steady.
Eat smaller amounts of foods with high potassium like bananas and oranges.
Limit how much protein you eat so your kidneys do not have to work too hard.
Drink the exact amount of water your doctor tells you to drink.
recovery_time: Many people start feeling better within a few weeks.
Some people need to stay in the hospital for a few days to get care.
Your recovery speed depends on what caused the kidney problem in the first place.
Sometimes it takes a few months for your kidneys to get fully back to normal.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest while you are feeling sick and weak.
Take very short, slow walks around your room when you have some energy.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Stop moving and rest right away if you feel dizzy or very tired.
recommended_tests: Give a blood sample to check how well your kidneys are cleaning your body.
Give a urine sample to look for signs of trouble in your kidneys.
Get an ultrasound scan so doctors can take a picture of your kidneys.
Check your blood pressure and weight every single day.
when_to_visit_doctor: you feel very tired and sick

acute otitis media.basic_details: Acute otitis media is a painful ear infection that happens when fluid gets trapped behind your eardrum and germs grow. It is very common in children and often starts after a cold.
emergency_signs: Blood or pus draining from ear
things_to_avoid: Putting cotton swabs deep in ear
Drinking from a bottle while lying flat
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water and warm liquids to stay hydrated.
Eat soft foods if chewing makes your jaw and ear hurt.
Eat fruits and vegetables with vitamin C to help your body heal.
Avoid foods that cause allergies if they tend to plug up your ears.
treatment_options: wait and see if it gets better
use warm cloth on the ear
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within two to three days.
Pain and fever usually go away completely in about a week.
Some fluid might stay in your ear for a few weeks, which is normal.
Hearing usually goes back to normal once all the fluid drains away.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest while you have a fever and feel weak.
Avoid swimming or getting water inside your sore ear.
Take it easy and do not do heavy workouts until your ear pain is gone.
Keep your head propped up on extra pillows when resting to help your ears drain.
recommended_tests: A doctor will look inside your ear with a special lighted tool called an otoscope.
The doctor might gently blow a puff of air into your ear to see if the eardrum moves.
A hearing check might be done if ear infections happen a lot.
Fluid from the ear might be tested if the infection does not get better with medicine.
when_to_visit_doctor: pain does not get better in two days
fluid or pus comes out of the ear

acute pancreatitis.basic_details: Acute pancreatitis is a sudden swelling and irritation of your pancreas, which is a small organ near your stomach that helps you digest food. This causes a very bad bellyache and makes you feel sick.
diet_recommendation: Do not eat or drink anything at first so your belly can rest and heal.
Start drinking clear liquids like water or broth slowly when your doctor says it is okay.
Eat small, plain meals like plain rice, toast, and applesauce as you start feeling better.
Stay away from greasy, fatty, or spicy foods, and do not drink any alcohol.
treatment_options: not eating food for a short time
surgery to remove gallstones if needed
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better and go home from the hospital in a few days.
It can take a few weeks for your body to fully heal and get your strength back.
Severe cases might need a longer stay in the hospital and more time to rest at home.
Listen to your body and take things slow so you do not push yourself too hard.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and get as much rest as you can during the first few days.
Take very short, slow walks around your room once you feel a little stronger.
Do not do any heavy lifting, running, or hard workouts while you are healing.
Slowly go back to your normal daily chores only when your doctor says it is safe.
recommended_tests: Get blood tests to check how well your organs are working and find out why you hurt.
Have a belly scan, like an ultrasound or CT scan, to look closely at your pancreas.
Do an MRI scan if the doctor needs a better picture of your tummy area.
Have your heart checked with a simple monitor to make sure you are stable.
when_to_visit_doctor: very bad belly pain that does not stop
throwing up a lot and cannot keep water down

acute respiratory distress syndrome (ard.basic_details: Acute respiratory distress syndrome, or ARDS, is a serious lung condition where fluid fills up in your air sacs, making it very hard to breathe and get enough oxygen into your body.
precautions: Seek emergency care for breathing issues
diet_recommendation: Eat small, easy-to-chew meals so you do not get too tired while eating.
Drink plenty of water and other fluids to stay hydrated.
Include soft foods like soups, mashed potatoes, and smoothies if swallowing is hard.
Ask a doctor if you need special liquid drinks that give you extra energy and strength.
recovery_time: Healing from ARDS usually takes many weeks or even months.
Most people spend time in the hospital, and some need extra care in a rehab center.
You will likely feel very tired for a long time after leaving the hospital.
Full recovery happens slowly, day by day, as your lungs get stronger.
physical_activities: Start with simple breathing exercises while sitting or lying in bed.
Move your arms and legs gently while in bed to keep your blood flowing.
Take short, slow walks around your room with help when you feel a bit stronger.
Join a gentle lung rehab program guided by experts to safely rebuild your strength.
recommended_tests: Chest X-rays to look at your lungs and see how much fluid is inside.
Blood tests to check how much oxygen and carbon dioxide are in your body.
Pulse checks using a small clip on your finger to measure your oxygen levels.
Breathing tests to check how well your lungs are working over time.

acute sinusitis.basic_details: Acute sinusitis is a sudden swelling in the spaces inside your nose and head. It makes it hard to breathe through your nose and can cause a lot of face pain.
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of plain water to help thin out the mucus in your head.
Eat warm chicken soup to soothe your throat and help clear your nose.
Add a little garlic and ginger to your meals to help fight the sickness.
Eat fresh fruits like oranges that have vitamin C to boost your body.
treatment_options: apply a warm wet cloth to the face
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within seven to ten days.
Some mild stuffiness can sometimes hang around for up to two weeks.
You should rest as much as possible during the first few days.
Call a doctor if you are not getting better after ten full days.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest while your body is fighting the infection.
Take slow, gentle walks around the house if you feel up to moving.
Avoid heavy workouts or lifting gym weights until your head stops hurting.
Do not go swimming, as pool water can irritate your sensitive nose.
recommended_tests: A regular doctor will usually just look inside your nose with a small light.
Your doctor might gently press on your cheeks and forehead to check for pain.
You rarely need an X-ray unless your sickness lasts a very long time.
A nose swab is sometimes used if doctors think germs are causing it.
when_to_visit_doctor: symptoms last longer than ten days
symptoms get better then get much worse

acute stress reaction.basic_details: An acute stress reaction is a heavy emotional and physical shock that happens right after living through a very scary or stressful event. It can make you feel mixed up, nervous, or numb for a short time.
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay strong.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep calm.
Stay away from too much coffee and sugary drinks.
Eat warm, comforting meals like soups and whole grains.
treatment_options: talk to a mental health helper
rest in a safe and quiet place
spend time with family or friends
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within a few days.
Some stress feelings might last for up to four weeks.
Healing happens faster when you rest and talk about it.
Every person recovers at their own speed and time.
physical_activities: Take slow, gentle walks outside in the fresh air.
Do deep breathing exercises to help lower your heartbeat.
Try light stretching to release tight muscles in your body.
Avoid heavy workouts until you feel completely calm again.
recommended_tests: Talk with a doctor to check how you are feeling inside.
Answer simple questions about your sleep and mood.
Check your blood pressure to see if your body is stressed.
No special blood tests or X-rays are usually needed.
when_to_visit_doctor: if fear does not go away after a few days
if you cannot sleep or eat
if you feel very sad all the time
if you cannot do your daily work

adhesive capsulitis of the shoulder.basic_details: Adhesive capsulitis, also known as frozen shoulder, is a painful condition where your shoulder joint becomes stiff and very hard to move.
emergency_signs: Sudden loss of feeling in arm
Pain shooting down the left arm
things_to_avoid: Forcing the arm past its limit
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your joints healthy.
Eat foods like fish and nuts that help lower body swelling.
Try to cut down on sugary snacks and processed foods.
recovery_time: It can take anywhere from several months to a couple of years to fully heal.
The healing happens in slow steps, starting with easing the pain.
Being patient is very important because your shoulder gets better very slowly.
Doing your daily gentle stretches helps speed up your recovery time.
physical_activities: Do gentle arm swings and stretches taught by a physical therapist.
Use a towel behind your back to slowly pull your arm up.
Avoid heavy lifting or sudden, jerking movements with the bad arm.
Stop exercising right away if you feel sharp or intense pain.
recommended_tests: Let a doctor gently move your arm to see how far it can go.
Get an X-ray to make sure nothing else is wrong with your bones.
Sometimes an MRI is done to look closely at the shoulder tissue.
Talk about your pain history and when it hurts the most.
when_to_visit_doctor: pain wakes you up at night

adjustment reaction.basic_details: An adjustment reaction happens when you have a hard time dealing with a big life change or stress, like a new job, a move, or a breakup, making you feel very sad or worried.
emergency_signs: Feeling life is not worth living
Inability to get out of bed
things_to_avoid: Taking on too many new tasks
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body and mind healthy.
Drink lots of water every day to stay hydrated and feel your best.
Try to cut back on too much sugar and junk food, as they can mess with your mood.
Limit how much caffeine and alcohol you have, because they can make you feel more anxious.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within a few weeks or months after the big change happens.
The time it takes to heal is different for everyone, so try not to rush yourself.
Recovery can be faster if you talk about your feelings with someone you trust.
You will have good days and bad days, and that is a totally normal part of healing.
physical_activities: Go for a nice, easy walk outside every day to clear your head.
Try simple stretching or yoga to help your body let go of built-up stress.
Do fun hobbies or light exercises that make you smile and keep you busy.
Get a good amount of sleep each night so your body and brain can rest.
recommended_tests: A friendly chat with a doctor or counselor to talk about how you are feeling.
Answering simple questions on a paper about your daily mood and stress levels.
A basic blood check just to make sure other health issues are not causing your tiredness.
A routine check of your blood pressure and heart rate to see how your body handles stress.
when_to_visit_doctor: Feeling very sad for a long time

adrenal adenoma.basic_details: An adrenal adenoma is a small, non-cancerous growth that forms on your adrenal glands, which are tiny organs sitting above your kidneys. Most of the time these growths do not cause any harm or symptoms, but sometimes they can make too many hormones.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Limit the amount of salt and sugary snacks you eat.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
recovery_time: If you do not need surgery, you can live your normal life right away.
If you have surgery to remove it, you may need a few weeks to heal at home.
Expect to feel tired for the first week or two after an operation.
Full healing from surgery usually takes about four to six weeks.
physical_activities: Go for gentle daily walks to keep your body moving safely.
Avoid heavy lifting and intense workouts until your doctor says it is okay.
Do light stretching exercises to help your muscles stay relaxed.
Stop exercising right away if you feel dizzy, sick, or very tired.
recommended_tests: Get regular blood tests to check your body's hormone levels.
Do urine tests to see how well your adrenal glands are working.
Have a CT scan or MRI so doctors can take pictures of the growth.
Check your blood pressure often to make sure it stays in a safe range.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have high blood pressure that is hard to control
if you gain weight quickly for no clear reason
if you feel very weak or tired all the time
if you have sudden, severe belly or back pain

alcohol abuse.basic_details: Alcohol abuse is when a person drinks too much alcohol, making it hard to control and causing problems in their daily life and health.
precautions: Tell friends about your goal to stop
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water and other healthy drinks to wash out toxins and stay strong.
Eat whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Choose lean proteins like chicken, fish, and beans to help repair your muscles and organs.
recovery_time: The first week is usually the hardest, as your body gets used to not having alcohol.
Most physical withdrawal signs start to get much better after about one to two weeks.
Feeling mentally strong and getting back on track can take several months or even a full year.
Healing is a lifelong journey, and taking it one day at a time is the best way to succeed.
physical_activities: Go for a short walk every day to clear your head and boost your mood.
Try gentle stretching or yoga to help your body relax and release stress.
Do fun hobbies like gardening or swimming to keep your body and mind busy.
Start with light exercises and slowly build up as you feel stronger and healthier.
recommended_tests: Simple blood tests to check how well your liver is working.
General blood counts to see if you have enough vitamins and iron.
A quick chat with a doctor or counselor to talk about your feelings and drinking habits.
Blood pressure and heart checks to make sure your heart is staying healthy.

alcohol intoxication.basic_details: Alcohol intoxication happens when you drink too much alcohol faster than your body can process it, leading to changes in behavior and mental state.
precautions: Eat a full meal before drinking
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to help your body wash out the alcohol.
Eat plain foods like toast or crackers to settle your stomach.
Drink clear broths or sports drinks to get back lost salts.
Avoid greasy or spicy foods that can make your stomach upset.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within 12 to 24 hours.
Your body needs a full night of good sleep to reset.
Severe cases may need a hospital stay for a day or two.
Feeling tired and sluggish can last for a full day after drinking.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and get plenty of rest until you feel steady.
Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you are fully sober.
Take slow, short walks around the house only if you feel balanced.
Avoid hard workouts or heavy lifting while your body is recovering.
recommended_tests: A breathalyzer test to check the amount of alcohol in your breath.
A blood test to check your sugar and alcohol levels.
A urine test to see how well your body is flushing toxins.
A physical check by a nurse to watch your breathing and heart rate.

alcohol withdrawal.basic_details: Alcohol withdrawal happens when a person who drinks a lot suddenly stops or cuts back. The body and brain struggle to adjust, causing shaking, sweating, and feeling very sick.
emergency_signs: Seeing things that are not there
things_to_avoid: Quitting alone if a heavy drinker
Taking other drugs to calm down
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water and clear juices to stop your body from drying out.
Eat simple foods like soup, crackers, and toast if your stomach feels upset.
Eat small meals often to keep your energy up while you heal.
Take vitamins, especially B vitamins, to help your body and brain recover.
recovery_time: Most physical symptoms start within a few hours and peak in two days.
The worst physical shaking and sweating usually go away after about a week.
Feeling tired and having trouble sleeping can last for a few weeks.
Mental healing and cravings can take many months of ongoing support.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest during the first few days while your body detoxes.
Do very light walking around the room only when you feel steady and strong enough.
Avoid heavy lifting, driving, or hard exercise until your doctor says it is safe.
Try slow breathing and gentle stretching to help calm your body and mind.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check your vitamin levels, liver health, and hydration.
A heart check to make sure your pulse and blood pressure are safe.
A urine test to check for other substances in your body.
A simple brain and alertness check by a nurse or doctor.

alcoholic liver disease.basic_details: Alcoholic liver disease happens when drinking too much alcohol over a long time damages your liver, making it hard for your body to clean your blood.
precautions: Ask a doctor before taking pills
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Eat lean protein like chicken, fish, beans, and eggs.
Drink plenty of water and stay away from sugary drinks.
recovery_time: Mild liver damage can start to heal within a few weeks of stopping alcohol.
Severe damage can take many months or even years to get better.
Some long-term damage may never fully go away, but you can stop it from getting worse.
Your personal recovery speed depends entirely on how much you drank and your overall health.
physical_activities: Take easy, short daily walks around your neighborhood.
Do light stretching in your living room to stay limber.
Avoid heavy lifting or very hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel too tired.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check how well your liver is currently working.
An ultrasound picture of your belly to look at the size of your liver.
A special scan that checks how stiff or scarred your liver is.
A physical exam where the doctor gently presses on your stomach.

allergy.basic_details: An allergy happens when your body overreacts to harmless things like pollen, dust, or certain foods. This makes your immune system fight back, causing sneezing, rashes, or a runny nose.
things_to_avoid: Going out on high pollen days
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your immune system stay strong.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body hydrated and clear out irritants.
Stay away from foods that you already know give you an upset stomach or rashes.
Try eating foods with ginger or turmeric, as they can help calm down swelling in your body.
treatment_options: Avoid the things that cause allergy
recovery_time: Mild allergy symptoms like a sneeze or sniffle usually go away in a few hours.
If you stay away from the thing that triggers it, you will feel better very fast.
Skin rashes might take a few days to completely fade away.
Some seasonal allergies can last for a few weeks while the weather changes.
physical_activities: Try to work out indoors in a clean room when the pollen count outside is very high.
Take a quick shower and wash your clothes after exercising outside to remove dust.
Do light stretching or yoga at home to stay active without breathing in outdoor air.
Avoid heavy workouts in parks with lots of grass and trees on windy days.
recommended_tests: Get a skin prick test where a doctor puts tiny drops of allergens on your arm to see what causes a reaction.
Take a blood test to check if your body makes special antibodies against specific things.
Keep a daily diary of what you eat and touch to find out what triggers your symptoms.
Visit a doctor for a physical checkup to look at your skin, eyes, and breathing.

allergy to animals.basic_details: An allergy to animals happens when your body overreacts to proteins found in an animal's dander, saliva, or urine. This causes annoying symptoms like sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes when you are around pets.
precautions: Keep pets out of the bedroom
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help boost your overall immune system.
Drink lots of water every day to help keep your throat and nose clear.
Include foods with healthy fats, like fish and nuts, to help calm body swelling.
Try to eat less processed foods and sugar to keep your body feeling its best.
recovery_time: Sneezing and itchy eyes usually start to fade within a few hours of leaving the animal.
Stuffy noses and lingering breathing issues can sometimes take a full day to completely clear up.
If your home has a lot of trapped pet dander, it might take a few days of cleaning to feel totally normal.
Long-term allergy treatments, like allergy shots, can take many months to train your body to stop reacting.
physical_activities: Try to exercise outdoors or in pet-free indoor gyms instead of people's homes with pets.
Wash your hands and change your clothes right after you finish working out near animals.
Take slow, easy breaths during workouts if your chest feels a bit tight from dust.
Shower immediately after outdoor sports where you might have brushed against animals or outdoor allergens.
recommended_tests: Get a simple skin prick test where a doctor puts tiny drops of animal proteins on your skin to see if it bumps up.
Take a blood test to check if your body makes special allergy antibodies when it sees animal dander.
Keep a daily diary of your sneezes to show your doctor when your allergies act up the most.
Have a doctor listen to your lungs with a stethoscope if your breathing gets heavy around pets.
when_to_visit_doctor: sneezing and runny nose last very long

alopecia.basic_details: Alopecia is a common condition that makes your hair fall out in small patches or all over your head. It happens when your body's defense system accidentally attacks the places where hair grows.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day to keep your body healthy.
Include foods like fish, eggs, and beans to help your hair grow strong.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Avoid eating too much junk food and sugary snacks.
recovery_time: Hair can start growing back on its own in a few months without any treatment.
For some people, it might take a year or longer to see new hair.
Hair might grow back and then fall out again later on.
Every person's healing time is different and depends on the type of hair loss.
physical_activities: Go for light walks outside to keep your body moving and happy.
Try gentle yoga or stretching to help lower your daily stress.
Do fun hobbies that make you feel relaxed and good about yourself.
Avoid heavy workouts that make you sweat a lot if they make you uncomfortable.
recommended_tests: Have a doctor look closely at your scalp and skin.
Do a simple blood test to check if your body is missing important vitamins.
Check your hormone levels with a routine blood check.
Do a gentle hair pull test to see how easily your hair comes out.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel worried about hair loss

alzheimer disease.basic_details: Alzheimer's disease is a brain condition that slowly makes it hard to remember things, think clearly, and do daily tasks. Over time, a person may need more help from family and friends.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables every day.
Choose healthy fats like olive oil and nuts for snacks.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Eat fish and whole grains that are good for brain health.
treatment_options: getting support from family and caregivers
recovery_time: Alzheimer's is a long-term condition that does not go away.
Symptoms usually get worse slowly over many years.
Good daily care can help slow down memory loss.
Support and comfort can improve daily life for a long time.
physical_activities: Take short, gentle walks outside every afternoon.
Do light stretching in the morning to stay flexible.
Dance slowly to favorite music in the living room.
Play simple catch with a soft ball for arm movement.
recommended_tests: Memory puzzles and simple talk tests with a doctor.
Brain scans like an MRI to look inside the head.
Blood tests to check for other health problems.
Checkups to see how well the person handles daily tasks.
when_to_visit_doctor: when memory loss starts to get worse
when the person forgets how to do easy tasks
when mood or personality changes a lot
when they get lost in familiar places

amblyopia.basic_details: Amblyopia, also called lazy eye, is when one eye does not work together properly with the brain, making the vision in that eye weaker. It usually starts during childhood.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of carrots and sweet potatoes to help your eyesight.
Include green leafy vegetables like spinach in your daily meals.
Eat fish rich in good oils to support overall eye health.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body healthy.
treatment_options: covering the strong eye with a patch
recovery_time: It can take several weeks to many months to see improvement.
Children often get better faster than adults do.
You must follow the daily eye patch routine for it to work.
Recovery speed is different for every single person.
physical_activities: Play fun games that require you to wear a patch over your strong eye.
Do simple puzzles or draw pictures to help your lazy eye focus.
Play catch with a soft ball to practice hand and eye teamwork.
Limit screen time on phones and tablets to give your eyes a rest.
recommended_tests: A standard reading chart test to check how well you see letters.
An eye drop test to make your pupils bigger for a better look inside.
A cover test to see how well your eyes line up together.
A special light check of the back of your eye to make sure it is healthy.
when_to_visit_doctor: if a child squints a lot
if one eye turns inward or outward
if vision seems blurry in one eye

amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (als).basic_details: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or ALS, is a rare sickness that makes the nerves in your body slowly stop working. Over time, this makes your muscles weak and hard to move.
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods that are very easy to chew and swallow.
Choose foods with lots of calories to keep your energy up.
Drink plenty of water and liquids to avoid drying out.
Eat smaller meals more often if eating a big meal is too hard.
recovery_time: There is no known cure to make this sickness go away completely.
Special care focuses on keeping you comfortable and safe each day.
Good daily habits and support can help you live a better life.
The timeline is different for everyone, as the sickness moves at its own pace.
physical_activities: Do gentle stretches with help to keep your arms and legs loose.
Go for light walks if your body feels strong enough.
Work with a physical therapist to learn safe and easy movements.
Rest often so you do not make your weak muscles too tired.
recommended_tests: Electrical tests on your muscles to see how they talk to your nerves.
Pictures of your brain and spine to check your overall health.
Blood tests to make sure no other sickness is causing your trouble.
Breathing checks to see how well your lungs are working.

anal fissure.basic_details: An anal fissure is a tiny tear in the skin around the bottom area. It usually happens when passing hard poop and can cause pain or a bit of blood.
emergency_signs: Large amount of blood in toilet
things_to_avoid: Sitting on toilet for a long time
diet_recommendation: Eat lots of high-fiber foods like fruits, veggies, and whole grains.
Drink plenty of water every single day to keep your tummy happy.
Eat beans and lentils to help soften your daily bathroom trips.
Avoid eating too much fast food, chips, or foods with very little fiber.
recovery_time: Small tears usually start feeling better within a few days to a couple of weeks.
Full healing can sometimes take up to four to six weeks if you eat right.
Doing warm water soaks daily helps speed up how fast you heal.
Call your doctor if the sharp pain does not get better after a couple of weeks.
physical_activities: Take short, gentle walks to keep your blood flowing nicely.
Avoid heavy lifting until the area is fully healed and pain-free.
Try not to sit on hard surfaces for very long periods of time.
Skip intense cycling or horseback riding until the skin is better.
recommended_tests: A doctor will usually just look at the area gently with your permission.
They might ask you questions about your bathroom habits and diet.
Sometimes they gently check inside with a tiny tool to make sure nothing else is wrong.
Blood tests are rarely needed unless the doctor wants to check for other tummy issues.
when_to_visit_doctor: you see a lot of blood

anemia.basic_details: Anemia is a common condition where your body does not have enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen to your organs, making you feel very tired and weak.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of red meat, chicken, and fish to get iron.
Eat dark green leafy vegetables like spinach every day.
Eat beans, lentils, and nuts for extra strength.
Drink orange juice with your meals because vitamin C helps your body soak up iron.
recovery_time: You might start feeling a bit better in just one to two weeks.
It usually takes about two to three months to get your iron back to normal.
Severe cases can take several months of steady care to fully heal.
Your recovery speed depends on following your doctor's food and medicine plan.
physical_activities: Take slow, short walks around your house or yard.
Stop and rest right away if you feel dizzy or out of breath.
Do light stretching instead of heavy workouts.
Avoid running or heavy lifting until your energy comes back.
recommended_tests: Get a complete blood count test to check your blood cells.
Test your ferritin levels to see how much iron is stored in your body.
Check your vitamin B12 levels with a simple blood draw.
Test your folate levels to make sure you have enough B vitamin.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel very tired every day

anemia due to chronic kidney disease.basic_details: Your kidneys are not working well, so they cannot make enough of a special signal your body needs to build healthy blood. This leaves you feeling very tired and weak.
diet_recommendation: Eat foods with iron like beans, lentils, and lean red meats.
Include foods with vitamin C, like oranges, to help your body use iron better.
Limit foods high in salt, phosphorus, and potassium to protect your kidneys.
Drink the amount of water and liquids that your doctor tells you is safe.
recovery_time: This is usually a long-term condition that needs ongoing care rather than a quick fix.
You might start feeling a bit more energetic after a few weeks of starting treatment.
It can take several months for your blood counts to return to a safe, steady range.
You will need regular check-ups for the rest of your life to stay healthy.
physical_activities: Take short, gentle walks around your house or neighborhood when you have energy.
Do light stretching to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Stop and rest immediately if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or very weak.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts until your doctor says your strength is back.
recommended_tests: A simple blood test to check your hemoglobin levels and see how much iron is in your body.
Blood tests to check how well your kidneys are filtering waste products.
A test to measure your ferritin, which shows how much iron your body has stored away.
Blood pressure checks at every doctor visit to keep your heart safe.

anemia of chronic disease.basic_details: Anemia of chronic disease is a low red blood cell count that happens because your body is fighting a long-term illness or infection. Your body hides away iron so that bad germs cannot use it, but this also leaves your blood with too little iron to make healthy cells.
things_to_avoid: Taking extra iron pills on your own
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body strong.
Include lean meats, beans, and lentils in your daily meals.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Eat foods with vitamin C, like oranges, to help your body use nutrients better.
recovery_time: Healing takes time because it depends entirely on getting the main sickness under control.
You might start feeling a little more energetic within a few weeks of treating the root cause.
Full recovery can take several months as your body slowly builds up healthy blood again.
Your doctor will need to check your blood often to see how well you are healing.
physical_activities: Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel tired or weak.
Take short, easy walks around your house or neighborhood when you have energy.
Avoid heavy lifting or very hard workouts until your strength comes back.
Slowly add more gentle movement to your day as you start to feel better.
recommended_tests: A simple blood test called a complete blood count checks your red blood cell levels.
Tests to check your body's iron stores and how it handles iron.
Blood checks to look for signs of ongoing inflammation or long-term sickness.
Kidney function tests to make sure your body is working the way it should.
when_to_visit_doctor: you feel very tired all the time

angina.basic_details: Angina is chest pain that happens when your heart does not get enough oxygen-rich blood. It is a warning sign that your heart is working too hard.
emergency_signs: Pain spreading to arm or jaw
Pain that won't go away with rest
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Cut down on greasy, fried, and fast foods.
Use less salt in your food to help keep your blood pressure low.
treatment_options: Take rest when chest pain starts
Heart surgery or stents if needed
recovery_time: Chest pain from a single attack usually goes away in a few minutes when you rest.
Feeling better overall can take a few weeks of eating right and taking medicine.
Healing takes longer if you need heart surgery or procedures.
It is a lifelong journey of taking care of your heart every single day.
physical_activities: Take slow, gentle walks every day to build your strength.
Stop immediately and rest if your chest starts to hurt.
Avoid heavy lifting or pushing hard objects.
Do light stretching to keep your body moving without stressing your heart.
recommended_tests: An electrical tracing of your heartbeat to check for problems.
Walking on a treadmill while hooked up to monitors to see how your heart handles stress.
Taking pictures of your heart using sound waves.
Blood tests to check your sugar and cholesterol levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: If chest pain happens more often
If pain lasts longer than usual
If medicine does not stop the pain
If you feel dizzy or short of breath

ankylosing spondylitis.basic_details: Ankylosing spondylitis is a type of arthritis that causes pain and stiffness in your spine. Over time, some bones in the back can fuse together, making it harder to bend.
things_to_avoid: Sitting in one position for long
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink lots of water every day to stay healthy and hydrated.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and processed foods that can cause swelling.
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition, meaning it does not go away completely in a few weeks.
Good days and bad days happen, and how you feel can change from week to week.
Most people find their pain gets much easier to manage after starting the right treatment plan.
Healing and feeling better is an ongoing journey that takes steady daily care.
physical_activities: Take gentle walks every day to keep your back loose and moving.
Do easy stretching exercises in the morning to wake up stiff muscles.
Try swimming, because the water supports your body while you exercise.
Practice good posture when sitting and standing to protect your spine.
recommended_tests: X-rays to let the doctor look closely at the bones in your spine.
Blood tests to check for signs of swelling or irritation in your body.
MRI scans to get a very clear picture of your joints and tissues.
Physical movement checks where the doctor sees how far you can bend and twist.

anxiety.basic_details: Anxiety is a mental health condition where a person feels very worried, nervous, or scared all the time, even when there is no real danger. It can make it hard to relax and get through the day.
emergency_signs: Chest pain like a heart attack
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to keep your body healthy and calm.
Try to eat less sugar and junk food, as they can make you jittery.
Cut back on coffee and energy drinks because caffeine can make you feel more nervous.
recovery_time: Everyone feels better at their own speed, so there is no fixed timeline.
Some people start feeling better in a few weeks with the right help.
For others, it can take a few months of daily practice and care.
Learning to manage anxiety is a lifelong journey with good days and bad days.
physical_activities: Go for a short walk outside every day to clear your mind.
Try simple stretching or yoga to help your tight muscles relax.
Dance to your favorite music in your room to boost your mood.
Do deep breathing exercises when you feel your heart racing.
recommended_tests: Talk with a doctor or mental health expert about how you feel.
Answer a simple questionnaire about your daily worries and sleep.
Get a basic blood test to make sure other health issues are not causing your stress.
Have a chat about your sleep habits and daily stress levels.

aortic valve disease.basic_details: Aortic valve disease happens when the door in your heart that controls blood flow does not work the right way. This makes your heart work harder to pump blood to the rest of your body.
precautions: Go to all heart doctor visits
diet_recommendation: Eat less salt to help keep your blood pressure at a healthy level.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink plenty of water instead of sugary sodas and juices.
treatment_options: eating healthy food with less salt
surgery to fix or replace the valve
putting a new valve in through a tube
recovery_time: If you just take medicine, recovery is about feeling better slowly over a few weeks.
If you have surgery, you will usually need one to two weeks to rest at home.
Most people can return to their normal daily routine after about six to eight weeks.
Full healing inside your body can take a few months of taking it easy.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks every day to keep your body moving safely.
Avoid heavy lifting and pushing hard things that make you strain.
Stop right away if you feel dizzy, tired, or have chest pain.
Join a gentle heart-healthy exercise program if your doctor says it is okay.
recommended_tests: An ultrasound of your heart to take pictures of how the valve is working.
An electrical tracing of your heart to check its beat.
An X-ray of your chest to look at the size of your heart and lungs.
Blood tests to check your overall health and how well your organs work.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you feel dizzy or faint
when your legs start to swell

aphthous ulcer.basic_details: An aphthous ulcer is a small, painful sore that forms inside your mouth, usually on the tongue or inner cheeks. They are very common and not catching, but they can make eating and talking hurt a little.
diet_recommendation: Eat soft and bland foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and oatmeal.
Stay away from spicy, salty, and sour foods that can sting the sore.
Drink plenty of cool water to keep your mouth clean and hydrated.
Avoid sharp foods like chips and crusty bread that can scratch the sore.
recovery_time: Most small sores go away completely on their own within one to two weeks.
The sharp pain usually starts to get better after the first three or four days.
Larger sores might take up to six weeks to heal fully.
Eating carefully can help the sore heal a little bit faster.
physical_activities: You can keep doing all your normal daily exercises and activities.
There is no need to stay home or rest in bed because of a mouth sore.
Avoid any contact sports if you are worried about getting hit in the face.
Keep up with your regular sports and hobbies without worry.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually do not need any special tests for a normal mouth sore.
A dentist or doctor can just look at the sore with their eyes.
Blood tests may be done only if you keep getting sores over and over.
A tiny skin sample is rarely taken if a sore lasts for many months.
when_to_visit_doctor: The sore lasts more than three weeks
The pain is very bad and stops you from eating
You have a high fever with the sore

aplastic anemia.basic_details: Aplastic anemia is a rare condition where your body stops making enough new blood cells. This makes you feel very tired and more likely to get sick or bleed easily.
diet_recommendation: Eat thoroughly cooked foods to avoid harmful germs and food poisoning.
Wash all fresh fruits and vegetables very carefully before eating them.
Drink plenty of clean water every day to stay well-hydrated.
Eat protein-rich foods like eggs, beans, and lean meats to help your body stay strong.
recovery_time: Recovery takes a long time, often lasting from several months to a few years.
How fast you get better depends a lot on your age and overall health.
Some people start feeling better soon after starting the right treatments.
Regular doctor visits are needed for a long time to make sure you stay healthy.
physical_activities: Stick to very light activities like slow, short walks around your home.
Avoid contact sports and rough games where you could easily get bruised or cut.
Listen to your body and rest right away when you start feeling tired.
Ask your doctor before starting any new exercise routine, even gentle ones.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check the number of red cells, white cells, and platelets you have.
A bone marrow test to look closely at how blood cells are being made inside your bones.
Frequent check-ups to see how well your treatments are working over time.
Tests to check your vitamin levels and overall organ health.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have a high fever
if you bleed or bruise easily
if you feel dizzy or short of breath

appendicitis.basic_details: Appendicitis happens when a small finger-like pouch attached to your large intestine gets blocked and swollen. It causes sharp pain in your lower right belly that needs quick medical help.
emergency_signs: Sharp pain in lower right belly
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
things_to_avoid: Taking pain pills before seeing doctor
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of clear water and broth to stay hydrated.
Eat plain foods like rice, toast, and bananas after surgery.
Stay away from greasy, fried, and very spicy foods.
Avoid sugary drinks and sweets until your tummy feels better.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better after a couple of weeks.
Full healing inside your body usually takes about four to six weeks.
Take plenty of rest in the first few days to heal fast.
Listen to your body and do not rush back to normal routines.
physical_activities: Take short, slow walks around your house to help healing.
Do not lift anything heavy for at least a few weeks.
Avoid hard exercises like running or gym workouts until cleared.
Rest as much as possible and sleep whenever you feel tired.
recommended_tests: A physical check where the doctor gently presses your belly.
A blood test to see if your body is fighting an infection.
A urine test to make sure it is not a bladder issue.
An ultrasound or CT scan to take pictures of your tummy.
when_to_visit_doctor: Severe pain in lower right belly

arrhythmia.basic_details: Arrhythmia is a heart condition where your heart beats too fast, too slow, or in an irregular way. This happens when the electrical signals that tell your heart how to beat do not work the right way.
precautions: Keep a record of funny heartbeats
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables every day.
Drink less coffee and other drinks with a lot of caffeine.
Cut down on salty foods to help keep your blood pressure normal.
Drink enough water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
recovery_time: It depends a lot on what caused your heart to beat out of rhythm.
Many people feel better within a few weeks after starting treatment.
If you need a minor surgery, healing usually takes a couple of weeks.
Living with it is a lifelong journey of taking care of your heart.
physical_activities: Take gentle, daily walks to keep your heart strong without rushing it.
Try light stretching or slow yoga to help your body stay relaxed.
Avoid heavy lifting and sports that make you feel dizzy or tired.
Always stop exercising right away if your chest starts to hurt.
recommended_tests: An ECG test to take a picture of your heart's electrical beats.
A small monitor you wear for a day or two to track your rhythm.
Blood tests to check for things like low vitamins or minerals.
An ultrasound of your heart to look at its size and shape.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel your heart skipping beats often
You feel very tired for no reason

arthritis of the hip.basic_details: Arthritis of the hip happens when the cushion inside your hip joint wears away. This makes the bones rub together, causing pain and making it hard to move your leg.
emergency_signs: Fever with a hot hip joint
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose fish like salmon because it helps calm down swelling in your joints.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy.
Try to eat less junk food and sugary snacks, as they can make swelling worse.
recovery_time: Healing takes time because joints wear down slowly over many years.
You might feel better in a few weeks if you rest and do gentle stretches.
If you need a hip surgery, it usually takes a few months to feel back to normal.
Listen to your body and do not rush the healing process.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks on flat ground to keep your hips moving.
Try swimming or water aerobics, which are very easy on your sore joints.
Do gentle leg stretches while sitting or lying down on a soft mat.
Avoid heavy lifting or running that can put too much pressure on your hip.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray so the doctor can take a picture of the inside of your hip bone.
Tell the doctor where it hurts and how long you have felt the pain.
Let the doctor move your leg around to see which parts feel stiff.
Take a blood test if the doctor wants to check for other types of body swelling.

ascending cholangitis.basic_details: Ascending cholangitis is a painful bacterial infection in the tubes that carry digestive juices from your liver. It happens when something like a gallstone blocks the flow, causing germs to back up.
emergency_signs: Severe pain in upper right belly
diet_recommendation: Eat very low-fat foods to give your liver and gallbladder a rest.
Choose plain foods like white rice, toast, and boiled potatoes.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Avoid greasy, spicy, and fried foods until you feel completely better.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within a few days of getting hospital treatment.
Complete healing at home usually takes about two to four weeks.
You might need extra time to recover if doctors had to do a procedure to clear a blocked tube.
Go back to your doctor for follow-up checks to make sure the infection is completely gone.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest during the first few days when you are the sickest.
Take very short, slow walks around your room to keep your blood moving.
Do not lift anything heavy or do hard chores until your doctor says it is safe.
Slowly add back your normal daily tasks as your strength returns over a few weeks.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check for signs of ongoing infection and see how well your liver is working.
An ultrasound of your belly to look at your liver and find any trapped gallstones.
A special CT scan to get a clearer picture of your internal tubes and organs.
An upper scope procedure (ERCP) that lets doctors look inside the tubes and clear any blockages.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have yellow skin or eyes
if you have a very high fever
if you feel severe belly pain
if you feel very confused or dizzy

asperger syndrome.basic_details: Asperger syndrome is a way your brain works that makes it hard to talk to people and understand social rules. People with this condition often have very strong interests in one or two special topics.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated and feel good.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and candy.
Stick to regular meal times so your body has a steady routine.
common_medicines: No specific medicine cures Asperger syndrome
Medicine for attention problems if needed
Medicine for sleep trouble if needed
recovery_time: Asperger syndrome is a lifelong way of life, not a temporary sickness.
You do not recover from it, but you learn how to handle daily life better.
Learning new social skills takes time and a lot of practice.
Most people get much better at managing their feelings as they grow older.
physical_activities: Take fun walks outside in the fresh air every day.
Play sports or games that help you burn off extra energy.
Do yoga or deep breathing exercises if you feel stressed out.
Try swimming or riding a bike to keep your body strong and happy.
recommended_tests: Talk with a special doctor who listens to how you think and act.
Answer questions about how you feel in different social situations.
Have family members share stories about how you acted growing up.
Do puzzle or talking games to see how your brain solves problems.
when_to_visit_doctor: When you notice delayed social skills in a child
When anxiety or stress becomes hard to manage
When school or work is very hard to handle
When you need help with daily routines

asthma.basic_details: Asthma is a long-term breathing problem where the tubes carrying air to your lungs get swollen and narrow, making it hard to breathe. It often causes coughing, wheezing, and chest tightness.
things_to_avoid: Exercising in cold air without warming up
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay strong.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your airways moist.
Try to stay away from foods that give you allergies or upset your stomach.
Eat healthy foods with omega-3 fats, like fish, to help fight swelling in your body.
treatment_options: Stay away from dust and smoke
Take deep breaths with an exercise plan
recovery_time: Asthma is a lifelong condition, so it does not completely go away.
An asthma attack can start to feel better within 5 to 15 minutes after using a quick-relief inhaler.
You can feel much better overall within a few weeks of taking your daily control medicines.
Staying away from your triggers helps you stay healthy and symptom-free for a long time.
physical_activities: Go for light walks or do gentle swimming to keep your body active.
Always warm up slowly before you start any fun games or exercises.
Keep your rescue inhaler close by every time you play sports.
Stop and rest right away if you start coughing or feeling short of breath.
recommended_tests: A breathing test called spirometry to check how well your lungs are working.
A peak flow meter test where you blow hard into a small plastic tube to measure your breathing power.
Allergy tests to find out what things in the air make your asthma worse.
A doctor's checkup to listen to your chest with a stethoscope.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your quick-relief inhaler does not work
You wake up at night with trouble breathing
You need your inhaler more than usual

astigmatism.basic_details: Astigmatism is a very common eye condition that makes things look blurry or stretched out. It happens because the front part of your eye is shaped a bit more like a football than a round basketball.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of leafy green veggies like spinach and kale to keep your eyes healthy.
Eat colorful fruits like oranges and berries for good vision vitamins.
Eat fish like salmon because it has good oils for your eyes.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your eyes from getting dry.
recovery_time: Astigmatism is not an illness, so you do not recover from it like a cold.
If you get new glasses or contact lenses, it only takes a few days to get used to them.
If you choose eye surgery, your eyes usually feel better within a few days to a week.
Your vision stays clear as long as you wear your correct glasses or lenses.
physical_activities: You can play all your favorite sports and games without any worries.
Wear unbreakable sports glasses or goggles to keep your eyes safe during rough games.
Take regular breaks from looking at phone or computer screens so your eyes do not get tired.
Wear sunglasses outside on bright days to protect your eyes from the sun.
recommended_tests: An eye doctor will look closely at your eyes using a special lighted microscope.
You will look through a big machine with different lenses to see which ones make letters clear.
The doctor will shine a bright light into your eye to check its shape.
You might read letters from a chart on the wall to check how blurry your sight is.
when_to_visit_doctor: When your eyes feel tired often

atelectasis.basic_details: Atelectasis happens when a small part of your lung, or a whole lung, collapses because the tiny air sacs inside lose their air and deflate. This makes it a bit harder to breathe deeply.
precautions: Walk as soon as possible after surgery
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay strong.
Choose soft foods if you feel too tired to chew big meals.
Eat smaller meals more often so your stomach does not push on your lungs.
recovery_time: Mild cases often start getting better in just a few days.
Full healing can take a couple of weeks depending on the main cause.
Doing your breathing exercises every day speeds up your recovery.
Resting as much as possible helps your lungs heal faster.
physical_activities: Take slow, deep breaths several times every hour.
Use a special breathing tool given by your doctor to practice.
Take short, gentle walks around your room when you feel up to it.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard sports until your doctor says it is safe.
recommended_tests: Get a chest X-ray to let the doctor look inside your lungs.
Do a CT scan if the doctor needs a clearer picture of your chest.
Have a pulse check on your finger to see how much oxygen is in your blood.
Do a simple breathing test to see how well your lungs are working.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you feel very short of breath
If you have a high fever with a cough
If chest pain does not go away

athlete's foot.basic_details: Athlete's foot is a common itchy rash on the skin of your feet, usually caused by a fungus that likes warm and wet places.
things_to_avoid: Wearing the same shoes every day
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay strong.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your skin healthy.
Eat less sugary foods because sugar can help fungus grow.
Include garlic in your meals, as it can help fight off germs.
recovery_time: Mild cases usually start to feel better in one to two weeks.
It can take up to four weeks for the skin to heal completely.
You must keep putting cream on for a few days after it looks gone.
Severe cases might take longer if the skin gets cracked or sore.
physical_activities: Take a break from running or heavy gym workouts until your feet heal.
Do light stretches or upper body workouts while sitting down.
Wear open shoes or go barefoot at home to let your feet breathe.
Avoid swimming pools and public gym floors so you do not spread it.
recommended_tests: A doctor can usually just look at your feet to know what it is.
They might gently scrape a tiny bit of skin to check under a microscope.
Sometimes they send a skin sample to a lab to be extra sure.
You rarely need any blood tests for this simple skin problem.
when_to_visit_doctor: The rash does not go away
Signs of infection like pus appear

atonic bladder.basic_details: An atonic bladder is a condition where the muscles in your bladder become weak and loose, making it hard to squeeze out pee normally. This can lead to your bladder getting too full without you realizing it.
precautions: Go to the bathroom on a schedule
things_to_avoid: Drinking too much fluid right before bed
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your system clean.
Stay away from spicy foods and caffeine, as they can irritate your bladder.
Eat plenty of fiber-rich foods like fruits and veggies to avoid constipation, which can press on your bladder.
Limit how much you drink right before bed so you do not wake up as much.
recovery_time: Healing takes time because weak muscles need weeks or months to get stronger.
Some people get better quickly with the right treatment and routine.
Others might need long-term care or daily help to empty their bladder safely.
Your recovery speed depends entirely on what caused your bladder to become weak in the first place.
physical_activities: Try gentle walking every day to keep your body moving and healthy.
Do pelvic floor exercises, often called Kegels, if your doctor says it is okay.
