Avoid heavy lifting or hard sports that put too much pressure on your belly.
Do not do any painful workouts that make it harder for you to pee.
recommended_tests: A simple ultrasound to look at your bladder and see how much pee is left inside.
A test where a tiny tube is put in to measure how well your bladder holds and lets out water.
Basic urine tests to check for any hidden germs or infections.
A scan of your kidneys to make sure the backup of pee is not hurting them.
when_to_visit_doctor: you have severe lower belly pain
you see blood in your pee

atrial fibrillation.basic_details: Atrial fibrillation is a common heart problem where your heart beats too fast and out of its normal rhythm. This can make you feel tired or dizzy because your heart is not pumping blood as well as it should.
emergency_signs: Sudden weakness in arm or face
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Cut back on salty foods to help keep your blood pressure low.
Drink less coffee, energy drinks, and other sources of caffeine.
Limit how much alcohol you drink, or try not to drink it at all.
recovery_time: This condition is usually lifelong, so the goal is long-term management rather than a quick cure.
Many people start feeling better within a few weeks of finding the right treatment plan.
It takes time to get used to new daily habits and medicine schedules.
Regular check-ups help your doctor see how well you are improving over the months.
physical_activities: Go for gentle daily walks to keep your heart strong without overdoing it.
Try light swimming or riding a stationary bike at an easy pace.
Stop right away and rest if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or tired.
Always talk to your doctor before starting any new exercise routine.
recommended_tests: An electrocardiogram to look at the electrical signals in your heart.
A small monitor you wear for a day or longer to track your heart rhythm.
An ultrasound of your heart to check its size and how well it pumps blood.
Simple blood tests to check your overall health and vitamin levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: your heart beats too fast often
your medicine makes you feel bad

atrial flutter.basic_details: Atrial flutter is a heart condition where your upper heart chambers beat way too fast, making your heart rhythm out of sync.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Cut back on salty foods to help keep your blood pressure down.
Drink less coffee and energy drinks because caffeine can make your heart race.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
common_medicines: beta blockers to slow heart rate
treatment_options: electric shock to reset heart rhythm
catheter ablation to fix heart signals
recovery_time: Many people start feeling better within a few days after starting the right treatment.
If you need a minor heart procedure, you might need a couple of weeks to rest at home.
Recovery speed depends a lot on your overall health and age.
Always listen to your body and don't rush back into heavy tasks too fast.
physical_activities: Take light, easy walks around your neighborhood.
Do gentle stretching to keep your body moving without stressing your heart.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Stop exercising immediately if you feel dizzy, tired, or short of breath.
recommended_tests: An ECG test that puts sticky patches on your chest to record your heartbeats.
Wearing a small monitor for a few days to track your heart rhythm while you go about your day.
An ultrasound of your heart to look at its size and how well it pumps blood.
Simple blood tests to check your overall health and vitamin levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: if your heart beats too fast often
if you feel dizzy or lightheaded

atrophic skin condition.basic_details: Atrophic skin condition is a problem where your skin becomes very thin, fragile, and sometimes looks wrinkled or sunken. This happens because the skin loses its normal fullness and strength over time.
emergency_signs: Skin tearing easily and bleeding heavily
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your skin hydrated from the inside.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables loaded with vitamins to help your skin stay healthy.
Include foods with healthy fats, like avocados and nuts, to nourish your skin.
Eat enough protein, such as chicken, beans, or eggs, to help repair weak skin.
recovery_time: Skin healing takes a very long time because the skin is already weak and thin.
Minor cuts or scratches can take a few weeks or even months to fully heal.
Consistency with daily moisturizers helps speed up how your skin feels over months.
Severe skin thinning is often permanent, but proper care stops it from getting worse.
physical_activities: Do light walking or gentle stretching to keep your body moving safely.
Avoid rough sports or heavy lifting that could easily scrape or tear your skin.
Wear loose-fitting clothes so your clothes do not rub against and hurt your skin.
Be very careful not to bump into sharp corners or hard objects around the house.
recommended_tests: A simple physical check where a doctor looks closely at your skin.
A gentle touch test to see how stretchy and thin your skin really is.
A blood test to check if you are missing important vitamins or nutrients.
A tiny skin sample test if the doctor needs to look at your skin cells.
when_to_visit_doctor: if it gets red and hot

atrophic vaginitis.basic_details: Atrophic vaginitis happens when the walls of the vagina become thin, dry, and swollen because the body makes less of a hormone called estrogen. This often happens after a woman goes through menopause.
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body and skin hydrated.
Eat foods with plant hormones like tofu, soy milk, and flaxseeds.
Eat colorful fruits and vegetables to keep your immune system strong.
Limit spicy foods, caffeine, and alcohol, as they can sometimes irritate your bladder.
recovery_time: Mild dryness can start feeling better within a few days of using a good moisturizer.
Prescription treatments like estrogen cream usually take a few weeks to show big improvements.
It can take up to two or three months of steady treatment for the tissue to fully heal and feel normal.
This is an ongoing condition, so you will need to keep up with your routine to stay comfortable.
physical_activities: Do daily pelvic floor exercises, like Kegels, to keep your pelvic muscles strong and healthy.
Go for gentle daily walks to boost your overall blood flow and mood.
Wear loose-fitting cotton underwear and clothes to let air in and stop irritation.
Try to avoid tight jeans or sitting in wet swimsuits for a long time.
recommended_tests: A simple physical checkup by your doctor to look at the skin and tissues.
A urine test to make sure you do not have a bladder infection.
A gentle swab test to check for any bacteria or yeast causing discomfort.
A talk with your doctor about your health history and when your symptoms started.
when_to_visit_doctor: if over-the-counter creams do not help

atrophy of the corpus cavernosum.basic_details: Atrophy of the corpus cavernosum is a condition where the spongy tissue inside the penis shrinks or weakens over time. This can lead to trouble getting or keeping an erection.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your blood flowing well.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread instead of white bread.
Eat healthy fats found in fish, nuts, and olive oil.
Drink lots of water every day and stay away from sugary drinks.
common_medicines: Pills to help with blood flow
recovery_time: It usually takes many months to see real improvements.
Healing happens slowly step by step, so you need to be very patient.
Some people might need long-term care to manage the condition.
Your total recovery time depends a lot on your age and overall health.
physical_activities: Go for brisk walks every day to keep your heart and blood strong.
Do pelvic floor exercises, also known as Kegels, to strengthen the area.
Try gentle swimming or cycling to stay active without pushing too hard.
Avoid sitting for too many hours in a row without taking a break to move.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where your doctor examines the area with their hands.
An ultrasound scan to look at the blood flow inside your penis.
Blood tests to check your sugar levels and hormone amounts.
A nighttime test to check if you get natural erections while sleeping.
when_to_visit_doctor: When you notice a change in size
If you have ongoing erection problems
If you feel pain in the area
For regular check-ups with a specialist

attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.basic_details: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, or ADHD, is a brain condition that makes it hard to pay attention, sit still, and control actions. People with ADHD might get easily distracted, talk a lot, or act without thinking.
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Include foods with protein like eggs, fish, and beans to help focus.
Drink lots of water to keep your brain and body energized.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and drinks, as they can cause energy crashes.
recovery_time: ADHD is a lifelong condition, so it does not completely go away like a cold.
Many people learn good coping skills that make daily life much easier over time.
Symptoms often change and become easier to manage as a person grows into an adult.
Consistent habits and support help people feel better and succeed every single day.
physical_activities: Play sports like soccer or basketball to help burn off extra energy.
Go for daily walks or bike rides to clear your mind and improve focus.
Try yoga or simple stretching to help calm your body and relax.
Do fun dance routines at home to stay active and happy.
recommended_tests: Talking with a doctor or mental health expert about your daily habits.
Filling out special questionnaires about your behavior with family or teachers.
Hearing and vision checks to make sure nothing else is causing the trouble.
Looking closely at your medical history and how you act in different places.
when_to_visit_doctor: hard time paying attention at school or work
moving around too much and cannot sit still
acting without thinking all the time
trouble making friends and keeping jobs

autism.basic_details: Autism is a way your brain works differently that affects how you talk, play, and connect with other people. Everyone with autism is unique and has their own special strengths.
emergency_signs: Refusing to eat or drink for days
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to help your body stay healthy.
Try foods with healthy fats like fish and nuts.
Limit sugary snacks and drinks to feel your best.
recovery_time: Autism is not a sickness, so you do not recover from it or get cured.
You learn new skills and grow at your own pace over your whole life.
Help and support can make daily tasks easier as you get older.
Progress happens step by step with practice and patience.
physical_activities: Go for fun walks or run around in the park.
Play games like catching a ball or jumping rope.
Try swimming to help your body feel strong and relaxed.
Dance around your room to your favorite music.
recommended_tests: Talk with a doctor who asks questions about how you act and feel.
Have someone watch how you play and talk with others.
Fill out simple forms with your family about your habits.
Do fun puzzles or games to see how your brain solves problems.
when_to_visit_doctor: does not speak by age two

autonomic nervous system disorder.basic_details: Your body's automatic control system has trouble working right. This system helps run things you don't have to think about, like your heartbeat and digestion.
precautions: Add salt to diet if doctor advises
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every single day to keep your blood pressure stable.
Eat smaller meals more often so you do not feel dizzy or too full.
Add a little extra salt to your food if your doctor says it is okay.
Stay away from alcohol and drinks with a lot of caffeine.
recovery_time: This is usually a long-term condition, so recovery means learning to manage daily symptoms.
Some people feel much better within a few weeks after starting the right treatment.
It often takes months of trying different habits to find what makes you feel good.
Times vary a lot for each person depending on what caused the problem.
physical_activities: Do light walking or swimming to stay active without pushing your body too hard.
Wear special tight socks, called compression stockings, when you exercise.
Always stand up very slowly from a sitting or lying position to avoid dizziness.
Stop exercising right away and rest if you feel tired, sweaty, or lightheaded.
recommended_tests: A special table test where they tilt you up to check your blood pressure and heart rate.
A breathing test to see how well your heart responds when you take deep breaths.
A sweat test to check if your body is making sweat the normal way.
Blood tests to check for vitamins, sugar levels, and other common health signs.
when_to_visit_doctor: fast heart beat all the time

balanitis.basic_details: Balanitis is a common skin issue where the tip of the penis becomes red, swollen, and sore. It is usually caused by irritation or a mild infection.
precautions: Keep the area clean and dry
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to help flush your body.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your immune system strong.
Cut back on sugary foods and drinks, as sugar can help infections grow.
Eat yogurt with live cultures to help keep your body in a healthy balance.
treatment_options: Wash and dry the area carefully
recovery_time: Most mild cases start to feel better in just two to three days.
Full healing usually takes about one week if you follow treatment.
If you have sensitive skin, it might take a little longer to clear up completely.
Always finish your whole medicine routine so the problem does not come back.
physical_activities: Take a short break from heavy workouts until the soreness goes away.
Wear loose and soft underwear to stop rubbing and extra irritation.
Avoid swimming in public pools until the skin is fully healed.
Take a break from sexual activity until the area is completely better.
recommended_tests: A simple visual check by your family doctor or nurse.
A gentle skin swab to check for tiny germs or yeast.
A routine sugar test, because high sugar can sometimes cause this issue.
Checking your urine to make sure there is no hidden infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain does not go away in a few days
You see pus or bad smell
It is hard to pull back the foreskin

bell palsy.basic_details: Bell's palsy is a sudden weakness or paralysis of the muscles on one side of your face. It happens when the nerve that controls your facial muscles gets swollen or blocked.
emergency_signs: Sudden weakness in arms or legs
precautions: Protect the eye if it won't close
things_to_avoid: Ignoring the symptom without seeing a doctor
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, soup, and mashed potatoes if chewing is hard on the weak side.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your body healthy and hydrated.
Chew your food slowly and use the stronger side of your mouth to help.
Avoid very salty foods so you do not hold onto extra water and swelling.
common_medicines: Eye drops to keep the eye wet
recovery_time: Most people start to see signs of getting better within two to three weeks.
Full recovery of facial strength usually takes between three to six months.
A small number of people may have mild leftover weakness after a year.
Your recovery speed depends on how early you start your treatment.
physical_activities: Do gentle facial exercises in front of a mirror to help wake up your sleeping muscles.
Massage your face softly with clean fingers to help blood flow and ease tight spots.
Go for short, easy walks outside to stay active and keep your mood up.
Try to rest as much as you can so your body and nerve have time to heal.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually do a quick physical check of your face, arms, and legs to test your nerves.
Blood tests might be done to check for infections like diabetes or Lyme disease.
Sometimes a special scan of your head is done to make sure nothing else is wrong.
A nerve test might be used if your doctor wants to see how well your facial nerve is working.
when_to_visit_doctor: Right when one side of your face drops
If your eye cannot close fully
If you have pain behind your ear
If your symptoms do not get better after a few weeks

benign kidney cyst.basic_details: A benign kidney cyst is a harmless, non-cancerous fluid-filled sac that grows on or inside the kidney. Most people with these cysts do not have any symptoms or need treatment.
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every single day to keep your kidneys clean.
Eat less salt to help keep your blood pressure at a healthy level.
Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables with every meal.
Try to limit processed foods and sugary drinks as much as possible.
common_medicines: antibiotics if there is an infection
no medicine needed for simple cysts
treatment_options: draining the fluid with a needle
recovery_time: No recovery time is needed if you are just monitoring the cyst.
If you need a minor procedure, you can usually go home the very same day.
Most people feel completely back to normal within a few days after a procedure.
You will only need a short rest period if your doctor has to drain the fluid.
physical_activities: You can continue doing your normal daily activities without any worries.
Light exercises like walking and stretching are great for staying healthy.
Avoid heavy lifting or rough contact sports until your doctor says it is safe.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel tired or sore.
recommended_tests: An ultrasound scan uses sound waves to take a clear picture of the cyst.
A CT scan gives your doctor a detailed 3D look inside your belly.
Blood tests check how well your kidneys are filtering your blood.
A urine test checks your pee for any signs of infection or other issues.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you feel sharp pain in your back or side
if you see blood in your pee
if you have a fever and chills
if your belly feels very full or swollen

benign paroxysmal positional vertical (b.basic_details: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, or BPPV, is a common inner ear issue that causes sudden, short spells of feeling like the room is spinning when you move your head.
precautions: Sleep with your head slightly raised
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to avoid feeling dizzy from dehydration.
Eat healthy meals with fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
Try to eat less salt because too much salt can affect fluid levels in your inner ear.
Limit or avoid caffeine and alcohol as they can make dizziness worse.
treatment_options: Waiting for it to go away
recovery_time: Many people feel much better just hours or days after getting the right treatment.
Some people might feel a little off-balance for a few weeks.
Doing special head movements guided by a doctor speeds up healing a lot.
The spinning spells can sometimes come back later in life, but they can be treated again.
physical_activities: Do special head turning exercises given by your doctor to put ear crystals back in place.
Move slowly when getting out of bed or standing up from a chair.
Avoid quick head movements or looking straight up at the ceiling for a while.
Rest for a short time if a dizzy spell hits, and avoid driving until it passes.
recommended_tests: A doctor will likely watch your eye movements while moving your head in specific ways.
You may be asked to sit down and lie back quickly to see if your room starts spinning.
Most people do not need expensive brain scans or blood tests.
An ear specialist might check your hearing if you have other ear symptoms.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you feel dizzy for the first time
If dizziness does not get better
If you fall or pass out
If you have a very bad headache or numbness

benign prostatic hyperplasia (bph).basic_details: Benign prostatic hyperplasia, or BPH, is when the prostate gland gets bigger as men get older. This can squeeze the tube that carries pee out of the body, making it hard or painful to go to the bathroom.
things_to_avoid: Drinking too much caffeine or alcohol
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink less coffee, tea, and soda, especially at night.
Limit how much alcohol you drink to help your bladder.
Cut back on very spicy and greasy foods that can irritate your bladder.
treatment_options: Take daily pills to relax prostate muscles
Take pills to shrink the prostate
Surgery to remove extra prostate tissue
Minimally invasive heat or laser treatments
recovery_time: If you just take medicine, you might start feeling better in a few weeks.
If you need a simple procedure, you usually recover at home in a few days.
If you have surgery, it can take a few weeks to fully heal and feel normal.
Your doctor will tell you when you can go back to your normal daily routine.
physical_activities: Take a daily walk to keep your body moving and healthy.
Do special pelvic floor exercises to help control your bladder.
Avoid heavy lifting until your doctor says it is safe.
Stay active, but listen to your body and rest if you feel tired.
recommended_tests: A chat with your doctor about your bathroom habits and symptoms.
A simple physical check by your doctor to feel the size of your prostate.
A test where you pee into a special funnel to check the strength of your stream.
An ultrasound picture to see how much pee is left in your bladder.
when_to_visit_doctor: You have trouble starting to pee
Your urine stream is very weak
You wake up often at night to pee
You feel like your bladder is not fully empty

benign vaginal discharge (leukorrhea).basic_details: Benign vaginal discharge, or leukorrhea, is a common and normal fluid from the vagina that helps keep it clean and healthy. It is usually harmless and not a sign of any serious infection.
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body healthy and hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits and green vegetables to boost your immune system.
Include plain yogurt with live bacteria in your daily meals.
Try to eat less sugary foods and junk food.
treatment_options: keep the area clean and dry
recovery_time: Normal discharge happens all the time as a healthy body process.
If it is caused by a minor imbalance, it usually gets better in a few days.
Following good daily hygiene helps the condition clear up quickly.
If you use treatment from a doctor, you should feel better within one week.
physical_activities: You can do all your normal daily exercises and workouts.
Choose loose and comfortable clothes when you go to the gym.
Change out of sweaty workout clothes as soon as you finish exercising.
Avoid sitting in a wet swimsuit or sweaty gym clothes for a long time.
recommended_tests: A simple physical checkup by a doctor is usually enough.
A cotton swab test may be done if your doctor wants to check for germs.
The doctor might check the acidity level of the vaginal fluid.
A urine test may be done to make sure there is no bladder infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: discharge changes color to yellow or green
you feel pain in your lower belly

bipolar disorder.basic_details: Bipolar disorder is a health condition that causes extreme shifts in your mood, energy, and activity levels. You might switch between feeling very high and energetic to feeling very low and sad.
things_to_avoid: Making big life decisions during a mood swing
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to keep your body and brain hydrated.
Try to eat meals at the same time each day to keep your energy steady.
Cut back on sugary snacks and too much caffeine like coffee.
recovery_time: Healing takes time and looks different for everyone.
You might start feeling a bit better after a few weeks of treatment.
It is a lifelong journey of managing good days and hard days.
Staying on track with your care helps you feel well faster.
physical_activities: Go for a short, easy walk outside in the fresh air.
Try gentle stretching or yoga to help your body relax.
Dance around your room to your favorite happy songs.
Do some light gardening or housework to keep moving.
recommended_tests: Talking with a counselor about how you feel inside.
Simple blood checks to make sure your body is healthy.
Answering some easy questions about your sleep and daily moods.
Checking your overall body health with your main doctor.

bladder cancer.basic_details: Bladder cancer happens when bad cells grow out of control in the part of your body that holds your pee. It is a very treatable condition, especially when found early.
emergency_signs: A large amount of blood in urine
things_to_avoid: Delaying a doctor visit if you see blood
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water every single day to flush out your system.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables with every meal to keep your body strong.
Choose whole wheat bread and brown rice instead of white bread and sugary snacks.
Stay away from heavily processed meats, spicy foods, and drinks with too much caffeine.
common_medicines: Chemotherapy put right into the bladder
Medicine that helps the body fight the cancer
treatment_options: Surgery to take out the cancer
Surgery to take out the whole bladder
recovery_time: Most people need a few weeks of rest at home after having surgery.
You might feel tired and weak for the first month as your body heals itself.
Healing goes faster if you listen to your doctor and do not rush your daily tasks.
Full recovery can take a few months depending on the exact treatment you had.
physical_activities: Take short, slow walks around your house or yard to keep your blood moving.
Avoid heavy lifting, gym workouts, and hard running until your doctor says it is safe.
Do gentle breathing exercises to keep your lungs strong while you rest.
Listen to your body and stop right away if you feel any sharp pain or dizziness.
recommended_tests: Looking inside your bladder with a tiny, lighted camera to check for problems.
Taking a small sample of your pee to look for blood and tiny bits of sickness.
Getting pictures taken of your inside parts using a special scan machine.
Taking a tiny piece of skin from your bladder to test it in a lab.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain in your lower back or side

bladder disorder.basic_details: A bladder disorder is a health problem that makes it hard to hold or let out pee normally. It can make you feel like you need to go to the bathroom all the time.
emergency_signs: Large amount of blood in urine
precautions: Go to the bathroom on a schedule
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of plain water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Stay away from spicy foods that can upset your tummy and bladder.
Cut back on coffee, soda, and alcohol as they make you need to pee more.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy.
recovery_time: Many people start feeling better in a few weeks with the right care.
Mild cases can clear up in just a few days by drinking more water.
Long-term issues may take a few months of steady treatment to improve.
Healing time is different for everyone, so be patient with your body.
physical_activities: Go for gentle daily walks to keep your body moving.
Do pelvic floor exercises to make your bladder muscles stronger.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts that put pressure on your belly.
Take gentle stretching breaks if you sit for a long time.
recommended_tests: A simple test where you pee in a cup to check for germs.
An ultrasound scan to look at your bladder on a screen.
A small camera test to look inside your bladder.
A diary test where you write down every time you go to the bathroom.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you see blood in urine
If you feel pain in the lower belly

bladder obstruction.basic_details: Bladder obstruction happens when something blocks the flow of urine out of your body. This makes it hard to pee and can cause discomfort.
precautions: Drink fluids as advised by doctor
things_to_avoid: Drinking too much fluid at once
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to help flush out your system.
Eat more fruits and vegetables to keep your stomach happy.
Stay away from spicy foods that might irritate your bladder.
Cut back on drinks with caffeine and alcohol, as they can make you pee more.
treatment_options: using a thin tube to drain urine
recovery_time: Many people start feeling better a few days after starting treatment.
If you need a small procedure, it may take a couple of weeks to heal.
Full recovery depends on what is causing the block and your overall health.
Your doctor will schedule follow-up visits to check on your healing progress.
physical_activities: Take light and easy walks to keep your body moving gently.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until your doctor says it is okay.
Try gentle stretching to help your body stay relaxed.
Rest as much as you need while your body is healing.
recommended_tests: A simple ultrasound to take a picture of your bladder and see how it looks.
A urine test to check for any signs of infection or blood.
A test to measure how much urine is left in your bladder after you try to go.
A doctor check-up where they gently press on your lower belly.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you cannot pee at all
if you have severe lower belly pain
if you see blood in your pee
if you have a high fever with chills

blepharitis.basic_details: Blepharitis is a common eye condition that makes your eyelids red, swollen, and itchy. It happens when tiny oil glands near your eyelashes get blocked.
emergency_signs: Eye becomes completely red and swollen
precautions: Wash eyelids gently with baby shampoo
diet_recommendation: Eat more fish like salmon because it helps your eyes stay healthy.
Snack on walnuts and flaxseeds to get good oils for your skin and eyes.
Eat plenty of fresh fruits and colorful vegetables every single day.
Drink lots of water to keep your body and eyes from drying out.
treatment_options: Putting a warm cloth on eyes
Stopping eye makeup for a while
recovery_time: Most people start to feel a little better after one week of daily cleaning.
It can take a few weeks for the redness and swelling to fully go away.
You might need to keep doing your eye cleaning routine for a long time.
Because the condition can come back, doing daily care helps keep it away.
physical_activities: You can still go for normal walks and do light exercises outside.
Wear sunglasses outside to protect your sore eyes from dust and wind.
Take breaks from looking at phone or computer screens so your eyes can rest.
Avoid swimming pools for a short time if the pool chemicals make your eyes sting.
recommended_tests: An eye doctor will look closely at your eyelids using a bright magnifying light.
The doctor might gently press on your eyelids to check the oil glands.
Sometimes they take a tiny sample from your eyelid to check for germs.
They may test how well your eyes make tears to see if they are too dry.
when_to_visit_doctor: If home care does not help
If the eye becomes very sensitive to light

bone cancer.basic_details: Bone cancer is a serious disease where bad cells start growing wildly inside the bones, making them weak and painful. It can start in the bone itself or spread from other parts of the body.
emergency_signs: Severe deep bone pain at night
Sudden large swelling on a bone
precautions: Attend all doctor and scan appointments
things_to_avoid: Heavy physical stress on the bone
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day to keep your body strong.
Drink lots of water and milk to help keep your bones healthy.
Eat foods with protein, like beans, chicken, and eggs, to help your body heal.
Stay away from sugary snacks and junk food that can make you feel weak.
treatment_options: surgery to take out the cancer
recovery_time: Healing takes a very long time, often many months or even a few years.
Every person heals at their own speed, so try not to rush your body.
You will need many follow-up visits with your doctor to check your healing.
Resting as much as possible is the most important part of getting better.
physical_activities: Start with very gentle stretches in bed so your body does not get stiff.
Take short, slow walks around your room when you feel a little stronger.
Work with a helper who guides your body safely through easy exercises.
Stop moving right away and rest if you feel any sharp pain or dizziness.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray so the doctor can look closely inside your bones.
Have a special body scan that uses pictures to find where the bad cells are.
Give a little blood so the nurse can check how well your body is doing.
Have a tiny piece of the bad bone gently taken out to be tested in a lab.
when_to_visit_doctor: bone pain that does not go away
feeling very tired and losing weight

bone disorder.basic_details: A bone disorder is a health problem that makes your bones weak, fragile, or misshapen, causing them to break or hurt easily.
reason: Lack of calcium or vitamin D
emergency_signs: Bone breaking easily from a minor fall
things_to_avoid: Walking in dark or slippery areas
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy foods like milk, cheese, and yogurt to get calcium.
Eat green leafy vegetables like spinach and broccoli to help your bones grow strong.
Eat foods rich in vitamin D, such as eggs and fish, or foods with added vitamins.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body healthy and working well.
recovery_time: Healing time is different for everyone and depends on which bone is hurt.
Minor bone weakness can take several months of healthy habits to improve.
Healing from a broken bone usually takes about six to eight weeks.
Severe bone conditions may need long-term care and regular check-ups for years.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks every day to keep your bones and muscles active.
Do light stretching exercises to help your body stay flexible and loose.
Try low-impact workouts like swimming that do not put too much stress on bones.
Avoid heavy lifting or sudden, hard movements that could hurt your bones.
recommended_tests: Get a special X-ray to let the doctor look closely inside your bones.
Take a bone density scan to measure how strong and thick your bones are.
Do a simple blood test to check your vitamin and calcium levels.
Have a physical check-up where the doctor tests how well you move and bend.

bone spur of the calcaneous.basic_details: A bone spur of the calcaneus is a small, extra piece of hard bone that grows on the bottom of your heel. It often causes sharp pain in your foot when you walk or stand.
emergency_signs: Swelling and redness spreading up the leg
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your joints and tissues healthy.
Eat foods with healthy fats, like fish and nuts, to lower swelling.
Try to eat less sugary and processed foods, as they can make swelling worse.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better in a few weeks with simple home care.
It can sometimes take a few months for the heel pain to go away completely.
Healing takes longer if you keep standing or walking on hard floors all day.
Being patient and resting your foot is the best way to speed up recovery.
physical_activities: Rest your foot and avoid running or jumping until the heel feels better.
Do gentle toe stretches every morning before you take your first steps.
Roll your foot gently over a frozen water bottle while sitting down.
Choose low-impact activities like swimming instead of heavy sports.
recommended_tests: A doctor will press on your heel to find the exact spot that hurts.
An X-ray picture of your foot will clearly show the extra bone growth.
A foot specialist might check how you walk to see where pressure goes.
Doctors may ask about your daily shoes and work habits to find the cause.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain does not go away with rest
It hurts too much to walk
Your heel becomes very red or swollen
You feel numbness in your foot

brachial neuritis.basic_details: Brachial neuritis is a sudden and painful condition that affects the nerves in your shoulder and arm. It usually starts with sharp pain, followed by weakness or numbness in the affected arm.
emergency_signs: Sudden complete loss of feeling in arm
Extreme sharp pain in shoulder or arm
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Include protein like chicken, fish, beans, or eggs to help repair your nerves and muscles.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your body healthy.
treatment_options: waiting for it to heal naturally
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better and notice less pain within a few weeks.
Getting full strength back in your arm can take several months, and sometimes up to a year.
Healing happens slowly, so you will need to be very patient with your body.
Your recovery speed depends on how much your nerves were hurt at the start.
physical_activities: Rest your arm completely during the first sharp pain stage so it does not get worse.
Do gentle stretching movements once the sharp pain starts to fade away.
Work with a physical therapist to learn safe, easy exercises for your shoulder.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard arm workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
recommended_tests: Get a nerve test, called an EMG, to check how well the nerves in your arm are working.
Have an MRI scan to take clear pictures of your shoulder and neck area.
Do blood tests if your doctor wants to check for other health issues or infections.
Have a physical exam where your doctor checks your arm strength, reflexes, and feeling.
when_to_visit_doctor: numbness in the hand or arm
pain that does not get better

brain cancer.basic_details: Brain cancer happens when bad cells grow wildly inside the head and form a clump called a tumor. This clump can push on parts of the brain that help you think, feel, and move.
emergency_signs: Complete loss of vision or speech
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body strength.
Drink lots of water every single day to stay hydrated.
Choose soft foods like soups and mashed potatoes if chewing feels too hard.
Eat smaller meals more often if you do not feel like eating a big plate.
recovery_time: Healing takes a very long time and is different for every single person.
You will need many weeks or months of rest after treatments like surgery.
Progress happens in tiny steps, so you might have good days and bad days.
Getting better is a team effort with your doctors, nurses, and family helping out.
physical_activities: Go for short, slow walks around your house or yard when you feel strong enough.
Do gentle stretching sitting down to keep your muscles loose and active.
Stop moving right away and rest if you start to feel dizzy or too tired.
Let helpers guide you so you do not lose your balance and fall down.
recommended_tests: Get a special picture scan of your head like an MRI to see inside the brain.
Have a doctor check how well your body moves, speaks, and thinks.
Give small blood samples so nurses can check how your body is doing.
Take a quick eye test to make sure the pressure in your head is not hurting your sight.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel dizzy or lose balance

breast infection (mastitis).basic_details: Mastitis is a painful infection of the breast tissue that often happens to women who are breastfeeding. It causes the breast to become swollen, red, hot, and painful.
emergency_signs: Red streaks spreading on the breast
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water and healthy fluids every day to keep your body strong.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Include whole grains like brown rice or whole wheat bread in your meals.
Eat foods with protein like chicken, beans, or eggs to regain your energy.
treatment_options: applying warm compresses to the breast
resting and drinking plenty of water
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within two to three days of starting treatment.
The full infection usually goes away completely in about one to two weeks.
Resting as much as possible helps your body heal up a lot quicker.
Call your doctor right away if your pain or fever does not get better after a couple of days.
physical_activities: Take plenty of bed rest and avoid heavy lifting or hard chores.
Go for short, slow walks around your house only when you feel up to it.
Avoid wearing tight bras or clothes that press hard against your chest.
Do light stretching only if it does not hurt your upper body.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where the doctor gently looks at and feels your breast.
A simple check of your body temperature using a thermometer to look for fever.
A breast milk test in some cases to find out what kind of germ is causing the issue.
Blood tests only if the doctor needs to check for a deeper infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have a high fever
if red streaks appear on the breast
if pain and swelling get worse
if you see pus or blood in the milk

broken tooth.basic_details: A broken tooth happens when a tooth cracks, chips, or breaks due to biting something hard, a fall, or tooth decay. This can cause pain and make the tooth sensitive to hot and cold foods.
emergency_signs: Severe swelling of the face or jaw
precautions: Use a cold pack on the cheek
things_to_avoid: Eating very hot or cold foods
Using strong painkillers directly on the gum
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like soup, mashed potatoes, and yogurt.
Drink plenty of water, but avoid very hot or very cold drinks.
Chew your food on the opposite side of your mouth away from the broken tooth.
Avoid hard, crunchy, sticky, or sugary foods that can hurt the tooth more.
common_medicines: pain pills you can buy without a prescription
recovery_time: Small chips can often be fixed by a dentist in just one visit.
Major breaks that need crowns or root canals may take a few weeks to fully heal.
Pain and swelling usually get much better within two to three days after treatment.
Healing time depends on how bad the break is and what kind of fix the dentist does.
physical_activities: You can do your normal daily activities right away if you feel okay.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts if your pain medicine makes you sleepy.
Wear a mouthguard if you play sports to protect your teeth from more damage.
Rest and relax as much as possible while waiting for your dentist appointment.
recommended_tests: A visual check by a dentist to look closely at the broken tooth.
A dental X-ray to see if the root of the tooth is damaged.
A bite test where you bite down on a special stick to find where it hurts.
A temperature test using cold air or water to check if the nerve is okay.
when_to_visit_doctor: if your face starts to swell
if you see bleeding from the tooth

bunion.basic_details: A bunion is a hard, painful bump that forms on the outside of the big toe. It happens when the big toe pushes against your other toes, forcing the joint to stick out.
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and vegetables every day to keep your bones strong.
Drink plenty of water to help your body stay healthy and fight swelling.
Eat foods with healthy fats, like fish and nuts, to calm down body swelling.
Try to eat less junk food and sugary snacks that can make swelling worse.
recovery_time: If you just change your shoes and rest, your foot can feel better in a few weeks.
If you have surgery to fix the bump, it can take six to eight weeks just for the bone to heal.
Full healing and getting back to all normal sports can take up to a few months.
Listening to your doctor and resting helps your foot heal much faster.
physical_activities: Wear wide and soft shoes that give your toes plenty of room to wiggle.
Avoid high heels and tight shoes that squeeze your toes together.
Do gentle toe stretches, like pulling your big toe straight with your fingers.
Go swimming or ride a stationary bike to stay active without hurting your foot.
recommended_tests: Let a foot doctor look at your foot and gently press on the bump.
Get an X-ray picture taken so the doctor can see the bone inside your toe.
Walk in front of the doctor so they can see how you step and walk.
Tell the doctor when the pain starts and what makes it hurt more.
when_to_visit_doctor: When pain stops you from walking
If you have diabetes and foot pain
When the toe looks very crooked
If home treatments do not help

burn.basic_details: A burn is an injury to your skin caused by heat, chemicals, electricity, or the sun. It can make your skin red, swollen, painful, or blistered.
emergency_signs: Burn covers a large body area
precautions: Run cool water over the burn
Keep the burn clean and covered
Get a tetanus shot if needed
things_to_avoid: Putting ice directly on the burn
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your skin heal faster.
Eat chicken, eggs, or beans to help repair the damaged skin.
Stay away from very sugary foods and drinks.
treatment_options: cool the burn with cool water
keep the area clean and dry
recovery_time: Very small and mild burns usually heal in a few days.
Minor burns with blisters often take one to two weeks to get better.
Deep or larger burns can take a month or more to fully heal.
Big scars might take many months to fade away over time.
physical_activities: Rest a lot during the first few days so your body can heal.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard exercises that stretch the burned skin.
Do very gentle movements to keep your joints from getting stiff.
Stay out of direct sunlight while your skin is still healing.
recommended_tests: A simple visual check by a doctor to see how deep the burn is.
Checking your body temperature to make sure there is no fever.
Blood tests if the burn is very large to check for hidden issues.
Looking closely at the wound for any signs of swelling or pus.
when_to_visit_doctor: if the burn is very large
if skin turns black or white
if you see signs of infection
if it is on the face or hands

bursitis.basic_details: Bursitis is when the small, fluid-filled sacs that cushion your bones and joints become swollen and painful. It usually happens from doing the same movement over and over again.
emergency_signs: Joint becomes very red and hot
Cannot move the joint at all
precautions: Avoid the activity that caused it
things_to_avoid: Kneeling or leaning on hard surfaces
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay healthy.
Choose foods like fish and nuts that help bring down swelling.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and greasy fast food.
recovery_time: Mild cases often start to feel better in just a few days.
Most people heal completely within a few weeks of rest.
Healing can take longer if you keep doing the same activity.
Listening to your body is the best way to speed up recovery.
physical_activities: Rest the sore joint and avoid the movement that caused the pain.
Do very gentle stretches once the sharp pain starts to go away.
Try low-impact exercises like swimming to stay active safely.
Stop right away if any movement makes the pain worse.
recommended_tests: A doctor will press on the sore spot to check for swelling.
You might get an X-ray to look closely at the bones nearby.
An ultrasound scan can show the fluid-filled sac clearly.
Sometimes a doctor takes a small sample of the fluid to test it.
when_to_visit_doctor: The joint is very red and warm

callus.basic_details: A callus is a thick, hard patch of skin that forms when your hands or feet rub against something too much. It is your body's way of protecting the skin underneath from getting hurt.
things_to_avoid: Cutting the callus with a knife
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your skin soft and hydrated from the inside.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body the vitamins it needs for healthy skin.
Include foods with healthy fats, like nuts and avocados, to help your skin stay smooth.
Avoid eating too much processed junk food so your body can heal itself faster.
treatment_options: Gently file with a pumice stone
recovery_time: Small calluses usually start feeling better within a few days once you stop the rubbing.
It can take one to two weeks for the thick skin to completely soften and go away.
If the callus is very old or thick, it might take a month of good care to heal.
Healing takes longer if you keep wearing the same shoes or doing the same actions.
physical_activities: Wear comfortable, well-fitting shoes that do not pinch or rub your feet.
Put on soft gloves when you are lifting heavy things or working with tools.
Take a break from walking or running long distances until the sore spot heals.
Do light stretching exercises that do not put extra pressure on your hands or feet.
recommended_tests: A simple visual check by a doctor to look at the shape and size of the hard skin.
A quick check of your shoes and how you walk to find what caused the rubbing.
A gentle touch test by a health expert to see if it hurts when you press it.
A basic skin check to make sure the thick spot is not a wart or something else.

carbon monoxide poisoning.basic_details: Carbon monoxide poisoning happens when you breathe in too much of a gas that has no smell or color. This gas replaces the oxygen in your blood and makes it hard for your body to work properly.
reason: Car engines left running in a garage
things_to_avoid: Sleeping while a gas heater is broken
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to help flush toxins out of your body.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body helpful vitamins.
Choose light meals that are easy on your stomach while you feel sick.
Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy foods until your upset stomach goes away.
treatment_options: Breathe high flow oxygen through a mask
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy in severe cases
recovery_time: Mild cases can make you feel better within a few hours of breathing fresh air.
Moderate cases might take a few days of rest and oxygen to fully heal.
Severe cases can take weeks or even months for your brain and body to recover.
Some people might need ongoing checkups if they still feel dizzy or confused.
physical_activities: Rest completely in bed and avoid any hard work for the first few days.
Walk slowly around your home only when you feel steady and not dizzy.
Do not drive a car or operate heavy machinery until a doctor says it is safe.
Slowly add light daily tasks back into your routine as your strength comes back.
recommended_tests: A blood test checks the amount of carbon monoxide still trapped in your blood.
A pulse oximeter clip on your finger measures how much oxygen is in your blood.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) checks to make sure your heart beat normally.
A neurological exam tests your thinking, memory, and balance to check for brain health.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel dizzy or have a headache indoors
You feel sick and other people in the house do too
You suspect a gas leak in your home
You have confusion or trouble thinking

cardiac arrest.basic_details: Cardiac arrest happens when the heart suddenly stops beating correctly and can no longer pump blood to the body. This is a life-threatening emergency that needs immediate help.
things_to_avoid: Waiting to see if they wake up
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Cut down on salty and greasy foods to keep your heart safe.
Drink lots of water instead of sugary sodas.
treatment_options: Advanced life support in a hospital
recovery_time: The first few weeks at home are for resting and healing.
Getting back your strength takes a few months of slow progress.
Mental healing takes time since this is a very scary event.
Every person heals at their own speed based on their health.
physical_activities: Start with very short, slow walks around your house.
Join a medically supervised heart rehab program if possible.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard sports until the doctor says yes.
Stop moving and rest right away if you feel dizzy or tired.
recommended_tests: An electrical picture of your heart to check its rhythm.
An ultrasound of your heart to see how well it pumps.
Blood tests to check for damage and other health signs.
Pictures of your heart blood vessels to look for blockages.
when_to_visit_doctor: Call emergency services immediately if someone collapses
If the person is not breathing normally
If the person has no pulse
Follow up with a heart doctor after recovery

recovery_time: Many people start to feel better within a few days of changing their diet and drinking more water.
It can take a few weeks of daily effort to get your bowel habits back to normal.
Some people need to manage this long-term with daily healthy habits.
Healing time is different for everyone and depends on what is causing the problem.
physical_activities: Go for a brisk walk for thirty minutes every day to help wake up your bowels.
Do light stretching or yoga poses that gently squeeze your belly area.
Try to stay active and avoid sitting down for too many hours in a row.
Do gentle tummy massages to help push trapped gas and stool forward.
recommended_tests: A simple blood test to check if a slow thyroid or low vitamin level is causing the issue.
A doctor's physical exam pressing gently on your belly to check for blockages.
A stool test to make sure there is no hidden bleeding or infection.
An X-ray of your stomach to see how much waste is built up inside.

chronic glaucoma.basic_details: Chronic glaucoma is a long-term eye condition where fluid builds up, putting pressure on your eye. Over time, this pressure can damage your optic nerve and lead to vision loss if not treated.
reason: High fluid pressure in the eye
emergency_signs: Nausea and vomiting with eye pain
precautions: Take prescribed eye drops exactly as told
things_to_avoid: Taking cold medicines without asking a doctor
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of colorful fruits and vegetables like carrots and spinach to keep your eyes healthy.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay well hydrated.
Try to cut down on too much caffeine from coffee and soda.
Eat fish that are rich in good fats, like salmon, at least once a week.
recovery_time: This is a lifelong condition, so there is no total cure or quick recovery.
Your vision can be protected and saved if you stick to your daily routine.
If you have eye surgery, your eye will usually need a few weeks to heal.
You will need regular check-ups for the rest of your life to monitor your eyes.
physical_activities: Go for light daily walks to keep your body and eyes healthy.
Do gentle exercises like yoga, but avoid poses where your head goes below your heart.
Stay away from heavy weightlifting that makes you strain and hold your breath.
Ask your doctor which sports and exercises are safe for your specific eyes.
recommended_tests: Get a puff-of-air test to check the pressure level inside your eyes.
Have an eye doctor look closely at the back of your eye to check your nerve.
Take a visual field test to see if you are missing any parts of your side vision.
Have your eye drainage channels measured to see how fluid flows out.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you see halos around lights

chronic knee pain.basic_details: Chronic knee pain is a long-lasting ache, soreness, or stiffness in one or both knees that does not go away easily. It can make everyday actions like walking, climbing stairs, or standing up very difficult.
reason: Repetitive strain from work or sports
emergency_signs: Cannot put any weight on the leg
things_to_avoid: Sitting with knees bent tightly for hours
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Include fish and nuts in your meals to fight body swelling.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your joints moving smoothly.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and fried fast foods.
recovery_time: Healing takes a very long time because the pain has been there for months or years.
You might start feeling a little bit better after a few weeks of gentle care.
Full recovery depends on your age, weight, and how well you follow your routine.
Some people need months of steady daily habits to keep the pain away for good.
physical_activities: Go for gentle walks on flat ground instead of running or jumping.
Try swimming or water aerobics to take the heavy pressure off your knees.
Do simple leg stretches while sitting comfortably in a chair.
Avoid deep squats, heavy lifting, and any sports that twist your knees.
recommended_tests: Take a quick picture X-ray so the doctor can look closely at your knee bones.
Have a special detailed body scan to check the soft cushions inside your knee.
Give a small blood sample if the doctor needs to check for hidden sickness.
Let a trained helper gently push and bend your leg to see where it hurts.

chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (c.basic_details: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD, is a long-term lung problem that makes it hard to breathe. It damages your airways and makes you feel very tired and out of breath.
reason: Exposure to workplace dust and chemicals
emergency_signs: Extreme shortness of breath while resting
precautions: Stay indoors on bad air quality days
diet_recommendation: Eat smaller meals more often so your stomach does not push on your lungs.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep the mucus in your chest thin.
Eat healthy foods like fruits, vegetables, and lean meats to keep your body strong.
Try to eat less salt to help keep your breathing from feeling heavy.
recovery_time: COPD is a lifelong condition, meaning it does not go away completely.
Good daily habits can help you feel better and breathe easier within a few weeks.
It takes time to learn how to manage your breath during your daily routine.
You will have good days and bad days, and recovery is about managing symptoms over your lifetime.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks every day to build up your strength.
Do simple stretching exercises to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Practice slow, deep breathing exercises while you sit or lie down.
Stop and rest right away if you start feeling dizzy or very short of breath.
recommended_tests: A breathing test where you blow hard into a tube to check how well your lungs work.
A chest picture or scan to let doctors look closely at the inside of your lungs.
A small finger clip test to check how much oxygen is in your blood.
A simple check where a doctor listens to your breathing and heartbeat with a stethoscope.
when_to_visit_doctor: When breathing gets much harder than usual
When your cough brings up dark mucus
When you have a fever and chills
When your lips or fingernails turn blue

chronic otitis media.basic_details: Chronic otitis media is a long-lasting ear infection that keeps coming back and can cause fluid to drain from your ear.
emergency_signs: Swelling and redness behind the ear
precautions: Keep water out of the ear
Go to all ear doctor appointments
things_to_avoid: Putting cotton swabs in the ear
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your immune system strong.
Drink lots of water every day to help your body stay healthy.
Choose healthy foods like chicken, fish, and beans to help your body heal.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and processed foods while you are healing.
recovery_time: Most ear infections start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment.
It can take a few weeks for your ear to completely dry out and heal.
If you have had the problem for a long time, it might take a few months to fully fix.
Always finish all your medicine, even if your ear feels better quickly.
physical_activities: Keep your head and ears completely dry when you take a bath or shower.
Avoid swimming in pools or lakes until your doctor says it is safe.
Do not fly in airplanes if your ear is very painful or blocked.
Go for gentle walks, but avoid heavy exercise that makes you sweat a lot into your ears.
recommended_tests: A doctor will look inside your ear with a special lighted tool.
You might take a hearing test to see if your ears are working okay.
The doctor might take a tiny sample of the liquid coming out of your ear to test it.
You may need a special scan of your head if the infection does not go away.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have bad ear pain
If fluid keeps coming out of the ear

chronic pain disorder.basic_details: Chronic pain disorder is a long-lasting condition where your body keeps feeling pain for months or even years. It can happen all over or in one spot, making everyday tasks hard to do.
emergency_signs: Sudden loss of feeling or movement
precautions: Work with a pain management doctor
Talk to a mental health counselor
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body feel better.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your muscles and joints happy.
Try to eat less fast food and sugary snacks, as they can make swelling worse.
Include healthy fats like fish and nuts to help calm down body aches.
recovery_time: There is usually no set end date because this is a long-term condition.
Most people focus on learning how to manage the pain instead of making it vanish completely.
Good days and bad days are normal as you figure out what works for you.
Healing happens slowly over many months with steady care and patience.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks outside to keep your body moving.
Try easy stretching exercises to keep your joints from getting stiff.
Do water aerobics, since the water takes the weight off your joints.
Listen to your body and stop right away if an activity makes the pain worse.
recommended_tests: General blood tests to check if something else is causing your body to ache.
X-rays to let the doctor look closely at your bones and joints.
A simple talk with your doctor where you point out where it hurts and how long.
Nerve checkups to see how well your body sends feeling signals.

chronic pancreatitis.basic_details: Chronic pancreatitis is a long-lasting swelling of your pancreas, which is an organ behind your stomach that helps you digest food and control sugar.
reason: High levels of fat in the blood
emergency_signs: Severe upper belly pain spreading to the back
diet_recommendation: Eat small meals throughout the day instead of three large ones.
Choose low-fat foods because high-fat meals are hard for your body to handle.
Drink plenty of water every single day to stay well hydrated.
Stay completely away from alcohol as it can make your pain much worse.
treatment_options: eat small meals with less fat
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition, so healing happens slowly over many months.
Good days and bad days are normal as your body adjusts to new habits.
Following your doctor's daily plan helps you feel better much faster.
Most people start to notice steady improvement after a few weeks of treatment.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks around your neighborhood when you feel up to it.
Try gentle stretching or light yoga to keep your body moving without stress.
Stop exercising immediately if you start to feel sharp pain in your belly.
Avoid heavy lifting and very hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
recommended_tests: Get blood tests to check how well your organs are working.
Have special picture scans, like an ultrasound or CT scan, to look at your pancreas.
Do stool tests to see how well your body is breaking down the food you eat.
Check your blood sugar levels regularly to make sure they stay in a safe range.
when_to_visit_doctor: you lose a lot of weight

chronic rheumatic fever.basic_details: Chronic rheumatic fever is a long-term heart and joint problem that can happen after having a bad throat infection as a child. It makes your body's defense system accidentally hurt your own heart valves and joints.
emergency_signs: Fainting or severe shortness of breath
Sudden painful swollen joints with fever
things_to_avoid: Heavy physical exertion without doctor approval
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay strong.
Use less salt in your food to keep your heart from working too hard.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day instead of sugary sodas.
recovery_time: This is a lifelong condition, which means it does not just go away in a few weeks.
You will need regular check-ups with your doctor for the rest of your life to stay healthy.
Children who grow up with this often need medicine for many years to protect their heart.
Many people live normal, happy lives as long as they follow their doctor's rules carefully.
physical_activities: Do light walking or gentle stretching instead of heavy, exhausting workouts.
Stop and rest immediately if you start feeling tired, dizzy, or short of breath.
Avoid high-intensity sports that make your heart beat way too fast.
Ask your doctor exactly what kind of exercise is safe for your specific heart.
recommended_tests: Get a heart ultrasound to let the doctor look closely at how well your heart valves work.
Have regular blood tests to check if there is any swelling or infection in your body.
Do an electrocardiogram test to check the electrical rhythm and beats of your heart.
Get routine throat swabs if you feel a scratchy throat coming on, to catch infections early.

chronic sinusitis.basic_details: Chronic sinusitis is a long-lasting swelling of the spaces inside your nose and head. It makes it hard to breathe through your nose and can give you a stuffy, painful face.
emergency_signs: Swelling or redness around one eye
precautions: Use a humidifier in your bedroom
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to help thin out the mucus in your nose.
Eat fresh fruits and veggies to help your body fight off swelling.
Eat warm chicken soup to soothe your throat and clear your nose.
Try to cut back on dairy and sugary foods, as they can sometimes make mucus thicker.
common_medicines: Antibiotics if there is an infection
treatment_options: Putting warm cloths on your face
Surgery to open blocked nose passages
recovery_time: It can take several weeks or even months to feel completely better.
Some people manage symptoms for a lifetime with daily self-care habits.
Using a daily nose rinse speeds up how fast you feel relief.
If surgery is needed, full healing usually takes about 3 to 6 weeks.
physical_activities: Take gentle walks outside when the air is clean and not too cold.
Do light stretching indoors to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Avoid heavy workouts or swimming in chlorinated pools while your nose is very blocked.
Do breathing exercises in a steamy room to help open up your airways.
recommended_tests: A doctor may look inside your nose with a small, lighted tube.
You might get a head scan to see the blocked areas clearly.
An allergy test can check if certain things in the air make your nose swell.
A swap test might be done to check if germs are causing an infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have a very bad headache
If medicines do not help you feel better

cirrhosis.basic_details: Cirrhosis is a long-term condition where the liver gets scarred and cannot work the way it should. Over time, the healthy liver tissue is replaced by scar tissue, slowing down blood flow.
emergency_signs: Rapid swelling of the belly with fluid
precautions: Check with a doctor before taking any pills
things_to_avoid: Eating raw oysters or undercooked seafood
diet_recommendation: Eat less salt to stop your body from holding onto extra water.
Choose fresh fruits and vegetables every day for good nutrition.
Eat lean proteins like chicken, fish, or beans to keep your muscles strong.
Drink plenty of water unless your doctor tells you to drink less.
common_medicines: Blood pressure pills for vein health
Vitamins to make up for lost nutrients
treatment_options: Eat a healthy diet with less salt
Drain fluid buildup with a needle
Liver transplant for very sick patients
recovery_time: Cirrhosis is a long-term condition that usually does not go away completely.
Healing happens very slowly over many months or even years.
Sticking to your treatment plan helps you feel better and stops it from getting worse.
Regular check-ups are needed for the rest of your life to monitor your health.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks most days to keep your body moving.
Do light stretching to keep your muscles flexible and relaxed.
Avoid heavy lifting or very hard workouts that make you too tired.
Rest as soon as you feel worn out or out of breath.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check how well your liver is doing its job.
Ultrasound scans to take pictures of your liver and see the scar tissue.
Endoscopy to look inside your throat and stomach for swollen blood vessels.
FibroScan to measure how stiff or scarred your liver is.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your belly or legs swell up a lot
Your skin or eyes turn yellow
You feel very tired and confused

coagulation (bleeding) disorder.basic_details: A coagulation disorder is a health problem where your blood cannot make clots properly. This means you might bleed longer than normal if you get a cut or hurt yourself.
emergency_signs: Bleeding that will not stop after 10 minutes
precautions: Use a soft toothbrush and electric shaver
things_to_avoid: Contact sports like football or boxing
Taking aspirin or ibuprofen without asking
Ignoring a hard bump to the head
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of leafy green vegetables, but try to keep the amount you eat the same every day if you take blood thinners.

Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body strong and full of vitamins.
Avoid drinking alcohol because it can make it much harder for your blood to clot.
treatment_options: Avoiding certain pain relievers like aspirin
Taking iron pills for low blood count

If you have a sudden bleed inside your body, it can take a few weeks to feel better.
Healing time depends completely on how mild or severe your specific bleeding problem is.

Be very careful around the house to avoid bumping into furniture or sharp corners.

Have your doctor check your blood cell counts to make sure you have enough platelets.
Take genetic tests if your doctor wants to see if the problem runs in your family.
Get regular check-ups to make sure your bleeding levels are safe and steady.
when_to_visit_doctor: You have nosebleeds that will not stop
You bruise very easily for no reason
You notice blood in your urine or stool
Your cuts bleed for a long time

cold sore.basic_details: A cold sore is a small, painful blister that usually shows up on or around your lips. It is caused by a very common virus that spreads easily from person to person.

Sore lasting longer than two weeks
things_to_avoid: Kissing or sharing drinks while having a sore
Touching or picking at the sore
Direct hot sun on the face

Avoid eating very spicy, salty, or sour foods that can sting the sore.
Eat foods with lots of vitamins, like fruits and vegetables, to help your skin heal faster.
treatment_options: Put antiviral cream on the sore
Put ice on the sore to stop pain
Keep the area clean and dry

The painful blister usually pops and forms a dry scab after a few days.

Resting well helps your immune system heal the sore much quicker.

Wash your hands right away if you accidentally touch your face while working out.
Take a short break from swimming in public pools until the scab completely falls off.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually do not need any tests because they can just look at the sore to know what it is.
A doctor can gently swab the liquid from the blister if they want to be extra sure.
Blood tests are rarely needed, but can check if you carry the virus in your body.
Tell your doctor how often you get these sores so they can give you the best advice.
when_to_visit_doctor: The sore lasts more than two weeks
You have a very weak immune system

colonic polyp.basic_details: A colonic polyp is a small clump of cells that forms on the lining of your large intestine. Most are harmless, but doctors like to remove them because some can turn into cancer over time.

Drink lots of water to help your digestion stay smooth.
Try to eat less red meat and fatty or fried foods.

No specific pills to make polyps go away

Regular checks to watch for new polyps
Eating healthy food to prevent more polyps
recovery_time: If your polyps were removed during a test, you will feel better in a day or two.

Your doctor will tell you when you are fully healed.

Ask your doctor before you start going back to the gym.

If you have belly pain that does not go away
If your bowel habits change for a long time
If you feel very tired for no clear reason

common cold.basic_details: A common cold is a mild illness that makes you sneeze, cough, and have a stuffed-up nose. It is caused by tiny germs called viruses that pass easily from person to person.

You should feel completely normal in about ten days.

Avoid heavy workouts and going to the gym.
Take slow, short walks around the house only if you feel okay.
Do not push your body to work hard until you are well.

A doctor may look in your throat and listen to your chest.

Blood tests are rarely needed for a simple cold.
when_to_visit_doctor: if sick for over ten days

complex regional pain syndrome.basic_details: Complex regional pain syndrome is a condition that causes ongoing, severe pain in a limb, usually after an injury or surgery. Your nerves send wrong pain signals to your brain, making the affected body part very sensitive and swollen.

Complete inability to move the limb

Seek psychological support for chronic pain

Applying ice directly to the painful skin

Try to eat less junk food and sugary snacks that can cause body swelling.

Some people start feeling better in a few months with early treatment.
For others, it can take many years or become a long-term condition to manage.
Getting help early gives you the best chance of recovering faster.

Work with a physical therapist who knows how to help your specific pain.
Slowly try using the painful limb for everyday tasks like holding a cup.

Special skin temperature tests to see if one side is warmer or cooler than the other.
X-rays to make sure there are no hidden broken bones or other issues.

concussion.basic_details: A concussion is a mild brain injury that happens after a hard bump or blow to the head. It can temporarily change how your brain works and make you feel off.

precautions: Follow doctor's plan for returning to activities
Have someone monitor you for the first day
things_to_avoid: Taking strong sleep medicines without asking

Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal naturally.
Choose healthy proteins like chicken, fish, or beans for strength.
Avoid sugary snacks and drinks that can make your energy crash.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within one to two weeks.
Some people might need a little longer, up to a month, to heal fully.
Listen to your body and do not rush the healing process.
Every person heals at their own speed, so be patient with yourself.

Avoid playing sports or doing heavy workouts until a doctor says it is safe.
Slowly start light walking once your headache and dizziness go away.
Stop and rest immediately if any activity makes your symptoms worse.

conduct disorder.basic_details: Conduct disorder is a behavioral issue where a person has a hard time following rules and respecting the rights of others. They might act out aggressively or break rules repeatedly.

Good days and bad days will happen, and a bad day does not mean you failed.
Lasting change happens slowly as you learn new ways to handle your feelings.
physical_activities: Play team sports like soccer or basketball to learn how to share and follow rules.
Try running, swimming, or biking to burn off extra stress and angry energy.
Do calming activities like yoga or stretching to help your body relax.
Go for walks outside in nature to help clear your head when you feel upset.
recommended_tests: Talk with a counselor or psychologist who will ask questions about your daily life.
Have a chat with your parents and teachers so doctors can understand your behavior.
Get a checkup with a regular doctor to make sure your body is healthy and growing well.
Fill out some simple questionnaires about your feelings and how you react to things.

conductive hearing loss.basic_details: Conductive hearing loss happens when sound waves cannot travel easily through the outer or middle ear to reach the inner ear. It often makes sounds seem softer or harder to hear clearly.

Consider hearing aids or surgery if advised

If you need a minor procedure, it may take a few weeks for full healing.
Some long-term issues may take a few months to fully improve or adjust to.

A scan of your head if the doctor needs a closer look at the bones inside your ear.
when_to_visit_doctor: You have fluid coming out of your ear

congenital heart defect.basic_details: A congenital heart defect is a heart problem that you are born with. It means the heart did not form the right way while you were growing inside your mother.

A test that puts sticky patches on your chest to listen to your heartbeat.
Blood checks to make sure your body is healthy and strong.

conjunctivitis.basic_details: Conjunctivitis, commonly known as pink eye, is an irritation or infection of the clear membrane that covers the white part of your eyeball. It makes your eyes red, itchy, and watery.

Pus so thick the eye won't open

Eat fresh fruits like oranges and berries to help your body heal faster.
Include green vegetables like spinach in your meals for healthy eyes.
Avoid eating too much junk food or sugary snacks while you are sick.
treatment_options: Using a warm or cool wet cloth on eyes
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within three to seven days.
Mild cases caused by viruses usually go away on their own without strong medicine.
If you use the right eye drops, your symptoms can start fading in just a couple of days.
