Restraining them forcefully unless necessary for safety
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to avoid being low on fluids.
Eat simple, healthy foods like soups, fruits, and soft vegetables.
Eat small meals often if the person is too tired to finish a big plate.
Limit sweet snacks and heavy foods that can make a person sluggish.
recovery_time: It can take a few days to a few weeks to get back to normal.
Recovery happens faster when the main health problem is fixed quickly.
Some people might feel confused for a few months, especially older adults.
Every person heals at their own speed depending on their overall health.
physical_activities: Take short, slow walks around the room with help from a family member.
Do gentle stretching while sitting in a chair to keep the body moving.
Avoid heavy workouts or activities that could lead to a fall.
Rest often during the day so the body can save its energy.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check for infections, vitamins, or body chemical balance.
Urine tests to see if there is a hidden bladder infection.
Brain scans like a CT scan to check for head injuries or strokes.
Simple memory and attention checks by asking questions about the day and time.
when_to_visit_doctor: the person sees things that are not there
the person does not know where they are

dementia.basic_details: Dementia is a brain condition that makes it hard to remember things, think clearly, and do everyday tasks. It usually gets worse slowly over time.
reason: Multiple small strokes in the brain
emergency_signs: Refusal to eat or drink leading to dehydration
precautions: Keep a safe, familiar home routine
Use locks and alarms to prevent wandering
things_to_avoid: Arguing or correcting their memory loudly
Leaving them alone in risky places
diet_recommendation: Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink plenty of water to stay hydrated throughout the day.
Eat fish and nuts that are good for brain health.
recovery_time: Dementia is a long-term condition that does not fully go away.
Good care can help slow down how fast the condition gets worse.
Every person's journey with the condition is different.
Focus on having good days and keeping comfort high.
physical_activities: Take short, gentle walks outside every day.
Do light stretching to keep the body moving easily.
Dance slowly to favorite music in the living room.
Do simple household chores with help and supervision.
recommended_tests: Answer simple questions with a doctor to check memory.
Take pictures of the brain using special hospital machines.
Give blood samples to check for other health issues.
Have a physical check-up to test body strength and reflexes.

dental caries.basic_details: Dental caries is the medical name for cavities, which are tiny holes that form in your teeth when sugar and germs damage the hard outer shell.
reason: Eating too much sugar and sticky foods
precautions: Brush twice a day with fluoride toothpaste
diet_recommendation: Eat less candy, cookies, and other sugary snacks.
Drink plenty of plain water throughout the day.
Eat more fresh fruits and crunchy vegetables like apples and carrots.
Try to avoid sticky foods that stay on your teeth for a long time.
recovery_time: Small cavities fixed with fillings usually heal in just one or two days.
If you had a deep cavity fixed, your tooth might feel sensitive for a week.
Getting a crown put on can take a few weeks to feel completely normal.
Healing time depends on how big the cavity was and what treatment you needed.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily exercises and sports right away.
Avoid heavy workouts only if you feel dizzy or sick from a bad toothache.
You do not need to stay in bed or rest unless you just had major dental surgery.
Just keep your normal active routine while your teeth heal.
recommended_tests: Let the dentist look inside your mouth with a small mirror and light.
Take dental X-rays to see if there are hidden holes between your teeth.
The dentist will gently poke your teeth with a metal tool to check for soft spots.
Check if your teeth feel extra sensitive when you touch them or drink cold water.
when_to_visit_doctor: your tooth is sensitive to hot or cold
you see holes or dark spots on teeth

depression.basic_details: Depression is a very common mental health condition that makes you feel very sad, hopeless, and tired most of the time. It can take away your joy and make it hard to do your normal daily activities.
emergency_signs: Complete inability to get out of bed or eat for days
precautions: Talk to a therapist or counselor
Try to keep a simple daily routine
Stay connected with friends and family
things_to_avoid: Using drugs or alcohol to feel better
Stopping medication suddenly without asking a doctor
Making major life choices during a low period
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body and brain healthy.
Try to eat whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Eat fish or nuts that have healthy fats which are good for your brain.
Drink plenty of water every day to stay hydrated and feel less tired.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel a little better after taking medicine and talking to someone for 4 to 8 weeks.
A full recovery can take several months, so it is important to be patient with yourself.
Some people may need help for a year or more to make sure the sadness does not come back.
Recovery happens step by step, with some good days and some hard days mixed together.
physical_activities: Go for a short, easy walk outside every day to get fresh air and sunshine.
Do light stretching or simple yoga in your room to loosen up your body.
Dance to your favorite upbeat songs for just ten minutes to boost your mood.
Do gentle gardening or housework to keep your hands busy and your mind focused.
recommended_tests: Talk with a doctor or mental health helper who will ask you questions about how you feel.
Take a simple blood test to check if your body is low on important vitamins.
Check your thyroid levels through a blood test to make sure your body is working right.
Fill out a simple paper questionnaire with sad or happy faces to rate your daily mood.
when_to_visit_doctor: Feeling sad for more than two weeks
Loss of interest in fun activities
Changes in sleep or eating habits

dermatitis due to sun exposure.basic_details: Dermatitis due to sun exposure is a red, itchy skin rash that happens when your skin reacts badly to strong sunlight. It usually goes away when you stay out of the sun and take care of your skin.
reason: Too much UV light from the sun
Taking medicines that make skin sensitive to light
emergency_signs: Severe blisters covering a large part of the body
precautions: Apply cool, wet cloths to the skin
Drink lots of water to prevent dehydration
things_to_avoid: Applying heavy creams, butter, or oil on burns
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every single day to keep your skin hydrated.
Eat lots of fresh fruits like watermelon and oranges to help your skin heal.
Eat green vegetables like spinach to give your body good vitamins.
Stay away from spicy or salty foods that might make you feel too warm.
treatment_options: put cool wet cloths on skin
recovery_time: Most mild sun rashes start to feel better in just two or three days.
It usually takes about a full week for your skin to look normal again.
If your skin peels, let it fall off naturally while it heals.
Healing can take longer if the sunburn was very deep or painful.
physical_activities: Stay indoors and rest in a cool room while your skin is healing.
Avoid going outside in the bright sun, especially during the middle of the day.
Wear loose, soft cotton clothes that do not rub against your sore skin.
Skip heavy exercise that makes you sweat a lot until your skin is better.
recommended_tests: Show your skin to a doctor so they can look at the redness.
Tell the doctor if you have a fever or feel dizzy from the sun.
Let the doctor check if your skin has small blisters from the heat.
Answer questions about how long you stayed out in the sunshine.
when_to_visit_doctor: skin looks very bad with blisters
you feel very dizzy or sick

developmental disability.basic_details: Developmental disability is a group of conditions where a person may have trouble learning, speaking, or moving like others. It starts early in life and lasts throughout a person's life.
reason: Birth complications or lack of oxygen
precautions: Work closely with special education teachers
things_to_avoid: Ignoring milestones and hoping they catch up
Leaving the individual in unsafe environments
Isolating the family from support groups
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to stay healthy and active.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Limit sweet snacks, sugary drinks, and junk food.
recovery_time: This is a lifelong condition, so it does not fully go away.
People can keep learning and growing at their own speed.
Good daily support helps people feel better over time.
Regular practice of skills brings steady improvement year by year.
physical_activities: Go for fun daily walks in your neighborhood or park.
Play active games like catch, tag, or kicking a ball.
Join a local swimming class or splash around safely.
Dance around the living room to your favorite happy music.
recommended_tests: Visit the doctor for regular check-ups on your overall health.
Have your hearing checked to make sure you hear clearly.
Get your eyes tested to see if you need glasses.
Talk with specialists to see how well you learn and speak.

deviated nasal septum.basic_details: A deviated nasal septum happens when the wall inside your nose that separates your nostrils is crooked. This can make it harder to breathe through one side of your nose.
emergency_signs: Severe bleeding from the nose that won't stop
Clear fluid draining from the nose after a head injury
High fever with severe face pain
precautions: Use saline sprays to keep nose moist
Consider surgery if breathing is very hard
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your immune system strong.
Drink lots of water every day to keep the inside of your nose from drying out.
Eat warm soups and broths to help soothe your throat and ease congestion.
Try to avoid foods that cause you to have allergies, as they can swell your nose.
recovery_time: If you have surgery to fix it, you will likely feel much better after about one to two weeks.
It can take up to two months for your nose to completely heal on the inside.
Most people are able to go back to school or desk work within a week.
Swelling and stuffiness will slowly go away day by day as time passes.
physical_activities: Take easy, gentle walks around your house to help your body heal.
Stay away from heavy lifting and hard gym workouts for at least a few weeks.
Avoid contact sports like football or basketball so nobody bumps your nose.
Skip swimming in pools until your doctor says it is safe for your nose.
recommended_tests: Your doctor will look inside your nose with a small, lighted tool.
They might use a tiny camera on a thin tube to see deep inside your nose.
You may be sent for an allergy test to see if allergies are making it worse.
A CT scan might be done to take a detailed picture of your nasal bones.
when_to_visit_doctor: when you have trouble breathing through your nose
if you get frequent sinus infections
when nasal congestion does not get better with medicine

diabetic ketoacidosis.basic_details: Diabetic ketoacidosis is a dangerous emergency where your body runs out of insulin and builds up toxic acids in your blood. It usually happens when blood sugar gets way too high.
reason: Severe infection or illness while diabetic
emergency_signs: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Gasping for air or fast breathing
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Drink water if blood sugar is very high
things_to_avoid: Exercising when blood sugar is dangerously high
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to flush out extra sugar and stop dehydration.
Eat small meals with simple foods like broth and toast once your stomach settles.
Avoid sugary drinks, sodas, and candies that make your blood sugar spike.
Eat healthy foods like vegetables and lean proteins once you can eat solid food again.
treatment_options: getting fluids through a needle in the vein
taking insulin to lower blood sugar
treating the cause like an infection
recovery_time: Most people need to stay in the hospital for two to three days to get stable.
You will feel very tired and weak for several days after leaving the hospital.
Full recovery depends on getting your daily blood sugar and insulin routine under control.
You must follow up with your regular doctor within a week to stay on track.
physical_activities: Rest completely and avoid all exercise while you are sick in the hospital.
Start with very light walking around your house once you are home and feeling stronger.
Do not lift heavy things or do hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Always check your blood sugar before and after moving around to stay safe.
recommended_tests: Frequent blood sugar checks using a finger prick throughout the day.
Blood tests at the hospital to check your body's acid and salt levels.
Urine tests to check for harmful acids called ketones.
An A1C blood test to see your average blood sugar over the last three months.
when_to_visit_doctor: if blood sugar is very high and does not go down
if you throw up and cannot keep water down
if you feel very confused or dizzy
if you have severe stomach pain and trouble breathing

diabetic peripheral neuropathy.basic_details: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is nerve damage in your hands and feet caused by having too much sugar in your blood for a long time. It can make your skin feel numb, tingly, or painful.
emergency_signs: Black or dead skin on the toes
Open sore on the foot that will not heal
Severe spreading redness up the leg
Fever and chills with a foot wound
precautions: Check your feet every day for cuts or redness
Wash and dry feet carefully daily
things_to_avoid: Ignoring small cuts on the feet
Using hot water bottles on feet (can burn without feeling it)
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh vegetables and fruits every day.
Choose whole wheat bread and brown rice instead of white bread and white rice.
Drink plenty of water instead of sweet sodas and juices.
Cut back on sugary snacks, candies, and greasy fast foods.
recovery_time: Nerve damage usually does not go away completely, but it can be managed.
Symptoms can start to feel better within a few weeks or months of controlling your blood sugar.
Some people need long-term daily care to keep the pain under control.
Healing takes time and depends on how well you keep your diabetes in check every day.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks daily to help blood flow to your feet.
Do gentle stretching exercises to keep your legs and feet flexible.
Try swimming or riding a stationary bike since they are easy on your joints.
Avoid high-impact exercises like heavy running that can hurt your feet.
recommended_tests: Get your blood sugar checked regularly with an A1C test.
Have a doctor check the feeling in your feet using a soft brush or tuning fork.
Do nerve conduction studies to see how well your nerves are working.
Get routine blood and urine tests to check your overall health and kidney function.
when_to_visit_doctor: cuts or sores on feet that do not heal
burning or tingling in hands and feet

diabetic retinopathy.basic_details: Diabetic retinopathy is an eye condition caused by high blood sugar that damages the tiny blood vessels in the back of your eye. This can lead to blurry vision or even loss of sight if it is not treated.
emergency_signs: Seeing a dark shadow like a curtain over the eye
Sudden appearance of many floating spots
precautions: Get a dilated eye exam every year
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh vegetables and whole grains every day.
Cut down heavily on sugary snacks, candies, and sweet drinks.
Choose healthy fats like fish, nuts, and olive oil instead of greasy foods.
Drink lots of water throughout the day instead of soda or packaged juice.
recovery_time: There is no quick fix, as treating eye damage takes a steady, long-term effort.
Small laser treatments in the doctor's office usually heal within a few days.
Surgery for more advanced cases can take a few weeks to several months to heal.
Your vision may take time to stabilize after any procedure, so be patient.
physical_activities: Go for a comfortable, brisk walk for 30 minutes most days of the week.
Do light stretching or simple home yoga to stay active without straining your eyes.
Avoid heavy weightlifting or intense straining that raises your blood pressure too fast.
Always check with your doctor before starting any brand-new exercise routine.
recommended_tests: Get a dilated eye exam where drops are used to look deep inside your eyes.
Take an optical coherence tomography (OCT) scan to take pictures of your retina layers.
Do a regular blood test called an A1C to check your average blood sugar levels.
Have your blood pressure checked regularly during your visits to the clinic.
when_to_visit_doctor: You see dark spots or floating lines
You have yearly eye check-ups for diabetes

diaper rash.basic_details: Diaper rash is a very common skin problem where a baby's bottom gets red, sore, and warm to the touch. It usually happens when the skin sits in a wet or dirty diaper for too long.
reason: Leaving a wet or dirty diaper on too long
Reaction to baby wipes or soap
emergency_signs: Rash has bright red blisters or open sores
Rash spreads beyond the diaper area
precautions: Clean the area gently with water
Let the baby go without a diaper to air out the skin
Apply a thick layer of diaper cream (like zinc oxide)
things_to_avoid: Using baby wipes with alcohol or perfume
Rubbing the skin hard to clean it
Putting the diaper on too tightly
Ignoring a rash that gets worse after 3 days
diet_recommendation: Keep feeding your baby their normal milk, whether it is breast milk or formula.
If your baby is eating solid foods, offer plenty of water to keep them hydrated.
Hold off on trying new foods until the rash goes away, just in case it upsets their tummy.
Eat healthy foods yourself if you are breastfeeding, as this keeps your milk nutritious.
treatment_options: Keep the diaper area clean and dry
Let the baby go without a diaper for some time
Use warm water instead of wipes
recovery_time: Most simple diaper rashes start to look better in just two or three days.
If you keep the skin clean and dry, it usually clears up completely within a week.
Rashes caused by yeast or bacteria might take a little longer, around 7 to 10 days.
Call the doctor if the rash does not get better after a week of home care.
physical_activities: Give your baby plenty of 'diaper-free time' to let their skin breathe and stay dry.
Let your baby kick and play safely on a big towel spread out on the floor.
Avoid putting tight pants or plastic covers over the diaper so air can flow.
Keep tummy time short if the diaper rubs against the sore spot too much.
recommended_tests: Most diaper rashes do not need any special medical tests at all.
A doctor can usually just look at the red skin to know what it is.
If the rash will not go away, the doctor might gently swab the skin to check for germs.
Very rarely, a blood test might be done if the baby has a fever or other sickness.
when_to_visit_doctor: If the rash does not get better in a few days
If the skin starts to bleed or blister
If the baby has a fever
If pus comes out of the rash

dislocation of the elbow.basic_details: An elbow dislocation happens when the bones of your arm pop out of their normal spot at the elbow joint. This usually happens after a bad fall onto an outstretched hand.
reason: Pulling a child's arm too hard
emergency_signs: Arm looks deformed or bent incorrectly
Hand turns pale, cold, or blue
Loss of feeling in the hand or fingers
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Support the arm with a sling
Go to physical therapy after the doctor fixes it
things_to_avoid: Trying to pop the elbow back in yourself
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Include foods rich in calcium like milk and cheese to keep your bones strong.
Eat lean meats and beans to help repair your injured arm muscles.
Drink plenty of water every day to stay healthy and hydrated.
common_medicines: Prescription pain medicine for severe pain
treatment_options: Doctor putting the bone back in place
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better after about 4 to 6 weeks.
It can take several months for your arm to get completely back to normal.
Following your doctor's advice carefully will speed up your healing time.
Do not rush the healing process or you might hurt your elbow again.
physical_activities: Rest your arm completely in a sling during the first few days.
Do gentle finger and wrist movements to keep your blood flowing.
Slowly start easy stretching exercises only when your doctor says it is safe.
Avoid heavy lifting and sports until your elbow is fully healed.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray to let the doctor see if any bones are broken.
Have a physical exam where the doctor gently checks your arm movement.
Sometimes an MRI is done to check the soft tissues and ligaments.
Check your pulse and hand feeling to make sure nerves and blood flow are fine.
when_to_visit_doctor: Right away if your arm looks crooked
If you cannot move your arm or hand
If your hand feels numb or cold
If pain and swelling do not get better

dislocation of the shoulder.basic_details: A shoulder dislocation happens when the top bone of your arm pops out of its normal socket in your shoulder blade. This can cause sharp pain and make it very hard to move your arm.
reason: Heavy fall directly on the shoulder
Sudden strong pull on the arm
emergency_signs: Shoulder looks out of place or square
Severe pain and inability to move the arm
precautions: Keep the arm close to the body in a sling
Do physical therapy exercises once healed
things_to_avoid: Asking a friend to pull it back into place
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Include foods rich in calcium like milk and cheese to keep your bones strong.
Eat lean meats and beans to help repair your injured muscles and tissues.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay healthy and hydrated.
treatment_options: putting the bone back in place
recovery_time: Most people start feeling a bit better within two to three weeks.
It usually takes about six to twelve weeks for the shoulder to heal completely.
Doing your gentle home exercises helps speed up your healing time.
Heavy lifting and hard sports may take several months before they are allowed again.
physical_activities: Rest your shoulder and avoid any sudden or jerky arm movements.
Wear your arm sling as told by your doctor to protect the joint.
Do very gentle swaying exercises only when your doctor says it is safe.
Slowly build up your strength with easy stretches once the pain goes away.
recommended_tests: An X-ray to check if any bones are broken or cracked.
A physical checkup where the doctor gently moves your arm to test stability.
An MRI scan if the doctor needs a closer look at your torn muscles or tendons.
A nerve check to make sure your hand and arm are getting proper feeling.
when_to_visit_doctor: right away if the shoulder is out
if you cannot move your arm
if you have numbness in your hand
if pain does not go away

dislocation of the vertebra.basic_details: Dislocation of the vertebra happens when the bones in your spine slip out of their normal place. This can cause pain and make it hard to move your back or neck.
emergency_signs: Inability to move arms or legs (paralysis)
Loss of bowel or bladder control
precautions: Hold the head and neck in a straight line
things_to_avoid: Taking off their helmet (if wearing one)
Trying to help them stand up
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of milk, cheese, and yogurt to keep your bones strong.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables every day to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water to keep your muscles and joints healthy.
Eat protein like chicken, fish, or beans to help repair your body.
treatment_options: doctor putting bone back in place
wearing a neck or back brace
recovery_time: Minor slips might take a few weeks to heal with rest and care.
Bad dislocations that need surgery can take several months to get better.
You will slowly start feeling better bit by bit each week.
Healing time depends a lot on how well you follow your doctor's rules.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest in the first few days to let your spine settle.
Do gentle stretches only when your doctor says it is safe to do so.
Take short, slow walks around your house to keep your blood moving.
Avoid heavy lifting, twisting, or playing sports until you are fully healed.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray so the doctor can take a picture of the slipped bones.
Have an MRI scan to check if any nerves or soft tissues got hurt.
Undergo a CT scan to get a very clear 3D view of your spine.
Do simple body movement checks with your doctor to test your strength.
when_to_visit_doctor: you have severe back or neck pain
you feel numb or weak in arms or legs
you had a bad fall or car crash

dislocation of the wrist.basic_details: A dislocation of the wrist happens when the bones in your hand slip out of their normal place where they meet your arm bone. This usually happens after a hard fall or a sports accident, causing pain and swelling.
emergency_signs: Fingers turn white, cold, or blue
Sudden severe numbness in the hand
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Immobilize the wrist with a splint or magazine
Keep the hand elevated above the heart
things_to_avoid: Trying to snap the wrist back in place
Using the hand to grip anything
Delaying a trip to the hospital
Taking pain meds and ignoring it
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and strong.
Include foods with calcium, like milk and cheese, to make your bones strong again.
Eat protein-like chicken, beans, or eggs to help repair your injured wrist.
treatment_options: doctor putting bone back in place
recovery_time: Most mild wrist dislocations take about 6 to 8 weeks to feel much better.
Severe cases that need surgery might take 3 to 6 months for a full recovery.
Your doctor may put your wrist in a cast or splint for the first few weeks.
Healing time depends on how well you rest your hand and follow your doctor's advice.
physical_activities: Rest your wrist completely during the first few weeks to let the bones stay in place.
Avoid lifting heavy bags, pushing doors open hard, or playing rough sports.
Do gentle finger wiggles to keep your blood flowing while the wrist is resting.
Do easy stretching exercises only after a doctor or physical therapist tells you it is safe.
recommended_tests: An X-ray is done first to see if any bones are broken or out of place.
A doctor will do a physical check by gently touching and moving your hand.
An MRI scan might be needed to look closely at torn ligaments or wrist tissue.
A CT scan may be used to get a very detailed 3D picture of the wrist bones.

dissociative disorder.basic_details: Dissociative disorder is a mental health condition where a person feels disconnected from reality, their memories, or their own identity. It is often a way the brain tries to cope with past stress or trauma.
reason: Severe childhood physical or emotional abuse
emergency_signs: Complete memory loss of where they are
Severe panic attacks or unsafe behavior
precautions: Work closely with a trauma therapist
Create a safe and calm home environment
Practice grounding techniques (focusing on the present)
things_to_avoid: Using drugs or alcohol to cope
Forcing the person to remember trauma aggressively
diet_recommendation: Eat balanced meals with whole grains, fruits, and vegetables to keep your mood steady.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to avoid feeling tired and dizzy.
Try to limit sugary snacks and drinks that can cause energy crashes.
Eat regular meals so your blood sugar stays stable and doesn't affect your focus.
recovery_time: Healing takes time and is different for every single person.
Some people start feeling better in a few months with good help.
For others, it can take several years of working through past stress.
Recovery has ups and downs, but steady progress is always possible.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks outside to help clear your head.
Try yoga or stretching to help your body feel calm and safe.
Do simple breathing exercises when you feel spaced out or confused.
Pick fun hobbies like swimming or dancing to stay connected to your body.
recommended_tests: Talk with a mental health expert who will ask you questions about your life.
Answer special questionnaires about your feelings and memory.
Have a basic physical checkup to make sure your body is healthy.
Talk about your past experiences to help the doctor understand your needs.
when_to_visit_doctor: you feel like you are not real
you hear voices in your head

diverticulitis.basic_details: Diverticulitis happens when small, bulging pouches in your digestive tract become inflamed or infected, causing belly pain.
reason: Feces getting trapped in colon pouches
Weak spots in the colon walls
emergency_signs: Severe, sudden pain in the lower left belly
Vomiting and unable to keep fluids down
Large amounts of blood in the stool
precautions: Go to the hospital or doctor right away
Switch to a liquid diet for a few days to rest the gut
Slowly add high-fiber foods back once healed
things_to_avoid: Eating heavy, hard-to-digest meals while in pain
diet_recommendation: Eat clear liquids like broth, water, and juice when your belly hurts bad.
Slowly add soft foods like yogurt, eggs, and white bread as you start feeling better.
Eat plenty of fiber-rich foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains once you are fully healed.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your digestion smooth and healthy.
treatment_options: eating only clear liquids for a few days
staying in the hospital for strong medicine
surgery to fix bad parts of the gut
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within a few days of starting treatment.
Mild cases usually clear up completely in about one to two weeks.
Severe cases or hospital stays might take a few weeks to heal.
Listen to your body and rest as much as possible while recovering.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest in bed during the first few days of a flare-up.
Take slow, gentle walks around your house to help your body heal.
Avoid heavy lifting, intense workouts, and hard straining until you are healed.
Slowly return to your normal daily routine as your belly pain goes away.
recommended_tests: Get a CT scan of your belly so doctors can see the inflamed pouches clearly.
Give blood samples to check for signs of infection or swelling in your body.
Provide a stool sample to rule out other stomach problems.
Have a colonoscopy later on, after you are fully healed, to check your colon.
when_to_visit_doctor: when you have new belly pain
if you start to throw up a lot
when you feel very tired and weak
if your belly feels very hard

diverticulosis.basic_details: Diverticulosis happens when small, weak spots in your large intestine push outward to form tiny pouches. Most of the time, these pouches do not cause any pain or health problems.
emergency_signs: Sudden, large amount of painless bleeding from the bottom
Sudden severe left-sided belly pain (turns into diverticulitis)
Inability to pass gas or stool
precautions: Eat a diet high in fiber (beans, veggies, whole grains)
Drink plenty of water every day
Exercise regularly to keep bowels moving
Use fiber supplements if approved by a doctor
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of high-fiber foods like beans, lentils, and whole grains.
Add fresh fruits and vegetables to your meals every single day.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to keep your digestion smooth.
Avoid eating foods that trigger pain or digestive discomfort for you.
treatment_options: Resting the bowel during mild pain
recovery_time: Since this is a lifelong condition rather than a temporary injury, there is no set recovery time.
If you get a mild infection, you usually start feeling better within a few days of starting treatment.
Most people bounce back very quickly if the infection is caught and treated early.
Making daily healthy choices prevents you from needing a long recovery in the future.
physical_activities: Go for a nice, easy walk every day to keep your digestion moving well.
Do light stretching or gentle yoga to help your body stay active.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense straining that puts too much pressure on your belly.
Listen to your body and rest if any movement causes you pain.
recommended_tests: A doctor may use a special camera test called a colonoscopy to look inside your colon.
A CT scan uses special pictures to check your belly for any signs of swelling or infection.
A blood test can show if your body is fighting off an infection.
A simple stool sample test can help check for hidden bleeding or tummy issues.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have severe belly pain
If you see blood in your stool
If pain does not go away

down syndrome.basic_details: Down syndrome is a natural condition where a person is born with an extra part in their body's instructions, called chromosomes. This means they may learn a bit slower and look a little different, but they can still live happy and full lives.
reason: Having an extra copy of chromosome 21
Older maternal age increases the chance
emergency_signs: Blue lips or struggling to breathe (heart defect sign)
precautions: Get regular heart and thyroid checkups
Engage in speech and physical therapy
Ensure a healthy diet and exercise
things_to_avoid: Treating them like they cannot learn
Ignoring signs of sleep apnea (loud snoring/gasping)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grain breads and pastas instead of white flour.
Drink lots of water instead of sugary sodas and juices.
Eat healthy proteins like chicken, fish, beans, and eggs.
recovery_time: Down syndrome stays with a person for their whole life, so there is no recovery time.
Growing and learning happen at a slower, steadier speed.
With good help and practice, people get better at daily tasks over the years.
Every single person moves at their own unique pace.
physical_activities: Go for fun daily walks in the park with family or friends.
Play games that involve catching and throwing balls to build strength.
Join swimming classes to help the body stay strong and flexible.
Dance around the living room to upbeat, fun music.
recommended_tests: Heart check-ups to make sure the heart is working nicely.
Eye doctor visits to check if glasses are needed to see well.
Ear check-ups to make sure sounds and words can be heard clearly.
Blood tests to check that the body's energy levels are healthy.

drug abuse.basic_details: Drug abuse happens when someone uses harmful or illegal drugs too much, which hurts their body and mind. It makes it very hard to stop using them without help.
reason: Trying to escape severe stress or trauma
emergency_signs: Unresponsive and cannot be woken up
precautions: Remove yourself from environments where drugs are used
things_to_avoid: Quitting highly addictive drugs cold-turkey without medical help
Keeping drug tools in the house
Substituting one illegal drug for another
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to help clean your body.
Eat foods with whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Stay away from too much sugar and junk food.
recovery_time: Getting better takes a long time and is different for everyone.
The first week is usually the hardest part of stopping.
Most people need a few months of daily support and care.
Staying healthy is a lifelong journey that takes ongoing effort.
physical_activities: Take short, easy walks outside in the fresh air.
Try gentle stretching or yoga to relax your body.
Dance to your favorite music to boost your mood.
Do fun hobbies that keep your hands and body busy.
recommended_tests: Urine tests to check for any drugs in your system.
Blood tests to see how well your organs are working.
Checkups to see how your heart and lungs are doing.
Talk sessions with a counselor to check your mental health.
when_to_visit_doctor: When wanting to stop drug use
When daily life is badly affected

drug abuse (barbiturates).basic_details: Drug abuse of barbiturates happens when someone takes sleeping pills or relaxants too often or without a doctor's help, which harms their body and mind.
reason: Misuse of prescription sleep or anxiety medicines
emergency_signs: Breathing stops or is dangerously slow
Skin turns cold, clammy, and blue
precautions: Call emergency services immediately for overdose
things_to_avoid: Quitting cold turkey (can cause deadly seizures)
Taking more than the prescribed dose
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to flush out harmful toxins.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Avoid sugary snacks and junk food that can make your mood swing.
treatment_options: slowly stop taking the drug with a doctor
recovery_time: The first week is usually the hardest as your body clears the drugs out.
Most physical withdrawal symptoms start to get better after about one to two weeks.
Mental healing and feeling like yourself again can take several months.
Full recovery is a lifelong journey that takes ongoing care and daily effort.
physical_activities: Start with light daily walks to get fresh air and gentle exercise.
Try simple stretching or beginner yoga to help relax tense muscles.
Do fun hobbies that keep your body moving without making you too tired.
Avoid heavy or hard workouts until your doctor says your body is strong enough.
recommended_tests: Urine tests to check if drugs are still present in your system.
Blood tests to make sure your liver and kidneys are working well.
Heart checks, like an EKG, to see if your heart is healthy.
Mental health check-ins to talk about your feelings and stress levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: when you want to stop using drugs
if you feel very sad or hopeless
if you have shaking or sweating

drug abuse (cocaine).basic_details: Cocaine abuse happens when a person uses the illegal drug cocaine so much that it harms their body, mind, and daily life. Stopping can be hard because the drug changes how the brain feels pleasure.
reason: Highly addictive nature of the drug
emergency_signs: Sudden inability to speak or move (stroke)
precautions: Call an ambulance for chest pain or seizures
Enter a professional addiction treatment center
things_to_avoid: Using cocaine with alcohol (creates a highly toxic chemical in the body)
Returning to environments that trigger use
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water every day to clean out your body.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to get your strength back.
Choose healthy foods like chicken, fish, and beans to heal your muscles.
Try to stay away from too much coffee or sugary drinks.
recovery_time: The first week is usually the hardest, with strong cravings and feeling very tired.
Most physical withdrawal symptoms start to fade after about one to two weeks.
Healing the brain and feeling happy again can take several months.
Full recovery is a lifelong journey that gets a little easier every single day.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks outside to get fresh air and sunshine.
Try gentle stretching or basic yoga to help your body relax.
Do fun hobbies like dancing or swimming to keep your body moving.
Avoid heavy workouts at first until your heart and body feel stronger.
recommended_tests: Urine tests are used to check if drugs are still in your body.
Blood tests check your overall health and organ function.
Mental health checks help doctors see how you are feeling emotionally.
Heart checks make sure the drug has not damaged your heart.

drug abuse (methamphetamine).basic_details: Methamphetamine drug abuse is a serious condition where a person uses a strong, harmful man-made drug that hurts their brain and body. It makes it very hard to stop using the drug without help.
emergency_signs: Severe chest pain and racing heart
precautions: Get dental care for tooth decay
things_to_avoid: Engaging with the person if they are violently paranoid
Ignoring high fever or chest pain
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to flush out toxins and stay hydrated.
Eat foods with protein, like chicken, beans, and eggs, to get your strength back.
Try to stay away from too much sugar and junk food.
treatment_options: staying at a special recovery center
learning ways to cope with stress
recovery_time: The first week is usually the hardest, focusing on getting the drug out of your body.
Most people start to feel physically better after a few weeks of being clean.
Healing the brain and changing habits can take many months or even a year.
Recovery is a lifelong journey that gets a little easier every single day.
physical_activities: Start with gentle walks outside to get fresh air and sunshine.
Try light stretching or yoga to help calm your mind and body.
Join group sports or fun fitness classes to stay busy and make healthy friends.
Always check with a doctor before starting any hard workouts.
recommended_tests: Urine tests are often used to check for drugs in your system.
Blood tests help doctors check your general health and organ function.
Mental health check-ups help find anxiety, depression, or other emotional needs.
Infectious disease screenings are important to make sure your heart and blood are safe.
when_to_visit_doctor: when you want to stop using drugs
if you feel very sad or hopeless
if you hear or see things that are not real

drug abuse (opioids).basic_details: Opioid drug abuse happens when a person uses strong pain medicines in a way that is not safe, leading to a strong physical need for them. It can harm health and daily life, but professional help and support can lead to a healthy recovery.
reason: Severe chronic pain leading to overmedication
Highly addictive properties of the drug
Turning to illegal drugs like heroin when prescriptions run out
emergency_signs: Breathing is very slow, shallow, or stops
Lips and fingernails turn blue or gray
precautions: Dispose of old prescription painkillers safely
things_to_avoid: Leaving the person alone to "sleep it off"
Mixing opioids with alcohol or sleeping pills
Taking painkillers not prescribed to you
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body important vitamins.
Drink lots of water every day to flush out toxins and stay hydrated.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Eat foods with good proteins like beans, chicken, and fish to help your body heal.
recovery_time: The first week is usually the hardest, focusing mostly on getting through physical withdrawal.
Most people start feeling much better physically after the first month of staying clean.
Mental healing and rebuilding healthy habits can take several months to a year.
Recovery is a lifelong journey that needs ongoing support and daily effort.
physical_activities: Start with short, gentle walks outside to get fresh air and light exercise.
Try simple stretching or beginner yoga to help relax tense muscles.
Engage in fun hobbies like swimming or cycling to keep your body moving.
Join group sports or fitness classes to stay active and make supportive friends.

Blood tests to check overall organ health and look for any hidden infections.
Mental health check-ups to understand emotional needs and moods better.
Screenings for common illnesses linked to drug use, such as specific viruses.
when_to_visit_doctor: when you want to stop using drugs
if you feel sad or anxious

drug poisoning due to medication.basic_details: Drug poisoning due to medication happens when you take too much of a medicine or mix the wrong pills. It can make you feel very sick and needs quick medical help.
reason: Taking too much medicine by mistake
Liver or kidneys failing to process normal doses
emergency_signs: Vomiting blood or severe stomach pain
precautions: Call poison control or emergency services immediately
Bring the pill bottles to the hospital
Keep all medicines out of reach of children
things_to_avoid: Making the person vomit unless told to by poison control
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of plain water to help flush your body out.
Eat light and soft foods like plain rice, toast, and bananas.
Stay away from spicy, greasy, or heavy foods until you feel better.
Avoid coffee, soda, and alcohol completely while you recover.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within one to three days.
Severe cases might need you to stay in the hospital for a week.
Your body will feel very tired for a few days after.
Total healing depends on how much and what kind of medicine was taken.
physical_activities: Rest in bed as much as possible during the first few days.
Do not do any heavy lifting, running, or hard workouts.
Take slow, short walks around the room only when you feel steady.
Wait until a doctor says you are fully healed before going back to normal routines.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check how much medicine is left in your body.
Urine tests to see if your kidneys are working okay.
Heart monitoring to make sure your heartbeat is safe and steady.
Breath tests to check your oxygen levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: feeling very sleepy or passing out

drug reaction.basic_details: A drug reaction happens when your body has a bad or allergic response to a medicine you took. It can cause skin rashes, itching, or even trouble breathing.
emergency_signs: Severe skin rash with blisters or peeling
Swelling of the lips, tongue, or face
precautions: Stop taking the medicine and seek emergency help
Tell all doctors about your drug allergies
Wear a medical alert bracelet for severe allergies
things_to_avoid: Taking the drug again just to see what happens
Mixing new prescriptions without checking with a pharmacist
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to help flush the medicine out of your body.
Eat plain foods like rice, bananas, and toast if your stomach feels upset.
Stay away from spicy or greasy foods that might make you feel worse.
Avoid alcohol completely while your body is healing from the reaction.
recovery_time: Mild rashes usually start to fade within two to three days after stopping the bad medicine.
More serious reactions might take one to two weeks to completely go away.
Your skin may need a little extra time to heal even after the rash is gone.
Always talk to your doctor if your symptoms do not start getting better soon.
physical_activities: Take a complete break and rest in bed until your body feels better.
Avoid heavy workouts and strenuous exercises that make you sweat a lot.
Stay out of the hot sun, as heat can make skin rashes much worse.
Wear loose and soft cotton clothing so it does not rub against your skin.
recommended_tests: Get a general blood test to check how your organs are handling the medicine.
Do an allergy skin test to find out which exact drug caused the problem.
Have a doctor check your skin closely to see how bad the reaction is.
Keep a list of your symptoms and show them to your doctor for safety.

drug withdrawal.basic_details: Drug withdrawal happens when your body reacts badly after you suddenly stop taking a substance or medicine it has gotten used to. This causes uncomfortable physical and emotional symptoms as your body tries to adjust.
emergency_signs: Severe seizures (especially from alcohol or sedatives)
Seeing or hearing things that are not there
precautions: Take prescribed medicines to ease symptoms
Rest in a safe, quiet place
things_to_avoid: Quitting alcohol or sedatives alone if heavily addicted
Taking other unapproved drugs to calm down
Being totally alone for the first few days
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water and juice to flush out toxins and stay hydrated.
Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body healthy vitamins.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Avoid sugary snacks and junk food that can make your mood swing up and down.
recovery_time: The worst physical symptoms usually peak within the first few days to a week.
Most people start to feel significantly better physically after about two weeks.
Mental cravings and mood changes can sometimes last for several months.
Total recovery time is different for everyone and depends on the specific substance.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks outside to get fresh air and ease your mind.
Try light stretching or easy yoga to help relax tense muscles in your body.
Avoid heavy workouts or intense lifting until your body feels stronger.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel too tired or dizzy.
recommended_tests: Blood tests are often done to check your general health and organ function.
Urine tests can help doctors see what substances are currently in your body.
Simple heart checks may be done to make sure your heart rate is safe.
Basic mental health check-ins help doctors understand your mood and stress levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: When feeling very sad or hopeless

dry eye of unknown cause.basic_details: Dry eye of unknown cause happens when your eyes do not make enough tears or the right kind of tears, and doctors are not quite sure why. This leaves your eyes feeling scratchy, tired, and sore.
reason: Looking at screens too long without blinking
emergency_signs: Eye becomes completely red and swollen
things_to_avoid: Sitting directly in front of fans or air vents
Wearing contact lenses if eyes are very dry

Eat more fish like salmon, because it has good oils that help make your tears better.
Add nuts and seeds like flaxseeds to your meals to help soothe dry eyes.
Eat colorful fruits and vegetables like carrots and spinach to keep your eyes healthy.
treatment_options: blocking tear ducts with tiny plugs
recovery_time: Dry eyes often cannot be completely cured, but you can feel much better by treating the symptoms daily.
You might start feeling some relief within a few days to a couple of weeks after using eye drops.
It takes time to figure out which daily habits and drops work best for your specific eyes.
You may need to keep up a daily eye care routine for a long time to stay comfortable.
physical_activities: Take lots of breaks when looking at screens like phones, computers, or the TV.
Remember to blink often when you are reading or working on a computer.
Wear sunglasses outside to protect your eyes from the wind and bright sun.
Avoid sitting right in front of blowing fans, air conditioners, or heaters.
recommended_tests: A special eye doctor checkup where they look closely at your eyes with a bright light.
A tear amount test, where tiny paper strips are placed under your eyelids to see how many tears you make.
An oil gland check to see if the edges of your eyelids are working properly.
A simple dye test using harmless orange drops to check for dry spots on the surface of your eyeball.
when_to_visit_doctor: if your eyes stay red and painful
if over-the-counter drops do not help
if your eyes feel very sensitive to light

dyshidrosis.basic_details: Dyshidrosis is a common skin problem that causes tiny, itchy blisters to form on the palms of your hands and the sides of your fingers. It usually happens because of stress, allergies, or having your hands wet for too long.

Red streaks spreading up the arm or leg
Severe pain preventing hand use or walking

Wear cotton gloves under rubber gloves when cleaning
things_to_avoid: Using harsh soaps or hand sanitizers

Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Try to eat fewer processed foods and foods with lots of added sugar.
Some people find that eating less nickel-rich food, like oats and nuts, helps their skin.

Avoid things that trigger your skin
Light therapy from a skin doctor

when_to_visit_doctor: Skin becomes very painful or red
You see pus or signs of infection

Answer simple questionnaire forms about your daily mood and sleep habits.
Get a routine blood check to make sure your low energy is not caused by other health issues.
Share your daily routines and life stress with a counselor to see what helps.
when_to_visit_doctor: When you feel sad for a long time
When sleep habits change a lot
If you lose interest in fun things

Sudden pressure changes (deep water diving or flying)

Cleaning the inside of the ear

Chewing your food well helps your jaw move, which naturally helps your ears.

eating disorder.basic_details: An eating disorder is a serious mental health condition where a person has an unhealthy focus on food, weight, and body shape. This can lead to dangerous eating habits that hurt their body and mind.

A need for control in life

Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your body healthy.

Weight checks done by a nurse in a gentle and supportive way.

Surgery to fix the fallopian tube

Wait until your doctor gives the green light before swimming or taking baths.

Take a break from heavy lifting and hard workouts for the first week.

The doctor will gently pull your eyelid to check how loose it is.
They might test how well your eyes make tears to see if they are too dry.
Your vision may be checked to make sure your sight is not getting worse.

Take a cool shower right after you work out to wash away sweat.
Wear loose and soft cotton clothes when you exercise to avoid rubbing your skin.

Keep a food diary to see if certain meals make your skin worse.
Check with a doctor if your red skin starts to look infected or swollen.
when_to_visit_doctor: Skin gets very red and painful
You see pus or yellow crust

Get vaccinated for flu and pneumonia
Exercise gently to keep lungs working
things_to_avoid: Being around smoke or strong fumes
Going outside in very cold air

Drink plenty of water every day to keep the mucus in your lungs thin and easy to cough up.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay strong.
Try to eat less salt so you do not hold onto extra water, which can make breathing harder.

A picture of your chest, like an X-ray, to look at the inside of your lungs.
A quick finger clip test to check the amount of oxygen in your blood.
A blood check to see how well your body takes in oxygen and gets rid of waste.

You feel more tired than usual
Your skin or lips look blue
Your breathing medicine does not help

encephalitis.basic_details: Encephalitis is a dangerous swelling of the brain, usually caused by a germ or virus. It can make you feel very confused, sleepy, and give you a bad headache.

Ignoring a severe headache with fever
Being outside unprotected in mosquito areas

Choose healthy foods like fruits and vegetables to help your brain heal faster.
Avoid junk food, sugary drinks, and heavy meals that make you feel sluggish.

Avoid playing sports, running, or doing heavy chores until the doctor says it is safe.
Start with very short, slow walks around the house when you begin to feel stronger.
Stop moving and rest immediately if you feel dizzy, tired, or get a headache.

Give a blood sample so the lab can look for signs of infection.
Do an EEG test, where sticky pads are put on your head to check how your brain is working.

endocarditis.basic_details: Endocarditis is a dangerous infection of the inner lining of your heart chambers and valves, usually caused by germs entering your bloodstream.

X-rays of your chest to see how your lungs and heart are doing.

endometriosis.basic_details: Endometriosis is a common condition where tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows outside of it, causing pain and heavy periods.

Use a heating pad for cramps
Discuss surgery options with a doctor if severe
