A cover test where the doctor looks at how your eyes move when one is covered.
A special machine scan to take pictures of the inside of your eyes.
A focusing test to see how well your eyes work together on close things.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your child turns their head to see

female genitalia infection.basic_details: A female genitalia infection happens when tiny germs like bacteria or yeast grow where they should not, causing itching, pain, and unusual discharge. It is a common problem that can be easily treated with the right care.
precautions: See a doctor for the correct medicine
things_to_avoid: Scented soaps, sprays, or bubble baths
Wearing wet swimsuits for a long time
Having physical intimacy until the infection clears
diet_recommendation: Eat plain yogurt with live cultures to help keep your body balanced.
Drink plenty of water every single day to help flush out your system.
Cut down on sugary foods and drinks because germs love sugar.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your immune system strong.
treatment_options: Keep the area clean and dry
recovery_time: Most minor infections start to feel better in just two to three days.
It usually takes about a full week to heal completely.
You must finish all your medicine even if you feel better early.
See a doctor again if symptoms do not go away after one week.
physical_activities: Rest as much as you can so your body has time to heal.
Wear loose cotton clothes instead of tight pants to stay dry.
Avoid heavy workouts or swimming until you are fully healed.
Do not use hot tubs or take very hot baths while healing.
recommended_tests: A doctor will look at the area to check for redness and swelling.
A simple swab test might be taken to find out what germ is causing it.
A urine test might be done to make sure it is not a bladder issue.
A pH test might be used to check the balance of the area.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you see bad smell or strange discharge

fibroadenoma.basic_details: A fibroadenoma is a very common, non-cancerous lump in the breast that feels firm and moves easily under the skin. It is completely safe and does not turn into cancer.
emergency_signs: The lump grows very fast suddenly
Skin over the breast becomes red and hot
Blood or fluid draining from the nipple
precautions: Have a doctor check any new breast lumps
Get ultrasounds or biopsies as recommended
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to keep your body healthy.
Try to eat less junk food and sugary snacks.
Include whole grains like brown rice and oats in your meals.
common_medicines: pain pills you can buy at the store
treatment_options: doing nothing and just watching it
taking a small sample with a needle
recovery_time: Most fibroadenomas stay the same size or go away on their own.
If you have surgery to remove it, you will feel better in a few days.
Normal daily life can usually restart within 24 to 48 hours after minor treatment.
Complete healing from a small surgery takes about one to two weeks.
physical_activities: You can safely do your normal everyday exercises and walks.
Wear a supportive sports bra if you feel any bounce or pain.
Avoid heavy lifting for a few days if you had surgery.
Listen to your body and stop if an activity hurts your chest.
recommended_tests: A doctor will gently feel the lump with their hands during a checkup.
An ultrasound uses sound waves to take a clear picture of the lump.
A mammogram uses low-dose X-rays to look closely at breast tissue.
A tiny needle test might be done to take a small sample and make sure it is safe.
when_to_visit_doctor: if your breast starts to hurt a lot
if you find a new lump

fibromyalgia.basic_details: Fibromyalgia is a long-term health condition that makes your whole body feel achy and tired all the time. It also makes certain spots on your body very sensitive to even a light touch.
reason: Abnormal pain signaling in the brain
emergency_signs: Sudden inability to move or extreme weakness
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to keep your body well-hydrated.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and processed foods.
Eat foods with healthy fats like fish, nuts, and olive oil.
recovery_time: Fibromyalgia is a long-term condition, so it does not completely go away.
Many people have good days and bad days with their pain.
Finding the right mix of care can make you feel better over a few months.
Learning to manage your daily energy helps you feel better over time.
physical_activities: Take short, gentle walks outside to keep your body moving.
Do light stretching every morning to loosen up stiff muscles.
Try water aerobics because the warm water is gentle on joints.
Practice slow, easy yoga to help relax your body and mind.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check for other health issues like thyroid problems.
A physical check by a doctor to find your tender body spots.
Sleep studies to see if you are getting deep rest at night.
A review of your medical history and daily pain symptoms.

flat feet.basic_details: Flat feet happen when the arches on the inside of your feet are missing or very low, causing your whole foot to touch the ground when you stand.
reason: Obesity putting extra weight on feet
emergency_signs: Sudden extreme pain in the foot or ankle
Inability to walk or put weight on the foot
precautions: Wear shoes with good arch support
Do stretching exercises for the foot and calf
diet_recommendation: Eat healthy foods like fruits and vegetables to keep your body weight down so your feet do not hurt.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your muscles and joints feeling good.
Eat foods with calcium like milk or yogurt to keep your leg and foot bones strong.
Try to eat less junk food and sugary snacks to avoid gaining extra weight.
recovery_time: Most people with flat feet do not need a full recovery because they can live a normal life with good shoes.
If you just started using arch supports, your feet might need a few weeks to get used to them.
If you have foot surgery, it can take a few weeks to a few months for your foot to heal.
Doing your foot exercises every day helps you feel better much faster.
physical_activities: Wear supportive sneakers that give your feet a nice, soft cushion.
Try rolling a tennis ball under the bottom of your bare foot while sitting down.
Stretch your calves and ankles gently every morning before you start walking.
Avoid walking barefoot on hard floors for a long time to keep your feet from aching.
recommended_tests: Stand with your feet wet on a piece of paper to see the shape of your footprint.
Let a foot doctor look closely at how you walk and stand.
Get a simple foot checkup where a doctor presses on your arches to check for pain.
Do an imaging scan if the doctor needs to look closely at the bones inside your foot.

flu.basic_details: The flu is a common sickness that makes you feel very tired, gives you a fever, and can make your body ache. It spreads easily from person to person when they cough or sneeze.
things_to_avoid: Touching your face with unwashed hands
Going to work or school while sick
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water, juice, and warm tea to stay hydrated.
Eat warm chicken soup to help soothe your throat and feel better.
Have easy-to-digest foods like bananas, rice, and toast.
Eat fruits with vitamin C, like oranges, to help your body fight the sickness.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within one week.
You might still feel a little tired for two weeks or even longer.
Getting plenty of sleep helps your body heal much faster.
Stay home until your fever is gone for at least 24 hours so you do not spread it.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and rest as much as you can.
Avoid heavy exercise, running, or going to the gym until you are fully well.
Only do light walking around your house if you feel up to it.
Listen to your body and stop moving if you feel dizzy or tired.
recommended_tests: A simple swab inside your nose can check if you have the flu.
Your doctor might check your throat to see why it hurts.
A nurse might take your temperature with a thermometer to check your fever.
Usually, doctors can just guess you have the flu based on how you feel without any tests.
when_to_visit_doctor: if fever lasts more than three days
if you have other serious health problems

fluid overload.basic_details: Fluid overload happens when your body holds onto too much water and salt. This makes it hard to breathe and causes your body to swell up.
emergency_signs: Rapid weight gain in a few days
Extreme swelling in legs or belly
precautions: Restrict fluid intake if doctor advises
things_to_avoid: Eating highly salted or processed foods
diet_recommendation: Eat less salt because salt makes your body hold onto extra water.
Drink only the amount of water or liquids your doctor tells you to.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables instead of salty, packaged snacks.
Choose healthy, simple home-cooked meals over fast food.
treatment_options: Take water pills to remove extra fluid
Eat less salt in your food
Drink less water and other liquids
Treat the main cause like heart or kidney problems
recovery_time: You might start feeling better and less swollen in just a few days.
It can take a couple of weeks for your body to get back to normal.
Your total healing time depends on what caused the extra water in the first place.
You may need ongoing checkups to make sure the water does not come back.
physical_activities: Take short, slow walks around your house if you feel up to it.
Do light stretching to keep your body moving gently.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Rest often during the day so your heart does not work too hard.
recommended_tests: Step on the scale every day to check your weight for sudden changes.
Get blood tests to see how well your kidneys are working.
Have a chest X-ray so the doctor can look for water in your lungs.
Do a heart check, like an ECG, to see how your heart is pumping.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your legs and feet swell more
You feel tired all the time

folate deficiency.basic_details: Folate deficiency happens when your body does not have enough vitamin B9, which makes you feel very tired and weak. Eating the right foods and taking vitamins can help you get your energy back.
reason: Diseases that block nutrient absorption (like Celiac)
precautions: Eat leafy greens, beans, and citrus fruits
Take folic acid vitamins if prescribed
diet_recommendation: Eat lots of dark green leafy vegetables like spinach and broccoli.
Include beans, peas, and lentils in your daily meals.
Eat breakfast cereals that have added vitamins.
Snack on fresh fruits like oranges, bananas, and lemons.
treatment_options: Change diet to include foods with extra vitamins
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within one to two weeks of treatment.
Your blood levels usually go back to normal in about two to three months.
You might need to take vitamins for a few months to keep your levels steady.
Recovery can take longer if your deficiency is very severe.
physical_activities: Stick to light walking until you start feeling less tired.
Do gentle stretching or easy yoga to keep your body moving.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts while you feel weak.
Slowly add more activity as your energy levels come back.
recommended_tests: Get a simple blood test to check your vitamin levels.
Do a complete blood count test to check your red blood cells.
Check your vitamin B12 levels at the same time.
Do follow-up blood tests after a few weeks to see if treatment is working.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel very tired all the time

food allergy.basic_details: A food allergy happens when your body's defense system mistakes a harmless food for something dangerous and overreacts. This can cause you to feel sick or get a rash after eating that specific food.
reason: Immune system reacting to harmless food proteins
emergency_signs: Swelling of lips, tongue, or face
precautions: Tell restaurant staff about your allergy
Know exactly what is in your food
things_to_avoid: Eating foods if you are unsure of the ingredients
Ignoring mild tingling in the mouth
diet_recommendation: Stay completely away from the foods that make you sick.
Always read the ingredient labels on food packages.
Tell restaurant staff about your allergies before you order.
Eat fresh, simple foods that you make at home so you know what is in them.
treatment_options: Go to hospital for severe reaction
recovery_time: Mild symptoms like a tummy ache or small rash usually go away in a few hours.
Severe reactions need quick help, but you can feel better within a day after getting treatment.
Your body heals fast once the bad food is completely out of your system.
You stay healthy as long as you do not eat the food that causes your allergy.
physical_activities: You can do normal exercises like walking or playing sports most days.
Avoid heavy workouts right after eating to help your stomach feel good.
Keep your rescue medicine close by when you go out to exercise.
Stop and rest right away if you start to feel dizzy or short of breath.
recommended_tests: Get a skin prick test done by a doctor to find out your exact triggers.
Take a blood test that looks for specific allergy proteins.
Keep a daily food diary to write down what you eat and how you feel.
Talk to an allergy specialist to plan safe tests for your body.

foreign body in the eye.basic_details: A foreign body in the eye means something small, like dust, an eyelash, or a tiny bug, has gotten stuck on or inside your eye. It can make your eye feel scratchy, hurt, and water a lot.
reason: Dust or sand blowing in the wind
Metal or wood shavings from working
emergency_signs: Unable to keep the eye open
precautions: Wear safety glasses when working with tools
Blink to let tears wash the object out
Rinse the eye gently with clean water or saline
things_to_avoid: Using sharp tools like tweezers to remove it
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body and eyes hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal quickly.
Include foods with healthy fats, like fish or nuts, to soothe your eyes.
Avoid salty foods that might make your eyes feel dry or irritated.
treatment_options: blink a lot to remove it
pull upper lid over lower lid
recovery_time: Most minor dust or dirt issues feel better within a few hours after washing out.
If the surface of the eye was gently scratched, it usually heals in 1 to 2 days.
If the object was stuck deep or needed a doctor to remove it, healing may take a few days.
Full comfort returns quickly as long as you do not rub your eye.
physical_activities: Rest your eyes by closing them and avoiding screens like phones and TVs.
Stay away from dusty or windy places until your eye is fully healed.
Do not play rough sports or swim while your eye is recovering.
Avoid heavy lifting or bending down so you do not put extra pressure on your face.
recommended_tests: A doctor will shine a bright light into your eye to look for the stuck object.
The doctor might gently pull down your lower eyelid to check underneath it.
A special yellow dye and blue light may be used to check for tiny scratches on the eyeball.
Vision tests might be done to make sure you can see clearly without any blurriness.
when_to_visit_doctor: you cannot get the object out

foreign body in the gastrointestinal tra.basic_details: This means you accidentally swallowed something that is not food, and it is now stuck in your stomach or intestines.
reason: Accidentally swallowing fish or chicken bones
precautions: Keep small objects away from young children
Go to the emergency room immediately
Follow doctor's advice on waiting for it to pass
things_to_avoid: Trying to make the person vomit
Eating solid food to push it down
Sticking fingers blindly down the throat
diet_recommendation: Stop eating and drinking right away until a doctor checks you.
Drink only small sips of water if your doctor says it is safe.
Eat soft foods only after the doctor tells you the object is gone.
Stay away from hard, crunchy, or chewy foods until you are fully healed.
recovery_time: Most people feel better within a few days after the object is taken out.
If the object passes on its own, you might recover in 24 to 48 hours.
If you needed surgery, it could take a few weeks to feel normal again.
Your doctor will tell you when you are completely healed.
physical_activities: Rest in bed and take it easy while you wait for treatment.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until the object is removed.
Take gentle, short walks only if your doctor says it is okay.
Listen to your body and stop moving if you feel pain in your stomach.
recommended_tests: An X-ray is often done to take a picture of what you swallowed.
A CT scan gives a clearer 3D picture of where the object is stuck.
A doctor might use a tiny camera on a flexible tube to look inside your throat.
Blood tests may be done to make sure your body is healthy and fighting off any germs.

foreign body in the throat.basic_details: A foreign body in the throat happens when an object, like food or a small toy, gets stuck or trapped while you are trying to swallow it.
reason: Large pieces of poorly chewed food
Children putting small toys in their mouth
emergency_signs: Complete inability to breathe or speak
precautions: Perform the Heimlich maneuver if they are choking
Cut children's food into very small pieces
things_to_avoid: Giving water to someone who is choking
Putting fingers blindly into the throat
Slapping the back while the person is standing upright (unless trained)
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to help wash the area down.
Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes or yogurt after the object is out.
Stay away from dry, crunchy, or hard foods until your throat feels better.
Avoid very hot drinks that can burn your sore throat.
recovery_time: Most small objects are removed quickly and you will feel better the same day.
Your throat might feel sore and scratchy for one to two days after.
Rest your voice if talking hurts your throat.
Go back to the doctor immediately if pain gets worse instead of better.
physical_activities: Rest quietly and avoid running or heavy lifting right away.
Do not do hard exercise until your swallowing feels completely normal.
Sit upright and try to stay calm to keep your breathing steady.
Avoid bending over too much if you feel like coughing.
recommended_tests: A doctor will look inside your mouth and throat with a light.
An X-ray might be done to check if a hard object is stuck.
A tiny camera on a flexible tube may be used to look deeper.
A quick check of your breathing and heart rate to make sure you are safe.

fracture of the ankle.basic_details: A fracture of the ankle means one or more of the bones in your ankle joint are broken. This usually happens from a bad twist, fall, or impact, causing pain, swelling, and trouble walking.
emergency_signs: Foot looking deformed or pointing the wrong way
Foot turning pale, cold, or blue
Inability to put any weight on it
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Apply ice wrapped in a towel
things_to_avoid: Trying to walk on the injured ankle
Trying to snap the bone back into place
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk, cheese, and yogurt to help your bones heal strong.
Include eggs, fish, and beans in your meals to give your body protein for tissue repair.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables every day to help reduce swelling and speed up healing.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to keep your body healthy while you rest.
recovery_time: Most simple ankle fractures take about six to eight weeks to heal firmly.
It can take several months before you can walk normally without any pain or limp.
Healing can take longer if the break is severe or if you need surgery.
Your age and overall health also play a big part in how fast your ankle heals.
physical_activities: Rest your foot and keep it propped up on pillows to bring down the swelling.
Use crutches, a walker, or a wheelchair so you do not put weight on the broken bone.
Do gentle toe wiggles and foot stretches while sitting to keep blood moving.
Follow a physical therapist's safe exercise plan once your doctor gives you the green light.
recommended_tests: Get a standard X-ray to let the doctor see the broken bone clearly.
Have a physical checkup where the doctor gently presses your foot to check the pain.
Do a CT scan if the doctor needs a closer, detailed look at complex bone pieces.
Get an MRI if the doctor wants to check for damage to your ankle ligaments and tendons.
when_to_visit_doctor: You cannot walk on the foot
The pain does not get better
You feel numbness in your toes

fracture of the arm.basic_details: A fracture of the arm means you have a broken bone in your arm. This usually happens from a fall, a hard hit, or an accident.
emergency_signs: Bone sticking out of the skin
precautions: Support the arm with a sling
things_to_avoid: Using the hand to grip objects
Applying heat to a new injury
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk, cheese, and yogurt to help your bones heal.
Eat green leafy vegetables like spinach and kale for extra bone strength.
Include eggs and fish in your meals to get important vitamins.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your whole body healthy.
recovery_time: Most simple arm bones take about 6 to 8 weeks to heal completely.
Young children usually heal a bit faster, sometimes in just 4 weeks.
Older adults or people with bigger breaks might need 12 weeks or more to get better.
Your arm might feel weak and stiff even after the bone is healed.
physical_activities: Rest your arm as much as possible during the first few weeks.
Wiggle your fingers often to keep the blood flowing in your hand.
Do light stretching only when your doctor or physical therapist tells you it is safe.
Avoid lifting heavy things, playing sports, or doing hard work with that arm.
recommended_tests: An X-ray is done first to see where and how the bone is broken.
A doctor will check your hand grip and finger feeling to test your nerves.
A blood test might be done if the doctor wants to check your overall bone health.
A follow-up X-ray is usually done a few weeks later to make sure the bone is healing right.
when_to_visit_doctor: if fingers turn blue or cold
if the cast feels too tight

fracture of the facial bones.basic_details: A fracture of the facial bones means that one or more bones in your face have a break or crack, usually caused by a hard hit or accident. This can make your face swollen, painful, and sometimes hard to move properly.
emergency_signs: Clear fluid draining from the nose or ears
Uncontrollable bleeding from the nose or mouth
precautions: Keep the person sitting up if possible to drain blood away from the throat
Apply ice gently to swollen areas
things_to_avoid: Moving the neck if a neck injury is possible
Applying heavy pressure to the broken face bones
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and applesauce so you do not have to chew hard.
Drink plenty of water and clear liquids to stay healthy and hydrated.
Eat blended soups that are easy to swallow and full of helpful vitamins.
Avoid crunchy, hard, or chewy foods that can hurt your jaw and face.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better after about 6 to 8 weeks.
Complete healing of the bone can take several months.
Swelling and bruising usually go away within the first two to three weeks.
Your doctor will check on you regularly to make sure the bones are healing right.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest and sleep so your body can heal the broken bones.
Avoid all sports, running, and heavy lifting for at least a few months.
Take gentle, short walks around your home only when you feel ready.
Do not let anything hit or bump your face while you are healing.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray so the doctor can see the cracks in your facial bones.
Have a CT scan to get a detailed 3D picture of your face and bones.
Do a physical exam where the doctor gently touches your face to check for pain and movement.
Take a vision test to make sure your eyes and eye muscles are working correctly.

fracture of the hand.basic_details: A fracture of the hand means you have a broken or cracked bone in your hand due to an injury or fall. It can cause pain, swelling, and make it hard to move your fingers.
emergency_signs: Total loss of feeling in fingers
Fingers cross over each other when making a fist
precautions: Remove all rings immediately before swelling starts
things_to_avoid: Trying to pull the fingers straight
Using the hand to lift things
diet_recommendation: Eat foods rich in calcium like milk, cheese, and yogurt to help your bones heal.
Eat plenty of fruits and vegetables to give your body the vitamins it needs.
Eat foods with protein like chicken, beans, and eggs to repair your tissues.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and strong.
recovery_time: Most hand fractures take about 6 to 8 weeks to heal properly.
Severe breaks or people who need surgery might take several months to fully heal.
You might need to wear a cast or splint for the first few weeks.
Your hand might feel weak or stiff even after the bone is healed.
physical_activities: Rest your hand as much as possible in the first few weeks.
Keep your hand raised above your heart to help bring down the swelling.
Do gentle finger stretches only when your doctor tells you it is safe.
Avoid lifting heavy things or playing sports until the doctor says you are healed.
recommended_tests: An X-ray is done to see the broken bone and check how bad it is.
A doctor's physical exam to check how well you can move your fingers.
A CT scan might be done if the doctor needs a closer look at the small wrist bones.
A follow-up X-ray later on to make sure the bone is healing straight.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you cannot move your fingers

fracture of the jaw.basic_details: A fracture of the jaw is a broken jawbone, usually caused by a hard hit to the face or an accident. It can make it very hard to chew, talk, or move your mouth normally.
emergency_signs: Teeth do not line up correctly anymore
Unable to open or close the mouth
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Support the jaw gently with a bandage under the chin
Eat only liquid foods once approved by a doctor
Keep the airway clear of blood
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of smoothies and protein shakes.
Eat smooth foods like yogurt, pudding, and applesauce.
Enjoy warm, blended soups that do not need any chewing.
Use a straw if your doctor says it is okay to drink easily.
recovery_time: Most broken jaws take about six weeks to heal together.
Your jaw might stay wired or rubber-banded shut for several weeks.
You will need to visit your doctor often to check the healing.
Soft foods are usually needed for a few months after healing starts.
physical_activities: Rest as much as you can to help your body heal fast.
Do not play any sports or rough games where you might get hit.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard work that makes you clench your teeth.
Take gentle walks around the house when you feel strong enough.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray picture of your face to see the broken bone.
Have a doctor feel and touch your jaw to check for pain spots.
Get a special 3D scan if the doctor needs a better look.
Do a bite check to see if your teeth line up the right way.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you cannot open or close your mouth

fracture of the leg.basic_details: A fracture of the leg means you have a broken bone in your lower limb. It usually happens from a hard fall or an accident, causing pain and swelling.
emergency_signs: Leg is bent at an unnatural angle
Foot turns cold, pale, or blue
Extreme pain making it impossible to move
precautions: Stop any heavy bleeding with pressure
things_to_avoid: Moving the person without medical help
Removing clothing by pulling it over the broken leg
diet_recommendation: Eat foods rich in calcium like milk, cheese, and yogurt to help make your bones strong again.
Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to give your body helpful vitamins.
Include chicken, fish, or beans in your meals to help your body heal its tissues.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy while you rest.
treatment_options: put a cast on the leg
rest and keep the leg still
recovery_time: Most simple leg breaks take about six to eight weeks to heal up nicely.
If the break is very bad, it might take a few months before you feel completely normal.
Your doctor will check on you with new scans to see how well the bone is growing back together.
Everyone heals at their own speed, so try to be patient with your body.
physical_activities: Rest your leg as much as you can during the first few weeks.
Use crutches or a walker so you do not put weight on the broken bone.
Do gentle stretches with your toes and ankles if your doctor says it is okay.
Avoid running, jumping, or heavy lifting until your doctor tells you it is safe.
recommended_tests: An X-ray is usually done first to see exactly where the bone is broken.
A doctor will check how well you can move your toes and feel your skin.
Sometimes a CT scan is needed to look at the broken bone in more detail.
Blood tests might be done to check your overall health before any surgery.
when_to_visit_doctor: the toes turn blue or cold
there is numbness in the foot

fracture of the neck.basic_details: A fracture of the neck means one of the bones in your neck has broken, usually due to a bad fall or accident. It needs very careful medical attention to keep you safe and help the bone heal.
emergency_signs: Total inability to move arms or legs (paralysis)
Loss of bowel or bladder control
precautions: Hold their head and neck in the exact position you found them
things_to_avoid: Lifting them up to sit or stand
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy or calcium-rich foods to help your bones get strong again.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body the vitamins it needs to heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and working well.
Eat protein like chicken, beans, or eggs to help repair your body tissues.
recovery_time: Most people need about 6 to 12 weeks for the bone in the neck to heal.
Full recovery and getting back to normal strength can take several months.
Healing time is different for everyone and depends on how bad the break was.
Follow all your doctor's rules to make sure you heal as fast as possible.
physical_activities: Rest as much as possible in the beginning and avoid moving your neck too much.
Wear your neck brace or collar all the time if your doctor told you to.
Do gentle neck exercises only when your doctor says it is safe to start.
Do not lift anything heavy or do hard sports until your doctor says you are fully healed.
recommended_tests: An X-ray is done first to look at the bones in your neck and find the break.
A CT scan might be used to get a much clearer, 3D picture of the broken bone.
An MRI scan may be done to check if your spinal cord or nerves are okay.
Regular doctor check-ups and follow-up scans to see how well the bone is healing.
when_to_visit_doctor: severe neck pain after an injury
numbness in the arms or hands

fracture of the patella.basic_details: A fracture of the patella means you have broken your kneecap, which is the small bone that protects the front of your knee. This usually happens from a hard fall on the knee or a sudden blow during an accident.
reason: Hitting the knee on the dashboard in a car crash
precautions: Use a splint to keep the knee from bending
things_to_avoid: Trying to walk on the leg
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of foods with calcium like milk, cheese, and yogurt to help your bones heal strong.
Include foods rich in vitamin D, such as eggs and fish, so your body can use the calcium properly.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables every day to give your body the vitamins it needs to repair itself.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay healthy and help your body recover.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better and can move around more after about 6 to 8 weeks.
It can take 3 to 6 months for your knee bone to fully heal and get back to normal strength.
How fast you heal depends on your age, overall health, and how bad the break was.
You might need extra time and patience if your break required surgery to fix.
physical_activities: Rest your leg as much as possible in the first few weeks and keep it raised up on pillows.
Do gentle leg exercises or stretches only if your doctor or physical therapist tells you to.
Avoid running, jumping, or putting heavy weight on your bad knee until it is fully healed.
Use crutches, a walker, or a knee brace to help you get around safely without falling.

Have a physical exam where the doctor gently touches and checks your knee for swelling and pain.
Get an MRI scan if the doctor needs to check the muscles and tendons around your kneecap.
Have your doctor check your blood circulation and feeling in your lower leg to make sure it is safe.

fracture of the pelvis.basic_details: A fracture of the pelvis is a break or crack in the large ring of bones located near the base of your spine that connects your legs to your body. It usually happens from hard falls or car accidents and can make standing or walking very painful.
reason: Minor falls in elderly people with weak bones
emergency_signs: Severe pain in the groin or hip
Numbness or tingling in the legs

Go to physical therapy after surgery
things_to_avoid: Allowing them to try and walk
Ignoring groin pain after a bad fall
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk, cheese, and yogurt to help your bones heal.
Eat leafy green vegetables such as spinach and broccoli for extra strength.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and working well.
Eat high-fiber foods like whole grains and fresh fruit to prevent stomach issues from resting.
recovery_time: Most people need about 8 to 12 weeks for the bone to heal.
Full recovery and getting back to normal strength can take up to 6 months.
Healing time depends on how bad the break is and your overall health.
Some people might feel minor aches for up to a year after the injury.
physical_activities: Stay in bed or on the couch to rest as much as possible in the first few weeks.
Use crutches, a walker, or a wheelchair when you need to move around.
Do gentle leg and ankle wiggles in bed to keep your blood flowing.
Work with a physical therapist later on to slowly rebuild your strength and walking skills.

Have a CT scan for a more detailed 3D look at the pelvis injury.
Give blood samples to check for overall health and blood loss.
Get a bone density scan to see how strong your bones are overall.
when_to_visit_doctor: severe pain in hips or groin

fracture of the rib.basic_details: A rib fracture is a crack or break in one of the bones in your chest that protects your lungs. It usually happens from a hard fall, a sports injury, or a car crash, and it hurts a lot when you breathe or cough.
reason: Severe coughing (in people with weak bones)
emergency_signs: A section of the chest moves opposite to normal breathing (flail chest)

Hold a pillow against the chest when coughing
things_to_avoid: Wrapping the chest tightly with bandages
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk, cheese, and yogurt to make your bones stronger.
Eat green leafy vegetables like spinach and broccoli to help your bones heal faster.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and working well.
Eat foods with protein, like eggs, chicken, and beans, to repair your body.
recovery_time: Most simple rib breaks take about 6 weeks to heal completely on their own.
You might start to feel a bit better and less sore after the first 2 weeks.
Sharp pain when you move or twist can stick around for a little over a month.
Full strength in your chest area usually returns after a couple of months of rest.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest and avoid heavy lifting or hard chores while your rib heals.
Take slow, deep breaths every hour to keep your lungs clear and avoid getting sick.
Hold a pillow tightly against your chest when you need to cough to ease the pain.
Take gentle, short walks around your house to stay active without hurting your chest.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray of your chest to let the doctor see the broken or cracked rib.
Have a physical exam where the doctor gently presses on your chest to find the sore spots.
Get a CT scan if the doctor needs a more detailed picture of your chest bones.
Do a pulse check or breathing test to make sure your lungs are working well.

fracture of the shoulder.basic_details: A fracture of the shoulder happens when one of the bones in your shoulder joint cracks or breaks, usually due to a fall or a hard hit. This causes sharp pain, swelling, and makes it very hard to move your arm.
emergency_signs: Extreme pain when trying to move the arm
precautions: Support the arm in a sling
Keep the arm close to the body
things_to_avoid: Asking someone to pull it into place
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk and yogurt to help your bones heal.
Include eggs, beans, and lean meats in your meals to repair body tissue.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body strength to recover.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and strong.
recovery_time: Most shoulder breaks take about six to eight weeks for the bone to mend.
It can take several months to get all your strength and movement back.
The first two weeks are usually the hardest when the pain is highest.
Your recovery speed depends on your age and how bad the break was.
physical_activities: Rest your arm completely inside a sling during the first few weeks.
Avoid lifting heavy objects or reaching up high with the hurt arm.
Do gentle finger and wrist wiggles to keep your blood flowing well.
Follow a physical therapist's safe, easy stretches when the bone heals.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray picture taken to see the exact crack in the bone.
Have a doctor feel and move your shoulder to check the pain level.
Do a special scan like a CT scan if the doctor needs a closer look.
Check your overall health with basic blood work if surgery is needed.

fracture of the skull.basic_details: A fracture of the skull is a break or crack in the bone surrounding your brain. It happens due to a strong hit or fall on the head.

Bruising behind the ears or around the eyes (raccoon eyes)

Wear helmets for biking and sports
things_to_avoid: Applying heavy pressure to the broken bone
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your brain and body hydrated.
Choose lean meats and beans to give your muscles and bones good protein.
Avoid junk food and sugary snacks that can slow down your recovery.
recovery_time: Most minor skull cracks start feeling better within a few weeks.
Full healing of the bone can take anywhere from two to three months.
Your brain needs extra weeks of rest even after the bone is healed.
Everyone heals at their own speed, so be patient with your body.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest during the first few days after the injury.
Take slow, short walks around your house when you feel a bit stronger.
Avoid heavy lifting, running, or working out until the doctor says yes.
Stay away from contact sports and activities where you might fall again.
recommended_tests: Get a CT scan so doctors can see the exact crack in your skull.
Have an X-ray to check the general shape of your head bones.
Take neurological check-ups to make sure your brain is working normally.
Undergo blood tests if your doctor needs to check your overall health.
when_to_visit_doctor: bleeding from the ear or nose

fracture of the vertebra.basic_details: A fracture of the vertebra is when one of the bones in your backbone breaks or cracks. This can cause sudden back pain and make it hard to move normally.
reason: Osteoporosis (weak bones crushing under normal weight)
emergency_signs: Inability to move arms or legs
Loss of bowel or bladder control
Severe pain radiating down the back or legs
precautions: Keep the person completely still and flat
Eat a diet rich in calcium and vitamin D
things_to_avoid: Letting them sit up or walk
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk, cheese, and yogurt to make your bones strong.
Eat green leafy vegetables like spinach and broccoli every day.
Drink plenty of water to keep your body healthy while you rest.
Eat foods with protein like eggs, beans, and chicken to help your body heal.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better after about 6 to 8 weeks.
Full healing of the bone can take up to 3 months or sometimes longer.
Your exact healing time depends on your age and how bad the break is.
Follow all doctor visits to make sure your back is healing the right way.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest during the first few days after the injury.
Avoid heavy lifting, twisting, or bending your back too much.
Do very gentle walking around the house once your doctor says you can.
Do light stretching exercises only if a physical therapist teaches you.
recommended_tests: An X-ray to take pictures of your bones and see the break.
A bone density scan to check if your bones are weak.
An MRI scan to look closely at the bones and nearby tissues.
A CT scan to get a detailed 3D view of your broken bone.
when_to_visit_doctor: severe back pain after a fall

fungal infection of the hair.basic_details: Fungal infection of the hair is a common skin issue where tiny germs grow on your scalp and hair strands. It can make your head itchy, flaky, and sometimes cause hair to break or fall out in small patches.
reason: Contact with infected animals (like cats or dogs)
emergency_signs: Large, painful, pus-filled bumps on the scalp
Sudden permanent hair loss in patches
Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
precautions: Wash all hats, combs, and bedding in hot water
things_to_avoid: Stopping medication before the doctor says to
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body fight the germs.
Choose whole foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread for overall health.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body clean and hydrated.
Try to eat less sugary foods and sweets, because germs like sugar to grow.
common_medicines: antibiotic pills if there is swelling
treatment_options: wash hair with special medical shampoo
do not share hats or combs with others
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better and less itchy within two to three weeks.

Your hair may take a few months to grow back fully and look healthy again.

physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily exercises and light workouts.
Wash your hair and scalp well right after you sweat a lot from playing sports.
Avoid heavy swimming in public pools until your scalp is fully healed.
Try not to wear tight hats or helmets for too long while you are healing.
recommended_tests: A doctor will look closely at your scalp using a special bright light.
The doctor might gently take a few small skin flakes or hairs to check under a microscope.
A simple lab test might be done to find out the exact type of germ causing the problem.
Blood tests are rarely needed unless the doctor wants to check your overall health.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you see round bald spots on the head
if the scalp becomes red and swollen
if hair starts falling out easily
if home shampoo does not work

fungal infection of the skin.basic_details: A fungal infection of the skin is a common rash caused by tiny germs that love warm and wet places on your body. It can make your skin itchy, red, and flaky.
reason: Living in a warm, moist climate
emergency_signs: Rash rapidly spreading and turning red/hot
precautions: Change sweaty clothes immediately after exercise

Eat more fresh vegetables and fruits to keep your body strong.
Drink plenty of water every day to help flush out your system.
Include yogurt in your meals to help keep your stomach healthy.
treatment_options: Apply anti-fungal cream on clean skin
Keep the skin dry and clean
Take oral anti-fungal pills if the infection is bad
recovery_time: Most simple skin infections start getting better in one to two weeks.

Change out of your workout clothes right away after moving around.
Stay away from swimming pools until your skin is totally healed.

A skin sample can be sent to a lab to find the exact germ.
Sometimes a special glowing light is used to check the rash.
when_to_visit_doctor: If the rash does not go away after two weeks
If the skin gets very red and hurts
If pus comes out of the rash

gallstone.basic_details: Gallstones are small, hard lumps that form inside your gallbladder, a little organ that helps with digestion. They can sometimes cause sharp pain in your upper belly.

Medicines to stop nausea and vomiting
treatment_options: Surgery to take out the gallbladder
Special sound waves to break up stones
Waiting and watching if there is no pain
Eating a low-fat diet to feel better
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within one to two weeks after surgery.
You might feel tired and sore for the first few days as your body heals.

A special X-ray scan gives your doctor a clearer look at your belly area.

when_to_visit_doctor: When you have sharp pain in your upper belly
If your skin or eyes turn yellow
When you have a fever and chills
If you throw up and cannot keep food down

ganglion cyst.basic_details: A ganglion cyst is a harmless, non-cancerous lump that usually forms along the tendons or joints of your wrists or hands. It is filled with a jelly-like fluid and can sometimes change size or disappear on its own.

Cyst gets red, hot, and infected

See a doctor to have it safely drained if painful
things_to_avoid: Smashing the cyst with a heavy object
Trying to pop it with a needle at home

creams to put on the skin for pain

taking out the fluid with a needle
surgery to take the cyst out

if the lump gets very big
if it makes it hard to move your hand or wrist
if you feel numbness or tingling

gastritis.basic_details: Gastritis is when the inside lining of your stomach gets swollen and irritated. This can cause a burning pain or ache in your upper belly.

when_to_visit_doctor: If stomach pain lasts for more than a week
If you feel very sick and want to throw up
If home medicine does not help
If you lose weight without trying

gastroduodenal ulcer.basic_details: A gastroduodenal ulcer is a painful sore that forms on the inside lining of your stomach or the upper part of your small intestine. It happens when digestive juices damage the sensitive walls of your belly.

Stop drinking alcohol, coffee, and soda, as they can irritate your sore.

Avoid heavy lifting or intense belly workouts while your sore is healing.
Try gentle stretching or deep breathing exercises to help calm your mind and body.

Blood tests to check if you are low on iron or have an infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: Stomach pain does not go away
You feel very sick and want to throw up
Your belly feels very hard and hurts a lot

Pictures taken of your belly and chest using special machines.
A test to see how well your food pipe squeezes food down.
when_to_visit_doctor: When you lose weight without trying
When you have pain for a long time

Cancer or polyps in the gut

gastroparesis.basic_details: Gastroparesis is a condition where your stomach takes way too long to move food down into your intestines. This can make you feel very full, sick to your stomach, or bloated after eating just a little bit.

Take prescribed medicines to help stomach movement

Choose soft foods that are very easy for your stomach to break down.
Stay away from foods high in fat and fiber because they take too long to digest.
Drink plenty of water and other liquids throughout the day to stay hydrated.

Eat low fat and low fiber foods
Change blood sugar levels if you have diabetes
recovery_time: Gastroparesis is often a long-term condition that you manage over time rather than cure completely.

A special scan using safe tracers to see inside your throat.

when_to_visit_doctor: If you see a lump in your neck
If it is hard to swallow food
If it is hard to breathe
If your voice sounds very hoarse

gonorrhea.basic_details: Gonorrhea is a common infection you can get from having sex. It can make it hurt when you pee or cause unusual discharge, but it is very easy to cure with medicine.

Avoid sex until infection is gone
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better just a few days after taking their medicine.

gout.basic_details: Gout is a painful type of arthritis that happens when hard crystals build up in your joints. It usually makes your big toe very sore, swollen, and red.

Eating a diet high in purines (red meat, seafood)

Pain so severe that even a bedsheet touching it hurts

Eat a healthy diet with less meat

Eat fewer red meats and shellfish like shrimp and crab.
Stay away from sugary sodas and foods with high-fructose corn syrup.
Limit or completely avoid drinking alcohol, especially beer.
treatment_options: Put ice on the sore joint
Eat less red meat and seafood
recovery_time: Sudden, painful attacks usually start to get better within 3 to 10 days.

Have a doctor look at fluid taken from your sore joint using a tiny needle.
Take an X-ray to see if your bones or joints have any long-term damage.
Get an ultrasound to check for tiny crystal buildups hiding inside your joints.
when_to_visit_doctor: When your joint hurts very badly
If you get a fever with the joint pain
When home remedies do not help

graves disease.basic_details: Graves' disease is an illness where your body makes too much thyroid hormone, making your body run too fast. This can make you feel nervous, lose weight quickly, and have a fast heartbeat.

Drink lots of water to keep your body from drying out.
Limit foods and drinks with a lot of caffeine like coffee and soda.
Be careful with foods high in iodine, such as seaweed and certain salts.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better a few weeks after beginning their medicine.
It usually takes several months for your hormone levels to get back to normal.
Some treatments can take a year or more to fully finish working.
You will need regular check-ups with your doctor for the rest of your life to stay healthy.
physical_activities: Keep your workouts light and easy, like walking or gentle stretching.
Stop exercising right away if you feel dizzy, super tired, or your heart races too fast.
Avoid heavy weightlifting or hard running until your doctor says it is safe.
Try relaxing activities like yoga or deep breathing to help calm your mind and body.
recommended_tests: Get blood tests often to check the levels of your thyroid hormones.
Have your doctor check your heart rate and blood pressure during visits.
Get an eye exam if your eyes feel puffy, dry, or look like they are bulging.
Do a bone density scan to make sure your bones are strong and healthy.

guillain barre syndrome.basic_details: Guillain-Barré syndrome is a rare condition where your body's immune system accidentally attacks your nerves, making your muscles feel weak and numb.

Sudden inability to walk or stand
Weakness spreading rapidly from legs to chest

Follow all hospital treatments (like IVIG or plasma exchange)
things_to_avoid: Waiting to see if weakness goes away
Trying to walk without support if legs feel weak
Eating solid food if swallowing becomes hard
Ignoring tingling in the hands and feet
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose lean meats and beans to keep your muscles strong.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Eat soft foods if you have any trouble chewing or swallowing.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better after a few weeks or months.
The worst part of the weakness usually happens within the first two to four weeks.

Avoid heavy lifting or exhausting workouts until your doctor says it is safe.

Blood tests to rule out other possible health issues and check your overall condition.

gum disease.basic_details: Gum disease is an infection of the tissues that hold your teeth in place. It is usually caused by bad brushing habits that let sticky germs build up on your teeth.

Drink plenty of water all day long to help wash away food bits.
Stay away from very sugary snacks and candies that feed bad mouth germs.
Eat crunchy fruits and veggies like apples and carrots to help clean your teeth naturally.
recovery_time: Mild redness and swelling usually go away in one to two weeks with good brushing.
Deep cleaning recovery takes a few days to feel completely normal again.
Healing time depends on how bad the infection is when you start treatment.
Following your dentist's daily cleaning steps helps you heal much faster.
physical_activities: Keep doing your normal daily exercises like walking or jogging.
Avoid heavy workouts on the day you have deep dental cleaning done.
Relax and rest if you feel tired or run down from the infection.
Keep up your normal active lifestyle while you heal.
recommended_tests: A dentist uses a small metal tool to measure the space between your teeth and gums.
Dental x-rays are taken to check if the jawbone is staying strong.
A visual check by your dentist to look for bleeding or red spots.
A check of your overall medical history to see what might be causing gum trouble.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your gums bleed when you brush
Your gums are red and swollen
You have bad breath that does not go away

gynecomastia.basic_details: Gynecomastia is a condition where male chest tissue swells and gets bigger than normal. It usually happens because of a change in your body's natural hormones.

Cut down on soy products and processed junk food.

Surgery to remove extra breast tissue
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within a few weeks if they change their habits.

Full healing and seeing the final body shape can take up to three months.
You can usually go back to a desk job or light school work in just a few days.

head and neck cancer.basic_details: Head and neck cancer is a serious disease where bad cells grow out of control in areas like your mouth, throat, nose, or voice box.

head injury.basic_details: A head injury happens when you hit your head hard, which can hurt your brain or skull. It is important to rest and watch for danger signs after this happens.

Clear fluid draining from nose or ears

hidradenitis suppurativa.basic_details: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a long-term skin condition that causes painful, boil-like lumps in areas where your skin rubs together, like your armpits or groin.

Listen to your body and rest right away if you feel dizzy or weak.
recommended_tests: Get a simple blood test to check your total calcium levels.
Get a test to check the amount of vitamin D in your blood.
Have your kidney health checked because kidneys help control calcium.
Check your parathyroid hormone levels to see how your body manages calcium.
when_to_visit_doctor: if your muscles feel very tight
if you have numbness in your fingers
if you feel dizzy or confused
if your heart feels like it is beating too fast

hypoglycemia.basic_details: Hypoglycemia is a health condition where the sugar level in your blood drops too low. This can make you feel weak, shaky, and dizzy.
reason: Taking too much insulin or diabetes medicine
Skipping a meal while on diabetes medicine
Drinking alcohol on an empty stomach
emergency_signs: Passing out or inability to wake up
precautions: Eat 15 grams of fast-acting sugar (like juice or candy) immediately
Carry sugar or a glucagon pen at all times
things_to_avoid: Driving if you feel shaky or dizzy
diet_recommendation: Eat small meals and healthy snacks throughout the day.
Carry quick sugar fixes like hard candies or fruit juice.
Choose whole grains and protein to keep your energy steady.
Avoid eating too many sugary sweets that cause a sudden crash.
recovery_time: Most people feel better within 15 minutes after eating sugar.
Full recovery from a severe episode can take a few hours.
Resting helps your body regain normal strength and balance.
Consistent daily habits prevent ongoing recovery setbacks.
physical_activities: Do light walking or easy stretching exercises every day.
Always eat a small snack before you start working out.
Stop exercising immediately if you feel dizzy or sweaty.
Keep a friend with you when you try new outdoor workouts.
recommended_tests: Finger-prick blood sugar checks using a home test kit.
A regular blood draw at a lab to check your average sugar.
A fasting test where you do not eat for a while first.
A continuous glucose monitor worn patch-style on your skin.

hypokalemia.basic_details: Hypokalemia means you have too little potassium in your blood. This makes your body feel weak because potassium helps your muscles and nerves work right.

Heart palpitations or very irregular heartbeat
Trouble breathing due to weak chest muscles

Get regular blood tests if taking water pills

Taking potassium supplements without a doctor's order
Heavy physical exertion when feeling weak

Include sweet potatoes and regular potatoes in your meals.
Eat spinach and other green leafy veggies often.
Snack on oranges and drink orange juice to boost your levels.

Change other medicines causing low potassium
recovery_time: Mild cases can get better in just a few days with food and pills.
Severe cases might need a few weeks to feel totally normal again.
You will feel your energy come back slowly as your levels go up.
Your recovery speed depends on how low your potassium was to start with.
physical_activities: Take gentle walks instead of doing hard workouts.
Skip heavy lifting until your doctor says your body is strong enough.
Stop exercising right away if your muscles start feeling weak or shaky.
Do light stretching to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
recommended_tests: Get a simple blood test to check your current potassium level.
Do a urine test to see if your body is losing too much potassium.
Have an ECG test to make sure your heart is beating nice and steady.
Get a basic metabolic panel to check your overall body health.
when_to_visit_doctor: If your muscles feel tight or hurt
If your heart feels like it is skipping beats
If you feel very tired all the time

hyponatremia.basic_details: Hyponatremia happens when there is too much water and not enough salt in your blood. This makes your body cells swell up and can make you feel very sick.
precautions: Drink fluids with electrolytes when sick
Follow doctor's advice on water intake
things_to_avoid: Drinking gallons of plain water very quickly
diet_recommendation: Drink less plain water throughout the day.
Eat salty snacks like pretzels or crackers if your doctor says it is okay.
Choose drinks that have helpful salts and minerals in them.
Avoid eating too many watery fruits and vegetables.
treatment_options: stop taking pills that cause water loss
get salt water through a needle in the arm
recovery_time: Mild cases can get better in just a few hours after drinking less water.
More serious cases can take a few days of careful care in a hospital.
Your body needs time for your brain and blood salt levels to match again.
Recovery speed depends heavily on finding out what caused the low salt.
physical_activities: Rest in bed until your doctor says your salt levels are back to normal.
Avoid heavy workouts or playing sports that make you sweat a lot.
Take very slow, short walks around your room only if you feel steady.
Do not lift heavy objects or do hard chores until you feel completely better.
recommended_tests: A simple blood test to check how much salt is in your body.
A urine test to see how much water and salt your kidneys are pushing out.
A basic check of your weight to watch for sudden changes in body water.
A blood pressure check to make sure your heart and blood are doing okay.
when_to_visit_doctor: you feel very tired all the time
you feel sick to your stomach

hypothyroidism.basic_details: Hypothyroidism happens when your neck makes too little of a special chemical that gives you energy. This makes your body slow down, and you might feel very tired and cold all the time.
reason: Lack of iodine in the diet
emergency_signs: Inability to stay awake or severe confusion
things_to_avoid: Stopping pills because you feel better
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables every day.
Choose whole grain breads and brown rice instead of white flour products.
Drink lots of water to help your body stay hydrated and work better.
Try not to eat too much junk food, sugar, and heavy oily meals.
recovery_time: This condition does not go away completely, so you will likely need medicine for life.
Most people start feeling much better and have more energy within a few weeks.
Your doctor will check your blood every few months to make sure your dose is right.

physical_activities: Go for gentle daily walks outside to keep your body moving and happy.
Try easy stretching or slow yoga to help loosen up stiff muscles.
Do light gardening or housework to stay active without getting too tired.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel low on energy.
recommended_tests: Get a simple routine blood test to check how well your neck gland is working.
Ask your doctor to check your blood sugar and iron levels just to be safe.
Have your doctor check your body weight and heart rate during checkups.
Repeat your main hormone blood test every few months as told by your doctor.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel very tired all the time
You gain weight for no clear reason
You feel cold when others do not
Your medicine dose needs a check

hypovolemia.basic_details: Hypovolemia means your body has lost too much water and blood. This makes it hard for your heart to pump enough blood to keep you healthy.
reason: Not drinking enough water for days
emergency_signs: Heart beating very fast but weakly
Skin turning cold, pale, and sweaty
precautions: Stop any visible bleeding with heavy pressure
Lay the person flat and raise their legs
Drink fluids if conscious and able to swallow
things_to_avoid: Waiting to see if they feel better
Giving fluids to someone who is unconscious

Eat salty snacks like pretzels or crackers to help your body hold onto water.
Drink sports drinks that have extra salts and minerals in them.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables that have a lot of water inside them, like watermelon.
treatment_options: Eating salty foods if told by a doctor
Treating the cause of blood or fluid loss

You may need a blood test to check your salt levels and overall blood health.
A urine test can show the doctor how much water is currently inside your body.
Doctors might use a special scan of your heart or belly to check your blood flow.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you feel very dizzy or confused
If you have extreme thirst and dry mouth
If you cannot keep any liquids down

idiopathic absence of menstruation.basic_details: Idiopathic absence of menstruation means your period stops for a long time, and doctors are not completely sure why it is happening.

precautions: Keep track of your periods on a calendar
See a gynecologist for a checkup
things_to_avoid: Over-exercising to the point of exhaustion

Include healthy fats like nuts, seeds, and olive oil in your meals.
Drink enough water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Make sure you get enough iron and calcium through your food or safe snacks.
recovery_time: Recovery is different for everyone and depends on the root cause.
It can take a few weeks or even several months to get your period back.
Being patient with your body is very important during this healing process.
Regular checkups help track your progress and see if treatments are working.
physical_activities: Do light exercises like walking, gentle yoga, or swimming.
Avoid doing too much heavy or intense workouts that stress your body.
Keep moving daily to help your body stay healthy and balanced.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel too tired.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check your hormone levels and overall health.
A pregnancy test just to make sure that is not the reason.
An ultrasound of your tummy to look at your reproductive organs.
Thyroid tests to see if your thyroid gland is working properly.
when_to_visit_doctor: periods stop for more than three months
you have very bad belly pain

Severe shortness of breath from blood loss

Take prescribed medicines to reduce bleeding
things_to_avoid: Heavy physical workouts during heavy flow

Your doctor might do an ultrasound to look at your womb.
A hormone blood test can check if your body chemicals are balanced.
Your doctor may ask you to track your period days on a calendar.
when_to_visit_doctor: Soaking through one or more pads every hour
Bleeding lasting longer than seven days

idiopathic infrequent menstruation.basic_details: Idiopathic infrequent menstruation means your monthly period happens much less often than normal, and doctors do not know the exact reason why.

things_to_avoid: Panic (it can be normal for some)
Ignoring other symptoms like hair loss

Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated throughout the day.
Try to eat less junk food and sugary snacks.

A pregnancy test to make sure that is not the cause.
A general health checkup to review your overall medical history.

idiopathic painful menstruation.basic_details: Idiopathic painful menstruation is a common condition where women experience strong, painful cramps in their lower belly during their monthly period without any clear underlying illness.

stopping medicines that slow down the gut

you cannot pass gas or poop
your belly looks very big and swollen
