if you have belly pain that does not go away
if you feel very weak and dizzy

intestinal obstruction.basic_details: Intestinal obstruction happens when your food, liquid, and gas get stuck and cannot pass through your belly normally. This can cause very bad belly pain, swelling, and throwing up.
reason: Scar tissue from previous stomach surgeries
emergency_signs: Severe, crampy belly pain that comes and goes
Inability to poop or pass gas
Vomiting, especially if it smells like stool
Belly becomes completely hard and swollen
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Stop eating or drinking until seen by a doctor
Follow all surgery or treatment advice
things_to_avoid: Taking laxatives to force it out (can burst the bowel)
Eating or drinking to push it down
Taking pain pills and waiting at home
diet_recommendation: Drink only clear liquids like water and broth when your doctor says it is okay.
Eat soft foods that are very easy for your tummy to break down.
Stay away from heavy, greasy, or spicy foods that can upset your stomach.
Eat small meals spread out through the day instead of big heavy meals.
treatment_options: Not eating or drinking to rest the gut
Putting a small tube through the nose to the stomach
Using a small scope to open the blockage
Surgery to fix the blocked part
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better after a few days in the hospital.
It can take a few weeks to get your full strength back at home.
Rest as much as you can so your belly can heal the right way.
Listen to your body and slow down if you start to feel tired.
physical_activities: Take very short and slow walks around your room to help your belly wake up.
Avoid lifting heavy things or doing hard workouts for several weeks.
Do not push your body too hard until a doctor says you are fully healed.
Get plenty of rest in your bed or on the couch while you heal.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray of your belly so doctors can see where the blockage is.
Have a CT scan to take clear pictures inside your stomach area.
Give blood samples so the doctor can check how your body is doing.
Let the doctor gently press and feel your belly to check for soreness.
when_to_visit_doctor: Severe belly pain that will not go away
Throwing up and you cannot keep food down
Big belly swelling or feeling very hard
Not passing gas or poop for a long time

intracerebral hemorrhage.basic_details: Intracerebral hemorrhage happens when a blood vessel inside the brain bursts and causes bleeding. This puts pressure on the brain and can damage brain cells.
emergency_signs: Sudden weakness or paralysis on one side of the body
precautions: Keep the person still and calm
things_to_avoid: Waiting to see if they get better
Giving the person aspirin (makes bleeding worse)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose foods low in salt to help keep your blood pressure down.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Stay away from greasy, fried, and very fatty foods.
recovery_time: The first few weeks in the hospital are for the most critical healing.
Many people see big improvements over the first three to six months.
Some healing and rebuilding can continue for a year or even longer.
Every person heals at their own speed, so try not to rush.
physical_activities: Start with very gentle movements in bed, like moving your fingers and toes.
Move up to short, slow walks around the room with help.
Work with a physical therapist to safely build back your strength.
Rest often and stop right away if you feel dizzy or very tired.
recommended_tests: CT scans to take quick pictures of your brain and check the bleeding.
MRI scans to get a more detailed look at the inside of your brain.
Regular checks of your blood pressure to make sure it stays normal.
Blood tests to check your overall health and how your body works.
when_to_visit_doctor: sudden weakness on one side of the body
sudden loss of balance or fainting

intracranial hemorrhage.basic_details: An intracranial hemorrhage is when a blood vessel inside the head bursts and bleeds into or around the brain. This can put pressure on the brain and needs quick medical help.
reason: Head trauma (like car accidents or falls)
emergency_signs: Sudden worst headache of your life
Unequal pupil sizes in the eyes
precautions: Keep the head slightly elevated if possible
things_to_avoid: Giving pain medication like aspirin or ibuprofen
Shaking the person to wake them up
Allowing the person to go to sleep if they had a bad fall
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose foods low in salt to help keep your blood pressure steady.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Avoid sugary drinks and processed snacks.
recovery_time: Healing takes a long time, often many months or even years.
The first few weeks in the hospital are crucial for heavy rest.
Every person heals at their own speed depending on the bleed size.
Long-term therapy may be needed to regain strength and speech.
physical_activities: Get complete bed rest during the early stages of healing.
Do very light movements only when the doctor says it is safe.
Work with a physical therapist to slowly practice walking.
Avoid heavy lifting, running, or hard exercise for many months.
recommended_tests: A CT scan of the head to take pictures of the brain.
An MRI scan to get a closer look at the injury.
Regular checks of your blood pressure and heart rate.
Blood tests to check how well your blood clots.

iridocyclitis.basic_details: Iridocyclitis is a condition where the colored part inside your eye gets swollen and hurts. It can make your eyes very sensitive to bright light and make your vision blurry.
emergency_signs: Extreme pain when looking at bright lights
precautions: Take prescribed steroid eye drops exactly as told
Wear dark sunglasses to help with light pain
things_to_avoid: Stopping eye drops before the doctor says
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy.
Choose healthy foods like fish and nuts that help fight swelling.
Try to eat less fast food and sugary snacks while you are healing.
common_medicines: Eye drops that stop pain and swelling
Steroid eye drops to reduce inflammation
Pills to lower eye pressure if needed
Antibiotics if infection is the cause
treatment_options: Using prescribed medicated eye drops daily
Wearing dark glasses to help with bright light
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within a few days of starting treatment.
Complete healing usually takes a few weeks, depending on the person.
Your vision might stay a bit blurry for a short while after the pain goes away.
Go to all your follow-up eye doctor visits to make sure it is fully gone.
physical_activities: Rest your eyes as much as you can during the first few days.
Stay away from heavy lifting or hard sports until your eye is healed.
Wear good sunglasses outside to protect your sore eyes from bright sunlight.
Take frequent breaks from looking at phones, computers, and TV screens.
recommended_tests: Have an eye doctor look closely inside your eye with a special bright light.
Take a simple blood test if the doctor thinks an illness caused the swelling.
Get your eye pressure checked to make sure it is safe.
Answer questions about your overall health to help find the root cause.
when_to_visit_doctor: If your eye becomes very red
If you feel severe eye pain
If bright light hurts your eyes

iron deficiency anemia.basic_details: Iron deficiency anemia is a very common condition where your body lacks enough iron. Without enough iron, your body cannot make enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen to your organs, making you feel very tired and weak.
precautions: Eat red meat, beans, and leafy greens
Take prescribed iron pills with vitamin C (like orange juice)
Find and treat the source of bleeding
things_to_avoid: Taking iron pills with milk, tea, or coffee (blocks absorption)
Taking iron supplements without a doctor's advice
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of red meat, chicken, and fish because they have iron your body easily uses.
Eat leafy green vegetables like spinach and kale to help boost your iron levels.
Eat foods with vitamin C, like oranges and bell peppers, to help your body soak up more iron.
Avoid drinking tea or coffee right after your meals because they can stop your body from taking in iron.
treatment_options: Treat the cause of blood loss
recovery_time: You might start feeling a little bit better and less tired after about two weeks of taking iron pills.
It usually takes around two months for your body to build its iron levels back up to normal.
You may need to keep taking your iron supplements for several months to make sure the iron stays full.
Your total recovery time depends on how low your iron was when you started treatment.
physical_activities: Keep doing light walks to stay active without pushing your body too hard.
Stop and rest immediately if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or overly tired.
Avoid heavy workouts and intense sports until your energy levels come back up.
Listen to your body and slowly do more exercise only as you start feeling stronger.
recommended_tests: Get a complete blood count test to check the number and health of your red blood cells.
Ask for a ferritin blood test to see how much iron your body has stored away.
Take a serum iron test to check the current amount of iron floating in your blood.
Get a test to check your hemoglobin levels, which show how well oxygen moves through your body.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel very tired all the time
Iron pills do not make you feel better

irritable bowel syndrome.basic_details: Irritable bowel syndrome is a common gut problem that causes belly pain, bloating, and changes in how often you use the bathroom. It is a long-term condition, but you can manage it well with diet and lifestyle changes.
reason: Overly sensitive nerves in the gut
emergency_signs: Severe, sharp belly pain with high fever (not normal for IBS)
Large amounts of blood in the stool
precautions: Eat a diet high in fiber (or follow a low-FODMAP diet)
Take prescribed medicines for diarrhea or constipation
things_to_avoid: Eating known trigger foods (like dairy, beans, or artificial sweeteners)
Drinking too much coffee or alcohol
diet_recommendation: Eat smaller meals more often instead of three big meals.
Drink plenty of water every single day to help your digestion.
Stay away from spicy, greasy, or fast foods that upset your stomach.
Eat more fiber slowly, like oats and fresh vegetables, to keep your tummy happy.
recovery_time: This is a lifelong condition, so there is no quick cure or final end date.
Most people start to feel much better within a few weeks of changing their diet.
Good and bad days will happen, and symptoms can come and go over time.
Finding the right treatment plan takes a little patience and time.
physical_activities: Go for a nice, easy walk every day to help your digestion work smoothly.
Try gentle yoga stretches to help release gas and tummy pain.
Do light swimming or cycling to stay active without stressing your body.
Practice deep breathing exercises to help lower your stress and calm your gut.
recommended_tests: A physical check-up where the doctor gently presses on your belly.
Blood tests to make sure you do not have other health issues.
Stool tests to check for germs or signs of inflammation in your gut.
A food diary test where you write down what you eat to spot trigger foods.
when_to_visit_doctor: You see blood in your stool

ischemia of the bowel.basic_details: Bowel ischemia happens when your intestines do not get enough blood flow. This lack of blood can damage your gut tissue and cause severe tummy pain.
reason: Blood clot blocking a gut artery
emergency_signs: Sudden, severe belly pain that feels out of proportion to how the belly looks
High fever and a hard belly
precautions: Seek emergency surgery or hospital care immediately
Take blood thinners if prescribed for heart issues
things_to_avoid: Taking pain pills and waiting at home
Eating heavy meals if you have chronic pain after eating
diet_recommendation: Eat very small meals throughout the day instead of three large ones.
Choose soft, blended foods that are very easy for your gut to digest.
Stay away from high-fiber foods like raw vegetables, nuts, and whole grains for now.
Drink plenty of water and clear liquids to keep your body hydrated.
treatment_options: surgery to fix blocked blood pipes
putting a tube to open blood pipes
recovery_time: Healing takes time and depends entirely on how badly your gut was hurt.
Mild cases treated quickly may start to feel better in just a few weeks.
If you had surgery to fix the blood flow, it could take a few months to fully recover.
Listen to your body and rest as much as possible while you heal.
physical_activities: Start with slow, gentle walks around your house to keep your blood moving.
Avoid heavy lifting, running, or hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Rest often during the day if you feel tired or weak.
Slowly add a little more walking each day as your strength comes back.
recommended_tests: A special X-ray using dye to look at the blood vessels in your belly.
A CT scan to take clear pictures of your intestines and blood flow.
Blood tests to check for signs of infection or inflammation in your body.
A scope test where a tiny camera looks inside your digestive tract.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have very bad belly pain
if your belly hurts right after eating
if you throw up and feel sick
if you have blood in your poop

ischemic heart disease.basic_details: Ischemic heart disease happens when the blood tubes that feed your heart get too narrow, so your heart does not get enough blood and oxygen.
emergency_signs: Pain spreading to the arm, neck, or jaw
precautions: Exercise moderately as approved by a doctor
things_to_avoid: Eating high-fat, fast, or fried foods
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole wheat bread and brown rice instead of white bread and white rice.
Cut down on greasy, fried, and fast foods.
Use less salt in your food to keep your blood pressure healthy.
recovery_time: Recovery is a lifelong journey of making healthy daily choices.
Most people start feeling better and stronger within a few weeks of changing their habits.
Healing after a heart procedure can take a few weeks to a couple of months.
It takes time for your heart to adjust, so you must be patient with your body.
physical_activities: Go for a short, gentle walk every day.
Do light stretching in the morning to keep your body moving.
Avoid heavy lifting or very hard workouts unless your doctor says it is okay.
Stop and rest immediately if you feel tired, dizzy, or get chest pain.
recommended_tests: An ECG test to check the electrical rhythm and beats of your heart.
A stress test to see how your heart handles physical work.
Blood tests to check your sugar and cholesterol levels.
An ultrasound picture of your heart to see how well it is pumping blood.

itching of unknown cause.basic_details: Itching of unknown cause means your skin feels very itchy all over, but doctors cannot easily find a clear reason why. It can make you feel uncomfortable and want to scratch a lot.
emergency_signs: Severe rash spreading over the whole body
precautions: Moisturize skin daily with thick creams
See a doctor for blood tests to check liver/kidneys
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your skin from getting too dry.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay healthy.
Try to eat less spicy food, as it might make your skin feel more warm and itchy.
Cut back on sugary drinks and snacks to help your body feel better overall.
recovery_time: Some people feel better in just a few days with simple skin creams.
If the itching is stubborn, it might take a few weeks to go away completely.
Healing time is different for everyone, depending on what is triggering it.
See a doctor if the itching does not get better after trying home care for two weeks.
physical_activities: Do light exercises like walking to stay active without sweating too much.
Wear loose and soft cotton clothes so your skin does not get rubbed the wrong way.
Avoid heavy workouts that make you sweat a lot, as sweat can make itching worse.
Take short and gentle walks instead of running hard outdoors.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check if your body is fighting any hidden sickness.
Skin checks to make sure you do not have tiny bugs or a rash.
Allergy tests to see if something you touch or eat is bothering your skin.
Liver and kidney function tests to make sure your inner organs are working well.
when_to_visit_doctor: If itching lasts more than two weeks
If it keeps you awake at night
If you also get a fever or lose weight
If home treatments do not work

jaw disorder.basic_details: A jaw disorder is a problem with the muscles or joints in your jaw that makes it hurt or hard to move when you chew or talk.
reason: Clenching the jaw due to stress
emergency_signs: Jaw gets completely locked open or closed
Severe pain preventing eating or drinking
Swelling of the face with a high fever
Sudden change in how the teeth fit together
precautions: Wear a night guard if you grind your teeth
Apply warm or cold packs to the jaw
things_to_avoid: Opening the mouth very wide (like a huge yawn)
Resting your chin on your hand
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and soup
Cut your food into very small pieces before eating
Avoid chewing gum and hard or crunchy snacks
Take small bites and chew slowly on both sides
recovery_time: Mild cases often get better in a few weeks with rest
Giving your jaw a break helps speed up healing
Severe pain might take a few months to fully go away
Some people need ongoing care if the pain comes back
physical_activities: Do gentle jaw stretching exercises recommended by a doctor
Put a warm cloth on your face to loosen tight muscles
Use a cold pack to bring down any sudden swelling
Try light neck and shoulder stretches to relax your upper body
recommended_tests: A physical check where the doctor feels your jaw as you open it
Dental x-rays to look at your teeth and jaw bone
An MRI scan to check the soft parts inside the jaw joint
A bite test to see how your teeth fit together
when_to_visit_doctor: hard to open or close the mouth
hearing clicking or popping with severe pain

joint effusion.basic_details: Joint effusion happens when too much fluid builds up inside or around a joint, like your knee. This makes the area swollen, puffy, and sometimes hard to move.
emergency_signs: Joint becomes extremely red and hot
Complete inability to move or put weight on the joint
precautions: Apply ice packs to reduce swelling
See a doctor to have the fluid drained and tested
things_to_avoid: Pushing through the pain during exercise
Applying heat to a newly swollen joint
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink plenty of water every single day to stay hydrated.
Eat healthy fats like fish and nuts to calm down swelling.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and processed fast foods.
treatment_options: Wrap the joint with an elastic bandage
recovery_time: Mild swelling usually goes away in just a few days with rest.
If the fluid buildup is caused by a minor injury, expect a couple of weeks to heal.
Severe cases or problems from arthritis can take several weeks or months to get better.
Your total healing time depends a lot on following your doctor's advice.
physical_activities: Rest the sore joint and avoid heavy lifting or running.
Do gentle stretches very slowly to keep your joint from getting stiff.
Try swimming or water walking since water takes pressure off your joints.
Stop moving right away if you feel sharp pain or extra soreness.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray to let the doctor see the bones inside your joint.
Have a doctor physically press and feel the joint to check the swelling.
Do an MRI scan if the doctor needs a very clear picture of the inside parts.
Get a small fluid sample taken with a tiny needle to check for infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: The skin over the joint is red and hot

juvenile rheumatoid arthritis.basic_details: Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis is a condition where a child's body gets confused and makes their joints swollen, stiff, and painful. It usually starts before the age of 16.
reason: Autoimmune system attacking healthy joints in children
emergency_signs: Red, painful eyes (can cause blindness if ignored)
precautions: Go to all eye doctor appointments (crucial to check for eye swelling)
Do physical therapy to keep joints moving
things_to_avoid: Pushing the child to do high-impact sports if in pain
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose fish, nuts, and healthy oils because they help calm down swelling in your body.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your joints moving smoothly.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and fast food, as they can make your body feel worse.
treatment_options: Taking medicine to stop pain and swelling
Using heat or ice on sore joints
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition, meaning it comes and goes over several years.
Many children have times where they feel great and have no pain at all.
With the right medicine and care, most kids can do normal daily things.
Some teenagers outgrow the condition completely as they become adults.
physical_activities: Go swimming because the water holds your weight and is very easy on sore joints.
Take gentle walks every day to keep your legs and feet from getting stiff.
Do fun stretching exercises to help your arms and legs move easily.
Stop and rest right away if a joint starts to hurt while you are playing.
recommended_tests: Get blood tests so the doctor can check what is making your body swell.
Have special pictures, like X-rays, taken to look inside your sore joints.
Let the doctor gently bend and press your joints to see where it hurts.
Visit the eye doctor regularly because this condition can sometimes affect your eyes.
when_to_visit_doctor: When joints stay swollen for a long time
When a child has a high fever with a rash
When joint pain stops normal walking
When eye redness or pain happens

kidney cancer.basic_details: Kidney cancer happens when bad cells grow out of control inside one or both of your kidneys. Your kidneys are body parts that clean your blood and make pee.
emergency_signs: Large amount of blood in the urine
Severe, sudden pain in the side or back
precautions: Attend all cancer treatment and scan appointments
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every single day to help flush your body.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body strong.
Eat less salt and salty foods to help protect your kidneys.
Choose healthy proteins like chicken and fish instead of heavy red meat.
treatment_options: Surgery to remove the tumor or kidney
Immunotherapy to boost the body defense
recovery_time: Rest a lot at home during the first few weeks after your treatment.
Expect healing to take several months, as every person heals at their own speed.
Go to all your follow-up checkups so the doctor can watch your healing.
Ask family or friends for help with heavy chores while you get your strength back.
physical_activities: Take slow, short walks around your house or yard to stay gently active.
Do not lift anything heavy until your doctor says it is safe.
Stop moving and rest right away if you feel tired or dizzy.
Slowly add more light movement as your body starts to feel better.
recommended_tests: Get blood tests so the doctor can check how well your organs are working.
Get urine tests to check your pee for any signs of trouble.
Have picture scans like CT scans so doctors can look inside your body.
Have checkups where the doctor gently presses on your belly to feel things.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you see blood in your urine
If you have pain in your side or lower back that does not go away
If you have a lump in your side or belly
If you lose weight without trying

kidney failure.basic_details: Kidney failure happens when your kidneys stop working well enough to clean your blood and remove extra water from your body. This causes harmful waste to build up and makes you feel very sick.
reason: Taking too many pain pills like ibuprofen over years
emergency_signs: Extreme swelling in the legs, face, or belly
precautions: Follow a strict kidney-friendly diet (low potassium/phosphorus)
Attend all dialysis appointments if prescribed
Control blood sugar and blood pressure tightly
Weigh yourself daily to check for fluid buildup
things_to_avoid: Drinking too much fluid (follow doctor's limits)
diet_recommendation: Eat less salt to help keep your blood pressure down and stop swelling.
Cut back on foods like bananas, oranges, and potatoes that are high in potassium.
Eat smaller amounts of meat and dairy to avoid overloading your body with protein waste.
Drink only the amount of water or liquids your doctor says is safe for you.
recovery_time: Kidney failure is usually a long-term condition that does not simply go away in a few weeks.
Some people with sudden failure can get better with quick hospital care.
Most people need ongoing treatments like dialysis for the rest of their lives.
Getting a new kidney through a transplant is a way some people fully recover.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks around your house or neighborhood when you feel up to it.
Do light stretching to keep your muscles loose without getting too tired.
Stop exercising right away if you feel dizzy, sick, or short of breath.
Always talk to your doctor before starting any new type of workout.
recommended_tests: Get regular blood tests to check how much waste is building up in your body.
Give urine samples so doctors can check how your kidneys are filtering.
Have your blood pressure checked often to make sure your heart is okay.
Get pictures taken of your kidneys, like an ultrasound, to look at their size and shape.

kidney stone.basic_details: A kidney stone is a hard lump that forms inside your kidneys from waste products in your blood. It can cause sharp pain in your back and side when it tries to move out.
reason: Diet high in salt and protein
emergency_signs: Severe, unbearable pain in the back or side
Pain that spreads to the groin
High fever and chills (signs of infection)
Vomiting constantly and unable to keep fluids down
precautions: Drink lots of water every day to flush the kidneys
Take prescribed medicines to help the stone pass or manage pain
Limit salt and animal protein in your diet
Strain your urine to catch the stone for testing
things_to_avoid: Drinking dark sodas or lots of tea/coffee
Ignoring a fever with back pain
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of plain water every single day to help flush the stone out.
Eat less salt because too much salt makes stones form faster.
Enjoy fresh lemon juice in water as it helps stop stones from growing.
Eat moderate amounts of calcium-rich foods like milk and yogurt.
treatment_options: Shock wave therapy to break stone
recovery_time: Tiny stones usually pass out on their own within one to three weeks.
If you need a simple sound wave treatment, you will feel better in a few days.
Recovery after minor surgery to remove a big stone takes about one week.
You might feel tired for a few days after passing a stone as your body rests.
physical_activities: Go for light walks to help shake the stone down and out of your body.
Jump gently up and down in place if you feel able to do so.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense gym workouts until the stone is fully gone.
Rest in bed when the pain is too sharp and strong.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray of your tummy to let the doctor see where the stone is hiding.
Give a urine sample so the lab can check for blood or infection.
Do a blood test to see how well your kidneys are working today.
Have a CT scan if doctors need a very clear picture of the stone's size.

knee ligament or meniscus tear.basic_details: A knee ligament or meniscus tear is an injury to the tough bands of tissue or rubbery cushion inside your knee. It usually happens from a sudden twist or hard hit, causing pain, swelling, and trouble moving the leg.
emergency_signs: Hearing a loud 'pop' followed by extreme pain
Knee suddenly giving out or collapsing
Knee locks and cannot be straightened
precautions: Rest and keep weight off the knee
Apply ice and wrap it with a bandage
See a doctor for an MRI or surgery consult
things_to_avoid: Playing sports on an injured knee
Applying heat right after the injury
Ignoring a knee that keeps buckling
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Include foods like chicken, fish, and beans to help repair your tissues.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your joints healthy.
Eat foods with healthy fats, like nuts and olive oil, to lower swelling.
common_medicines: Naproxen to help with knee pain
Doctor-prescribed pain medicine if pain is very bad
treatment_options: Rest the knee and stop doing hard activities
Put ice on the knee to bring down swelling
Physical therapy to make the knee strong again
Surgery to fix the torn part
recovery_time: Minor tears might start feeling better in just a few weeks.
If you need surgery to fix the tear, healing can take up to six months.
Resting the knee properly helps speed up how fast you get better.
Everyone heals at their own speed, so do not rush the process.
physical_activities: Rest your leg and avoid running or jumping while it heals.
Do gentle stretches and movements recommended by a physical therapist.
Try low-impact exercises like swimming once your doctor says it is okay.
Use crutches if walking puts too much weight and pain on the knee.
recommended_tests: A doctor will physically bend and push your leg to check where it hurts.
An MRI scan takes detailed pictures of the inside of your knee to see the tear.
An X-ray might be done to make sure no bones are broken.
Sometimes a special fluid test is done if the knee is very swollen.
when_to_visit_doctor: You heard a loud pop when the knee got hurt
Your knee feels loose or like it will give out
You cannot put any weight on your leg
Pain and swelling do not get better after a few days

labyrinthitis.basic_details: Labyrinthitis is an inner ear problem that makes you feel like the room is spinning. It usually happens when a common cold or flu virus travels to your ear.
emergency_signs: Severe dizziness and vomiting preventing standing
Sudden double vision or weakness in the face
precautions: Rest in a dark, quiet room
Take prescribed anti-dizziness or antibiotic medicines
Drink fluids to prevent dehydration from vomiting
things_to_avoid: Bright lights or reading, which can worsen dizziness
Walking without support if feeling dizzy
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body from drying out.
Eat small and light meals so you do not upset your stomach.
Cut back on salty foods because salt can make dizziness worse.
Avoid drinks with caffeine and alcohol as they can harm your balance.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better after one to three weeks.
Some mild dizziness can come and go for a few months.
Resting a lot in the first few days speeds up your healing.
Your body slowly learns to adjust to the inner ear balance problem.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and rest quietly when the spinning is at its worst.
Stand up slowly from your bed or chair to avoid sudden falls.
Do gentle head and eye exercises given by a doctor to retrain balance.
Avoid heavy lifting, running, or quick movements until you are healed.
recommended_tests: Have a doctor look inside your ears with a small lighted tool.
Follow a doctor's finger with your eyes to check how your brain works.
Walk in a straight line to see how well your balance is working.
Get a hearing test to make sure your inner ear is healthy.

lactose intolerance.basic_details: Lactose intolerance is a common tummy issue where your body has trouble breaking down the sugar found in milk and dairy products. This can lead to uncomfortable bloating, gas, and stomach pain after eating them.
reason: Body stops making the enzyme to digest milk sugar (lactase)
emergency_signs: Extreme, sharp belly pain (not just gas)
precautions: Avoid milk, cheese, and ice cream
Use lactase enzyme pills before eating dairy
Ensure you get enough calcium from other foods
things_to_avoid: Drinking large glasses of regular milk
Ignoring hidden dairy in processed foods
diet_recommendation: Choose milk and yogurt that are labeled lactose-free.
Eat plant-based milks like almond, soy, or oat milk instead of regular milk.
Try hard cheeses like cheddar, which usually have very little lactose.
Eat smaller portions of dairy at a time to see how your body feels.
treatment_options: Eat small amounts of dairy with meals
Take lactase pills before eating dairy
recovery_time: Your tummy usually starts feeling better within a few hours after eating dairy.
Gas and bloating often go away completely in less than a day.
It can take a couple of weeks of avoiding dairy to get your stomach fully back to normal.
Everyone reacts differently, so healing time depends on how much dairy you ate.
physical_activities: Go for a light, gentle walk after eating to help your stomach digest food better.
Do easy yoga stretches to help push out trapped gas and ease tummy cramps.
Stay active every day with fun exercises you enjoy, like swimming or biking.
Take a break from working out if your stomach hurts badly until you feel better.
recommended_tests: Take the breath test where you drink a sweet liquid and blow into a bag over time.
Try cutting out all dairy for two weeks to see if your symptoms go away on their own.
Ask your doctor for a blood test to check how your body reacts to sugar.
Keep a daily food diary to write down what you eat and when your stomach hurts.
when_to_visit_doctor: You have very bad belly pain
You see blood in your poop
Your diet changes do not help your stomach

laryngitis.basic_details: Laryngitis is when your voice box gets swollen and irritated, usually making your voice sound very hoarse or whispery.
reason: Yelling, singing, or talking too much
emergency_signs: Trouble breathing or noisy, high-pitched breathing
precautions: Rest your voice completely (do not even whisper)
Use a humidifier in your room
Treat acid reflux if that is the cause
things_to_avoid: Whispering (it strains the vocal cords more than talking)
Drinking alcohol or caffeine (they dry the throat)
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of warm water throughout the day to keep your throat wet.
Eat warm soups and soft foods that are easy to swallow.
Stay away from spicy foods that can burn your throat.
Avoid drinks with caffeine and alcohol because they dry you out.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within three to seven days.
Resting your voice completely helps you heal much faster.
If you keep talking too much, it might take a couple of weeks to get better.
See a doctor if your hoarseness lasts longer than two weeks.
physical_activities: Get plenty of physical rest so your body can fight off the illness.
Avoid heavy workouts or lifting heavy things while you feel sick.
Go for short, gentle walks around your house if you feel up to it.
Do not strain your body with high-energy sports until your voice is back.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually just listen to your voice and ask about your symptoms.
A small lighted tool might be used to look down your throat.
You might need a swab test if the doctor thinks you have an infection.
Most cases do not need any special lab tests or x-rays.
when_to_visit_doctor: you cannot speak for more than a few days
you have a very high fever

lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow).basic_details: Tennis elbow is a painful condition where the tendons in your arm are overworked, usually from repeating the same wrist or arm motions.
reason: Using plumbing, painting, or carpentry tools frequently
emergency_signs: Sudden inability to move the arm or wrist
Elbow becomes extremely red, hot, and swollen
Loss of feeling in the hand
precautions: Rest the arm from the activity causing pain
Wear a special elbow brace or strap
Apply ice to the outside of the elbow
things_to_avoid: Heavy lifting with the palm facing down
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Include foods like fish and nuts that help lower body swelling.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to keep your muscles and joints happy.
Try to cut down on sugary snacks and processed foods which can make swelling worse.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within a few weeks to a couple of months.
Severe cases can sometimes take six months to heal completely.
Giving your arm enough rest is the fastest way to get back to normal.
Trying to rush back into heavy tasks will only make the healing take longer.
physical_activities: Rest your arm and stop doing the exact movement that caused the pain.
Do gentle stretching exercises for your wrist and arm every single day.
Slowly build up arm strength using very light weights once the sharp pain stops.
Wear a supportive elbow brace when you finally start using your arm again.
recommended_tests: A simple physical check where the doctor presses on your elbow to find the pain.
Moving your wrist and arm in different directions to test your strength.
An X-ray to make sure there are no other bone problems in your arm.
An ultrasound or MRI scan to look closely at the damaged tendon if needed.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain does not go away with rest

lewy body dementia.basic_details: Lewy body dementia is a brain disease that causes problems with thinking, moving, and seeing things that are not there. It makes it hard for a person to do everyday tasks on their own.
reason: Abnormal protein buildup in the brain
emergency_signs: Severe sudden confusion or complete unresponsiveness
Severe falls leading to head injury
precautions: Keep a safe, structured home environment
Be aware of vivid hallucinations (a common symptom)
things_to_avoid: Taking certain antipsychotic medicines (they can be highly toxic for this disease)
Arguing with the person about their hallucinations
Leaving them alone in risky areas
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of soft foods if chewing becomes hard.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to avoid getting dizzy.
Eat small meals often so you do not feel too full.
Enjoy healthy foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition that does not go away.
Good care can help manage symptoms for many years.
Some days will feel better than other days.
Progress happens slowly, step by step, with support.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks every day.
Do simple stretching to keep the body loose.
Dance slowly to your favorite music at home.
Practice easy balance exercises while holding onto a chair.
recommended_tests: Memory and puzzle games with a doctor to check thinking.
Brain pictures like an MRI to look inside the head.
Heart checks to see how your body handles standing up.
Talking with a doctor about daily habits and sleep.
when_to_visit_doctor: seeing things that are not there

lice.basic_details: Lice are tiny bugs that live in human hair and feed on small amounts of blood from the scalp. They make your head feel very itchy and are easily spread from person to person.
reason: Head-to-head contact with an infected person
Sharing hats, brushes, or hair accessories
Common in crowded places like schools
emergency_signs: Severe skin infection on the scalp with pus
Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
precautions: Use special anti-lice shampoos exactly as directed
Comb wet hair with a fine-tooth metal nit comb
Wash all bedding and recently worn clothes in hot water
things_to_avoid: Using dangerous chemicals or kerosene on the head
Scratching the scalp until it bleeds
Panicking (lice are annoying but not dangerous)
diet_recommendation: Eat your normal, healthy meals every day.
Drink plenty of water to keep your body feeling good.
Include fruits and vegetables to stay strong.
There is no special food to avoid when you have lice.
treatment_options: Comb wet hair with a fine-tooth comb
Wash clothes and bedding in hot water
Seal non-washable items in plastic bags for two weeks
recovery_time: Most lice treatments work within a single day.
It may take up to two weeks to make sure all tiny eggs are gone.
Check your head daily for a week to catch any new bugs.
Repeat the treatment after a week if the doctor or box says so.
physical_activities: You can keep doing all your normal daily activities.
Try to avoid close head-to-head contact during sports or play.
Tie up long hair so it does not touch other people.
Wash your sports hats and helmets after wearing them.
recommended_tests: Look closely at the roots of your hair in bright light.
Use a fine-toothed comb to brush through wet hair and check for bugs.
Look for tiny white specks, called nits, stuck to hair strands.
Ask a family member to check the back of your neck and behind your ears.
when_to_visit_doctor: Medicine does not work after two tries
Skin has signs of infection from scratching
A baby under two months old has lice

lichen simplex.basic_details: Lichen simplex is a skin condition where a small patch of skin gets very itchy. Scratching it a lot makes the skin thick and leather-like.
reason: Chronic scratching or rubbing of the skin
High stress or anxiety leading to scratching
Bug bites that started the itch-scratch cycle
emergency_signs: The skin patch becomes infected with pus
Red streaks spreading from the area
Severe pain instead of just itching
precautions: Apply prescribed steroid creams to stop the itch
Keep the skin covered to prevent scratching
things_to_avoid: Scratching or rubbing the area (crucial for healing)
Using harsh soaps or hot water
Ignoring the urge to scratch without seeking treatment
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your skin healthy.
Drink lots of water every day to stop your skin from getting dry.
Try to eat foods with healthy fats, like fish and nuts, to soothe your skin.
Stay away from very spicy foods and alcohol, which can make you feel itchy.
treatment_options: cover the skin to stop scratching
recovery_time: Itching usually starts to get better within one to two weeks of treatment.
Thickened skin can take several weeks or a few months to go back to normal.
Healing takes much longer if you keep scratching the spot.
Your skin will heal faster if you follow your doctor's daily plan.
physical_activities: Do light exercises like walking or yoga to help lower your stress.
Wear loose and soft cotton clothes when you work out so they do not rub your skin.
Take a quick, cool shower right after sweating to wash off salt that causes itching.
Avoid swimming in pools with strong chemicals that can dry out your skin.
recommended_tests: A simple visual check by a skin doctor is usually enough to spot it.
The doctor might gently scrape a tiny piece of skin to check for germs.
An allergy test might be done to see if something you touch causes itching.
Blood tests are sometimes done to make sure nothing else is wrong inside your body.
when_to_visit_doctor: the skin looks infected or pus comes out
home treatments do not stop the itch
the itch makes it hard to sleep

lipoma.basic_details: A lipoma is a harmless, soft lump of fat that grows slowly right under your skin. It usually does not hurt and is not dangerous at all.
reason: Unknown causes (harmless overgrowth of fat cells)
emergency_signs: The lump becomes hard and painful
The skin over the lump becomes red and hot
Numbness or pain shooting down the arm or leg
precautions: Have a doctor examine the lump to confirm it is harmless
Monitor it for changes in size or pain
Consider surgical removal if it presses on a nerve
things_to_avoid: Squeezing or trying to pop it
Trying to cut it out at home
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and green vegetables every day.
Choose whole foods instead of processed or junk food.
Drink plenty of water to help keep your body healthy.
Cut down on sugary snacks and drinks.
recovery_time: If you have surgery to take it out, healing takes about one to two weeks.
You can usually go back to your normal routine the very next day.
Stitches, if you have any, are usually taken out in a week.
The small spot where it was removed fades away over time.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your light daily walks.
Avoid heavy lifting until your doctor says it is safe.
Stop any exercise if it hurts the spot where the lump was.
Gentle stretching is fine as long as it feels comfortable.
recommended_tests: A simple feel test by your family doctor.
An ultrasound to look under the skin at the lump.
A small tissue sample check if the doctor wants to be extra sure.
An MRI scan if the lump is very deep or unusually large.
when_to_visit_doctor: It starts to hurt a lot
It makes it hard to move

liver cancer.basic_details: Liver cancer happens when bad cells grow out of control in your liver, which is the big organ that cleans your blood. This makes it hard for your body to stay healthy and do its normal jobs.
reason: Chronic Hepatitis B or C infections
Exposure to certain molds on grains (aflatoxins)
emergency_signs: Sudden, severe pain in the upper right belly
Extreme yellowing of the skin and eyes
Rapid, massive swelling of the belly with fluid
precautions: Attend all medical scans and tests
things_to_avoid: Taking over-the-counter pills without a doctor's okay
diet_recommendation: Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and oats.
Drink plenty of water to keep your body hydrated.
Stay away from greasy, fried, and very salty foods.
treatment_options: killing cancer with heat or cold
blocking blood flow to the tumor
recovery_time: Healing takes a different amount of time for every person.
You will need many weeks or months to rest and feel strong again.
Your doctor will check on you often to see how you are healing.
Take things slow and do not rush your body to get better.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks around your house or yard.
Do gentle stretching to keep your body loose.
Stop and rest right away if you feel tired or out of breath.
Do not lift heavy things or do hard exercises.
recommended_tests: Get blood tests to see how well your liver is working.
Have pictures taken of your inside belly using a special scanner.
Do an ultrasound to look closely at your liver.
Sometimes the doctor takes a tiny piece of the liver to test it.
when_to_visit_doctor: feel very tired all the time

liver disease.basic_details: Liver disease means your liver is having trouble working the right way to clean your blood and keep you healthy. It can happen from bad food, heavy drinking, or catching certain sicknesses.
emergency_signs: Vomiting blood or having black, tarry stool
Skin and eyes turn bright yellow
precautions: Get vaccinated for Hepatitis A and B
Talk to a doctor before taking any supplements or pills
diet_recommendation: Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables every single day.
Drink plenty of water to help wash your body out.
Stay away from greasy, fried, and very fatty foods.
Cut down on salty snacks and sugary drinks like soda.
treatment_options: Eat healthy food with less salt
Liver transplant for very bad cases
recovery_time: Healing takes a long time, often many months or even years.
How fast you get better depends on how hurt your liver is.
Stopping bad habits like drinking alcohol helps you heal much faster.
Going to all your doctor visits helps keep your healing on track.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks around your neighborhood.
Do light stretching to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard workouts until you feel stronger.
Rest as much as you need when your body feels weak.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check how well your liver is doing its job.
An ultrasound picture of your belly to look right at your liver.
A special scan that checks how soft or hard your liver feels.
Checking your weight and belly size often with your doctor.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your skin or eyes turn yellow
Your belly swells up with pain
You feel very tired all the time

lumbago.basic_details: Lumbago is simply a common term for lower back pain. It can make your lower back feel stiff, sore, and hard to move.
emergency_signs: Loss of bowel or bladder control
Sudden numbness or weakness in the legs
Pain radiating past the knee down to the foot
precautions: Practice good posture and safe lifting
Use heat or ice packs for muscle pain
Do gentle back stretches and core exercises
things_to_avoid: Bending at the waist to lift things
Staying in bed for more than a day or two
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and green vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your muscles happy.
Choose healthy foods like fish, nuts, and beans to fight body swelling.
Try to stay away from a lot of sugary and greasy fast foods.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within a few days to a week.
Mild cases usually go away completely in about two weeks.
Severe back pain can sometimes take up to six weeks to heal fully.
Listen to your body and do not rush back into heavy work too fast.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks around your house to keep your back loose.
Do gentle stretching while lying flat on your back on a soft mat.
Avoid heavy lifting, intense workouts, and twisting your body suddenly.
Rest when you feel tired, but try not to stay in bed all day long.
recommended_tests: A doctor will press on your back and check how far you can bend.
You might get an X-ray to take a clear picture of your back bones.
An MRI scan may be done to look closely at your muscles and nerves.
Simple blood tests might be done if the doctor wants to check for illness.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain lasts more than a few weeks
Pain starts after a bad fall

lung cancer.basic_details: Lung cancer is a serious illness where bad cells grow too fast in the lungs and make it hard to breathe. It is often linked to smoking or breathing in unhealthy air.
reason: Exposure to radon gas or asbestos
emergency_signs: Coughing up large amounts of blood
Extreme, unexplained weight loss or weakness
precautions: Get lung cancer screenings if you are a heavy smoker
things_to_avoid: Ignoring a cough that won't go away
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose soft foods like soups if your throat feels sore.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated and strong.
Eat small, frequent meals if you do not feel very hungry.
treatment_options: Radiation therapy using high energy rays
Targeted therapy to stop cancer growth
recovery_time: Healing takes a very long time and is different for everyone.
Rest as much as possible to let your body get back its strength.
Go to all your follow-up checkups to see how you are doing.
Be patient with yourself on days when you feel very tired.
physical_activities: Take very short and slow walks around your house.
Do easy breathing exercises to keep your lungs working.
Stop moving right away if you feel dizzy or out of breath.
Ask a doctor before starting any kind of new exercise.
recommended_tests: Get a chest scan to let doctors look closely at your lungs.
Give blood samples so the medical team can check your health.
Have a small tissue check, called a biopsy, to test the cells.
Take breathing tests to see how well your lungs are working.
when_to_visit_doctor: You have a cough that does not go away
You feel pain in your chest

lyme disease.basic_details: Lyme disease is an illness you can get from the bite of a tiny tick. It often causes a skin rash and makes you feel very tired and achy, like you have the flu.
reason: Bite from an infected deer tick
Walking in tall grass or wooded areas
Living in areas with high tick populations
Having pets that bring ticks indoors
emergency_signs: Sudden weakness or paralysis on one side of the face
precautions: Take prescribed antibiotics exactly as told
Check your body for ticks after being outdoors
Wear long sleeves and pants in the woods
things_to_avoid: Squeezing a tick's body when trying to remove it
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink plenty of water every day to stay hydrated.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Eat foods with good bacteria, like yogurt, to keep your tummy healthy.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within a few weeks of starting medicine.
Some people might feel tired for a few months after treatment is done.
Healing time is different for everyone, so try to be patient with your body.
Go back to your doctor if your symptoms do not go away or if they get worse.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest while your body is fighting the illness.
Take short, gentle walks around your house or yard when you feel up to it.
Stop exercising right away if you start to feel too tired or dizzy.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts until you are fully healed.
recommended_tests: Blood tests that look for signs that your body fought off the tick germs.
A careful skin check by a doctor to look at your rash.
General blood counts to check your overall health and energy levels.
Joint checks if your knees or other body parts feel swollen and painful.
when_to_visit_doctor: you find a tick on your skin
you have fever and body aches

lymphadenitis.basic_details: Lymphadenitis happens when your body's infection-fighting glands, called lymph nodes, get infected and swell up, usually causing tender lumps under your skin.
reason: Skin wounds near the lymph node
emergency_signs: Lymph node becomes very red, hot, and extremely painful
Swelling makes it hard to breathe or swallow
precautions: Take prescribed antibiotics if the cause is bacterial
Apply warm, wet compresses to the swollen node
Rest and drink plenty of fluids
See a doctor to find the source of infection
things_to_avoid: Squeezing or poking the swollen node
Ignoring nodes that stay hard and swollen for weeks
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water and clear broths to help your body fight the infection.
Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes or yogurt if your throat or neck is sore.
Choose fresh fruits and vegetables to give your immune system extra strength.
Stay away from sugary snacks and drinks that can slow down your healing.
treatment_options: Putting warm cloth on the area
Surgery to drain pus if needed
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within one to two weeks.
Mild swelling in the glands can sometimes take a few weeks to completely go away.
Your healing time depends on what germ caused the sickness in the first place.
Go back to your doctor if the swelling does not get smaller after a week.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest so your body has enough energy to heal.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until the swollen lumps go down.
Take slow, gentle walks around your home only if you feel up to it.
Stop and rest right away if you feel dizzy or super tired.
recommended_tests: A doctor will gently feel your neck and body to check the swollen lumps.
A simple blood test may be done to look for signs of infection.
An ultrasound picture might be taken to look closely inside the swollen gland.
Sometimes a tiny sample of fluid is taken from the lump to find the exact germ.
when_to_visit_doctor: You have a very high fever

lymphedema.basic_details: Lymphedema is a condition where extra fluid builds up in your body tissues and causes swelling, usually in your arms or legs. It happens when your body's natural drainage system does not work properly.
reason: Surgery removing lymph nodes (like for cancer)
emergency_signs: Swollen arm or leg becomes hot, red, and very painful
High fever and chills (signs of severe infection)
precautions: Do special massage therapy (manual lymph drainage)
Protect the affected arm or leg from cuts and burns
things_to_avoid: Taking blood pressure or getting injections in the affected arm
Ignoring small cuts or bug bites on the limb
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every single day to help your body flush out extra fluid.
Eat less salt because salty foods make your body hold onto more water and cause more swelling.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy and strong.
Try to eat smaller meals so you can keep a healthy weight and put less pressure on your limbs.
recovery_time: Lymphedema is a long-term condition that does not go away completely, so it needs ongoing care.
You can see your swelling go down in a few weeks with the right daily habits and care.
Most people need to do daily routines for the rest of their lives to keep the swelling under control.
Your recovery speed depends on how early you catch the problem and start taking care of it.
physical_activities: Go for gentle walks every day to help the fluid in your arms and legs move around.
Do light stretches to keep your joints moving without putting too much stress on your body.
Wear your special compression wraps or sleeves while you work out to protect your skin.
Avoid heavy lifting or very hard workouts that make your swollen areas tired or strained.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where your doctor gently presses on your skin to see how much it swells.
An imaging scan that uses special pictures to look at how fluid moves inside your body.
Measuring the size of your arm or leg with a tape measure to track changes over time.
An ultrasound scan to check your blood flow and make sure there are no other blockages.

lymphoma.basic_details: Lymphoma is a type of cancer that starts in your immune system, which helps your body fight off germs. It makes your white blood cells grow out of control and form lumps in your body.
emergency_signs: Severe trouble breathing or chest pain from swollen chest nodes
Extremely high fever and drenching night sweats
precautions: Attend all cancer treatments and doctor visits
Wash hands often to prevent infections
things_to_avoid: Ignoring painless swollen lumps in the neck or armpits
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body strong.
Choose lean meats and beans to help repair your body.
Drink lots of water every single day to stay hydrated.
Avoid eating raw or undercooked foods to protect your weak immune system.
recovery_time: Treatment often takes several months, sometimes lasting up to half a year or more.
You will need plenty of time to rest at home after your treatments.
Every person heals at their own speed, so do not rush yourself.
Your energy will slowly come back over many weeks and months.
physical_activities: Take short and gentle walks around your house or yard.
Do light stretching in the morning to keep your body moving.
Stop and rest immediately whenever you start to feel tired.
Avoid heavy lifting and intense workouts while your body is healing.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check the health of your blood cells.
Special body scans to see where the lumps are located.
Taking a tiny sample of tissue to look at it under a microscope.
X-rays of your chest to check your lungs and heart.
when_to_visit_doctor: Swollen lymph nodes that do not go away

macular degeneration.basic_details: Macular degeneration is an eye problem that makes the center of your vision blurry. It usually happens as people get older, making it hard to read or see fine details.
reason: High blood pressure and high cholesterol
emergency_signs: Sudden, severe blurriness in the center of vision
Straight lines suddenly look wavy or bent
A dark, empty spot appears in the center of vision
Sudden complete loss of central vision
precautions: Take specific eye vitamins recommended by a doctor
Eat a diet rich in leafy greens and fish
Wear sunglasses to protect eyes from UV light
things_to_avoid: Eating diets high in saturated fats
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dark green veggies like spinach and kale.
Eat fish that are rich in healthy oils, like salmon, once or twice a week.
Snack on colorful fruits and vegetables like carrots, oranges, and berries.
Cut back on junk food, sugary drinks, and heavy fried foods.
recovery_time: This condition does not go away completely, so the focus is on managing it.
Your vision changes will likely happen slowly over a long period of time.
Getting used to visual aids like magnifying glasses takes a few weeks of practice.
Regular check-ups help track how well your eyes are doing over the years.
physical_activities: Go for daily walks outside while wearing good sunglasses.
Do light exercises like yoga or stretching to stay active and healthy.
Avoid heavy lifting or high-impact sports if your doctor advises against it.
Make sure your home is well-lit so you can move around safely without tripping.
recommended_tests: Have your eye doctor look closely at the back of your eyes during a regular exam.
Use a special grid chart at home to check if straight lines look wavy to you.
Take a test where pictures are taken of the inside of your eyes.
Have your doctor check your reading vision and need for new glasses.

magnesium deficiency.basic_details: Magnesium deficiency happens when your body does not have enough of an important mineral called magnesium. This can make you feel very tired, weak, and give you muscle cramps.
reason: Poor diet lacking vegetables and nuts
emergency_signs: Heart skipping beats or racing dangerously
precautions: Eat nuts, seeds, beans, and leafy greens
things_to_avoid: Taking too many supplements without doctor advice (can cause diarrhea)
diet_recommendation: Eat more green leafy vegetables like spinach.
Snack on nuts and seeds every day.
Include beans and lentils in your meals.
Eat whole grains like brown rice instead of white bread.
recovery_time: You might start feeling better within a few days of changing your diet.
It can take a few weeks of taking pills to fully fill your body's storage.
Severe shortages can take a few months to completely fix.
Your recovery speed depends on how low your levels were to start with.
physical_activities: Do light walking for 30 minutes a day to keep your body moving.
Do gentle stretching to help stop muscle cramps.
Try easy yoga to relax your muscles and mind.
Avoid heavy workouts until your energy levels come back up.
recommended_tests: Get a simple blood test to check your magnesium level.
Do a basic blood panel to check your overall health.
Check your calcium and potassium levels since they work together.
Ask your doctor for a routine checkup on your heart health.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your muscles keep shaking or cramping
You feel very tired all the time
Your heart feels like it is skipping beats
Pills you buy at the store do not help

male genitalia infection.basic_details: A male genitalia infection is an illness where germs or tiny bugs cause swelling, pain, or itching in the private parts. It can be uncomfortable, but it is usually easy to fix with the right care and medicine.
precautions: See a doctor for tests and medicine
Wash the area gently with mild soap daily
Take all prescribed antibiotics or creams
things_to_avoid: Having physical intimacy before the infection is fully cured
Using harsh soaps or scrubbing hard
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of plain water every day to help flush your body.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Stay away from sugary foods and drinks, as they can make infections worse.
Cut back on spicy foods and alcohol that might irritate your bladder.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better in just two to three days.
It usually takes about one week to heal completely.
Severe cases might need up to two weeks of rest and care.
Call your doctor if you do not feel better after a few days of medicine.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest in bed while your body is fighting the infection.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard workouts until you are fully healed.
Stay away from sexual activity until the infection is completely gone.
Wear loose and soft clothing so your skin does not get rubbed or hurt.
recommended_tests: A simple urine test to check for germs in your system.
A gentle swab test of the skin area to see what is causing the problem.
A blood test if the doctor needs to check your overall health.
A physical checkup where the doctor looks at the sore area.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you see pus or fluid
if redness does not go away

malignant hypertension.basic_details: Malignant hypertension is a very dangerous and sudden spike in blood pressure that can quickly harm your vital organs. It is a medical emergency that requires immediate care at a hospital.
emergency_signs: Chest pain and shortness of breath
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Take blood pressure medicines exactly as told
Check blood pressure at home regularly
things_to_avoid: Waiting at home to see if it goes down
diet_recommendation: Cut down heavily on salt and salty foods to help lower your blood pressure.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread instead of white bread.
Drink plenty of water and stay away from sugary sodas and energy drinks.
common_medicines: blood pressure pills given through a needle
pills to lower blood pressure fast
water pills to remove extra fluid
treatment_options: going to the hospital right away
slowly lowering blood pressure over hours
staying in the intensive care unit
