When regular medicines are not working

mumps.basic_details: Mumps is a common viral illness that makes the glands in your cheeks swell up and hurt. It spreads easily from person to person through coughing and sneezing.
reason: Breathing in droplets from an infected person's cough
emergency_signs: Extreme pain and swelling in the testicles
precautions: Stay isolated at home to prevent spreading it
Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Apply warm or cold packs to swollen cheeks
things_to_avoid: Sour or acidic foods (they make the salivary glands hurt)
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes, soup, and yogurt since chewing might hurt.
Drink plenty of water and clear liquids to stay hydrated.
Stay away from sour foods like lemons or oranges because they can make your jaw hurt more.
Avoid spicy or hard foods that can irritate your mouth and throat.
treatment_options: put warm or cold packs on swollen cheeks
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better and see the swelling go down after about one to two weeks.
You are usually contagious and need to stay home for at least five days after your cheeks start swelling.
Total healing time can vary, but resting helps speed up the process.
Keep track of your symptoms and call your doctor if you do not start improving after a week.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest to help your body fight off the virus.
Avoid heavy exercise, running, or lifting heavy things until you are fully better.
Take gentle, short walks around the house only if you feel strong enough.
Sleep as much as you can to give your body the energy it needs to heal.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually just look at your swollen cheeks and ask about your symptoms to tell if you have mumps.
A simple swab from inside your mouth can sometimes be used to test for the virus.
A blood test might be done to check for signs of the mumps virus in your body.
Your doctor may check your temperature and general health during a physical exam.
when_to_visit_doctor: you have a very high fever
you have a severe headache or stiff neck

muscle spasm.basic_details: A muscle spasm is when a muscle suddenly tightens up on its own and hurts. It usually goes away after a short time, but it can make the muscle feel very hard.
reason: Low levels of potassium, magnesium, or calcium
emergency_signs: Spasms spreading to the chest and affecting breathing
Muscle turns completely rigid and dark urine appears
Sudden weakness or numbness in the arms or legs
precautions: Gently stretch and massage the cramping muscle
Drink plenty of water and electrolytes
Apply heat to tense muscles, or ice to sore muscles
Eat foods rich in potassium (like bananas)
things_to_avoid: Pushing through the cramp and continuing to exercise
Sitting in one position for hours
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every single day to keep your muscles happy.
Eat bananas because they have potassium, which stops tight muscles.
Eat leafy greens like spinach to help your body stay strong.
Add a little bit of salt to your food if you sweat a lot.
recovery_time: Most muscle spasms go away in just a few minutes or hours.
Soreness after a bad spasm can last for one or two days.
Resting the muscle helps it feel better much faster.
If you stretch gently, the tight feeling usually leaves by tomorrow.
physical_activities: Do very light and slow stretches where the muscle hurts.
Go for short, easy walks to keep your blood moving.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until the muscle heals.
Try gentle yoga to make your body loose and flexible.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check if your body is low on important vitamins.
A simple physical checkup where the doctor presses on the sore spot.
Checking how much water is usually in your daily diet.
A nerve checkup if the spasms happen all the time.

muscular dystrophy.basic_details: Muscular dystrophy is a health issue that makes the body's muscles weaker and smaller over time. It happens because of changes in the genes that help keep muscles strong.
reason: Missing proteins needed for healthy muscles
emergency_signs: Severe trouble breathing or choking on food
Sudden inability to walk or stand
precautions: Attend regular physical and occupational therapy
Use walking aids or wheelchairs as advised
Get regular heart and lung checkups
things_to_avoid: Ignoring signs of a cold or chest infection
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose lean meats and fish to help keep your body strong.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated and healthy.
Eat foods high in calcium and vitamin D to protect your bones.
recovery_time: Muscular dystrophy is a long-term condition that does not go away completely.
Treatment focuses on managing daily life rather than a fast recovery.
Good daily habits can help slow down how fast the muscle weakness gets worse.
Progress is measured by how well you can keep doing your daily tasks.
physical_activities: Do gentle stretches every day to keep your joints moving easily.
Try light swimming or water aerobics since it is easy on the muscles.
Go for short, easy walks if you are able to do so safely.
Work with a physical therapist to learn safe and easy exercises.
recommended_tests: A simple blood test to check for certain proteins linked to muscles.
A painless test that checks the electrical signals in your muscles and nerves.
A small tissue check where the doctor looks at a tiny piece of your muscle.
Genetic testing using a blood sample to find the cause of the muscle weakness.

myasthenia gravis.basic_details: Myasthenia gravis is a long-term health issue that makes your muscles very tired and weak very easily. It happens when the signals from your nerves cannot properly reach your muscles.
reason: Immune system blocking nerve signals to muscles
emergency_signs: Inability to breathe or very shallow breathing
Inability to swallow saliva or food (choking)
Sudden complete drooping of the eyelids
Extreme weakness in arms or legs preventing movement
precautions: Take prescribed nerve medicines exactly on time
Eat soft foods if chewing becomes tiring
things_to_avoid: Taking new medications without asking a doctor (many worsen this disease)
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods that are very easy to chew and swallow.
Eat several small meals during the day instead of three big ones.
Rest for a little bit before you start eating your meal.
Drink plenty of water and other healthy liquids every day.
treatment_options: Medicine to calm the body's immune system
Surgery to remove the thymus gland
recovery_time: This is a lifelong health condition, which means it does not just go away completely.
Good days and bad days will happen, so your strength can go up and down.
Taking your daily medicine on time helps you feel better and stay strong.
Learning to rest early helps your body recover faster from tired feelings.
physical_activities: Do light walking around your house when you are feeling rested and strong.
Stop exercising the very second you start to feel your muscles getting tired.
Save your big chores for the time of day when you have the most energy.
Ask family members to help you with heavy lifting and hard physical work.
recommended_tests: A special blood test to look for tiny proteins that cause your muscle weakness.
An electrical test on your muscles to see how well they answer your nerves.
A picture scan of your chest to check a small organ near your heart.
A breathing test to make sure your chest muscles are working strongly.
when_to_visit_doctor: If your eyes droop more than usual
If you have trouble chewing or swallowing
If your medicine does not work well

myopia.basic_details: Myopia is a common eye condition where close objects look clear, but things far away look blurry because light does not focus correctly inside your eye.
reason: Too much close-up work (screens, reading) in childhood
emergency_signs: A dark curtain falling over your vision
Sudden appearance of many floating dark spots
precautions: Wear prescribed glasses or contact lenses
Take breaks using the 20-20-20 rule (look 20 feet away for 20 seconds)
Spend time outdoors in natural light
things_to_avoid: Holding phones or books very close to the face
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of green leafy veggies like spinach and kale to keep your eyes healthy.
Eat fish like salmon because it has good oils that help your vision.
Snack on carrots and oranges as they have vitamins that are good for your eyes.
Drink plenty of water every day to stop your eyes from getting dry.
common_medicines: Eye drops to slow down myopia
recovery_time: Myopia is a lifelong condition that usually stabilizes once you reach adulthood.
If you get laser eye surgery, your eyes will feel better within a few days to a week.
Full healing and stable vision after eye surgery can take up to a few months.
Your vision can still change over time, so you need regular check-ups every year.
physical_activities: Spend more time playing and walking outside in the daylight every day.
Take a break to look at something far away every twenty minutes when looking at screens.
Avoid playing contact sports without protective goggles to keep your eyes safe.
Do not read or look at your phone in very dark rooms.
recommended_tests: Get a standard eye chart test to read letters from far away.
Have an eye doctor look inside your eyes with a bright light and special tools.
Take a test that measures the exact shape and length of your eyeball.
Check your eye power using a machine that shines a light into your eyes.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have trouble seeing things far away
If you get frequent headaches from squinting
If your vision gets suddenly blurry

myositis.basic_details: Myositis is a health problem where your body's defense system accidentally attacks your muscles, making them weak and sore.
reason: Viral infections (like the flu or HIV)
emergency_signs: Severe trouble swallowing food or liquids
Inability to lift your head off the pillow
Dark brown urine with severe muscle pain
precautions: Take prescribed steroids or immune medicines
Use walking aids to prevent falls
things_to_avoid: Exposure to intense sunlight (for some types of myositis)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose lean meats and beans to keep your muscles strong.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Try to cut down on sugary snacks and fried foods that can cause swelling.
recovery_time: It usually takes several months to start feeling much better.
Some people might need a year or longer to fully heal.
Healing happens in small steps with good days and bad days.
Listening to your doctor and taking your medicine on time speeds up recovery.
physical_activities: Take gentle walks every day to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Do easy stretching exercises to keep your joints from getting stiff.
Work with a physical therapist who can show you safe movements.
Rest as soon as you feel tired and never push your body too hard.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check for signs of muscle damage and swelling.
Special pictures, like an MRI, to look closely inside your muscles.
A small check of your muscle strength to see how well they are working.
Electrical tests to check if your muscles and nerves are talking properly.
when_to_visit_doctor: if your muscles feel very weak
if you have ongoing muscle pain
if you have trouble standing up
if you feel very tired all the time

narcolepsy.basic_details: Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder that makes people feel very sleepy during the day and can cause them to fall asleep suddenly. It happens because the brain has trouble controlling when to sleep and wake up.
reason: Lack of hypocretin (a brain chemical that controls sleep)
emergency_signs: Suddenly collapsing and losing muscle control (cataplexy)
Inability to move or speak when waking up
precautions: Maintain a very strict sleep schedule at night
Inform teachers or coworkers about the condition
things_to_avoid: Heavy, high-carb meals during the day
Working night shifts or rotating shifts
diet_recommendation: Eat smaller, lighter meals during the day to avoid feeling extra sleepy after eating.
Drink plenty of water to help stay awake and focused.
Avoid eating heavy, sugary snacks right before you need to be active.
Limit or avoid caffeine and alcohol late in the day so they do not ruin your night sleep.
treatment_options: Take short naps during the day
recovery_time: Narcolepsy is a lifelong condition, so there is no quick cure or set recovery date.
Most people start to feel much better within a few weeks of finding the right medicine.
Good daily habits help control the sleepiness over time, making each month easier than the last.
Your symptoms might change as you get older, so you will keep working with your doctor.
physical_activities: Take short, planned naps during the day to refresh your brain and body.
Go for a brisk walk outside to get fresh air and wake yourself up.
Do light exercises like yoga or stretching to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Avoid dangerous activities like swimming alone or driving if you feel a sudden sleep wave coming.
recommended_tests: A special sleep study where you spend the night hooked up to machines so doctors can watch your sleep.
A daytime nap test where doctors measure how fast you fall asleep during the day.
A blood test to check if your body has other issues making you tired.
Keeping a daily sleep diary to write down when you sleep and how tired you feel.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you feel very sleepy all day
If you suddenly lose muscle control when laughing
If you see things right before falling asleep
If sleep problems ruin your daily work

nasal polyp.basic_details: Nasal polyps are soft, painless bumps that grow inside your nose or sinuses. They are caused by long-term swelling and can make it hard to breathe through your nose.
reason: Chronic inflammation of the nose lining
emergency_signs: Complete inability to breathe through the nose
precautions: Rinse sinuses daily with saline water
Use a humidifier in the home
things_to_avoid: Breathing in cigarette smoke or strong chemicals
Taking aspirin (some people with polyps have severe asthma reactions to it)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep the inside of your nose moist.
Try to eat foods with garlic and ginger, as they can help lower swelling.
Stay away from foods that trigger your allergies or make you feel stuffy.
recovery_time: If you just use sprays, you might start feeling better in a few weeks.
If you have surgery to remove them, it usually takes about one to two weeks to heal.
Your nose might feel stuffy for a little while as it heals from treatment.
It can take a few months for your sense of smell to fully come back.
physical_activities: Go for light walks to stay active without breathing too hard.
Avoid heavy workouts that make you breathe heavily through your nose.
Stay away from dusty or dirty places when you exercise outside.
Take breaks if you feel tired or if your nose starts to hurt.
recommended_tests: A doctor will look inside your nose with a small, lighted tool.
You might get a picture scan of your head to see how big the bumps are.
An allergy test can find out what is making your nose swell up.
A breathing check might be done to see how well air moves through your nose.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have trouble breathing through your nose
If your loss of smell does not go away
If you get frequent sinus infections
If your cold symptoms last more than 12 weeks

neonatal jaundice.basic_details: Neonatal jaundice is a very common condition in newborn babies that makes their skin and the whites of their eyes look yellow. It happens because there is too much of a natural yellow substance called bilirubin in their blood while their tiny liver learns how to process it.
reason: Baby's liver is not fully developed yet
Breaking down extra red blood cells after birth
Blood type mismatch between mother and baby
emergency_signs: Baby's skin turns yellow below the belly button
Baby is extremely sleepy and hard to wake up for feeding
Baby arches their back and neck backward
precautions: Feed the baby often (8-12 times a day) to flush out the yellow pigment
Have a doctor check the baby's bilirubin levels
Use special light therapy (phototherapy) if prescribed
Keep track of wet and dirty diapers
things_to_avoid: Putting the baby in direct, hot sunlight without doctor advice
Giving the baby water instead of milk
Ignoring a baby that refuses to eat
Waiting to see if deep yellow skin gets better on its own
diet_recommendation: Feed your baby often, about 8 to 12 times every single day, to help them poop out the extra yellow stuff.
If you are breastfeeding, keep doing it regularly and drink plenty of water yourself to stay healthy.
If your doctor tells you to use baby formula, make sure to give it to your baby as directed.
Wake up your sleepy baby for feeding times if they are sleeping too long during the day or night.
treatment_options: Frequent feeding with breast milk or formula
recovery_time: For most healthy babies born on time, the yellow color starts to fade within one to two weeks.
If your baby was born a little early, it might take up to three weeks for them to fully recover.
The light treatment usually takes just one or two days in the hospital to work its magic.
You will know your baby is getting better when their skin and eyes turn back to their normal color.
physical_activities: Let your baby rest and sleep as much as they want, because sleeping helps their little body grow strong.
Give your baby gentle tummy time only when they are wide awake and a grown-up is watching them.
Change your baby's clothes and diapers gently to keep them comfortable throughout the day.
Hold, cuddle, and rock your baby softly to keep them calm and happy while they heal.
recommended_tests: A quick prick on your baby's heel to take a tiny drop of blood and check the yellow levels.
A painless little device that looks like a small flashlight and is pressed gently against the baby's skin.
A simple urine check to make sure your baby's tummy and kidneys are working just right.
A routine check by the doctor who will look at your baby's skin and eyes in good lighting.
when_to_visit_doctor: Skin or eyes turn very yellow
Baby is hard to wake up
Baby cries in a high pitch

nerve impingement near the shoulder.basic_details: Nerve impingement near the shoulder happens when something rubs against or pinches a nerve, causing pain, numbness, or weakness in your arm.
reason: Heavy lifting or repetitive arm movements
emergency_signs: Sudden, total loss of feeling in the arm or hand
Arm becomes completely weak and unable to lift
Severe pain radiating into the chest
Loss of bowel or bladder control
precautions: Do gentle neck and shoulder stretches
things_to_avoid: Sleeping on your stomach with your neck twisted
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your muscles and nerves healthy.
Eat foods like fish and nuts to help lower body swelling.
Try to cut back on sugary snacks and fast food.
recovery_time: Minor pinches can start feeling better in just a few days.
Most people feel a lot better within four to six weeks.
Severe cases might take a few months of careful rest and care.
Healing time depends on how well you rest your shoulder.
physical_activities: Take a break from heavy lifting and hard workouts.
Do gentle stretching as told by a doctor.
Go for short, easy walks to keep your body moving.
Slowly build back strength with light arm movements later on.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where the doctor moves your arm to see where it hurts.
An X-ray to look at the bones in your shoulder.
An MRI scan to get a clear picture of the pinched nerve and muscles.
A nerve test to check how well your nerves are working.
when_to_visit_doctor: pain does not go away with rest
you feel numb in your arm or hand
you lose strength in your arm
pain wakes you up at night

neuralgia.basic_details: Neuralgia is a sharp, shooting pain that happens when a nerve gets damaged or irritated. It can feel like sudden shocks or burning in different parts of your body.
reason: Pressure on a nerve from a blood vessel or tumor
emergency_signs: Pain is so severe you cannot eat or drink (if in the face)
Sudden drooping on one side of the face
Thoughts of self-harm due to extreme pain
precautions: Take prescribed nerve-pain medications (like anti-seizure pills)
Protect the sensitive skin from wind or light touch
Apply warm compresses if it helps
things_to_avoid: Extreme cold or wind on the face
Taking basic painkillers (they usually do not work for nerve pain)
Chewing hard foods if facial pain is present
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your nerves stay healthy.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body hydrated.
Try to eat less sugar and junk food, as they can sometimes make body pain feel worse.
recovery_time: How long it takes to feel better is different for everyone.
Some people feel good in just a few weeks with the right rest and medicine.
Other people might have pain that comes and goes for many months or years.
Working closely with your doctor helps you heal as fast as possible.
physical_activities: Take gentle walks to keep your body moving without stressing your nerves.
Do light stretching to keep your muscles from getting too tight.
Try relaxing activities like yoga or deep breathing to help your body cope with pain.
Rest completely and avoid heavy lifting on days when the pain is very strong.
recommended_tests: A friendly chat with your doctor about where and how bad the pain hurts.
A gentle physical checkup where the doctor touches the sore spots to see how you react.
Special pictures of your inside body, like an MRI, to look closely at your nerves.
A tiny test that checks how well your nerves send messages by using very small, safe zaps.

neurofibromatosis.basic_details: Neurofibromatosis is a health condition that runs in families and causes soft bumps to grow on or under the skin. It can also affect the bones and the nerves.
reason: Missing proteins that control nerve growth
emergency_signs: Sudden weakness or numbness in arms or legs
A tumor grows very fast or becomes extremely painful
precautions: Get regular medical and eye exams
Seek physical therapy for bone issues
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day to keep your body strong.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated and help your body work its best.
Choose whole foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread instead of sugary snacks.
Eat foods with calcium, like milk or yogurt, to keep your bones healthy and strong.
recovery_time: This condition stays with a person for life, so there is no single date for a complete cure.
If you have surgery to remove a bothersome bump, healing the skin usually takes a few weeks.
Regular check-ups with your doctor will help manage symptoms as you grow older.
Most people live a long and normal life by learning how to manage their daily symptoms.
physical_activities: Go for daily walks to keep your heart healthy and your energy levels up.
Try gentle swimming because it is easy on your joints and muscles.
Do fun stretching exercises to keep your body flexible and loose.
Avoid rough contact sports that could cause hard bumps or injuries to your skin.
recommended_tests: Visit an eye doctor regularly to make sure your vision stays clear and healthy.
Have your doctor check your blood pressure at every routine visit.
Get skin checks done by a professional to monitor any changes in your spots or bumps.
Talk to your doctor about imaging scans if you have ongoing pain or numbness.

neuropathy due to drugs.basic_details: Neuropathy due to drugs happens when certain medicines damage your nerves, causing tingling, numbness, or pain mostly in your hands and feet.
emergency_signs: Sudden inability to walk or stand
Complete loss of feeling in the hands or feet
Open sores developing on numb feet
precautions: Tell the doctor immediately if you feel tingling while on medicine
Inspect feet daily for cuts or sores
things_to_avoid: Stopping the medication without asking the doctor
Using hot water bottles on numb feet
Ignoring the tingling hoping it goes away
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to give your nerves the vitamins they need.
Drink lots of water every day to help your body flush out toxins.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Try to eat foods with healthy fats, like fish and nuts, to support nerve health.
recovery_time: Healing nerve damage takes a lot of time, often ranging from a few months to a full year.
Some people feel better very quickly after stopping the bad medicine, while others take longer.
Your recovery speed depends on how long you took the medicine and how much damage was done.
Be patient with your body because nerves grow back and heal very slowly.
physical_activities: Go for gentle daily walks to keep your blood flowing and your muscles strong.
Do light stretching exercises to stop your joints and limbs from feeling stiff.
Try swimming or water aerobics because they are very gentle on your hands and feet.
Listen to your body and stop right away if any exercise causes sharp pain or numbness.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check your vitamin levels and make sure your organs are working well.
A special nerve test that measures how well your nerves send electrical signals.
A physical checkup where your doctor tests your reflexes, touch, and muscle strength.
A review of all your current medicines and medical history to find the exact cause.
when_to_visit_doctor: hands or feet start to tingle

neurosis.basic_details: Neurosis refers to a group of mental health conditions that cause distress, like chronic anxiety, fear, or sadness, but do not involve losing touch with reality. It often makes everyday life feel overwhelming.
emergency_signs: Severe panic attacks that feel like a heart attack
Complete inability to leave the house
precautions: Practice deep breathing and grounding exercises
things_to_avoid: Using alcohol or drugs to cope
diet_recommendation: Eat regular, balanced meals to keep your energy and mood stable.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Avoid too much caffeine, as it can make anxiety or nervousness worse.
Include foods rich in omega-3s, like walnuts or fish, which support brain health.
recovery_time: Therapy can start showing positive results in a few weeks or months.
Medications often take two to six weeks to build up and take full effect.
Recovery is a gradual process and varies greatly from person to person.
Ongoing support and lifestyle changes are usually needed for long-term relief.
physical_activities: Practice daily walking or light jogging to naturally boost your mood.
Try yoga or stretching to release physical tension built up from stress.
Do deep breathing exercises to help calm your nervous system.
Engage in group activities or sports if being around supportive people helps you feel better.
recommended_tests: A full psychological evaluation by a mental health professional.
Questionnaires to measure your levels of anxiety and depression.
Blood tests to rule out physical issues like a thyroid problem.
A general physical exam to ensure your overall body is healthy.

nonalcoholic liver disease (nash).basic_details: Nonalcoholic liver disease (NASH) happens when extra fat builds up in the liver and causes inflammation, even if you drink little or no alcohol. Over time, this swelling can cause damage and scarring to the liver.
reason: High blood sugar or Type 2 diabetes
emergency_signs: Skin and eyes turning bright yellow (jaundice)
precautions: Eat a healthy diet rich in vegetables and whole grains
things_to_avoid: Eating foods high in sugar and simple carbs
Taking unprescribed supplements or high doses of Tylenol
diet_recommendation: Focus on a plant-based diet full of fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
Cut down on sugary drinks and foods with added sugars or heavy syrups.
Choose healthy fats, like olive oil and nuts, instead of fried or greasy foods.
Avoid alcohol completely to protect your liver from extra stress.
recovery_time: Improving diet and losing weight can start healing the liver in a few months.
Reversing early liver fat buildup is possible with strict lifestyle changes.
If scarring has occurred, it may take years to manage and keep it from getting worse.
Lifelong healthy habits are required to prevent the condition from returning.
physical_activities: Aim for at least 30 minutes of brisk walking or swimming most days of the week.
Add light weightlifting twice a week to improve how your body uses sugar.
Stay active throughout the day by taking the stairs or doing household chores.
Slowly increase your exercise intensity so your body gets used to the routine.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check your liver enzymes and overall liver function.
An ultrasound of your belly to look for fat buildup in the liver.
A special scan called FibroScan to measure the stiffness or scarring of the liver.
In some cases, a liver biopsy to look at a tiny piece of liver tissue under a microscope.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you feel very tired all the time
If your belly hurts or swells

noninfectious gastroenteritis.basic_details: Noninfectious gastroenteritis is when your stomach and intestines get upset and irritated, but not because of germs or bugs. It usually happens from eating bad food, drinking too much alcohol, or taking certain medicines.
reason: Side effects of medicines (like ibuprofen or antibiotics)
Eating food with bacterial toxins (food poisoning)
Underlying gut diseases like Crohn's or Celiac
emergency_signs: Vomiting blood or material looking like coffee grounds
precautions: Drink plenty of water and clear fluids
Eat bland foods like toast, rice, and bananas
Stop taking irritating medicines after checking with a doctor
things_to_avoid: Spicy, greasy, or highly acidic foods
Taking anti-diarrhea pills if there is blood in the stool
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water and clear broths to stay hydrated.
Eat plain foods like white rice, toast, and bananas.
Stay away from spicy, greasy, or fried foods.
Avoid dairy products and caffeine until you feel better.
treatment_options: eat plain foods like rice and bananas
stay away from milk and spicy food
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within two to three days.
Severe tummy irritation can sometimes take up to a week to heal.
Your energy might stay low for a few extra days.
Eating too soon can make the recovery take longer.
physical_activities: Rest in bed as much as possible while your stomach heals.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until you are strong again.
Take slow, gentle walks around the house only if you feel up to it.
Listen to your body and stop moving if you feel dizzy or tired.
recommended_tests: Give a stool sample to double-check that no hidden germs are there.
Do a simple blood test to check your body's water levels.
Have a doctor press gently on your belly to check for soreness.
Talk through your recent meals and daily habits with your doctor.
when_to_visit_doctor: you have pain for many days
you see blood in your stool

nose disorder.basic_details: A nose disorder is a common health issue that affects how you breathe or smell through your nose. It can make your nose feel stuffy, runny, or blocked.
reason: Dry air or frequent nose picking
Structural defects like a deviated septum
emergency_signs: Nosebleed that will not stop after 20 minutes of pressure
Clear fluid leaking from the nose after a head injury
High fever and severe face pain
precautions: Use saline nasal sprays to keep the inside moist
Use a humidifier in your bedroom
Pinch the soft part of the nose and lean forward for nosebleeds
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of warm water and soup to keep your nose clear.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Avoid very cold drinks that might make a stuffy nose feel worse.
Stay away from spicy foods if they make your nose run too much.
recovery_time: Most minor nose issues start to feel better within three to five days.
If you have a mild allergy, it may take a week or two to clear up.
Getting plenty of sleep helps your body heal much quicker.
Give yourself time to rest until your breathing feels completely normal again.
physical_activities: Take gentle, relaxing walks in fresh air when you feel up to it.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until your nose is fully healed.
Do slow breathing exercises to help keep your airways open.
Stay indoors if the outside air is very dusty or smoky.
recommended_tests: A doctor may look inside your nose with a small, lighted tool.
You might get a gentle allergy skin test to find out what bothers your nose.
A simple breathing check can show how well air moves through your nose.
Sometimes a quick picture scan of your nose is done if it stays blocked.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have a nose bleed that does not stop
If nose pain is very bad
If you cannot breathe through your nose for weeks
If you have a bad smell and green mucus

obsessive compulsive disorder (ocd).basic_details: Obsessive compulsive disorder is a mental health condition that causes repeated unwanted thoughts and a strong urge to do certain things over and over.
emergency_signs: Thoughts of hurting yourself or others
Inability to eat, sleep, or leave the house due to fears
Washing or cleaning until the skin bleeds
precautions: Engage in specialized therapy (Exposure and Response Prevention)
things_to_avoid: Using alcohol or drugs to quiet the mind
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your brain stay healthy.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to keep your body feeling good.
Try to eat less sugar and junk food, as they can make you feel more jittery.
Eat regular meals so your blood sugar stays steady and your mood stays calm.
recovery_time: Getting better from OCD takes time and patience, and everyone heals at their own speed.
Some people start to feel a little better after just a few weeks of getting help.
For many people, recovery is a journey that takes several months of steady work.
You might have good days and bad days, and that is a normal part of getting better.
physical_activities: Go for a nice daily walk outside to help clear your head and lower stress.
Try simple yoga or stretching to help relax your body when you feel tense.
Do fun things like dancing or swimming to burn off extra nervous energy.
Spend time doing gentle workouts that make you happy without making you too tired.
recommended_tests: A friendly talk with a brain doctor to share what is on your mind.
Answering some easy questions on a paper about your daily habits and feelings.
A quick check-up with your regular doctor to make sure your body is healthy.
Talking about your thoughts and daily routines with a trained helper.
when_to_visit_doctor: Too much time spent on rituals
Hard to go to work or school

obstructive sleep apnea (osa).basic_details: Obstructive sleep apnea is a common sleep problem where your breathing stops and starts again and again while you sleep, usually because your throat muscles relax and block your airway.
reason: Throat muscles relaxing too much during sleep
emergency_signs: Waking up gasping for air or choking
Extreme daytime sleepiness leading to falling asleep driving
precautions: Use a CPAP machine exactly as prescribed
Sleep on your side instead of your back
diet_recommendation: Eat healthy meals with plenty of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains to help lose extra weight.
Try to eat dinner a few hours before bedtime so your stomach has time to digest.
Stay away from heavy, greasy, or spicy foods late at night because they can make it harder to breathe.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day, but cut back on drinks right before bed so you do not wake up.
treatment_options: Weight loss and sleeping on side
recovery_time: How quickly you feel better depends on the treatment you choose and how closely you follow your doctor's advice.
Many people notice they have more energy and less daytime sleepiness within just a few days of starting CPAP therapy.
If you need surgery to help open your airway, it can take a few weeks of rest to fully heal.
Making lifelong healthy habits like losing weight takes time, often several months of steady effort.
physical_activities: Go for a brisk walk, a bike ride, or a swim most days of the week to help your body stay strong and healthy.
Do light exercises like yoga or stretching to help you relax and get ready for a good night's rest.
Try to lose any extra weight through regular workouts, which can take a lot of the pressure off your neck and throat.
Avoid doing intense workouts right before bedtime, as this can give you too much energy and keep you awake.
recommended_tests: Stay overnight at a sleep center where experts can hook up sensors to watch your breathing, heart rate, and sleep patterns.
Use a simple take-home sleep test kit that tracks your breathing and oxygen levels while you sleep in your own bed.
Have a doctor look inside your nose, mouth, and throat to see if anything is blocking your airway.
Get blood tests if your doctor thinks other health issues, like thyroid problems, might be linked to your sleep trouble.
when_to_visit_doctor: You wake up gasping for air
You feel very tired all day
Your partner notices you stop breathing at night

onychomycosis.basic_details: Onychomycosis is a common fungal infection that makes your fingernails or toenails thick, discolored, and brittle. It usually starts as a small white or yellow spot under the tip of the nail and spreads deeper as it grows.
reason: Walking barefoot in public showers or pools
Having sweaty feet and wearing tight, damp shoes
emergency_signs: Redness and swelling spreading to the skin around the nail
Pus draining from under the nail
precautions: Keep feet clean and completely dry
Trim nails straight across and keep them short
things_to_avoid: Wearing the same sweaty shoes every day
Using nail polish to cover it up without treating it
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh garlic because it helps fight off fungus naturally.
Eat yogurt with live good bacteria to keep your body strong and balanced.
Cut down on sugary foods and drinks, as fungus loves to feed on sugar.
Drink lots of water every day to help flush toxins out of your body.
treatment_options: Paint special medicine on the nail
recovery_time: Fingernails usually take about 3 to 6 months to grow out completely healthy.
Toenails grow much slower and can take 12 to 18 months to heal fully.
You must keep applying your treatment every day until the old nail is completely gone.
If you stop treatment too early, the fungus will likely grow right back.
physical_activities: Go ahead and do your normal exercises, but keep your feet clean and dry.
Wear open-air shoes like sandals when working out so your feet can breathe.
Avoid walking barefoot in public gyms, locker rooms, or swimming pool areas.
Change out of sweaty socks and shoes immediately after your workout.
recommended_tests: A doctor will simply look closely at your nails to check for signs of fungus.
They might gently scrape a tiny bit of material from under your nail.
A lab test can look at the scrapings under a microscope to find the exact fungus.
Sometimes a small clipping of your nail is sent away to a lab for testing.
when_to_visit_doctor: The infection is spreading to other nails
You have diabetes and foot problems

open wound of the ear.basic_details: An open wound of the ear means the skin or tissue on or inside your ear is cut, scraped, or torn. It needs proper cleaning and care to heal well and stop germs from getting in.
emergency_signs: Bleeding that won't stop with pressure
Clear fluid leaking from the ear (brain fluid)
Part of the ear is torn off
precautions: Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth to stop bleeding
Keep the wound clean and dry
Get a tetanus shot if needed
things_to_avoid: Putting anything inside the ear canal
Washing the ear with harsh chemicals
Ignoring signs of infection like pus or fever
Delaying medical care for deep cuts
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your skin heal faster.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and strong.
Include foods with protein like chicken, beans, or eggs to repair the cut.
Stay away from junk food and sugary snacks so your body can fight off any germs.
treatment_options: keep the ear clean and dry
recovery_time: Small cuts on the outer ear usually start to feel better in just a few days.
Most open ear wounds take about one to two weeks to fully close up.
Deep cuts or wounds that needed stitches may take a little longer to heal.
You will know you are healed when the pain is gone and new skin has formed.
physical_activities: Avoid heavy lifting and hard exercises that make you sweat a lot.
Do not go swimming or get water inside your healing ear.
Rest as much as you can to give your body energy to fix the cut.
Keep your head still and avoid sudden movements that might pull on the ear.
recommended_tests: A simple physical check by a doctor to see how deep the cut is.
A quick hearing check to make sure the inside of your ear is working fine.
A gentle look inside the ear canal with a small lighted tool.
A swab test of the skin if the doctor thinks germs might be growing.
when_to_visit_doctor: if the cut is very deep
if you feel dizzy or confused

open wound of the eye.basic_details: An open wound of the eye happens when the outer part of your eye is cut or torn. This is a serious injury that needs a doctor right away.
emergency_signs: Blood inside the colored part of the eye
Loss of vision or extreme blurriness
precautions: Call an ambulance or go to the ER immediately
Place a hard shield (like a paper cup) over the eye for protection
Keep the other eye closed to prevent the injured eye from moving
things_to_avoid: Pressing on the eye or applying pressure
Trying to remove any object stuck in the eye
Rinsing the eye with water if it is deeply cut
diet_recommendation: Eat healthy foods like fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink plenty of water every day to stay hydrated.
Eat foods with protein, like chicken or beans, to repair your tissues.
Avoid salty foods so you do not swell up while recovering.
treatment_options: Go to the hospital right now
Do not touch or rub the eye
Put a hard shield over the eye
Surgery to fix the eye cut
recovery_time: Healing can take anywhere from a few weeks to a few months.
The first week is the most important time to rest your eye.
Your vision may be blurry for a while as it gets better.
You must go to all follow-up visits to make sure it heals right.
physical_activities: Stay in bed or rest quietly during the first few days.
Do not bend over or lift heavy things because it hurts your eye.
Avoid sports and hard workouts until your doctor gives you permission.
Wear an eye patch or shield to protect your eye from bumps.
recommended_tests: A special eye exam using a bright light to look closely at the cut.
A test to check how well you can see out of the injured eye.
An eye pressure test to make sure the inside of your eye is safe.
Special pictures or scans of your eye if the doctor needs a deeper look.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you bleed from the eye

open wound of the mouth.basic_details: An open wound of the mouth is a cut, scrape, or tear inside your mouth, lips, or gums. It can happen from biting your tongue, falling, or eating sharp foods.
reason: Accidentally biting the cheek or tongue
emergency_signs: Bleeding that will not stop after 15 minutes of pressure
precautions: Rinse the mouth gently with cool water
Apply pressure with a clean gauze or cloth
Suck on an ice cube to reduce swelling
things_to_avoid: Eating hot, spicy, or salty foods
Drinking from a straw (can restart bleeding)
Pulling the lip far away to look at the wound
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and soup until it heals.
Stay away from spicy, salty, or very sour foods because they will sting.
Drink plenty of cool water to keep your mouth clean and hydrated.
Avoid sharp or crunchy foods like chips that can scrape the sore.
recovery_time: Most small mouth cuts start feeling better in just a few days.
Complete healing usually takes about one to two weeks.
The inside of the mouth heals much faster than skin on the outside of the body.
If it hurts longer than two weeks, you should see a doctor.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily routines and light chores.
Avoid heavy sports or activities where you might get hit in the face.
Rest as much as you can so your body can repair itself quickly.
Try not to talk too much if moving your mouth makes the cut hurt.
recommended_tests: Most mouth cuts do not need any special medical tests at all.
A doctor might just look inside your mouth with a small light.
They may check if you need stitches if the cut is deep or wide.
Sometimes they check your teeth to make sure nothing else was damaged.
when_to_visit_doctor: bad smell or pus comes out

open wound of the neck.basic_details: An open wound of the neck is a cut or break in the skin on your neck that needs careful cleaning and healing. It is important to keep it safe from germs while it mends.
precautions: Apply firm, direct pressure to the bleeding (but do not choke the person)
Keep the person still and calm
things_to_avoid: Removing any object stuck in the neck
Moving the person's head or neck
Wrapping a bandage completely around the neck
Giving the person food or water
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods if swallowing hurts from the neck injury.
Drink plenty of water every day to help your body heal.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body strength.
Include healthy foods like chicken or beans to help fix your skin.
recovery_time: Small cuts on the neck usually take a week or two to close up.
Deep cuts or wounds needing stitches may take longer to heal completely.
You will need to visit the doctor to check how well the skin is mending.
The scar might take a few months to fade away.
physical_activities: Rest a lot and avoid hard work for the first few days.
Do not bend or twist your neck too fast so stitches stay safe.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard sports until the doctor says it is okay.
Take slow, gentle walks around the house when you feel better.
recommended_tests: The doctor will look closely at the cut to see how deep it is.
They may check if you can move your neck and swallow normally.
An X-ray might be done to make sure no bones are hurt.
Blood tests may be done if the doctor thinks there is an infection.

oppositional disorder.basic_details: Oppositional defiant disorder is a behavioral issue where a person is often angry, argues a lot with adults, and refuses to follow rules.
reason: Severe stress or abuse at home
emergency_signs: Violent behavior towards people or animals
Severe self-harm or thoughts of suicide
Total refusal to eat or drink
precautions: Seek family therapy and behavioral counseling
Set clear, consistent, and calm rules
things_to_avoid: Blaming the child without offering help
diet_recommendation: Eat healthy meals with plenty of fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated and feel good.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and candy, as sugar can make you hyper.
Eat at regular times so your mood stays steady and calm.
recovery_time: Getting better takes time and does not happen overnight.
Progress is different for everyone, taking a few months to even a few years.
Good days and bad days will happen while you are learning to cope.
Sticking with counseling and family support makes healing much faster.
physical_activities: Play outside games or run around to burn off extra energy.
Join a team sport like soccer or basketball to learn how to share and work together.
Try riding a bike or swimming to help your body and mind relax.
Do deep breathing or stretching exercises when you feel angry or upset.
recommended_tests: Doctors will talk to you and your parents to understand your feelings and actions.
Fill out simple questionnaires about how you behave at home and school.
Talk with a mental health counselor who listens and asks questions.
Checkups to make sure other health issues are not causing your behavior.
when_to_visit_doctor: When family life is very hard

oral mucosal lesion.basic_details: An oral mucosal lesion is a sore, patch, or unusual spot inside your mouth. It can happen from biting your cheek, hot food, or other irritation.
reason: Biting the inside of the cheek
Autoimmune diseases or weak immune system
emergency_signs: A sore that does not heal after 3 weeks (could be cancer)
White patches that cannot be scraped off
High fever and inability to swallow water
Sores spreading to the lips or face
precautions: Use prescribed numbing gels for pain
Have a dentist check any long-lasting sores
things_to_avoid: Poking the sore with your tongue or fingers
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and oatmeal that do not hurt your mouth.
Stay away from spicy, salty, and sour foods because they will sting the sore spot.
Drink plenty of plain water throughout the day to keep your mouth moist.
Avoid sharp or crunchy snacks like chips and crackers that can cut your mouth.
treatment_options: Laser or minor surgery if needed
recovery_time: Most simple sores in the mouth go away on their own within one to two weeks.
Healing can take a little longer if you keep accidentally biting the same spot.
If the sore lasts for more than two weeks, you should get it checked by a doctor.
Resting and eating well helps your body fix the sore much faster.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily exercises and activities without any problems.
Avoid heavy contact sports if you are worried about getting hit in the face or mouth.
Take plenty of rest if you feel tired or run-down while your mouth is healing.
Try to lower your stress levels, as stress can sometimes slow down mouth healing.
recommended_tests: A doctor or dentist will look closely inside your mouth using a small light.
They might gently touch the sore spot to check how soft or hard it feels.
If a sore does not heal, the doctor might take a tiny sample of the skin to test it.
They may ask about your daily habits like eating, smoking, or brushing to find the cause.
when_to_visit_doctor: If it does not heal in two weeks

oral thrush (yeast infection).basic_details: Oral thrush is a common fungal infection that causes painful white patches to form inside your mouth and on your tongue. It happens when a certain type of yeast grows too much.
emergency_signs: Pain so severe you cannot eat or drink
Infection spreading down the throat causing choking
precautions: Take prescribed antifungal mouthwashes or lozenges
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and soup that are easy to swallow.
Stay away from sugary foods and drinks because yeast feeds on sugar.
Avoid spicy, acidic, or crunchy foods that can hurt your sore mouth.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your mouth moist.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment.
The infection usually goes away completely in one to two weeks.
If you have a weak immune system, it might take a little longer to heal.
Keep taking your medicine for the full time your doctor tells you, even if you feel better.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily activities like walking or light chores.
Rest more if you feel tired while your body is fighting the infection.
Avoid heavy workouts if you feel weak or dizzy from being sick.
Get a good night's sleep every day to help your body heal faster.
recommended_tests: A simple visual check where a doctor looks inside your mouth.
A gentle scrape of the white patch to look at it under a microscope.
A swab test of your mouth to check what kind of germ is growing.
A blood test if your doctor wants to check your overall health and sugar levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you see white spots in your mouth
If the medicine does not work
If you have a weak immune system

orbital cellulitis.basic_details: Orbital cellulitis is a serious infection of the tissue around your eye, making it swollen, red, and painful. It happens when bacteria spread from your sinuses or a skin cut into the eye socket.
reason: Untreated sinus infection spreading to the eye
Bug bite or cut near the eye
emergency_signs: Eye bulging out of the socket
Severe loss of vision or double vision
High fever and extreme eye pain
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Take IV antibiotics as prescribed in the hospital
Follow up with an eye doctor and ENT
Treat sinus and dental infections early
things_to_avoid: Waiting to see if it gets better
Trying to treat it at home with warm compresses alone
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to help your body stay hydrated and fight the infection.
Eat soft foods like soup, mashed potatoes, and yogurt if your jaw hurts or it is hard to chew.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to give your immune system vitamins and strength.
Avoid eating very salty or processed foods that can make swelling and puffiness worse.
common_medicines: strong antibiotics given through a needle in the vein
antibiotic pills to take by mouth after leaving the hospital
pain medicine to help with the hurt
eye drops if the eye is dry or infected
treatment_options: staying in the hospital for strong medicine
surgery to drain pus if there is an abscess
watching the eye very closely with tests
resting in bed until the swelling goes down
recovery_time: Most people start feeling a bit better within two to three days of starting strong antibiotics.
Total healing usually takes about one to two weeks of finishing all your medicine.
You might need to stay in the hospital for a few days so doctors can watch your eye closely.
It can take a few weeks for all the swelling and redness to completely go away.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest and sleep so your body can use its energy to heal.
Avoid working, reading, or looking at computer screens if it strains your sore eye.
Do not do any heavy lifting, running, or hard exercise until the infection is completely gone.
Keep your head propped up on extra pillows while resting to help the swelling go down faster.
recommended_tests: A special picture scan, like a CT scan, to see how deep the infection has gone behind your eye.
Blood tests to check for signs of infection and see how well your body is fighting it.
A gentle swab of any discharge or pus from your eye to find the exact germ causing the problem.
Eye pressure checks and vision tests to make sure your eyesight is safe and working normally.
when_to_visit_doctor: when your eyelid becomes very red and swollen
if it hurts to move your eye
if you get a high fever with eye pain
orbital cellulitis.specialist: Ophthalmologist and Ear, Nose, and Throat Doctor

orthostatic hypotension.basic_details: Orthostatic hypotension is a sudden drop in blood pressure when you stand up too fast. This makes you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or like you might faint.
reason: Side effects of blood pressure medicines
Nerve damage from diabetes or Parkinson's
emergency_signs: Chest pain or a racing heart when standing
precautions: Stand up very slowly, especially from bed
things_to_avoid: Standing perfectly still for long periods
Drinking alcohol (it lowers blood pressure more)
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water every day to keep your blood pressure up.
Add a little extra salt to your food after talking to your doctor.
Eat smaller meals more often so blood does not rush to your stomach.
Limit or avoid drinking alcohol since it can lower your blood pressure.
treatment_options: Stand up slowly from sitting or lying down
recovery_time: There is no set time for a full recovery because it is a long-term condition.
Many people start feeling much better within a few weeks of changing their habits.
You manage the symptoms every day instead of curing it completely in most cases.
Working closely with your doctor helps you get better control over time.
physical_activities: Take your time when moving from sitting or lying down to standing up.
Flex your leg and tummy muscles before standing up to help pump blood.
Wear special support stockings to keep blood from pooling in your legs.
Avoid heavy workouts in very hot weather since heat lowers blood pressure.
recommended_tests: A blood pressure check while lying down, sitting, and standing up.
A tilt table test to see how your body reacts to changes in position.
Blood tests to check if you have low iron or other simple issues.
An electrocardiogram to make sure your heart is beating the right way.
when_to_visit_doctor: If dizziness does not go away
If you fall and get hurt
If standing up makes you feel very weak

osteoarthritis.basic_details: Osteoarthritis is a common joint problem where the cushioning inside your joints wears away over time. This makes moving hurt and can cause stiffness.
reason: Aging and natural wear of joint cartilage
Repetitive stress on the joints over years
emergency_signs: Joint becomes suddenly red, hot, and swollen (possible infection)
Inability to put any weight on the leg
Sudden extreme pain locking the joint
precautions: Do low-impact exercises like swimming or biking
Apply heat or ice to painful joints
things_to_avoid: High-impact sports like running on concrete
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose fish and nuts because they help calm down swelling in your joints.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body and joints hydrated.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and greasy fast food to stay at a healthy weight.
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition, meaning it does not just go away in a few weeks.
Good days and bad days will happen, and how you feel can change from week to week.
Following a healthy daily routine helps you feel better as time passes.
Listening to your body and resting when needed prevents the pain from getting worse.
physical_activities: Go for gentle walks to keep your legs moving without hurting your joints.
Try swimming or water aerobics because the water takes the heavy weight off your body.
Do easy stretching exercises every morning to stop your joints from feeling stiff.
Avoid heavy lifting or running that puts too much stress on your knees and hips.
recommended_tests: An X-ray picture lets the doctor look inside to see how much cushioning you have left.
A simple physical check where the doctor bends and moves your sore joints.
Blood tests might be done just to make sure no other sickness is causing the pain.
A doctor may ask questions about your daily pain levels to track how you are doing.
when_to_visit_doctor: pain wakes you up at night

osteochondroma.basic_details: Osteochondroma is a non-cancerous bone growth that develops during childhood or teen years, usually near the ends of long bones. It looks like a small bump made of bone and cartilage.
emergency_signs: The bone bump suddenly grows very fast
Severe new pain in the area
Numbness or tingling in the arm or leg
Loss of blood flow causing a cold hand or foot
precautions: Have a doctor check the bump to confirm it is benign
Monitor it for changes in size
Consider surgery if it presses on a nerve or blood vessel
Protect the area from direct hits
things_to_avoid: Heavy contact sports if the bump is large and exposed
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk and cheese to keep your bones strong.
Include green leafy vegetables in your meals for overall bone health.
Eat foods rich in vitamin D, such as eggs and fish, to help your body use calcium.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body healthy and working well.
recovery_time: If you do not need surgery, you can return to normal life right away.
If you have surgery to remove the bump, healing usually takes a few weeks.
Most people feel much better and back to normal within one to two months.
Complete healing of the bone can take up to three months after an operation.
physical_activities: Do gentle walking every day to keep your body moving safely.
Avoid heavy lifting or high-impact sports until a doctor says it is okay.
Do light stretching exercises to keep your joints from getting stiff.
Stop right away if any movement causes pain or sharp discomfort.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray to let the doctor clearly see the bone bump.
Have a physical check-up where the doctor feels the size of the growth.
Do an MRI scan if the doctor needs a closer look at the surrounding tissue.
Undergo a CT scan for a very detailed picture of the bone.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel new or severe pain
It is hard to move your joints
The skin over the lump looks red or swollen

osteochondrosis.basic_details: Osteochondrosis is a common problem in the joints and spine where the bone and cartilage wear down over time. This can cause stiffness, aches, and discomfort when you move around.
reason: Reduced blood supply to the growing bone
emergency_signs: Severe pain making it impossible for the child to walk
precautions: Use crutches or a brace if recommended
Provide a healthy diet for bone growth
things_to_avoid: Pushing the child to play sports through the pain
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and green vegetables every day to keep your bones strong.
Drink plenty of water to help keep your joints well lubricated.
Include foods like milk, cheese, and yogurt for a good boost of calcium.
Try to cut down on sugary snacks and greasy fast food that cause body swelling.
recovery_time: Minor aches and stiffness can start feeling better within a few weeks.
More serious joint or back flare-ups can take several months to truly heal.
Healing happens much faster if you rest properly and follow your care plan.
It requires ongoing daily care to keep the pain from coming back.
physical_activities: Take short, easy walks daily to keep your body moving without strain.
Do gentle stretching exercises to loosen up stiff muscles and joints.
Swimming is a great choice because the water takes the heavy pressure off your bones.
Avoid heavy lifting, intense jumping, or hard running that can hurt your back.
recommended_tests: An X-ray picture can show the doctor what your bones and joints look like.
An MRI scan helps the doctor see deep inside to check your muscles and cartilage.
Blood tests can be done to make sure there are no other hidden health issues.
A simple physical checkup where the doctor presses on sore spots to test your movement.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain does not go away with rest

osteomyelitis.basic_details: Osteomyelitis is a painful infection that gets deep inside your bones. It happens when germs travel through your blood or enter the bone through a cut or surgery.
reason: Bacteria entering through a deep wound
Blood infection spreading to the bone
Poor blood flow from severe diabetes
emergency_signs: Bone area becomes extremely red, hot, and swollen
Pus draining from the skin over the bone
precautions: Take long-term IV antibiotics as prescribed
things_to_avoid: Walking on an infected leg bone
Ignoring a wound that will not heal
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Choose foods high in protein like chicken, eggs, and beans to fix tissues.
Drink lots of water every single day to stay healthy.
Eat dairy products like milk and yogurt to keep your bones strong.
common_medicines: Pain pills to help with soreness
Special germ-killing liquids given in the arm
treatment_options: Surgery to clean out bad bone
Eating healthy food to help healing
recovery_time: It usually takes several weeks or even months to get completely better.
You might need medicine for many weeks to kill all the bad germs.
How fast you heal depends on how early you started your treatment.
You will need regular check-ups with your doctor to track your progress.
physical_activities: Rest your body and the infected bone as much as possible at first.
Avoid heavy lifting or running until your doctor says it is safe.
Do very gentle stretches only if your doctor tells you to.
Slowly start walking short distances as your bone starts to feel better.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check if your body is still fighting an infection.
X-rays to look inside your body and see the bone.
An MRI scan to get a very clear picture of the infected area.
A small sample test where doctors check the germ causing the problem.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have bone pain that does not go away
If skin near the bone is very red and hot
If you have a fever and feel sick
If a wound near a bone will not heal

osteoporosis.basic_details: Osteoporosis is a condition that makes your bones weak and brittle, so they can break easily like a dry twig. It happens when your body loses too much bone as you get older.
reason: Lack of calcium and vitamin D
emergency_signs: Bone breaking easily from a minor bump or fall
Numbness or weakness in the legs
precautions: Eat a diet rich in calcium and vitamin D
Remove tripping hazards at home to prevent falls
things_to_avoid: Walking in the dark or on slippery floors
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of foods rich in calcium, like milk, cheese, and yogurt.
Get enough vitamin D from sunshine and foods like eggs and fish to help your body use calcium.
Eat leafy green vegetables like spinach and kale every day.
Limit how much salt and soda you have, as they can weaken your bones.
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition, so it does not just go away in a few weeks.
Making your bones stronger takes many months or even years of good care.
If you break a bone, it usually takes about six to eight weeks to heal.
You will need to keep up with healthy habits for the rest of your life.
physical_activities: Do light weight-lifting exercises to make your bones and muscles stronger.
Go for regular walks to help keep your hips and legs strong.
Try simple balance exercises like standing on one foot to avoid falling.

Rest completely until the doctor says it's safe

Treat the root cause of the swelling

Take slow, gentle walks only if your doctor says it is safe for you.
Listen to your body and stop moving right away if your chest starts to hurt.

Get an X-ray picture of your chest to see the size and shape of your heart.

Avoid alcohol and sugary drinks which can slow down how your body heals.

peritonitis.basic_details: Peritonitis is a painful swelling of the inner lining of your belly, usually caused by a germ infection. It is a serious medical issue that needs a doctor's care right away.

Draining infected fluid from the belly

Feeling very dizzy or throwing up a lot

Drink warm or cool liquids to stay hydrated

Drink lots of cool water and clear broths to stay hydrated while healing.
Avoid eating spicy, sour, or crunchy foods that can scratch and irritate your throat.
Stay away from hot drinks and acidic juices until your throat feels much better.
treatment_options: Doctor drains the pus with a needle
Small cut to let the pus out
Surgery to remove tonsils if it happens again
recovery_time: Most people start feeling noticeable relief within two to three days after getting treatment.

Have a doctor run tests to find the cause

Have an X-ray or scan of your belly to look inside your stomach.

Give a sample to check for any hidden germs or infections.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you cannot keep any water down
If you feel very weak or dizzy
If vomiting lasts more than two days
If you see blood in the vomit

personality disorder.basic_details: A personality disorder makes it hard for a person to think, feel, and get along with others in a normal way. This can cause a lot of trouble in their daily life and relationships.

Learn healthy ways to handle intense emotions

Answer questions about how you act and feel in different situations.
Fill out simple paper forms that check your mood and habits.
Have a basic physical health checkup with your family doctor to make sure you are healthy.

phimosis.basic_details: Phimosis is a common condition where the skin at the tip of the male private part is too tight to pull back easily. It is often normal in young boys, but can need gentle care or treatment in adults.
