when_to_visit_doctor: High fever does not go down

pneumothorax.basic_details: A pneumothorax happens when air gets trapped in the space between your lung and your chest wall. This extra air pushes on your lung and can make it partly or fully collapse, causing sudden chest pain and trouble breathing.
reason: Genetics (tall, thin people are at higher risk)
Lung diseases like COPD or asthma
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Follow all instructions if a chest tube is placed
Rest completely while the lung heals
things_to_avoid: Flying in an airplane before the doctor approves
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to stay well hydrated.
Choose high-fiber foods like whole grains to prevent heavy straining.
Eat smaller, easy-to-digest meals so you do not feel uncomfortably full.
treatment_options: using a needle to remove air
putting a small tube in the chest
recovery_time: Most people start to feel significantly better within one to two weeks.
Full healing of the lung and chest area usually takes about four to six weeks.
Your recovery speed depends on how much of the lung collapsed and the treatment used.
You must rest a lot during the first few weeks to let your body repair itself.
physical_activities: Avoid heavy lifting, intense workouts, and contact sports for at least a month.
Do not fly in airplanes or go scuba diving until your doctor says it is completely safe.
Take slow, gentle walks around your home to keep your blood moving.
Stop immediately and rest if you feel any shortness of breath or sharp chest pain.
recommended_tests: A chest X-ray is the main picture test used to see the trapped air and the collapsed lung.
A CT scan may be done to get a more detailed look at your lungs and chest.
Pulse oximetry uses a small clip on your finger to check the oxygen level in your blood.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) might be done to check your heart and make sure it is beating normally.

poisoning due to analgesics.basic_details: Poisoning due to analgesics happens when a person takes too much pain relief medicine by accident or on purpose. This can make them very sick and requires quick medical help.
reason: Taking too much Tylenol (acetaminophen) or ibuprofen
emergency_signs: Yellowing of the skin and eyes
Extreme confusion or inability to wake up
precautions: Call poison control or emergency services immediately
Bring the pill bottles to the hospital
Keep medicines locked away from children
things_to_avoid: Making the person vomit unless told to by poison control
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to help flush the medicine out of your system.
Eat simple foods like plain toast, rice, or crackers if your stomach feels upset.
Avoid spicy, greasy, or heavy foods until your stomach feels completely normal.
Do not drink any alcohol while your body is healing from the medicine.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel a little better after one or two days of hospital care.
Full healing at home usually takes about one to two weeks depending on the amount taken.
Your energy levels might stay low for a short while as your body gets its strength back.
Follow-up checkups may take a few weeks to make sure your organs are working well.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest during the first few days while you are feeling weak.
Avoid heavy lifting, intense workouts, or hard labor until your doctor says it is safe.
Take slow, gentle walks around the room once you have more energy to help your body move.
Listen to your body and stop immediately if you feel dizzy or tired.
recommended_tests: Blood tests are done to check how much of the pain medicine is still in your body.
Liver function tests check if the medicine has caused any stress or damage to your liver.
Kidney function tests make sure your kidneys are working properly and filtering waste.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) checks your heart rhythm to make sure the medicine did not affect your heart.
when_to_visit_doctor: Immediately after taking too many pills
If you feel sick or throw up
If you feel very sleepy or dizzy

poisoning due to anticonvulsants.basic_details: Poisoning due to anticonvulsants happens when a person takes too much of their seizure-control medicine. This can make them very sleepy, dizzy, or sick.
reason: Taking too high a dose of seizure medicine
Mixing seizure pills with alcohol or other drugs
emergency_signs: Breathing becomes very slow or stops
Extreme confusion and loss of balance
precautions: Keep the person safe from falling
Bring all pill bottles to the hospital
Get regular blood tests to check medicine levels
things_to_avoid: Giving the person food or drink
Changing medicine doses without a doctor
Mixing medicines without checking with a pharmacist
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of plain water to help flush your body.
Eat light foods like toast and soup if your stomach feels upset.
Avoid alcohol completely while your body is healing.
Eat small meals throughout the day instead of big ones.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within one to three days.
Severe cases might need a few days of watching closely in the hospital.
You may feel tired or weak for a short time after going home.
Full recovery depends on how much extra medicine was taken.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest while you are recovering.
Avoid driving or using heavy tools until you are fully awake and steady.
Take very slow, short walks around your room only if you feel strong enough.
Ask for help if you need to stand up, as you might feel dizzy.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check the level of medicine in your body.
Heart monitoring tests to make sure your heart is beating normally.
Brain checks to see how alert and awake you are.
Urine tests to check how well your body is cleaning itself.

poisoning due to antimicrobial drugs.basic_details: Poisoning due to antimicrobial drugs happens when you take too much of a medicine used to fight infections, or when your body reacts badly to it. This can make you feel sick and can harm your organs if you do not get help.
reason: Taking the wrong dose of antibiotics
Liver or kidneys failing to clear the drug
precautions: Stop taking the medicine and seek emergency help
Tell all doctors about drug allergies
Drink water if able to swallow safely
Bring the medicine bottle to the hospital
things_to_avoid: Taking leftover antibiotics from an old illness
Taking anti-diarrhea pills if stool is bloody
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to help flush the medicine out of your body.
Eat plain foods like rice, toast, and bananas to be gentle on your stomach.
Stay away from spicy, greasy, or heavy foods until you feel better.
Avoid alcohol completely while your body is healing from the medicine.
treatment_options: Go to the hospital right away
Wash out the stomach if needed
recovery_time: Most people start to feel a bit better within one to two days.
Severe cases might take a week or longer to fully heal.
Your recovery speed depends on how much medicine you took.
Resting as much as possible helps your body bounce back faster.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and get plenty of rest for the first few days.
Do not do any heavy lifting, running, or hard exercises.
Take slow, short walks around the room only when you feel strong enough.
Stop moving and rest immediately if you feel dizzy or tired.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check how well your kidneys and liver are working.
A urine test to see how your body is filtering waste.
Heart monitoring to make sure your heartbeat is safe and steady.
Checking the levels of the medicine still in your bloodstream.

poisoning due to gas.basic_details: Poisoning due to gas happens when you breathe in harmful fumes or toxic gases, which makes it hard for your body to get enough clean air. This can make you feel very sick, dizzy, or short of breath.
reason: Running a car in a closed garage
emergency_signs: Passing out or inability to wake up
precautions: Install carbon monoxide detectors in the home
things_to_avoid: Staying inside the building to find the leak
Lighting a match or turning on light switches (could cause explosion)
Using generators or charcoal grills indoors
Ignoring dizziness or headaches when heating is on
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of plain water to help flush out your system.
Eat light foods like soups, toast, and crackers if your stomach feels upset.
Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy foods until you feel completely better.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body regain its strength.
recovery_time: Mild cases can get better within a few hours to a couple of days after getting fresh air.
Moderate exposure might take a week of rest for your lungs and body to heal.
Severe cases can take several weeks or months of ongoing medical care.
Your exact recovery time depends heavily on the type of gas and how long you breathed it in.
physical_activities: Rest completely in bed during the first few days while your body heals.
Avoid any heavy lifting, running, or hard workouts until a doctor says it is safe.
Take very slow, short walks around the house only when you feel strong enough.
Stop moving and rest immediately if you feel dizzy or out of breath.
recommended_tests: A blood test to check the amount of oxygen and harmful gases in your blood.
A pulse oximeter test using a small clip on your finger to check your oxygen levels.
A chest X-ray to make sure your lungs are clear and undamaged.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) to check that your heart is beating normally.

poisoning due to sedatives.basic_details: Poisoning due to sedatives happens when a person takes too many sleeping pills or calming medicines. This makes the brain and body slow down too much.
emergency_signs: Breathing is very slow or stops
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water to help flush the medicine out of your system.
Eat light foods like soup or toast if your stomach feels upset.
Avoid alcohol completely while your body is healing.
Eat small meals throughout the day so you do not feel too heavy or sick.
treatment_options: Go to the hospital right away
Give medicine to reverse the sedative
Watch the heart and breathing closely
recovery_time: Most people start to wake up and feel better within one to two days.
Total recovery from extreme tiredness can take up to a week.
Your sleep schedule might be messed up for a few days.
You may feel a bit weak or dizzy for a short time after getting out of the hospital.
physical_activities: Rest in bed as much as possible during the first few days.
Do not drive a car, ride a bike, or use heavy tools until a doctor says it is safe.
Take slow, short walks around the room only when you feel steady on your feet.
Ask a family member to help you if you need to get up to walk.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check how much medicine is still in your body.
Checks on your heart rate, blood pressure, and breathing speed.
A urine test to see if your kidneys are cleaning your blood properly.
Mental alertness checks to make sure you are waking up normally.
when_to_visit_doctor: Person is very sleepy or cannot wake up
Breathing is very slow or hard
Person took too many sleeping pills

polycystic kidney disease.basic_details: Polycystic kidney disease is a health issue where fluid-filled sacs, called cysts, grow inside your kidneys. This can make your kidneys get bigger and stop them from cleaning your blood the right way.
emergency_signs: Sudden severe pain in the back or side
Large amount of blood in urine
things_to_avoid: Taking ibuprofen or pain pills without asking
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of plain water all through the day to help flush your system.
Eat less salt to help keep your blood pressure at a healthy level.
Choose fresh fruits and vegetables instead of heavily packaged foods.
Eat smaller amounts of protein, like chicken or beans, to not overwork your kidneys.
treatment_options: eating healthy food low in salt
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition that does not simply go away in a few weeks.
Daily healthy habits help you feel your best over the course of your life.
If you need a special surgery to drain large cysts, healing takes a few weeks.
Regular check-ups help you manage the condition for the long run.
physical_activities: Go for light walks most days to keep your heart and body strong.
Try gentle swimming since it is easy on your back and belly.
Avoid rough sports or heavy weightlifting that could crash into your kidneys.
Do easy stretching to stay flexible and keep your body moving.
recommended_tests: Ultrasound scans to look at the size and number of cysts in your kidneys.
Blood tests to check how well your kidneys are cleaning your blood.
Urine tests to look for blood or other signs of trouble.
Regular blood pressure checks to make sure your heart stays safe.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have severe pain in your back or sides
if you see blood in your urine
if your blood pressure stays very high
if you have a fever and chills

polycystic ovarian syndrome (pcos).basic_details: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is a common health issue where a woman's body makes more of certain hormones than usual. This can cause irregular periods, weight gain, and make it harder to get pregnant.
emergency_signs: Very heavy bleeding soaking pads hourly
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh vegetables and fruits every day.
Choose whole wheat bread and brown rice instead of white bread and white rice.
Cut down on sugary snacks, candies, and sodas.
Eat healthy fats like nuts, seeds, and avocados.
common_medicines: Birth control pills to fix periods
Diabetes medicine to lower sugar and hormones
treatment_options: Eat healthy food and lose weight
recovery_time: PCOS is a long-term condition that does not completely go away.
Symptoms can be managed well and controlled over time.
Many women start to feel better and see regular periods within 3 to 6 months of changing habits.
Consistent daily care is needed to keep your body feeling healthy.
physical_activities: Go for a brisk walk for 30 minutes every day.
Try fun dancing or swimming to keep your heart healthy.
Do light yoga or stretching to help lower your stress levels.
Lift light weights or do bodyweight exercises like squats twice a week.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check your hormone and sugar levels.
An ultrasound scan to look at your ovaries.
A check of your blood pressure and cholesterol levels.
A pelvic exam done by your doctor to check for any physical signs.
when_to_visit_doctor: Your monthly period stops or is very late
You try to get pregnant for a year without success
You have very bad pelvic pain
You grow thick hair on your face

polycythemia vera.basic_details: Polycythemia vera is a rare blood disease where your bone marrow makes too many red blood cells. This makes your blood thick, which can slow down flow and cause health problems.
reason: Bone marrow makes too many red blood cells
emergency_signs: Sudden numbness or weakness on one side
precautions: Get regular blood drawn at the clinic
things_to_avoid: Hot baths that cause severe itching
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to help keep your blood from getting too thick.
Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body strong.
Try to eat less red meat and iron-rich foods, as iron can help your body make even more blood cells.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread instead of white bread and sweets.
treatment_options: Removing extra blood from the body
Taking medicines to lower blood cell count
Treating itchy skin and other symptoms
recovery_time: This is a long-term condition that does not go away completely, so it needs lifelong care.
With the right treatment, most people live a normal life span and feel much better.
You will need regular check-ups with your doctor to keep your blood counts stable.
Energy levels can improve quickly once your blood is no longer too thick.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks every day to keep your blood moving and your heart healthy.
Do light stretching to stay flexible without pushing your body too hard.
Stop and rest immediately if you start feeling dizzy, tired, or out of breath.
Avoid heavy, intense workouts or contact sports to lower your risk of injury and bleeding.
recommended_tests: Routine blood tests to check the number of red blood cells in your body.
Genetic blood tests to look for specific gene changes linked to this condition.
Bone marrow biopsies to see how your blood cells are being made inside your bones.
Regular checks of your blood pressure and iron levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel dizzy or have severe headaches
You notice unusual bleeding or bruising
You have pain or swelling in your legs

polymyalgia rheumatica.basic_details: Polymyalgia rheumatica is a condition that causes strong stiffness and aching in your shoulders, neck, and hips. It usually happens to older adults and makes everyday movements hard.
emergency_signs: Loss of vision in one eye
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Cut back on sugary snacks and salty foods to avoid swelling.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day.
treatment_options: Take steroid pills to lower swelling
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within a few days of starting treatment.
Total recovery usually takes anywhere from one to two years.
Some people might need treatment for a bit longer if symptoms return.
Your doctor will slowly lower your medicine dose as you get better.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks every day to keep your joints moving.
Do light stretching to help reduce stiffness in your shoulders and hips.
Avoid heavy lifting and intense workouts until you are fully healed.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel tired.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check for signs of inflammation in your body.
A blood count test to check for anemia, which is common with this condition.
Kidney and liver function tests to make sure you are healthy overall.
Physical exams where your doctor checks your muscle strength and movement.
when_to_visit_doctor: If shoulder and hip pain starts
If stiffness happens in the morning

post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd).basic_details: Post-traumatic stress disorder, or PTSD, is a mental health condition that can happen after you go through a very scary or shocking event. It causes bad memories, nightmares, and makes you feel on edge long after the event is over.
things_to_avoid: Using alcohol or drugs to forget
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and veggies every day.
Drink a lot of water to keep your body healthy.
Try to eat less sugar and junk food.
Eat healthy fats like fish and nuts to help your brain.
recovery_time: Healing from PTSD takes time and is different for everyone.
Some people start to feel better in a few months.
Others may need help for several years to heal fully.
Taking small steps every day leads to long-term healing.
physical_activities: Go for short, relaxing walks outside in nature.
Try gentle stretching or yoga to calm your body.
Do light workouts like swimming or riding a bike.
Dance to your favorite music to lift your mood.
recommended_tests: Talk with a mental health doctor about your feelings.
Fill out simple question sheets about your daily mood.
Have a basic check-up with your family doctor.
Sleep studies if you have trouble resting at night.
when_to_visit_doctor: if fear does not go away
if you feel very sad often
if daily life is too hard

postoperative infection.basic_details: A postoperative infection happens when germs get into a cut or wound after you have surgery. It can cause redness, swelling, pain, and sometimes fever.
emergency_signs: Red streaks spreading from the wound
precautions: Wash hands before touching the bandage
Keep the wound clean and dry
things_to_avoid: Touching the wound with dirty hands
Soaking in a bathtub or pool
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to flush out toxins.
Eat foods with protein, like chicken, eggs, and beans, to repair your skin.
Stay away from sugary snacks and junk food that can slow down healing.
treatment_options: second surgery to wash out infection
recovery_time: Most minor infections start getting better within a few days of starting treatment.
It can take two to four weeks for the skin and wound to heal completely.
Larger or deeper infections might take a month or more to go away.
Your healing time depends a lot on your overall health and following doctor orders.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest in bed so your body can fight the infection.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until the wound is fully healed.
Take short, gentle walks around the house to keep your blood moving.
Do not stretch or pull the skin around the area where you had surgery.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check if your body is fighting an infection.
A swab test where a doctor gently touches the wound to find the exact germ.
Temperature checks to see if you have a fever.
Imaging scans, like an x-ray, if the doctor needs to look deeper inside.
when_to_visit_doctor: wound smells bad or has pus

postpartum depression.basic_details: Postpartum depression is a deep sadness and heavy worry that some mothers feel after having a baby. It is very common and makes it hard to care for yourself and your new little one.
reason: Sudden drop in hormones after birth
Stress of caring for a new baby
emergency_signs: Total inability to get out of bed
precautions: Ask family for help with the baby
things_to_avoid: Hiding your feelings out of guilt
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and veggies every day to keep your energy up.
Drink lots of water to help your body heal and stay strong.
Eat fish, nuts, and eggs to help boost your mood.
Try not to eat too much sugary food or fast food.
treatment_options: Getting help with the baby and sleep
recovery_time: Every mom is different, so healing takes its own sweet time.
Many women start to feel better within a few months with good help.
Some moms might need up to a year to feel fully like themselves again.
Be patient and kind to yourself on both good and hard days.
physical_activities: Take a slow, gentle walk outside in the fresh air.
Do some light stretching to help your tired muscles relax.
Try deep breathing exercises when you feel stressed or overwhelmed.
Do not push your body too hard; rest whenever you can.
recommended_tests: Answer a simple set of questions about your feelings with your doctor.
Get a blood test to check if your thyroid is working right.
Check your vitamin levels, like vitamin D and iron, with a blood check.
Talk openly with a mental health expert about your thoughts and emotions.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel very sad or hopeless every day
You cannot bond with your baby
You feel like you cannot care for your baby
You feel very anxious or have panic attacks

preeclampsia.basic_details: Preeclampsia is a serious condition during pregnancy marked by high blood pressure and signs that some organs, like the liver and kidneys, may not be working properly.
reason: Problems with blood vessels in the placenta
emergency_signs: Severe headache that will not stop
Severe pain in the upper right belly
Sudden massive swelling of face and hands
diet_recommendation: Eat less salt to help keep your blood pressure down.
Drink plenty of water every day to stay well hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables with every meal.
Avoid greasy, fried, and very sugary foods.
treatment_options: Stay in the hospital for tests
recovery_time: Blood pressure usually starts to go down within a few days after having the baby.
Most women feel much better after about six weeks post-delivery.
Some mothers might need a few months for their bodies to fully heal.
Doctors will keep checking your health for several weeks after you go home.
physical_activities: Rest in bed as much as your doctor tells you to.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard chores around the house.
Take very slow, short walks only if your doctor says it is safe.
Keep your feet up when you sit down to help with swelling.
recommended_tests: Check your blood pressure many times a day.
Give a urine sample to test for protein.
Have blood tests to check how your liver and kidneys are doing.
Get ultrasound scans to check on the baby's growth and health.
when_to_visit_doctor: You have a very bad headache
You have pain in your upper belly
Your face and hands swell up fast

premature atrial contractions (pacs).basic_details: Premature atrial contractions (PACs) are extra heartbeats that start in the upper chambers of your heart, making it feel like your heart skipped a beat or did a flip-flop. They are usually harmless and very common.
emergency_signs: Heart racing very fast and not slowing down
precautions: See a cardiologist for a checkup
diet_recommendation: Drink less coffee, soda, and other drinks with caffeine
Cut back on alcoholic drinks since they can trigger extra heartbeats
Eat plenty of fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated
treatment_options: Cut down on caffeine and alcohol
recovery_time: Extra heartbeats often come and go naturally without needing a long recovery
Many people feel better within a few minutes just by resting and breathing deeply
If caused by stress, you might feel better after a few days of relaxation
It is a chronic condition for some, meaning it may happen from time to time over your life
physical_activities: Do light exercises like walking, swimming, or gentle yoga
Avoid working out too hard if it seems to bring on the extra beats
Try deep breathing or meditation to help keep your body and heart calm
Stop and rest immediately if you feel dizzy or short of breath while moving
recommended_tests: An electrocardiogram (ECG) to take a picture of your heart's electrical signals
A small monitor you wear for a day or two to catch the extra beats
Blood tests to check if your vitamin levels or thyroid are normal
An ultrasound of your heart to make sure your heart muscle is healthy
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel your heart skip beats often
You feel pain in your chest

premature ovarian failure.basic_details: Premature ovarian failure means your ovaries stop working normally before you turn 40. This makes it harder to get pregnant and lowers your body's natural female hormones.
emergency_signs: Severe depression and thoughts of self-harm
precautions: Discuss hormone replacement therapy with a doctor
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of dairy products like milk and yogurt to keep your bones strong.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables every day to help your whole body stay healthy.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for steady energy.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
recovery_time: This condition does not go away completely, so it needs ongoing care.
Most women start feeling better within a few weeks of beginning hormone treatment.
Bone health improvements take many months of steady care and good habits.
You will need regular check-ups with your doctor for the rest of your life.
physical_activities: Go for brisk walks for 30 minutes most days to keep your heart healthy.
Do light weightlifting or yoga to make your bones and muscles stronger.
Try deep breathing or meditation to lower your daily stress levels.
Avoid very heavy or exhausting workouts that make you feel too tired.
recommended_tests: Get a blood test to check your hormone levels.
Have a bone density scan to see how strong your bones are.
Get a pelvic ultrasound to look closely at your ovaries.
Do genetic blood tests if your doctor wants to check for specific causes.

premature ventricular contractions (pvcs.basic_details: Premature ventricular contractions are extra heartbeats that make your heart feel like it is skipping a beat or fluttering. They are very common and usually not harmful for most people.
reason: Heart disease or past heart attack
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body and heart hydrated.
Cut back on coffee, energy drinks, and other things with a lot of caffeine.
Eat less salty food to help keep your blood pressure steady.
Limit or avoid drinking alcohol, as it can trigger these extra beats.
common_medicines: Beta blockers to calm the heart
treatment_options: Cutting back on caffeine and stress
Catheter ablation to fix heart signals
recovery_time: Because this is a long-term heart rhythm pattern rather than a short injury, there is no set recovery time.
Many people notice their symptoms come and go depending on their stress and sleep levels.
Making healthy lifestyle changes can help you feel better in just a few weeks.
Some people stop feeling these extra beats entirely once they lower their daily stress.
physical_activities: Do light exercises like walking, swimming, or gentle bike riding.
Always warm up slowly before you start working out.
Stop and rest right away if you feel dizzy, super tired, or short of breath.
Avoid super intense workouts if you notice they make your heart flutter more.
recommended_tests: An ECG test to take a quick picture of your heart's electrical signals.
A small monitor you wear for a day or two to record your heartbeats.
Blood tests to check if your body has the right amount of important vitamins and minerals.
An ultrasound of your heart to make sure the heart muscle is strong and healthy.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you feel new or worse dizziness
If your heart feels like it is racing constantly
If you feel very short of breath
If you faint or pass out

premenstrual tension syndrome.basic_details: Premenstrual tension syndrome is a mix of body and mood changes that happen to many women a week or two before their monthly period starts. It can make you feel grumpy, tired, or bloated.
reason: Normal hormonal changes before a period
emergency_signs: Pain so severe you cannot walk
precautions: Use a heating pad for cramps
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and veggies every day.
Cut down on salty foods to stop feeling bloated.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated.
Try to eat less sugar and caffeine so your mood stays steady.
recovery_time: Symptoms usually go away on their own a couple of days after your period starts.
You might feel better within a few hours after taking pain medicine.
Making healthy lifestyle changes can make you feel better over the course of two to three monthly cycles.
Resting during the tough days helps your body bounce back faster.
physical_activities: Go for a short, easy walk outside to clear your mind.
Do some light stretching or yoga to loosen up tight muscles.
Swim gently to help with body aches and cramps.
Try slow breathing exercises to help you feel calm and relaxed.
recommended_tests: Keep a daily diary to track your moods and body pains.
Do a basic blood check to make sure your iron levels are normal.
Have a chat with your doctor about your monthly cycle history.
Check your vitamin levels with a simple blood test if you feel extra tired.

presbyacusis.basic_details: Presbyacusis is the slow loss of hearing that happens naturally as people get older. It usually affects both ears equally and makes it hard to hear high-pitched sounds.
emergency_signs: Sudden complete loss of hearing in one ear
precautions: Look at people when they speak
things_to_avoid: Using cotton swabs deep in the ear
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy.
Include fish in your meals, as it has good fats for your ears.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Try to eat less salt and junk food to protect your overall health.
recovery_time: Hearing loss from aging cannot be reversed or cured completely.
Getting used to a hearing aid can take a few weeks of practice.
Learning to read lips or use new communication tools takes time.
Accepting the change in your ears is an ongoing process of adjustment.
physical_activities: Go for daily walks to keep your body moving and healthy.
Do light stretching exercises to stay active and flexible.
Try gentle yoga to help you relax and lower your stress.
Stay away from very loud places like concerts or noisy construction zones.
recommended_tests: Get a basic hearing checkup with an ear doctor or specialist.
Take a pure-tone test where you listen for beeps in headphones.
Try a speech test to see how well you understand words in noise.
Have your ears checked for any wax blocking the ear canal.
when_to_visit_doctor: family says you turn the TV up too loud
ringing in your ears gets worse

presbyopia.basic_details: Presbyopia is a normal eye condition where your eyes slowly lose the ability to focus up close as you get older. It usually starts when people reach their 40s.
reason: Natural aging of the eye lens
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of green leafy vegetables like spinach and kale to keep your eyes healthy.
Eat colorful fruits like oranges and carrots which are great for your vision.
Eat fish that have healthy oils, such as salmon, at least once a week.
Drink plenty of water every day to stop your eyes from feeling dry.
recovery_time: Presbyopia is a natural part of aging, so it does not completely go away.

Have an eye doctor look inside your eyes with a special light to check their overall health.

when_to_visit_doctor: If the spot starts to bleed
If it hurts or feels itchy
If it changes color or size fast
If you are not sure what the spot is

Avoiding loud noises to protect hearing

If you feel ringing in your ears

Eat soft foods if your stomach feels upset or weak.

Surgery to wash out the joint

Blood tests to check if your body is fighting off a bad infection.
X-rays of the sore joint to look inside and see if the bones are safe.

You cannot move the painful joint
You have a fever with joint pain

Keep the rash clean and dry

If the rash is near your eye
If the pain is very bad

sialoadenitis.basic_details: Sialoadenitis is a painful swelling of the glands in your mouth that make spit, usually caused by a germ infection or a tiny block.

Avoid heavy lifting, running, or hard workouts until you feel fully well.

Blood tests may be ordered if the doctor thinks you need a closer checkup.

sick sinus syndrome.basic_details: Sick sinus syndrome is a heart condition where the natural pacemaker of your heart fails to set a steady and normal pace. This can cause your heart to beat too slow, too fast, or skip beats.

Drink lots of water and stay away from too much caffeine.
Cut down on salty and greasy foods to keep your heart healthy.

Most people return to their normal daily routine within one month.
Total healing time depends on your age and overall health.
physical_activities: Take light walks every day to keep your body moving gently.

Join a gentle heart rehabilitation program if your doctor suggests it.

An ultrasound of your heart to see how well it is pumping blood.

Resting as soon as you feel tired helps your body bounce back much faster.
Healing time depends on how well you drink water and rest when you feel unwell.
physical_activities: Do light walking or gentle stretching to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Always stop and rest the moment you start feeling short of breath or overly exhausted.
Avoid heavy sports or running so hard that you push your body past its safe limits.

Go for regular check-ups with your main doctor to keep an eye on your health.

things_to_avoid: Heavy lifting if it causes pain
Ignoring a lump that gets hard or grows fast
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to stay well hydrated.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and oats.
Limit very salty and processed foods to avoid swelling.
recovery_time: If you do not have surgery, it just stays the same and heals on its own.
If you have minor surgery to remove it, normal healing takes about two weeks.
Most people can go back to light daily tasks within a few days.
Full healing of the sore area can take up to a month.
physical_activities: Rest and avoid heavy lifting for the first few days.
Wear supportive underwear to help ease any pulling or pain.
Skip hard exercises like running or weightlifting until you feel better.
Slowly go back to your normal workouts when your doctor says it is okay.
recommended_tests: A doctor will gently feel the area with their hands during a physical check.
An ultrasound uses safe sound waves to take a clear picture of the fluid sac.
Sometimes a bright light is shined through the scrotum to see if the lump is filled with fluid.
A simple urine test might be done to make sure there is no infection.
when_to_visit_doctor: if the lump gets very big
if the scrotum turns red or hot
if you feel a new hard lump

spina bifida.basic_details: Spina bifida is a condition where a baby's spine does not close all the way before birth. This can cause some nerve and muscle weakness.
reason: Lack of folic acid during early pregnancy
emergency_signs: Sudden inability to move the legs
Loss of bowel or bladder control
High fever with a red, swollen back
Severe swelling of the baby's head
precautions: Take folic acid before and during pregnancy
Work closely with a medical team for the child
Use wheelchairs or leg braces as prescribed
things_to_avoid: Latex products (many with this condition are allergic)
Ignoring fevers or changes in leg strength
Poor skin care that could lead to bedsores
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to keep your tummy healthy.
Include foods with fiber like beans and whole grains.
Eat foods with calcium like milk or yogurt for strong bones.
recovery_time: Recovery after back surgery usually takes several weeks to heal.
Getting used to walking aids is a lifelong learning process.
Every person heals at their own speed and time.
Regular check-ups help your body stay strong as you grow.
physical_activities: Try swimming to build strength without hurting your joints.
Do gentle stretches every day to keep your muscles loose.
Play sports using your arms and wheelchair if you use one.
Go for short, easy walks if your doctor says it is okay.
recommended_tests: Get regular check-ups with your spine doctor.
Have your kidneys checked to make sure they are healthy.
Take picture scans of your back to see how your spine looks.
Do tests to check how well your bladder is working.
when_to_visit_doctor: problems with bladder or bowel control

spinal stenosis.basic_details: Spinal stenosis happens when the space inside your backbone gets too narrow. This can squeeze your nerves and cause pain, numbness, or weakness in your back and legs.
reason: Aging and arthritis in the spine
emergency_signs: Loss of bowel or bladder control
Sudden severe numbness in the groin or inner thighs
Extreme weakness in the legs preventing standing
Pain so severe you cannot move
precautions: Use a cane or walker to prevent falls
Lean forward slightly when walking to relieve pain
things_to_avoid: Staying in bed for too long
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your joints hydrated.
Stay away from sugary snacks and junk food that can cause unwanted weight gain.
recovery_time: Healing takes time and usually improves slowly over several weeks or months.
Mild cases often get better with simple rest and gentle home care.
Severe cases that need surgery might require a few months to fully heal.
Listening to your body and not rushing helps ensure a safe and steady recovery.
physical_activities: Take short, easy walks on flat ground to keep your body moving safely.
Try gentle water aerobics, as the water takes pressure off your spine.
Do simple stretching exercises for your back taught by a professional.
Avoid heavy lifting, twisting, or high-impact sports that hurt your back.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray so doctors can look closely at the bones in your spine.
Have an MRI scan to take detailed pictures of your nerves and tissues.
Take a CT scan if your doctor needs a sharper 3D view of your backbone.
Undergo a nerve checkup test to see how well your nerves are working.

spondylitis.basic_details: Spondylitis is a type of long-term swelling in the spine that causes back pain and stiffness. Over time, it can make your back feel very tight and hard to move.
emergency_signs: Sudden severe back pain after a minor fall
Red, painful eyes with blurry vision
precautions: Do daily stretching and back exercises
things_to_avoid: Sitting in slouched positions for hours
Using very thick pillows under the head
Heavy physical strain on the back
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to help lower body swelling.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread for better energy.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your joints and muscles hydrated.
Try to eat less sugary snacks and fried foods, as they can make swelling worse.
recovery_time: Spondylitis is a lifelong condition, so recovery means managing symptoms rather than a total cure.
Good days and bad days will happen, and pain levels can change over weeks and months.
Daily stretching and medicine help you feel better and recover from stiff mornings faster.
Staying active consistently helps you feel good for the long run instead of just a few days.
physical_activities: Do gentle stretching every morning to help your back feel less stiff.
Go for short, easy walks daily to keep your spine moving smoothly.
Try swimming, as the water takes the heavy pressure off your back joints.
Do easy yoga poses designed to make your back and neck more flexible.
recommended_tests: An X-ray of your back lets the doctor see the bones in your spine.
An MRI scan helps the doctor look closely at the soft parts around your spine.
Blood tests check if there is high swelling or inflammation inside your body.
A physical checkup where the doctor gently moves your back to see where it hurts.
when_to_visit_doctor: Back pain does not go away with rest
Stiffness makes it hard to move in the morning
Pain wakes you up at night
Breathing feels hard due to chest stiffness

spondylolisthesis.basic_details: Spondylolisthesis is a back condition where one of your spine bones slips out of place and rests on the bone below it. This can sometimes pinch nerves and cause lower back pain or leg discomfort.
reason: Birth defect in the spine bones
Sports that put stress on the lower back (like gymnastics)
emergency_signs: Loss of bowel or bladder control
Sudden extreme weakness in the legs
Severe numbness spreading down the legs
precautions: Wear a back brace if prescribed
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body stay healthy and fight inflammation.
Include dairy products or leafy greens like spinach to give your bones the calcium they need.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to keep your back muscles and joints well hydrated.
Try to eat foods high in fiber, like whole grains and beans, to keep your weight in a healthy range.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within a few weeks to a couple of months by resting and being careful.
Full healing takes time, often a few months, depending on how far the bone has slipped.
Doing gentle daily exercises helps speed up your recovery and keeps your back strong.
Listening to your body and not rushing back into heavy lifting will help you heal faster.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks on flat ground to keep your body moving without hurting your back.
Do gentle stretching exercises that your doctor or physical therapist shows you.
Try water aerobics, as the water takes the pressure off your spine while you move.
Avoid heavy lifting, twisting your back sharply, or high-impact sports like running.
recommended_tests: An X-ray of your lower back is usually the first test to see if a bone has slipped.
An MRI scan might be done to get a closer look at your nerves and soft tissues.
A CT scan can sometimes be used to give a very detailed picture of the bone structure.
A physical checkup where the doctor gently presses on your spine and tests your leg strength.
when_to_visit_doctor: back pain does not get better

spondylosis.basic_details: Spondylosis is a normal wear and tear of the spine as people get older. It can cause stiffness and pain in the neck or back.
reason: Wear and tear on spinal discs
emergency_signs: Sudden loss of feeling in arms or legs
Loss of bowel or bladder control
Severe pain radiating down an arm or leg
precautions: Use heat or ice packs for pain
things_to_avoid: High-impact sports like running on hard surfaces
Slouching at a desk all day
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your joints healthy.
Include fish and nuts in your meals to lower swelling and pain.
Eat foods with calcium like milk and cheese to keep bones strong.
recovery_time: Mild pain can go away in just a few days with rest.
Moderate stiffness may take a couple of weeks to feel better.
Long-term wear and tear needs ongoing care rather than a quick fix.
Doing daily exercises helps speed up how fast you feel normal again.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks to keep your back moving gently.
Do slow stretching to help loosen up a stiff neck or back.
Try swimming because water takes the pressure off your spine.
Avoid heavy lifting or twisting your back too fast.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray so the doctor can look at the bones in your spine.
Take an MRI scan to check the soft parts like disks and nerves.
Have a physical checkup where the doctor moves your arms and legs.
Do a nerve test if your hands or feet feel numb or tingly.
when_to_visit_doctor: pain spreads to arms or legs

spontaneous abortion.basic_details: A spontaneous abortion, often called a miscarriage, is when a pregnancy ends on its own before the baby can live outside the womb. This usually happens very early in the pregnancy for reasons that are mostly out of anyone's control.
reason: Genetic or chromosomal problems in the baby
emergency_signs: Heavy bleeding soaking more than a pad an hour
precautions: Seek medical help immediately if bleeding starts
things_to_avoid: Having physical intimacy for a few weeks afterward
Blaming yourself (it is rarely caused by the mother's actions)
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water and clear liquids to stay hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body regain strength.
Choose iron-rich foods like beans and leafy greens to help with blood loss.
Eat warm, simple foods like soups that are easy on your stomach.
recovery_time: Physical healing usually takes a few weeks for bleeding and cramping to stop.
Your hormone levels can take several weeks or a couple of months to return to normal.
Emotional healing takes time, and it is normal to feel sad or grief-stricken for a while.
Every person heals at their own pace, so listen to your body and don't rush.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest during the first few days after it happens.
Avoid heavy lifting, intense workouts, and strenuous chores for at least two weeks.
Take short, gentle walks around your home only when you feel up to it.
Wait until your doctor says it is safe before swimming or taking baths.
recommended_tests: Have a check-up with your doctor to make sure your body has healed fully.
Get a blood test to check your hormone levels and make sure they are dropping properly.
Ask your doctor if blood tests are needed to check for iron levels or other vitamins.
Discuss genetic or other special tests with your doctor only if you have had multiple losses.

sprain or strain.basic_details: A sprain is when you stretch or tear a ligament, which connects bones. A strain is when you stretch or tear a muscle or tendon.
emergency_signs: Hearing a loud 'pop' during the injury
Inability to put any weight on the joint
Joint looks visibly bent or deformed
Extreme swelling and immediate dark bruising
precautions: Apply ice wrapped in a towel
Keep the injured part elevated above the heart
things_to_avoid: Trying to use the injured limb immediately
Applying heat during the first 48 hours
Ignoring a joint that gives out constantly
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your muscles healthy.
Include chicken, fish, or beans in your meals to repair your tissues.
Eat foods like nuts and seeds to help lower swelling.
recovery_time: Mild sprains or strains usually start feeling better in one to two weeks.
More painful or deeper injuries can take four to eight weeks to heal.
Severe tears might need a few months of rest and care.
Everyone heals at their own speed, so do not rush your body.
physical_activities: Rest the injured part and avoid using it for the first few days.
Do very gentle stretches only after the sharp pain goes away.
Slowly return to walking or light movement as you feel stronger.
Stop right away if any movement causes sharp pain or extra swelling.
recommended_tests: A doctor will check the sore spot with their hands to see how it feels.
They might gently move your joint to test your range of motion.
An X-ray may be done to make sure your bone is not broken.
An MRI might be used if the doctor needs a closer look at the tissue.
when_to_visit_doctor: pain does not get better after a few days
you cannot walk or move the joint
you see a strange shape or bump
numbness or tingling in the area

stenosis of the tear duct.basic_details: Stenosis of the tear duct means your tear drainage tube is blocked or narrowed. This causes your eyes to water all the time and can sometimes lead to painful swelling or sticky fluid.
emergency_signs: Eye becomes completely red and swollen shut
Thick, foul-smelling pus draining from the eye
Severe eye pain and vision changes
precautions: Apply warm, wet compresses to the eye
Massage the area gently as directed by a doctor
Use prescribed antibiotic drops if infected
things_to_avoid: Wearing contact lenses during an infection
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal well.
Include foods with Vitamin C like oranges to boost your immune system.
Try to eat less salty food to prevent any extra swelling around your eyes.
treatment_options: massage the corner of the eye
a tiny tube to open the duct
surgery to make a new drain
recovery_time: If you just need simple massage or probing, you might feel better in a few days.
If you have minor surgery, the eye usually feels better in about one to two weeks.
Full healing inside the tear duct can sometimes take up to four to six weeks.
Your doctor will check on you during follow-up visits to make sure you are healing right.
physical_activities: You can go for light walks outside while wearing sunglasses to block wind and dust.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts that strain your face for a few weeks.
Stay away from swimming pools until your doctor says your eye is fully healed.
Try not to rub or press hard on your eyes while playing sports or moving around.
recommended_tests: A simple eye doctor checkup where they look closely at the corners of your eyelids.
A special dye test where colored drops are put in your eye to see if they drain down your nose.
A tiny probe test where the doctor gently checks if the tear pipe is open.
An imaging scan if the doctor needs a closer look at the bone structure around your tear duct.
when_to_visit_doctor: your eye is very red and hurts
you have swelling near your nose
yellow or green pus comes out of the eye

stomach cancer.basic_details: Stomach cancer happens when unhealthy cells start growing out of control inside your stomach. It can make it hard to eat and digest food properly.
reason: Diet high in salty or smoked foods
things_to_avoid: Eating salty, smoked, or pickled foods
diet_recommendation: Eat five or six small meals throughout the day instead of three big ones.
Choose soft foods that are very easy for your stomach to digest.
Drink plenty of water and clear liquids to stay hydrated.
Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods that can upset your stomach.
recovery_time: Healing takes a lot of time, and every single person is different.
You might feel very tired for the first few weeks or months after treatment.
Full recovery often takes several months as your stomach learns to work again.
Regular check-ups with your doctor will show how well your body is healing.
physical_activities: Start with short, gentle walks around your house or yard.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard exercises until your doctor says it is safe.
Listen to your body and rest whenever you feel tired.
Slowly add a little more walking each day as you get your strength back.
recommended_tests: An endoscopy, where a tiny camera looks inside your stomach.
Blood tests to check your overall health and energy levels.
CT scans to take clear pictures of the inside of your body.
A small tissue check, called a biopsy, to test cells closely.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have belly pain that does not go away
If you feel full after eating a small amount
If you lose weight without trying
If you throw up blood or have dark poop

strep throat.basic_details: Strep throat is a common bacterial infection that makes your throat feel very sore and scratchy. It can also make swallowing painful and cause your tonsils to look red and swollen.
reason: Breathing in droplets from a sneeze or cough
emergency_signs: Severe trouble breathing or swallowing saliva
Dark brown urine or severe joint pain later on
precautions: Drink warm fluids or eat popsicles
things_to_avoid: Stopping antibiotics early because you feel better
Going to school or work while contagious
Eating rough, crunchy foods that hurt the throat
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and scrambled eggs that do not hurt when you swallow.
Drink lots of cold water and warm liquids like tea with honey to soothe your throat.
Avoid eating spicy, crunchy, or acidic foods like chips or citrus fruits that can scratch your throat.
Eat ice cream, popsicles, or soup to keep your throat numb and comfortable.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within 24 to 48 hours after starting antibiotics.
You must finish all your medicine even if you feel completely better so the sickness does not come back.
Your throat pain and fever should completely go away in about 3 to 5 days.
You might feel tired for a few days, so give your body enough time to rest and heal.
physical_activities: Stay home and rest in bed as much as possible while you are sick and contagious.
Avoid heavy exercise, running, or playing sports until your fever is gone and you have energy back.
Sleep and relax so your body can fight off the infection faster.
Do not return to work or school until you have taken antibiotics for at least 24 hours and have no fever.
recommended_tests: Get a rapid strep test where a doctor rubs a cotton swab gently against the back of your throat.
Wait a few minutes for the rapid test to show if strep bacteria are present.
Do a throat culture test if the rapid test is negative but the doctor still thinks you have strep.
Check your temperature with a thermometer to see if you have a fever.
when_to_visit_doctor: if your throat hurts very bad
if you have a high fever
if it is hard to swallow
if white spots are on your tonsils

stress incontinence.basic_details: Stress incontinence is when you leak a little pee by accident when you cough, sneeze, laugh, or jump. It happens because the muscles that hold your pee in get a bit weak.
precautions: Do Kegel exercises daily to strengthen muscles
Talk to a doctor about surgery or devices if severe
things_to_avoid: Drinking too much caffeine or alcohol
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day so your body stays healthy.
Stay away from spicy foods that can make your bladder angry.
Cut back on soda and coffee because they make you pee more often.
Eat more fruits and veggies to stop tummy troubles like pushing too hard.
recovery_time: Getting better takes time and does not happen overnight.
Most people start seeing good changes after doing special exercises for a few months.
Some folks might need a small surgery, which takes a few weeks to heal from.
Every person's body is different, so healing takes its own sweet time.
physical_activities: Do daily squeeze exercises, often called Kegels, to make your bottom muscles strong.
Go for nice and easy walks to stay active without hurting your tummy.
Try gentle yoga to help relax your body and mind.
Avoid heavy lifting and jumping jacks until your muscles get much stronger.
recommended_tests: A simple pee test to make sure you do not have an infection.
A chat with your doctor where you talk about how often you leak.
A special test to see how well your bladder holds water.
An ultrasound picture to look at your bladder and belly area.
when_to_visit_doctor: It stops you from doing normal things
You have pain when you pee
You see blood in your pee

stricture of the esophagus.basic_details: A stricture of the esophagus is when your food pipe narrows down, making it hard for food and liquids to go down easily into your stomach.
reason: Scar tissue from severe acid reflux
emergency_signs: Food completely stuck in the throat
precautions: Eat small bites and eat slowly
Drink plenty of water with meals
things_to_avoid: Eating large pieces of tough meat
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes, yogurt, and oatmeal.
Take small bites and chew your food very well.
Drink plenty of water with your meals to help push food down.
Avoid dry, hard, or sticky foods that can get stuck.
common_medicines: Acid blockers to stop stomach acid
treatment_options: Surgery to fix the tight spot
recovery_time: You may feel better a few hours after a doctor stretches your food pipe.
Full healing can take a few days if your throat was very irritated.
Some people need more than one stretching session to feel totally normal.
You can usually go back to your normal routine the very next day.
physical_activities: You can do light walking and everyday household chores right away.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts for a day or two.
Do not strain your neck or chest area too much.
Listen to your body and rest if you feel tired.
recommended_tests: An upper endoscopy where a tiny camera looks inside your food pipe.
A barium swallow test where you drink a special liquid while taking X-rays.
A biopsy where a small tissue sample is checked for other issues.
A check of your throat by a specialist using a lighted tube.

stroke.basic_details: A stroke happens when blood suddenly stops flowing to a part of your brain. This lack of blood can damage brain cells and make it hard to move, speak, or think clearly.
reason: Blood clot blocking an artery in the brain
Burst blood vessel in the brain
emergency_signs: Sudden numbness or weakness on one side of the face or body
Sudden trouble speaking or understanding speech
Sudden complete loss of vision in one eye
Sudden severe headache with no known cause
precautions: Call emergency services immediately (time is brain)
Take prescribed blood thinners and blood pressure pills
Go to physical and speech therapy
things_to_avoid: Waiting to see if symptoms go away
Giving the person aspirin (unless told to by a doctor, as it could worsen bleeding)
diet_recommendation: Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables every single day.
Choose whole wheat bread and brown rice instead of white bread and white rice.
Use much less salt on your food to help keep your blood pressure low.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day and stay away from sugary sodas.
recovery_time: Most people see the fastest healing happen in the first three to six months.
Some people get better quickly, while others need a year or more to heal.
Healing continues slowly even years after the stroke first happened.
Every person's body is different, so recovery takes its own unique time.
physical_activities: Go for short, gentle walks around your house or neighborhood.
Do simple stretching exercises to keep your arms and legs moving smoothly.
Practice standing up and sitting down from a chair to build leg strength.
Work with a helper to gently move your fingers and hands.
recommended_tests: A brain scan pictures test, like a CT scan or MRI, to look inside your head.
A heart check to see if your ticker is beating normally.
Blood tests to check your sugar and cholesterol levels.
A test to see how well you can safely swallow food and water.

stye.basic_details: A stye is a small, painful red bump that forms on the edge of your eyelid, usually caused by a blocked oil gland. It looks and feels a lot like a pimple right near your eyelashes.
reason: Bacterial infection of an eyelash follicle
Blocked oil gland in the eyelid
emergency_signs: Redness spreading to the cheeks or face
precautions: Apply a warm, wet cloth to the eye for 10 minutes
Wash hands before touching the face
things_to_avoid: Squeezing or trying to pop the stye
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body healthy and hydrated.
Include foods with healthy fats, like fish and nuts, to support eye health.
Try to cut down on sugary snacks and drinks while your eye is healing.
treatment_options: put a warm cloth on the eye
do not squeeze or pop it
recovery_time: Most styes start to get better within three to five days.
The bump usually goes away completely within one to two weeks.
Applying warm compresses early can help speed up your healing time.
Never try to pop or squeeze the stye, as this can make healing take much longer.
physical_activities: You can do light walking and normal daily chores without any problem.
Avoid swimming pools until the stye is gone to keep dirty water out of your eye.
Skip heavy gym workouts that make you sweat a lot into your eyes.
Take a break from wearing contact lenses and stick to regular glasses.
recommended_tests: Most styes do not need any special lab tests to be diagnosed.
A doctor can easily spot a stye just by looking closely at your eyelid.
An eye doctor might use a special lighted magnifying tool for a better look.
A swab test is rarely done only if the infection keeps coming back.
when_to_visit_doctor: it does not get better after a week

subacute thyroiditis.basic_details: Subacute thyroiditis is a temporary swelling of your thyroid gland, usually caused by a viral infection like a cold. It can make your neck feel sore and tender.
reason: Recent viral infection (like a cold or flu)
Immune system reacting to the virus
precautions: Take prescribed heart medicines if your heart races
things_to_avoid: Taking extra thyroid hormone pills without asking a doctor
Heavy exercise if the heart is racing
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Choose soft foods if your throat feels sore or hard to swallow.
Limit spicy and very hot foods if they irritate your throat.
common_medicines: heart rate pills like beta blockers
treatment_options: checking thyroid levels with blood tests
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within a few weeks to a few months.
The whole healing process can take anywhere from three to six months.
Your energy levels and neck pain will improve slowly over time.
Your doctor will check on you regularly to see how your thyroid is healing.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest and sleep to let your body fight the illness.
Avoid heavy lifting and intense workouts while your neck hurts.
Take gentle, short walks around your house if you feel up to it.
Slowly return to your normal routine only when your energy comes back.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check how well your thyroid is working.
Blood tests to check for signs of swelling or inflammation in your body.
A painless picture test, called an ultrasound, to look at your thyroid.
A special scan that uses a tiny, safe amount of tracer to see thyroid activity.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you have pain in the front of your neck
if your heart beats too fast
if you feel very nervous or shaky
if you lose weight without trying

subarachnoid hemorrhage.basic_details: A subarachnoid hemorrhage is a serious type of bleeding in the space that surrounds the brain. It usually happens when a weak spot on a blood vessel in the brain bursts.
emergency_signs: Sudden, worst headache of your life
precautions: Keep the person flat and still
things_to_avoid: Giving the person pain pills like aspirin
Waiting to see if they wake up
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink lots of water to stay hydrated and avoid getting constipated.
Cut down on salty and greasy foods to keep your blood pressure low.
common_medicines: medicine to prevent blood vessel spasms
treatment_options: surgery to fix the broken blood vessel
putting a small coil inside the blood vessel
resting in a quiet hospital room
recovery_time: Most people need to stay in the hospital for a few weeks to be closely watched.
It usually takes several months to start feeling like your normal self again.
Every person heals at their own speed, so try not to rush the process.
You may need ongoing check-ups with your doctor for a long time.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest and sleep as much as your body tells you to.
Start with very gentle walking around your house when you feel ready.
Do not lift anything heavy or do hard exercises until your doctor says it is safe.
Avoid any sports or activities where you could fall or hit your head.
recommended_tests: Special brain scans like a CT scan or MRI to look at the blood vessels.
Check your blood pressure regularly throughout the day.
Blood tests to make sure your body is working properly and medicines are safe.
Checking your heart with an ECG test to see how well it is beating.
when_to_visit_doctor: throwing up and feeling very sick

subconjunctival hemorrhage.basic_details: A subconjunctival hemorrhage happens when a tiny blood vessel breaks just under the clear surface of your eye. This makes a bright red patch appear on the white part of your eye, but it is harmless and does not affect your vision.
reason: High blood pressure or blood thinners
emergency_signs: Blood spreading to the colored part of the eye
precautions: Use artificial tear drops if the eye feels scratchy
Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners
things_to_avoid: Stopping blood thinners without asking a doctor
Worrying (it looks scary but is usually harmless)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy.
Drink lots of water every day to stay well hydrated.
Include foods with vitamin C to help your blood vessels stay strong.
Avoid eating too much salty food to keep your blood pressure normal.
treatment_options: wait for it to heal on its own
stop blood thinners only if your doctor says so
recovery_time: The bright red spot usually goes away completely within one to two weeks.
As it heals, the red patch might change color, looking a bit like a fading bruise.
You do not need to stay home from work or school while your eye heals.
Call your doctor if the redness does not start to get better after two weeks.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily activities without any worries.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts that make you strain too hard.
Do not rub your eye, even if it feels a little bit itchy or weird.
Wear protective glasses if you are doing sports or work that could hurt your eye.
recommended_tests: A doctor can check your eye with a basic light to make sure everything is okay.
You might need a simple blood pressure check to see if it is too high.
Your doctor may ask about any recent heavy coughing, sneezing, or straining.
Usually, no special lab tests or X-rays are needed for this condition.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you feel pain in your eye
if your vision changes or gets blurry
if you have bleeding in both eyes
if it does not go away after two weeks

subdural hemorrhage.basic_details: A subdural hemorrhage happens when blood pools between the brain and its outer covering, usually because of a head injury. This extra blood puts pressure on the brain and can cause serious health issues.
reason: Severe head injury (like a car crash)
Severe alcohol abuse leading to frequent falls
emergency_signs: Unequal pupil sizes in the eyes
Sudden weakness on one side of the body
precautions: Tell the medics if the person is on blood thinners
Follow all surgery and recovery instructions
things_to_avoid: Ignoring a head injury in an older person
Shaking the person to wake them up
Leaving them alone after a bad fall
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay well hydrated.
Include foods rich in protein, like chicken, fish, or beans, to regain your strength.
Avoid alcohol completely because it can interfere with healing and medicines.
recovery_time: Most people need several weeks to feel better, depending on how bad the injury was.
Mild cases may heal in a few weeks with plenty of rest.
Severe cases or surgeries might take many months for a full recovery.
Your brain needs ongoing check-ups to make sure the healing is going well.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest during the first few weeks after the injury.
Avoid heavy lifting, intense workouts, and sports until your doctor says it is safe.
Take short, gentle walks around your home once you start feeling a bit stronger.
Stop and rest immediately if you feel dizzy, tired, or get a headache.
recommended_tests: A CT scan of your head to take clear pictures of the bleeding.
An MRI scan to get a closer and more detailed look at your brain tissue.
Regular blood tests to check how well your blood clots and if your organs are healthy.
Neurological exams to test your memory, balance, speech, and reflexes.
when_to_visit_doctor: weakness on one side of the body

substance-related mental disorder.basic_details: A substance-related mental disorder happens when using drugs or alcohol changes how your brain works, making it hard to control your habits and feelings.
reason: Long-term abuse of drugs or alcohol
precautions: Seek emergency medical or psychiatric help
Remove all drugs and alcohol from the home
things_to_avoid: Arguing with the person about their hallucinations
Quitting heavy alcohol use cold turkey at home (can cause deadly seizures)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to flush out toxins.
Eat meals with lean protein and whole grains to keep your energy steady.
Stay away from too much sugar and caffeine, as they can make you feel more anxious.
recovery_time: The first few weeks are the hardest while your body cleans itself out.
Most people start to feel much better physically after a few months.
Healing your mind and changing old habits can take a full year or more.
Recovery is a lifelong journey that requires daily care and patience.
physical_activities: Go for short daily walks to clear your mind and boost your mood.
Try yoga or gentle stretching to help your body relax.
Join a fun team sport or exercise class to stay connected with others.
Do heavy cleaning or gardening to keep your body busy and active.
recommended_tests: Simple blood tests to check your overall physical health and nutrition.
Urine tests to make sure you are staying away from harmful substances.
Talk sessions with a counselor to check how your mind and mood are doing.
Liver function checks to see if your body is recovering well.
when_to_visit_doctor: you feel very sad or hopeless

syphilis.basic_details: Syphilis is a common infection spread through sexual contact that creates sores on the body. If it is not treated by a doctor, it can cause bigger health problems over time.
reason: Skin-to-skin contact with a syphilis sore
emergency_signs: Inability to walk or move legs
precautions: Take prescribed penicillin or antibiotics immediately
Tell all physical intimacy partners to get tested
things_to_avoid: Having physical intimacy before the infection is fully cured
Ignoring painless sores on the genitals
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your immune system strong.
Drink lots of water every day to help your body stay hydrated and clean.
Eat healthy foods like chicken, fish, and beans to help your body heal faster.
Try to stay away from sugary drinks and fast food while you are getting better.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better and are cured a few weeks after getting their medicine.
Healing time can take a little longer if you have had the infection for a long time.
You must stay away from sexual contact until your doctor says the infection is completely gone.
Your doctor will want to check your blood again later to make sure you are fully healed.
physical_activities: You can do light walking and gentle stretching while you are healing.
Rest as much as you can so your body has the energy to fight the infection.
Avoid heavy workouts or hard exercises until your body feels strong again.
Stop any activity right away if you feel tired or dizzy.
recommended_tests: Doctors use a simple blood test to check if you have the infection.
Sometimes the doctor will check any sores on your skin to test them.
You should also get tested for other infections that happen the same way.
Your partner should get tested and treated too so you do not pass it back and forth.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you see a painless sore
if you have a strange rash
if you feel sick after sex

systemic lupus erythematosis (sle).basic_details: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a long-term health issue where your body's defense system gets confused and attacks your own healthy tissues and organs. This can cause swelling, pain, and tiredness.
reason: Autoimmune system attacking the body's own tissues
Sun exposure or viral infections triggering it
emergency_signs: Dark brown urine or extreme swelling (kidney failure)
precautions: Wear strong sunscreen and protective clothing
things_to_avoid: Stopping medications without a doctor's okay
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day to keep your body strong.
Choose whole grain foods like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Try to cut down on very salty, sugary, and greasy foods.
recovery_time: Lupus is a lifelong condition, so it does not go away completely in a few weeks.
You will have times when you feel great and other times when you feel very tired.
Good days and bad days will come and go, which is a normal part of the journey.
Working closely with your doctor helps you have more good days than bad ones.
physical_activities: Take gentle walks outside when you have enough energy.
Try light stretching or easy yoga to keep your joints moving smoothly.
Stop and rest right away if you start feeling too tired or dizzy.
Avoid heavy workouts or lifting very heavy things on days you feel weak.
recommended_tests: Give a little blood so the doctor can check how well your organs are doing.
Give a urine sample to see if your kidneys are healthy.
Get your blood pressure checked regularly during your visits.
Have your doctor check your skin and joints for any new swelling or rashes.

teething syndrome.basic_details: Teething syndrome is a normal stage when a baby's new teeth start pushing through their gums, which can make them fussy and sore.
reason: Baby teeth growing and pushing through the gums
emergency_signs: Complete refusal to drink any liquids
Baby is extremely sleepy or hard to wake up
precautions: Give the baby a firm rubber teething ring
Gently rub the gums with a clean finger
Give child-safe pain relievers if approved by a doctor
Wipe drool from the face to prevent rashes
things_to_avoid: Using numbing gels with benzocaine (dangerous for babies)
Tying teething necklaces around the baby's neck (choking hazard)
Giving them hard foods they can choke on
diet_recommendation: Offer cool foods like chilled applesauce or yogurt to soothe sore gums.
Give your baby cold water in a cup if they are old enough.
Stick to soft and easy-to-chew foods when teeth are hurting.
Keep up with regular milk feeds, even if they eat a little less solid food.
treatment_options: gentle gum massage with clean finger
wipe drool often to stop rash
recovery_time: Pain and fussiness usually last only 3 to 7 days for each new tooth.
Symptoms tend to flare up right before a tooth breaks through the skin.
Once the tooth is fully out, the pain goes away quickly.
Every child is different, so some teeth pop out with zero trouble.
physical_activities: Let your baby chew on safe, clean teething toys to ease the pressure.
Give them a chilled, damp washcloth to chew on for quick relief.
Play extra games and give lots of cuddles to help distract them from pain.
Keep up with normal nap and bedtime routines as much as possible.
recommended_tests: Most babies do not need any medical tests for teething.
Your doctor can just look inside the baby's mouth to check the gums.
A temperature check is useful if you think the baby might have a fever.
Visit the doctor if the baby has unusual symptoms like a bad cough or rash.
when_to_visit_doctor: baby has bad diarrhea or vomiting
baby cries nonstop and will not calm down
ear pain or signs of ear infection

temporary or benign blood in urine.basic_details: Temporary or benign blood in urine means there is a little blood in your pee that is not caused by a serious illness. It often goes away on its own without needing any major treatment.
reason: Menstrual blood mixing in the toilet
emergency_signs: Severe pain in the back or side
precautions: See a doctor to confirm it is not serious
Take antibiotics if a minor infection is found
things_to_avoid: Ignoring the blood if it happens more than once
Assuming it is fine without getting a doctor's check
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to flush out your system.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy.
Limit spicy foods that might irritate your bladder.
Cut down on salty snacks and processed foods.
common_medicines: no medicine needed for benign causes
treatment_options: treat the root cause if found
recovery_time: Most people see the blood disappear within a few days.
It can sometimes take up to a couple of weeks to fully clear up.
Resting well helps your body heal much faster.
You should follow up with your doctor to make sure it is gone.
physical_activities: Keep doing your normal, everyday light walking.
Avoid heavy weightlifting until the bleeding completely stops.
Stay away from intense running or jumping exercises for a short while.
Listen to your body and rest if you feel tired.
recommended_tests: A simple urine test to check for blood cells and signs of infection.
A blood test to make sure your kidneys are working properly.
An ultrasound picture of your tummy to look at your bladder and kidneys.
A doctor's physical checkup to find any obvious causes.

temporomandibular joint disorder.basic_details: Temporomandibular joint disorder is a problem with the hinge that connects your jaw to your skull, causing pain and clicking when you chew. It makes moving your mouth uncomfortable.
emergency_signs: Jaw gets completely locked open or closed
