Severe pain preventing eating or drinking
Face swells up with a high fever
Sudden change in how teeth fit together
precautions: Wear a night guard if you grind your teeth
Apply warm or cold packs to the side of the face
things_to_avoid: Resting your chin on your hand
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, applesauce, and mashed potatoes so your jaw does not have to work hard.
Cut your food into small pieces to make chewing much easier.
Stay away from hard foods like nuts, hard candies, and raw carrots.
Avoid very chewy foods like gum and sticky candy that make your jaw tired.
recovery_time: Mild jaw pain can often get better in a few weeks with simple home care.
More stubborn jaw issues can take a few months of steady rest and treatment to heal.
Healing speed depends on how well you follow rest rules and avoid hard chewing.
Some people need ongoing care over many months if the jaw problem comes back often.
physical_activities: Do gentle jaw stretching movements slowly as taught by a physical therapist.
Practice soft smiling and opening your mouth just a little bit without forcing it.
Keep up with light daily exercises like walking to stay healthy overall.
Avoid heavy sports or activities that might cause accidental bumps to your face and jaw.
recommended_tests: A dentist or doctor will feel your jaw and listen for popping sounds when you open your mouth.
You might get an X-ray to look at the bone shape of your jaw joint.
An MRI scan can be done to check the soft cushion inside your jaw joint.
A CT scan may be used to get a very detailed picture of the jaw bones.
when_to_visit_doctor: if treatments at home do not work

tendinitis.basic_details: Tendinitis happens when the thick cords that attach your muscles to your bones become irritated and sore. This usually happens from doing the same movement over and over again.
reason: Repetitive movements (like typing, throwing, or painting)
Aging and loss of tendon flexibility
emergency_signs: Sudden tear feeling with excruciating pain
Complete inability to move the joint
Joint becomes extremely red and hot
precautions: Apply ice packs to reduce swelling
things_to_avoid: Pushing through the pain during exercise
Repeating the activity that caused the pain
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to keep your joints happy.
Include foods like fish and nuts that help calm down swelling.
Eat enough protein like chicken, beans, or eggs to help fix your tissues.
recovery_time: Minor soreness can get better in just a few days if you rest.
Most people start feeling much better within two to four weeks.
If the pain has been there a long time, it can take a few months to heal.
Healing takes longer if you try to rush back to hard work too fast.
physical_activities: Rest the sore body part and stop doing the thing that hurts it.
Do very gentle stretches once the sharp pain starts to go away.
Try low-impact exercises like swimming instead of running or heavy lifting.
Gradually build your strength back up with very light weights or bands.
recommended_tests: Let a doctor gently press on the sore area to check where it hurts.
Move your joint around to see how far and how easily it can go.
Get an X-ray just to make sure there are no broken bones.
Have an ultrasound or MRI taken to get a clear picture of the sore tendon.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain does not get better with rest
You have a fever or the area is very hot
You cannot move the joint at all

tension headache.basic_details: A tension headache is a very common type of headache that feels like a tight band is wrapped around your head. It is usually caused by stress, anxiety, or holding your body in a stiff position for too long.
reason: Eye strain from looking at screens
emergency_signs: Sudden, worst headache of your life
Headache comes with a high fever and stiff neck
Numbness or weakness on one side of the body
precautions: Rest in a quiet, dark room
Drink water and get enough sleep
things_to_avoid: Taking pain pills every single day (causes rebound headaches)
Staring at screens for hours without a break
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day because being thirsty can cause headaches.
Eat your meals on time so your blood sugar does not drop too low.
Limit how much coffee and soda you drink each day.
Eat fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains to keep your body healthy.
treatment_options: put a warm or cold pack on your head
recovery_time: Many tension headaches go away in just thirty minutes to a few hours.
Some headaches might last all day if you stay stressed out.
Getting a good night of sleep usually makes the pain go away completely.
Resting in a quiet, dark room helps your body heal faster.
physical_activities: Go for a short, easy walk outside to help your tight muscles relax.
Stretch your neck and shoulders gently every day to release tension.
Try light yoga or deep breathing exercises to calm your mind.
Avoid heavy workouts until your headache is completely gone.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually do not need tests and can just talk to you about your pain.
A doctor might check your blood pressure to make sure it is normal.
Sometimes a doctor will test your reflexes and eye movement.
A special brain scan is rarely needed unless your headache is very unusual.
when_to_visit_doctor: headaches happen more than two times a week
headaches stop you from doing normal things

testicular disorder.basic_details: A testicular disorder is a health issue that affects the testicles, which are the male reproductive glands. It can cause pain, swelling, or other uncomfortable symptoms.
emergency_signs: Sudden, severe, unbearable pain in the testicle
Scrotum becomes bright red, hot, and swollen
precautions: Wear an athletic cup during contact sports
See a doctor for any new pain or swelling
things_to_avoid: Ignoring a hard lump because it doesn't hurt
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to stay well hydrated.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Limit eating junk food, sugary snacks, and greasy meals.
recovery_time: Most minor issues start feeling better within a few days.
More serious conditions or surgeries may take a few weeks to heal.
Always follow your doctor's advice to heal as fast as possible.
Go back for your follow-up visits to make sure you are fully better.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest and avoid heavy work while you heal.
Do not lift heavy objects or do hard exercises for a while.
Wear supportive underwear to help reduce pain and swelling.
Take slow, gentle walks only when your body feels ready.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where the doctor gently feels the area.
An ultrasound scan to look inside the scrotum using sound waves.
Urine tests to check for signs of infection.
Blood tests to check for other health issues or inflammation.

testicular torsion.basic_details: Testicular torsion happens when the testicle twists around inside the body, cutting off its own blood supply. This causes sudden, very strong pain and swelling, and it needs a quick doctor's help.
reason: Testicle twists on its cord, cutting off blood flow
Happens often during sleep in young men
emergency_signs: Sudden, extreme, agonizing pain in one testicle
Testicle sits higher than normal or at an odd angle
Rapid, massive swelling of the scrotum
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately (surgery is needed within hours to save it)
Rest completely while waiting for help
things_to_avoid: Waiting to see if the pain goes away
Taking pain pills and going to sleep
Eating or drinking (you will likely need surgery)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to stay healthy.
Eat high-fiber foods like whole grains to avoid straining when going to the bathroom.
Avoid junk food and heavy, greasy meals right after surgery so your stomach stays settled.
treatment_options: surgery to stitch testicle in place
surgery to remove testicle if damaged
recovery_time: Most people start feeling a bit better after one to two weeks.
It usually takes about four to six weeks to fully heal from surgery.
Mild swelling and bruising can stick around for a few weeks.
Always follow up with your doctor to make sure everything is healing right.
physical_activities: Rest completely for the first few days after your surgery.
Do not lift anything heavy for at least a month.
Avoid running, jumping, and playing sports until your doctor gives the green light.
Take slow, short walks around the house to help your blood flow once you feel up to it.
recommended_tests: A physical exam where the doctor gently checks the painful area.
An ultrasound scan that uses sound waves to look at the blood flow to your testicle.
A urine test to check for other issues like infections.
Blood tests to check your overall health before any surgery.

thoracic aortic aneurysm.basic_details: A thoracic aortic aneurysm is a weak, bulging spot in the main blood vessel that carries blood from your heart to your body, located in your chest. If it gets too big, it can be very dangerous, so doctors like to keep a close eye on it.
reason: High blood pressure weakening the blood vessel
emergency_signs: Sudden, severe tearing or ripping pain in the chest or upper back
Sudden weakness or inability to move legs
precautions: Get regular medical scans to check its size
Follow doctor's advice on safe exercise limits
things_to_avoid: Ignoring severe chest or back pain
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread.
Cut down on salty foods to help keep your blood pressure low.
Drink plenty of water instead of sugary sodas and drinks.
common_medicines: blood pressure pills to lower stress on the aorta
pain medicine if there is discomfort
treatment_options: regular checkups with scans to watch the size
surgery to replace the weak part of the blood vessel
placing a small tube called a stent to fix the artery
recovery_time: If you do not need surgery, recovery means resting and keeping your stress low every day.
If you have surgery, staying in the hospital usually takes about 5 to 7 days.
Healing fully at home after surgery can take around 6 to 12 weeks of gentle rest.
Your doctor will schedule regular checkups over the coming months to see how you are healing.
physical_activities: Go for short, easy walks around your house or neighborhood to stay gently active.
Do not lift anything heavy, like groceries, furniture, or heavy boxes.
Avoid hard exercises like running, heavy weightlifting, or intense sports.
Stop moving right away if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or sharp pain in your chest.
recommended_tests: A painless picture test of your chest, called a CT scan, to see the size of the bulge.
An ultrasound of your heart, called an echocardiogram, to check how well your heart is working.
Regular checks of your blood pressure to make sure it stays at a safe, low level.
An X-ray of your chest to look at the shape of your heart and main blood vessels.
when_to_visit_doctor: you feel a new pain in your chest or back
you have trouble breathing or swallowing
it is time for your regular heart checkup

thoracic outlet syndrome.basic_details: Thoracic outlet syndrome happens when blood vessels or nerves in the space between your collarbone and first rib get squeezed. This can cause pain in your shoulders and neck, and numbness in your fingers.
reason: Repetitive arm movements (like pitching a baseball)
emergency_signs: Arm turns completely blue, pale, or cold
Sudden extreme swelling of the arm
Total loss of feeling or movement in the hand
precautions: Do physical therapy to improve posture
Apply heat or ice as directed
things_to_avoid: Carrying heavy bags on your shoulders
Sleeping with arms above your head
diet_recommendation: Eat fresh fruits and vegetables every day to help your body heal.
Choose foods that fight swelling, like salmon, nuts, and olive oil.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your muscles happy.
Limit junk food and sugary snacks that can make your body feel worse.
recovery_time: Mild cases can start feeling better in just a few weeks with rest.
More serious cases might take a few months of steady care to heal.
Doing your daily stretches helps speed up how fast you get better.
Full recovery depends on how well you follow your doctor's plan.
physical_activities: Do gentle neck and shoulder stretches to loosen tight muscles.
Take short walks to keep your whole body moving without heavy lifting.
Work with a physical therapist to learn safe and easy exercises.
Avoid heavy lifting or high-impact sports that strain your shoulders.
recommended_tests: Get an X-ray to let the doctor look closely at your bones and ribs.
Have an ultrasound to check how the blood flows through your veins.
Do an electrical test to see how well your nerves are working.
Take an MRI scan to get a clear picture of your muscles and tissues.

threatened pregnancy.basic_details: A threatened pregnancy means you are having some early warning signs like bleeding, but the pregnancy is still going and can often turn out just fine with rest.
reason: Unknown causes (bleeding often happens with no clear reason)
emergency_signs: Bleeding soaking more than a pad an hour
Passing large blood clots or tissue
precautions: Rest in bed if advised by a doctor
Use pads instead of tampons to check bleeding amount
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to stay hydrated.
Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables for good health.
Choose whole grains like brown bread and oatmeal.
Avoid raw or undercooked meat, fish, and unwashed foods.
recovery_time: Most women start feeling better within a few days of resting.
The risk period usually passes after the first few weeks.
Every woman's body heals at its own speed, so do not rush.
You will need to wait until your doctor says you are fully in the clear.
physical_activities: Stay in bed or on the couch as much as possible.
Avoid heavy lifting, pushing, or pulling anything around the house.
Skip hard workouts, running, and jumping until your doctor says it is okay.
Limit walking to short, slow trips to the bathroom or kitchen.
recommended_tests: Get an ultrasound to check on the baby's heartbeat.
Have blood tests to check your pregnancy hormone levels.
Let your doctor check your blood pressure and overall health.
Report any new cramps or bleeding right away for quick checks.

thrombocytopenia.basic_details: Thrombocytopenia means you have a low number of platelets in your blood, which are the tiny cells that help your body stop bleeding. This can make you bruise easily or bleed longer than normal if you get hurt.
emergency_signs: Bleeding from a cut that will not stop
Sudden severe headache or confusion (brain bleeding)
Large, dark bruises appearing for no reason
precautions: Use a soft toothbrush and electric shaver
Tell dentists and doctors about your condition
things_to_avoid: Taking aspirin or ibuprofen (they thin the blood)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to stay healthy.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body hydrated.
Avoid drinking alcohol because it can lower your platelet count even more.
Cook your meat and eggs all the way through to avoid food poisoning.
recovery_time: Mild cases can get better in just a few weeks or months.
Some people might need treatment for a longer time if the issue keeps coming back.
Your recovery speed depends a lot on what is causing your low platelets.
You will need regular blood checkups to see how fast you are healing.
physical_activities: Do light walking to stay active without hurting yourself.
Stay away from rough sports like football or boxing where you might get hit.
Use a soft toothbrush so your gums do not start bleeding.
Be very careful around sharp tools and heavy items to avoid cuts and bruises.
recommended_tests: Get a complete blood count test to check your exact platelet numbers.
Have your doctor look closely at a tiny drop of your blood under a microscope.
Get a small sample of your bone marrow taken if your doctor needs more clues.
Do allergy or immune system blood tests to find the root cause.
when_to_visit_doctor: Bleeding gums that will not stop
Tiny red dots appear on the skin

thrombophlebitis.basic_details: Thrombophlebitis happens when a blood clot forms in a vein and causes painful swelling, usually in your legs. It makes the skin feel warm, red, and tender right over the spot.
reason: Blood clot in a vein near the skin
Having an IV line in the hospital
emergency_signs: Sudden shortness of breath (clot moved to lungs)
Severe swelling of the entire arm or leg
precautions: Apply warm compresses to the painful vein
Elevate the affected arm or leg
things_to_avoid: Ignoring chest pain or breathing issues
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your blood flowing smoothly.
Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables to stay healthy.
Cut down on salty foods so your body does not hold onto extra water.
Try to eat fewer greasy or fatty foods to protect your heart and veins.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling better within one to two weeks.
Mild swelling and redness can sometimes stick around for a few weeks.
Following your doctor's advice helps you heal much faster.
Call your doctor if your pain gets worse instead of better after a few days.
physical_activities: Take short, gentle walks every day to keep the blood moving in your legs.
Avoid sitting or standing still in one place for too long.
Prop your legs up on pillows when you are resting to lower the swelling.
Skip heavy lifting and hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
recommended_tests: An ultrasound uses sound waves to take pictures of the inside of your veins.
A physical check lets your doctor look closely at the red and swollen spot.
Blood tests may be done to check how well your blood clots.
Your doctor might ask about your health history and past surgeries.

thyroid nodule.basic_details: A thyroid nodule is a small, usually harmless lump that forms inside your thyroid gland in the front of your neck. Most of these lumps are not cancer and do not cause any health problems.
emergency_signs: Severe trouble breathing or choking feeling
Sudden rapid growth of the lump
Heart racing and extreme sweating (if making too much hormone)
precautions: Have a doctor check the lump with an ultrasound
Get blood tests for thyroid levels
Attend follow-up appointments to monitor size
things_to_avoid: Ignoring a growing lump in the neck
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Include whole grains like brown rice and oats in your meals.
Drink lots of water to keep your body hydrated.
Try to cut back on processed foods and too much sugar.
recovery_time: If you do not need surgery, there is no recovery time needed.
If you have a small needle test, you can go back to normal life right away.
If the lump is removed with surgery, most people heal within two weeks.
You might feel tired for a few days after any medical procedure.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily exercises without worry.
Go for light walks to stay active and keep your mood up.
Avoid heavy neck lifting or intense straining until your doctor says it is okay.
Listen to your body and rest if you feel too tired.
recommended_tests: An ultrasound uses safe sound waves to take a picture of the lump in your neck.
A blood test checks if your thyroid is working at the right speed.
A small needle test might be done to take a tiny sample of the lump to check it closely.
Your doctor may check your neck with their hands during a routine visit.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you feel a lump in your neck
If your voice changes or sounds hoarse
If you have trouble swallowing or breathing
If the neck lump grows bigger fast

tic (movement) disorder.basic_details: A tic disorder is a health issue that causes your body to make sudden, repeated movements or sounds that you cannot easily control. These can look like quick blinks, shoulder shrugs, or head jerks.
emergency_signs: Tics causing severe self-injury (like hitting oneself)
Severe depression or thoughts of self-harm
Sudden onset of severe tics after a throat infection (PANDAS)
precautions: Take prescribed medicines if tics cause pain or social issues
Ensure a supportive school or work environment
Manage stress and get enough sleep
things_to_avoid: Punishing or yelling at the person for the tics
Too much screen time before bed
Drawing constant attention to the tics
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your brain and body healthy.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to give your body good energy.
Try to eat less sugar and candy, as sugar can sometimes make you feel more jittery.
Stay away from too much soda or coffee with caffeine, because it can make tics happen more often.
recovery_time: Every person is different, so there is no exact timeline for how long tics last.
Many children find that their tics get much better or go away completely as they grow up.
Some people have tics that come and go all through their lives, but they learn to live with them easily.
Stress and being tired can make tics worse for a little while, but resting helps them calm down.
physical_activities: Doing fun sports like swimming or running helps burn off extra energy and keeps you calm.
Yoga and deep breathing exercises are great for relaxing your body and mind.
Try to get a good night's sleep every single night so your body can rest.
Take short breaks during the day if you feel stressed out or overwhelmed.
recommended_tests: A doctor will talk to you and watch your movements to figure out if you have tics.
Sometimes, doctors do a simple check of your nervous system to make sure everything is working right.
Blood tests might be done just to check if other health things are normal.
Brain scans are rarely needed, but a doctor might use them if they want to look closer at other causes.

tietze syndrome.basic_details: Tietze syndrome is a harmless condition that causes pain and swelling in the cartilage where your ribs connect to your breastbone. It can feel scary because it hurts near the heart, but it is not dangerous.
reason: Swelling of the cartilage connecting ribs to the breastbone
emergency_signs: Crushing chest pain radiating to the arm (must rule out heart attack)
precautions: Go to the ER first to make sure it is not a heart attack
Apply heat or ice to the chest
things_to_avoid: Assuming chest pain is just Tietze without a doctor's check
Pushing on the chest to see if it hurts
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and green vegetables to help lower body swelling.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to keep your body healthy.
Try to eat less fast food and sugary snacks, as they can make body soreness worse.
Include healthy fats like fish and olive oil in your meals to soothe inflammation.
treatment_options: Put a warm pack on the chest
Put a cold pack on the chest
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within a few weeks.
Sometimes the sore feeling can linger for a few months before going away completely.
Every person heals at their own speed, so try to be patient with your body.
If the pain comes back, it usually goes away faster the second time.
physical_activities: Take slow, gentle walks to keep your body moving without straining your chest.
Stop right away if any exercise makes your chest hurt more.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard gym workouts until the pain is completely gone.
Do easy stretching for your arms and back only if it feels comfortable.
recommended_tests: Doctors often press on your chest to see if the sore spot matches your pain.
You might get a chest x-ray to make sure the pain is not coming from your lungs.
An electrical heart test or EKG may be done just to prove your heart is completely healthy.
Blood tests are sometimes used to check if there is any other swelling in your body.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel dizzy or short of breath
You are not sure if it is heart trouble

tinnitus of unknown cause.basic_details: Tinnitus of unknown cause means you hear ringing or buzzing in your ears, but doctors cannot find a clear reason why it is happening.
emergency_signs: Ringing sounds like a pulsing heartbeat in sync with your pulse
precautions: See an ear doctor for a hearing test
Use white noise machines to help sleep
things_to_avoid: Loud concerts or machinery without earplugs
Cleaning inside the ear with cotton swabs
High doses of aspirin (can worsen ringing)
diet_recommendation: Cut down on salty foods to help keep your blood pressure steady.
Drink less coffee and soda because caffeine can make the ringing louder.
Try to avoid alcohol as it can change blood flow to your inner ear.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your body healthy.
common_medicines: Vitamin B12 if levels are low
treatment_options: Hearing aids to boost outside sounds
Counselling to help cope with the noise
recovery_time: There is no set timeline because the condition is different for everyone.
Many people find the ringing bothers them less over time as they get used to it.
Some people notice it goes away on its own after a few weeks or months.
For others, it can last a long time, but learning to ignore it helps a lot.
physical_activities: Go for regular walks to lower stress and keep your heart healthy.
Try gentle yoga or stretching to relax your neck and shoulder muscles.
Do light workouts, but avoid very loud fitness classes that could hurt your ears.
Practice deep breathing exercises to help calm your mind when the ringing feels loud.
recommended_tests: A hearing test with a specialist to check how well you hear different sounds.
Looking inside your ears with a small light tool to check for wax buildup.
A scan of your head, like an MRI, to make sure there are no hidden issues.
Blood tests to check for things like low vitamins or thyroid problems.
when_to_visit_doctor: The noise happens in only one ear
You also feel dizzy or lose balance
The ringing starts after a head injury
The noise stops you from sleeping or working

tonsillar hypertrophy.basic_details: Tonsillar hypertrophy means the two small lumps in the back of your throat have grown bigger than normal. This can sometimes make it a bit hard to breathe or swallow.
emergency_signs: Child stops breathing during sleep (sleep apnea)
Severe choking or inability to swallow solid food
Extreme daytime sleepiness from poor sleep
precautions: Have a doctor check the throat
Monitor sleep for loud snoring or breathing pauses
Consider surgery to remove them if breathing is blocked
things_to_avoid: Ignoring loud snoring or breathing pauses in children
Feeding the child large pieces of hard food
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes, yogurt, and soup that do not hurt your throat.
Drink lots of cold water and ice water to keep your throat cool and calm.
Avoid crunchy or spicy foods like chips and hot peppers that can scratch your throat.
Stay away from very sour juices that might sting when you swallow.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better within one to two weeks with proper rest.
If you have surgery to remove the tonsils, full healing usually takes about ten to fourteen days.
Your throat will feel the most sore around the third to fifth day after treatment.
Listen to your body and take it slow until you can swallow normally again.
physical_activities: Rest in bed or on the couch as much as possible during the first few days.
Avoid heavy lifting, running, or hard workouts for at least two weeks.
Take short, gentle walks around the house when you feel a little stronger.
Skip contact sports to keep your neck and throat safe from bumps.
recommended_tests: A doctor will look inside your mouth with a small light to see your tonsils.
They might gently press on your neck to check for swollen lumps.
A quick throat swab might be done to check for any germs or infections.
Sometimes, a sleep study is suggested to see if the big tonsils are blocking your breathing at night.

tonsillitis.basic_details: Tonsillitis is when the two round lumps at the back of your throat get swollen and infected, making it hurt to swallow. It is very common and usually goes away with a little self-care.
reason: Sharing drinks with an infected person
emergency_signs: Extreme swelling on one side of the throat (abscess)
precautions: Take all antibiotics if a bacteria caused it
Drink warm fluids or eat popsicles
Rest and get plenty of sleep
things_to_avoid: Going to school or work while contagious
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes, yogurt, and oatmeal that do not hurt your throat.
Drink lots of warm liquids like tea with honey or warm soup to feel better.
Stay away from spicy, crunchy, or sour foods that can scratch and irritate your throat.
Eat cold things like ice cream or ice pops to help numb the pain and swelling.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better in about 3 to 7 days.
If you take antibiotics, make sure to finish all of them even if you feel better.
Your throat might stay a little sore for a few extra days after the main sickness is gone.
Call your doctor if you still feel sick after a week or if you get worse.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and get plenty of rest so your body can fight off the infection.
Avoid heavy workouts, running, or heavy lifting until you have all your energy back.
Do light walking around the house only when you feel up to it.
Sleep with your head propped up on extra pillows to help your throat feel less stuffed.
recommended_tests: A doctor will use a small light to look inside your mouth at your red and swollen throat.
The doctor might gently press on your neck to check for swollen lumps under your jaw.
A quick throat swab test might be done to see what kind of germ is making you sick.
A blood test is rarely needed unless the doctor wants to check for other sicknesses.

tooth abscess.basic_details: A tooth abscess is a painful pocket of pus caused by a bacterial infection inside the tooth or gum. It happens when germs get deep into the tooth through a cavity or crack.
emergency_signs: Severe swelling spreading to the eye or neck
Extreme throbbing pain making sleep impossible
precautions: Rinse the mouth with warm salt water
things_to_avoid: Trying to pop the swelling yourself
Putting pain pills directly on the gums (it causes burns)
Ignoring the pain hoping it goes away
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like yogurt, mashed potatoes, and soup so you do not hurt your sore tooth.
Stay away from very hot or very cold foods and drinks because they can trigger sharp pain.
Avoid sweet foods and sugary drinks that can feed the bad bacteria in your mouth.
Chew your food on the opposite side of your mouth away from the bad tooth.
recovery_time: Pain usually starts to get much better within two to three days after seeing the dentist and starting treatment.
It can take a week or two for the entire infection to completely go away.
Full healing of the gum and jawbone can take a few weeks depending on the treatment needed.
If you need a root canal or tooth pull, healing from the dental procedure itself takes a few days.
physical_activities: Rest as much as possible for the first couple of days to let your body fight the infection.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard workouts because they can increase blood flow to your head and make the throbbing worse.
Try to keep your head propped up on pillows even when resting to help bring down swelling.
Take slow, gentle walks if you feel up to it, but stop right away if you feel dizzy or tired.
recommended_tests: A dentist will do a visual check of your teeth and gums to look for swelling and redness.
A dental X-ray is usually taken to see how far the infection has spread into the jawbone.
The dentist might gently tap on your tooth to see which one is causing the pain.
A temperature test using hot or cold items might be done to check if the nerve inside the tooth is still alive.

tooth disorder.basic_details: A tooth disorder means there is a problem with your teeth or gums, such as pain, decay, or crookedness. It can make eating and smiling uncomfortable.
emergency_signs: Fever and pus draining from gums
precautions: Brush twice a day with fluoride toothpaste
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like mashed potatoes, yogurt, and soup so you do not hurt your teeth.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your mouth clean.
Stay away from very sugary candies, sodas, and sticky snacks that cause cavities.
Avoid foods that are too hot or too cold if your teeth feel sensitive.
recovery_time: Small issues like a minor toothache can get better in a few days.
Fixing a cavity with a filling usually heals within one to two days.
Having a tooth pulled out can take a week or two for the gums to heal completely.
Major treatments like root canals or braces can take several weeks or months to fully settle.
physical_activities: You can keep doing your normal daily walks and light exercises.
Wear a protective mouthguard if you play contact sports to keep your teeth safe.
Avoid heavy lifting or intense workouts right after having dental surgery.
Relax and rest if you feel dizzy or weak from a bad toothache.
recommended_tests: A dentist will look inside your mouth with a small mirror and a light.
Take dental X-rays to see what is happening underneath your teeth and gums.
A tap test where the dentist gently touches your teeth to find where it hurts.
A cold test to check if the nerves inside your teeth are still healthy.

torticollis.basic_details: Torticollis is a common neck problem where your head twists or tilts to one side on its own. It can make your neck muscles tight and hurt when you try to turn your head.
reason: Birth defect or positioning in the womb
emergency_signs: Numbness or weakness in the arms
precautions: Apply heat to the tense neck muscles
things_to_avoid: Ignoring it if a baby always looks to one side
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your muscles healthy.
Include foods with calcium and magnesium, like milk and nuts, to relax muscles.
Try to eat less junk food and processed food that can cause swelling.
recovery_time: Mild cases often get better on their own in just a few days.
Cases treated with stretching and medicine usually improve within two to four weeks.
More stubborn or long-term neck twisting can take a few months to fully fix.
Doing your daily stretches helps speed up how fast you heal.
physical_activities: Do gentle neck stretches every day to slowly turn your head side to side.
Put warm packs on your neck before moving it to help loosen the tightness.
Take short walks to keep your whole body moving without straining your neck.
Avoid heavy lifting or sudden, fast movements until your neck feels normal.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where the doctor watches how you move your head and neck.
An X-ray picture to check the bones in your neck and spine.
An MRI scan if the doctor needs a closer look at the soft muscles and tissues.
Nerve tests to make sure your neck nerves are working the right way.
when_to_visit_doctor: neck pain does not go away
head stays stuck to one side
pain starts after a head injury
you feel numbness in your arms

tourette syndrome.basic_details: Tourette syndrome is a condition that makes people make sudden movements and sounds called tics, which they cannot easily control. It usually starts when a person is a child.
emergency_signs: Tics that cause severe physical injury (like hitting the head)
Severe depression or thoughts of self-harm
Complete inability to function in school or work
precautions: Educate teachers and coworkers about the condition
Take prescribed medicines if tics are painful
things_to_avoid: Punishing the person for their tics
Ignoring signs of anxiety or ADHD (often co-occur)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink lots of water to keep your body healthy.
Try to eat less sugar and candy, as it can sometimes make you feel too excited.
Eat meals at regular times to keep your energy steady.
recovery_time: Tourette syndrome is a long-term condition, so it does not just go away quickly.
Many children find that their tics get much better as they grow into adults.
Some people have tics that come and go throughout their whole life.
With time and practice, you can learn how to manage and live well with it.
physical_activities: Do fun sports like swimming, running, or riding a bike to burn off extra energy.
Try yoga or slow stretching to help your body and mind relax.
Take breaks when you feel tired from moving too much.
Play outside in the fresh air to help reduce stress and worry.
recommended_tests: Doctors usually just watch how you move and listen to your sounds to know what it is.
There is no special blood test for this condition.
Sometimes a doctor will take pictures of your brain just to make sure everything is okay.
Your doctor might ask questions about when your tics started and how often they happen.

toxic multinodular goiter.basic_details: Toxic multinodular goiter is a condition where your thyroid gland develops several lumps that make too much thyroid hormone, speeding up your body.
reason: Lumps on the thyroid making too much hormone
emergency_signs: Severe trouble breathing or choking feeling
precautions: Consider surgery or radioactive iodine as recommended
diet_recommendation: Eat a balanced diet with plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables.
Be careful with seaweed and foods very high in iodine.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated.
Limit caffeine and sugary drinks, as they can make your heart race.
recovery_time: If you take medicine, you might start feeling better in a few weeks.
If you have surgery, normal daily activities usually resume in two weeks.
Full healing and getting your energy back can take a few months.
Regular doctor check-ups are needed to make sure you stay healthy.
physical_activities: Stick to light walking until your doctor says you can do more.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts while your heart beats fast.
Try gentle stretching or relaxing yoga to lower your stress.
Slowly add your usual exercise back as your energy levels improve.
recommended_tests: Blood tests to check your thyroid hormone levels.
An ultrasound picture to look at the lumps on your thyroid.
A thyroid scan to see how your gland is working.
Heart checks like an EKG if your heart is beating too fast.
when_to_visit_doctor: you feel your heart beating too fast
you notice a lump in your neck
you feel very nervous or shaky

tracheitis.basic_details: Tracheitis is an infection and swelling of your windpipe, which is the main air tube leading to your lungs. It often causes a barking cough and throat pain.
emergency_signs: Severe trouble breathing or gasping for air
precautions: Go to the emergency room immediately
Keep the person calm to help breathing
things_to_avoid: Delaying a trip to the hospital
Trying to look down the throat with fingers or a spoon
Giving cough suppressants without a doctor's okay
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of warm water and clear soup to keep your throat moist.
Eat soft foods like oatmeal and mashed potatoes if swallowing hurts.
Include honey in your tea to help calm your coughing.
Stay away from spicy and sour foods that can make your throat burn.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within 5 to 7 days.
A mild cough might stick around for up to two weeks.
Getting plenty of sleep helps your body heal faster.
If you do not get better after a week, call your doctor.
physical_activities: Stay in bed and rest as much as possible for the first few days.
Avoid heavy workouts, running, or lifting heavy things until you heal.
Take very light, slow walks around the house only if you feel strong enough.
Stay away from dusty or smoky places that can make you cough more.
recommended_tests: A doctor will listen to your breathing with a stethoscope.
You might need a throat swab to check for germs.
A chest X-ray can be done to make sure your lungs are clear.
A simple blood test may be used to see if your body is fighting an infection.

transient ischemic attack.basic_details: A transient ischemic attack is like a mini stroke where blood flow to your brain stops for a very short time. It does not cause lasting harm, but it is a serious warning sign that a full stroke might happen soon.
reason: Temporary blood clot in the brain
emergency_signs: Sudden numbness or weakness in the face, arm, or leg
Sudden loss of vision in one eye
Sudden severe dizziness or loss of balance
precautions: Call emergency services immediately (even if symptoms go away)
Take prescribed blood thinners and blood pressure pills
things_to_avoid: Ignoring the symptoms because they disappeared quickly
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables every single day.
Choose whole wheat bread and brown rice instead of white bread and white rice.
Cut down heavily on salty foods to help keep your blood pressure low.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day and stay away from sugary sodas.
treatment_options: Surgery to clear neck blood vessels
recovery_time: The actual warning signs usually go away completely within a few minutes to an hour.
You will need to rest at home for a few days to let your body calm down.
Most people start feeling back to normal within a week with proper care.
Long-term recovery means making healthy daily choices for the rest of your life.
physical_activities: Start with slow, easy walks around your house or yard.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Try gentle stretching in the morning to keep your body moving smoothly.
Slowly build up your walking time bit by bit each week.
recommended_tests: A brain scan picture helps doctors see what is going on inside your head.
An ultrasound of your neck checks if blood flows easily up to your brain.
A heart check helps see if your heart is beating in a steady and normal way.
Simple blood checks are done to look at your sugar and fat levels.
when_to_visit_doctor: For regular checkups of your heart

trichiasis.basic_details: Trichiasis is an eye problem where your eyelashes grow inward and rub against your eyeball. This causes irritation, redness, and can hurt your eye if not fixed.
emergency_signs: Thick pus draining from the eye
A white spot appearing on the colored part of the eye
precautions: See an eye doctor to have the lashes safely removed
Wear sunglasses to protect the irritated eye
Consider minor surgery to fix the eyelid
things_to_avoid: Trying to pull the eyelashes out yourself with tweezers
Ignoring the feeling of something in the eye
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits like oranges and berries to help your eyes stay healthy.
Eat green vegetables like spinach to give your eyes good nutrients.
Drink lots of water every day to keep your body and eyes from drying out.
Eat fish or nuts because they have healthy oils that are good for your eyes.
treatment_options: removing the eyelash with special tools
using electricity to stop hair growth
surgery to fix the eyelid position
recovery_time: Most people feel better within a few days after a doctor removes the bad eyelashes.
If you need a simple procedure, your eye might take one to two weeks to fully heal.
You should rest your eyes and avoid hard work for the first couple of days.
Go back to your eye doctor if your eye still hurts after a week.
physical_activities: Take a break from heavy lifting and hard workouts for a few days so your eyes can heal.
Stay away from dusty or dirty places where things can blow into your healing eyes.
Avoid swimming in pools or lakes until your doctor says it is safe.
Wear sunglasses outside to protect your sensitive eyes from bright sun and wind.
recommended_tests: An eye doctor will look closely at your eyelashes using a special lighted magnifying tool.
The doctor might check how well your eyelids close and how your tears flow.
They can test your vision to make sure the rubbing eyelashes did not hurt your sight.
A quick dye test might be done to see if the eyelashes scratched the front of your eye.
when_to_visit_doctor: your eye feels like something is stuck in it
your eye turns very red and hurts
your eye is sensitive to bright light

trichomonas infection.basic_details: Trichomonas infection is a very common sexually transmitted infection caused by a tiny parasite. It can cause itching, burning, and unusual discharge, but many people do not have any symptoms at all.
emergency_signs: Painful sores or bleeding from the genitals
precautions: Tell all physical intimacy partners to get treated
things_to_avoid: Having physical intimacy before the infection is fully cured
Drinking alcohol while on the medication (causes severe vomiting)
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to help your immune system stay strong.
Drink lots of water every day to help flush out your body.
Eat yogurt with live cultures to keep your good bacteria balanced.
Try to cut back on sugary foods and drinks while you are healing.
treatment_options: Treat all sexual partners at the same time
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better within a week of starting their medicine.
You must finish all your pills, even if your symptoms go away quickly.
Avoid having sex until you and your partner finish your treatment and are completely healed.
Go back for a follow-up test a few months later to make sure the infection is totally gone.
physical_activities: You can do light walking and everyday movements while you heal.
Avoid heavy workouts or gym activities if they cause extra irritation or pain.
Stay away from swimming pools or hot tubs until your treatment is fully finished.
Wear loose and comfortable clothing to let your skin breathe and stay dry.
recommended_tests: A simple swab test taken from the genital area by a healthcare worker.
A quick urine test to check for the tiny parasite in your pee.
A lab test that looks at a fluid sample under a microscope.
Screening tests for other common sexually transmitted infections just to be safe.
when_to_visit_doctor: When you feel itching or burning
If symptoms do not go away

trigeminal neuralgia.basic_details: Trigeminal neuralgia is a health issue that causes sudden, severe pain in your face, like a sharp electric shock. Even touching your face lightly, brushing your teeth, or eating can set off the pain.
reason: Blood vessel pressing on a facial nerve
emergency_signs: Pain so severe you cannot eat or drink for days
Thoughts of self-harm due to extreme pain
precautions: Take prescribed nerve pain medicines (like anti-seizure pills)
Protect your face from cold wind
things_to_avoid: Taking standard pain pills (they rarely work)
Extreme cold temperatures on the face
diet_recommendation: Eat soft foods like soup, yogurt, mashed potatoes, and smoothies so you do not have to chew hard.
Eat and drink things that are at room temperature because hot or cold food can trigger face pain.
Cut your food into very small pieces to make eating easier on your jaw.
Drink plenty of water and healthy drinks through a straw to avoid touching your lips too much.
recovery_time: Recovery is different for everyone, ranging from a few weeks to many months.
You might have days where you feel great and other days where the pain comes back.
Finding the right medicine dose takes time, so patience is very important.
Some people need small surgeries or procedures, and healing from those can take a few weeks.
physical_activities: Go for gentle, relaxing walks outside to help lower your daily stress.
Try easy breathing exercises or meditation to help your body stay calm when pain happens.
Avoid heavy workouts or running that cause your face to bounce or shake too much.
Stay away from outdoor activities on very windy or cold days, as the wind hitting your face can trigger pain.
recommended_tests: Get a special brain scan called an MRI to let doctors look closely at your nerves.
Answer questions from your doctor about where the pain hurts and what makes it start.
Have a physical exam where the doctor gently touches parts of your face to check your feeling.
Let your doctor test how well your face muscles and nerves are working.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel sharp pain in your face
Pain does not go away with rest
Pills do not stop the face pain
Pain makes it hard to eat or talk

trigger finger (finger disorder).basic_details: Trigger finger is a common problem where one of your fingers gets stuck in a bent position and then snaps straight. It happens when the tunnel that holds your finger tendon gets swollen and irritated.
reason: Inflammation of the tendon in the finger
emergency_signs: Finger is completely locked and turning blue
Severe redness and swelling spreading up the hand
Sudden loss of feeling in the finger
precautions: Rest the hand and avoid repetitive gripping
See a doctor for a steroid injection if needed
things_to_avoid: Forcefully pulling the locked finger straight
Heavy lifting or carrying heavy bags
Using power tools with strong vibrations
diet_recommendation: Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to help reduce swelling in your body.
Include foods like fish and nuts that help fight body irritation.
Drink plenty of water every day to keep your joints healthy.
Try to eat less sugary and processed foods, as they can make swelling worse.
treatment_options: small surgery to release the tendon
recovery_time: Mild cases can start feeling better in a few weeks with simple rest.
Using a finger splint at night often helps healing take just a few weeks.
If you need a doctor's shot, it can take a couple of weeks to see full relief.
Severe cases that need simple hand surgery may take a few weeks to months to fully heal.
physical_activities: Do gentle hand stretches, like opening and closing your fist slowly.
Soak your hand in warm water before moving your fingers to loosen them up.
Avoid heavy gripping, tight squeezing, or lifting very heavy items for a while.
Take frequent breaks if you are doing repetitive hand tasks like typing or gardening.
recommended_tests: A doctor will usually just look at and feel your finger to make the diagnosis.
They will ask you to bend and straighten your finger to see how it catches.
You rarely need an X-ray, but a doctor might order one to rule out other bone issues.
Sometimes a quick physical check of your hand strength and grip is all that is needed.
when_to_visit_doctor: finger gets stuck and will not straighten
pain does not go away with rest
finger is very swollen or red
you cannot use your hand normally

ulcerative colitis.basic_details: Ulcerative colitis is a long-term health issue that makes the inside of your large bowel red, swollen, and full of tiny sores. This causes belly pain and you may need to rush to the bathroom a lot.
reason: Stress (makes symptoms worse, doesn't cause it)
things_to_avoid: Eating high-fiber foods during a flare-up
diet_recommendation: Eat smaller meals more often instead of three big ones.
Drink plenty of water to keep your body from drying out.
Stay away from very spicy or greasy foods that upset your belly.
Choose soft, plain foods like white rice, bananas, and cooked carrots when your belly hurts.
recovery_time: This is a lifelong condition, so there is no single date when you are fully cured.
Good days and bad days will come and go in waves over many years.
You can feel completely normal for long stretches if you take your medicine.
Healing a bad flare-up can take a few weeks to a few months of good care.
physical_activities: Take gentle, slow walks outside when you feel up to it.
Try light stretching or easy yoga to help you relax.
Rest as much as you can when you feel tired or weak.
Avoid heavy lifting and hard workouts until your belly feels better.
recommended_tests: A doctor looks inside your bottom with a tiny camera to check your bowel.
Giving a little sample of your stool to check for germs or bleeding.
Blood tests to see if you are low on iron or have an infection.
Pictures like an X-ray or scan of your belly to see the swelling.
when_to_visit_doctor: When belly pain gets very bad
When you have blood in your stool
When you have a high fever

urethral disorder.basic_details: A urethral disorder is a health issue with the tube that carries pee out of your body. It can cause pain or trouble when you try to use the bathroom.
emergency_signs: Severe pain in the lower belly
Blood or pus in the urine
precautions: See a urologist if symptoms continue
things_to_avoid: Using perfumed soaps on the genitals
Ignoring a burning feeling when urinating
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every single day to clean out your system.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal faster.
Try to stay away from spicy foods that might make your bladder upset.
Cut down on coffee and soda because they can irritate the tube.
recovery_time: Most people start feeling much better within a few days of starting treatment.
It can take a couple of weeks for the body to heal completely.
Following your doctor's exact advice will help you get better a lot quicker.
If you stop taking your medicine too early, the problem might come back.
physical_activities: Get plenty of rest and avoid heavy lifting while you are healing.
Take gentle walks around your house to keep your blood flowing well.
Stay away from riding bicycles until your doctor says it is safe.
Skip hard exercises or running until the pain completely goes away.
recommended_tests: Give a small sample of your pee so a lab can check for germs.
Have a gentle doctor check the area with their hands to find the trouble.
Do a painless scan using sound waves to look inside your body.
Look inside the tube with a tiny, safe camera if your doctor needs a better view.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you feel pain when peeing
if you see blood in urine

urethral stricture.basic_details: A urethral stricture is when the tube that carries pee out of your body gets too narrow. This makes it hard, painful, or slow to pee.
reason: Scar tissue from past infections (like STIs)
Past use of a urinary catheter
emergency_signs: Severe pain in the lower belly
precautions: See a urologist for treatment or surgery
Get treated for urinary infections immediately
Take prescribed medicines to relax the bladder
things_to_avoid: Delaying medical care if you can't pee
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your pee flowing easily.
Eat fresh fruits and vegetables to help your body heal well.
Stay away from spicy foods that might irritate your bladder.
Cut down on caffeine and alcohol so you do not have to run to the bathroom all the time.
treatment_options: minor surgery to cut the scar
open surgery to rebuild the tube
using a small tube to help pee

diet_recommendation: Eat lots of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Drink plenty of water to help flush your body.
Stay away from greasy, fried, and fast foods.
Do not drink any alcohol while your liver heals.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel better in a few weeks.
It can take a couple of months for your liver to fully heal.
Some types can last a long time and need years of care.
Your recovery speed depends on which type of virus you have.
physical_activities: Get lots of bed rest, especially when you feel very tired.
Take slow, short walks around your house when you have some energy.
Do not lift heavy things or do hard workouts.
Stop exercising right away if you feel dizzy or worn out.
recommended_tests: Get simple blood tests to check how well your liver is working.
Take special germ tests to find out which virus you caught.
Have your doctor check your belly with an ultrasound picture.
Do regular follow-up checkups to see how your liver is healing.

viral warts.basic_details: Viral warts are small, rough bumps on the skin caused by a very common virus. They are totally harmless and can pop up on your hands, feet, or other parts of your body.
reason: Direct skin contact with a wart
emergency_signs: Wart bleeds heavily and won't stop
Skin around the wart becomes red, hot, and infected
Severe pain preventing walking (if on the foot)
precautions: Keep the wart covered with a bandage
Wash hands after touching the wart
things_to_avoid: Picking, scratching, or biting the wart
Trying to cut the wart off yourself
Using the same nail clipper on the wart and healthy nails
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables to keep your immune system strong.
Drink lots of water throughout the day to help your body stay healthy.
Eat foods with vitamin C, like oranges and strawberries, to help heal your skin.
Try to cut down on sugary snacks and drinks, as sugar can slow down healing.
treatment_options: Small surgery to cut it out
recovery_time: Some warts go away all by themselves without any treatment in a few months.
Home treatments usually take about two to three weeks to show good results.
Stubborn warts might need a few weeks or months of doctor visits to fully clear up.
Be patient, because skin takes time to heal and grow back smooth and normal.
physical_activities: Keep exercising normally, but cover your warts with a bandage so they do not touch other things.
Wear shoes if you have warts on your feet so you do not slip or hurt them.
Wash your hands and feet well with soap and water after you finish working out.
Avoid sharing your gym towels, shoes, or socks with anyone else.
recommended_tests: Most of the time, a doctor just looks at the skin with their eyes to spot a wart.
Your doctor might gently scrape the top layer of skin to check for tiny dark dots.
Very rarely, a tiny piece of skin is taken off to test if the doctor is not sure.
You usually do not need any blood tests or big hospital machines for a simple wart.
when_to_visit_doctor: Warts are painful or bleed easily
They do not go away with home care
You have diabetes or weak immunity
They spread to your face or private parts

vitamin b12 deficiency.basic_details: Vitamin B12 deficiency happens when your body does not have enough of this important vitamin, which helps keep your blood and nerve cells healthy. This can make you feel very tired, weak, and dizzy.
reason: Strict vegan or vegetarian diet without supplements
Gut diseases like Crohn's or Celiac
emergency_signs: Sudden inability to walk or balance
Extreme tingling and numbness in hands and feet
precautions: Eat meat, dairy, or fortified cereals
Take prescribed B12 pills or get B12 shots
things_to_avoid: Strict diets without talking to a doctor
diet_recommendation: Eat more eggs, cheese, milk, and yogurt.
Eat meat, fish, and chicken if you eat animal foods.
Choose breakfast cereals that have extra vitamins added to them.
Try plant milk and nutritional yeast if you do not eat meat or dairy.
treatment_options: Take vitamin B12 pills every day
Get vitamin B12 shots from a doctor
Eat more foods with vitamin B12 like meat and eggs
Treat the main cause of the low vitamin
recovery_time: Most people start feeling a little bit better in just a few days.
Your energy levels usually come back to normal after a few weeks of treatment.
It can take a few months to fully fix low vitamin levels in your blood.
Some nerve symptoms might take a long time to go away completely.
physical_activities: Take short, easy walks outside to get some fresh air and light exercise.
Do gentle stretching at home to keep your body moving without getting too tired.
Rest as much as you need to when your body feels weak.
Slowly add more activity to your day as your energy starts to return.
recommended_tests: Get a simple blood test to check how much Vitamin B12 is in your body.
Ask for a complete blood count test to check for anemia.
Check your folate levels because it works together with Vitamin B12.
Ask your doctor to test your iron levels to make sure you are not missing anything else.
when_to_visit_doctor: You feel very tired all the time
Your hands and feet feel numb or tingly
You feel very weak or dizzy

vitreous degeneration.basic_details: Vitreous degeneration is a normal aging process where the jelly inside your eye becomes more watery and forms little clumps that look like floating spots. These spots are harmless most of the time and you just learn to live with them.
reason: Jelly inside the eye shrinks and clumps together
emergency_signs: Sudden shower of hundreds of new floating spots
Flashes of light in the eye
A dark shadow or curtain over your vision
precautions: Get a dilated eye exam to ensure the retina is not torn
things_to_avoid: Heavy lifting or straining if you have flashes
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of colorful fruits and vegetables like carrots, spinach, and oranges every day.
Drink plenty of water to keep your body and eyes well hydrated.
Include fish in your meals because it has healthy fats that are good for your eyes.
Try to eat less junk food and sugary snacks to keep your overall health in good shape.
common_medicines: No specific medicine heals this condition
treatment_options: Waiting for the brain to ignore floaters
Laser therapy to break up large floaters
Surgery to remove the vitreous gel
recovery_time: There is no set recovery time because it is a natural change in the eye rather than an illness.
Your brain is amazing and will usually learn to ignore the floating spots within a few weeks or months.
The spots might not completely go away, but they will likely bother you much less over time.
If you suddenly see flashes of light, you need to see a doctor right away for a checkup.
physical_activities: You can safely do all your normal daily activities without any worry.
Enjoy light exercises like walking, yoga, and gentle stretching to stay healthy.
Try to avoid very heavy contact sports or activities where someone might hit you in the face.
Wear protective eyewear if you are doing yard work or projects that could hurt your eyes.
recommended_tests: A dilated eye exam where the doctor puts special drops in your eyes to look inside.
A careful check of the back part of your eye, called the retina, to make sure it is healthy.
A quick vision test to check how clearly you can see things near and far.
An eye pressure test to make sure the inside of your eye is safe and normal.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you suddenly see many new floaters
If you see flashes of light in your vision
If a dark shadow or curtain covers your sight
If your vision becomes blurry suddenly

vocal cord polyp.basic_details: A vocal cord polyp is a small, soft bump like a blister that forms on your vocal cords from overuse or strain. It makes your voice sound very rough, breathy, or hoarse.
reason: Yelling, singing, or using the voice too much
emergency_signs: Complete loss of voice for weeks
precautions: Go to speech therapy to learn safe talking habits
things_to_avoid: Drinking too much caffeine or alcohol
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of room temperature water all day to keep your throat wet.
Eat warm, soft foods that are easy to swallow and do not scrape your throat.
Stay away from spicy and greasy foods that can cause acid reflux and burn your throat.
Cut back on coffee and soda because they dry out your vocal cords.
recovery_time: Most people start to feel much better a few weeks after they rest their voice.
If you need a minor surgery to remove it, full healing takes about two to three weeks.
You must rest your voice completely for several days right after surgery so it heals right.
Doing speech therapy can take a few months to help you learn how to speak without hurting your throat again.
physical_activities: Do light walking around your house to stay active while your throat heals.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts that make you strain your neck and throat muscles.
Try to relax and do gentle breathing exercises to lower stress in your body.
Get plenty of sleep every night so your body has time to heal itself.
recommended_tests: A doctor will use a tiny, lighted camera put through your nose or mouth to look right at your vocal cords.
They might ask you to make different sounds to see how your vocal cords move and vibrate.
A speech specialist might listen to your normal speaking voice to check how hoarse it sounds.
Sometimes they take a tiny tissue sample during surgery to make sure the bump is just a normal polyp.
when_to_visit_doctor: hoarse voice lasts over two weeks

vulvar disorder.basic_details: A vulvar disorder is an issue that causes pain, itching, or irritation in the outer parts of the female private area. It can happen due to infections, allergies, or skin problems.
reason: Allergic reaction to soaps or clothing
Skin conditions like eczema or lichen sclerosus
emergency_signs: Inability to urinate due to pain
precautions: Wash the area with plain warm water only
Use prescribed steroid or antifungal creams
See a gynecologist for a proper diagnosis
things_to_avoid: Scented soaps, bubble baths, and wipes
Wearing tight pants or wet swimsuits
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body healthy.
Eat more fresh fruits and vegetables to help your skin heal.
Eat yogurt with live cultures to keep your body balanced.
Try to eat less sugar and junk food, as they can sometimes make itching worse.
treatment_options: keep the area clean and dry
recovery_time: Mild irritation from a simple allergy can go away in just a few days.
If you need medicine from a doctor, you might start feeling better in one to two weeks.
More stubborn skin conditions can take a few weeks or even months to fully clear up.
Healing takes longer if you keep scratching or irritating the sensitive skin.
physical_activities: Wear loose-fitting cotton underwear to let the skin breathe and stay dry.
Take a break from heavy workouts like cycling or running until the area feels better.
Avoid swimming pools with strong chemicals like chlorine until you are healed.
Take gentle walks instead of intense exercises to keep your body moving without rubbing the skin.
recommended_tests: A physical checkup where the doctor looks closely at the sore area.
A gentle swab test to check for tiny germs or infections.
A small skin sample check if the doctor needs to look closer at the skin cells.
An allergy skin patch test to see if certain soaps or fabrics are causing the trouble.
when_to_visit_doctor: if you see open sores or lumps
if the itching does not stop
if there is a bad smell or pus

vulvodynia.basic_details: Vulvodynia is a health issue that causes ongoing pain, burning, or discomfort in the private area for no clear reason. It can make everyday things like sitting down or wearing tight pants feel very painful.
emergency_signs: Severe depression or thoughts of self-harm due to chronic pain
Inability to sit down or walk
precautions: See a specialist in pelvic pain
Use prescribed nerve pain medicines or creams
Go to pelvic floor physical therapy
things_to_avoid: Ignoring the emotional toll of chronic pain
diet_recommendation: Drink plenty of water every day to keep your body hydrated.
Eat fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains to stay healthy.
Try to eat less spicy food and citrus fruits if they make you feel worse.
Cut back on sugary foods and drinks that might cause irritation.
recovery_time: Healing takes a different amount of time for every person.
Some people feel better in a few months with the right care.
For others, managing the pain can take a year or even longer.
Patience is very important because progress can happen slowly.
physical_activities: Wear loose-fitting cotton underwear and soft, loose clothes.
Take gentle breaks from sitting down for too long.
Avoid riding bicycles or doing exercises that put pressure on the area.
Do special pelvic floor stretches taught by a trained expert.
recommended_tests: Have a gentle physical checkup with your doctor to look at the area.
Do a cotton swab test to find out exactly where it hurts.
Give a urine sample to check for any hidden infections.
Talk with your doctor about your health history and pain patterns.
when_to_visit_doctor: Pain lasts more than a few days

white blood cell disease.basic_details: White blood cell disease happens when your body makes the wrong number or kind of white blood cells, which makes it hard to fight off germs.
emergency_signs: High fever that will not go away
precautions: Follow treatments by a blood doctor (hematologist)
things_to_avoid: Eating raw or undercooked meat and unwashed vegetables
Being around people with colds or flu
diet_recommendation: Eat thoroughly cooked meats and eggs to avoid food poisoning.
Wash all fruits and vegetables very well before eating them.
Drink plenty of clean water every single day to stay hydrated.
Choose fresh, healthy foods like whole grains and cooked veggies.
recovery_time: Healing can take anywhere from a few weeks to several months depending on the type.
You will need regular check-ups with your doctor to see how you are healing.
Resting a lot helps your body get its strength back faster.
Your energy levels will slowly return to normal as your blood counts improve.
physical_activities: Take short, easy walks around your house or yard when you feel up to it.
Stop and rest immediately if you start feeling tired or dizzy.
Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until your doctor says it is safe.
Do gentle stretching to keep your body moving without tiring you out.
recommended_tests: Get a simple blood draw so the lab can count your white blood cells.
Have your doctor check your temperature and overall body health.
Do extra blood tests to check how well your organs are working.
Get a small check of your bone marrow if your doctor needs a closer look.
when_to_visit_doctor: If you have a high fever
If you feel very tired all the time
If you bleed or bruise easily

whooping cough.basic_details: Whooping cough is a very contagious lung infection that causes bad coughing fits ending in a high-pitched whoop sound. It makes breathing hard, especially for children.
reason: Breathing in droplets from a sneeze or cough
emergency_signs: Baby's face or lips turn blue during a coughing fit
precautions: Get the pertussis vaccine (DTaP or Tdap)
Eat small meals to avoid vomiting
things_to_avoid: Being around babies if you have a cough
Giving cough suppressants (they usually do not work for this)
Ignoring a cough that ends in a 'whoop' sound
diet_recommendation: Drink lots of water and clear broths to stay hydrated and loosen thick mucus.
Eat soft foods like oatmeal, yogurt, and mashed potatoes that are easy to swallow.
Eat small, frequent meals so coughing does not make you throw up a large meal.
Stay away from spicy, greasy, or crunchy foods that can scratch and irritate your throat.
treatment_options: taking antibiotics to stop the sickness
using a humidifier for the air
recovery_time: The illness can last for many weeks or even up to a few months.
The worst coughing fits usually happen during the second and third weeks.
You will slowly start to cough less often as your body heals.
Feeling tired and weak can stick around for a while after the coughing stops.
physical_activities: Get plenty of bed rest to help your body fight the infection.
Avoid heavy workouts, running, or anything that makes you breathe too fast.
Sit up or prop yourself up with pillows to make breathing easier while resting.
Take slow, gentle walks around the house only when you feel strong enough.
recommended_tests: A swab test where a soft stick is rubbed inside your nose or back of your throat.
A blood test to check if your body is fighting off the infection.
A chest X-ray to look at your lungs and make sure there is no pneumonia.
A physical checkup where the doctor listens to your lungs with a stethoscope.
when_to_visit_doctor: you make a loud whooping sound when breathing
you feel very tired and weak

yeast infection.basic_details: A yeast infection is a very common itchy rash caused by an overgrowth of tiny fungus. It usually happens in warm, moist areas of the body.
emergency_signs: Severe pelvic pain or fever (signs of a different infection)
precautions: Use over-the-counter or prescribed antifungal creams
Keep the affected skin clean and completely dry
things_to_avoid: Using scented soaps, sprays, or bubble baths
Wearing wet workout clothes or swimsuits
Having physical intimacy until the infection is cured
diet_recommendation: Eat less sugary foods because sugar helps the yeast grow.
Eat more plain yogurt with live cultures to keep good bacteria healthy.
Drink plenty of water every day to flush out your system.
Eat lots of fresh vegetables and whole grains for overall health.
treatment_options: Keep the affected area dry and clean
recovery_time: Mild cases usually start feeling better in two to three days.
Most infections completely go away within one week.
Stubborn cases might take up to two weeks to fully heal.
Always finish all your medicine even if you feel better.
physical_activities: Take a break from heavy workouts until the skin heals.
Avoid swimming in pools while you have the infection.
Wear loose and breathable clothes when you do light movement.
Shower and change out of sweaty clothes right away after moving.
recommended_tests: A doctor can often just look at the rash to know what it is.
A gentle swab of the area can be tested in a lab.
A simple blood test might check your sugar levels if infections keep happening.
An acidity test of the skin or fluid can confirm the type of fungus.
when_to_visit_doctor: This is your very first yeast infection
You have fever or severe pain

rheumatoid arthritis.basic_details: Rheumatoid arthritis is a long-term health issue where your body's defense system mistakenly attacks your joints. This makes your joints swollen, stiff, and painful, especially in the hands and feet.
emergency_signs: Joint becomes extremely red, hot, and swollen
diet_recommendation: Eat plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables every day.
Include fish like salmon that are good for your body.
Drink lots of water instead of sugary drinks.
Try to eat less processed snacks and fast food.
treatment_options: taking medicine to stop joint damage
recovery_time: This condition stays with you for life, so it does not completely go away.
You can have long periods where you feel much better with very little pain.
Treatment helps you feel good and keeps your joints working well.
Bad flare-ups can last for days or weeks before settling down.
physical_activities: Go for gentle daily walks to keep your body moving.
Try swimming since water takes the weight off your sore joints.
Do light stretching every morning to reduce body stiffness.
Rest and stop exercising right away if you feel sharp pain.
recommended_tests: Get simple blood tests to check for body inflammation.
Take X-ray pictures of your hands and feet to look at joint health.
Have your doctor gently press and check your joints for swelling.
Run special antibody blood tests to help confirm the exact issue.
when_to_visit_doctor: you have new joint pain and swelling
your joints feel warm and look red
morning stiffness lasts more than an hour
your medicines are not helping your pain
